entries.name: Addicted Approach
entries: For some, the consumption of substances is the entirety of their life. For berserkers of the Addicted Approach, substances cause their fury to burn stronger and deeper, granting significant benefits.

entries.name: Slythmonger Savvy
entries: {@i {@b Addicted Approach:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency in your choice of brewer's kit or spicer's kit. Additionally, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid the low or addiction to substances. Lastly, you can consume substances as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, and when you do so, you can also enter a rage as a part of this same {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Freedom Through Slavery
entries: {@i {@b Addicted Approach:} 3rd level} While you are raging or experiencing the high of a substance, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} that would force you to act against your will, be {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened}, or prevent you from attacking a creature. If you are both raging and experiencing the high of a substance, you are instead immune to effects that would force you to act against your will or would prevent you from attacking a creature.

entries.name: Release the Beast
entries: {@i {@b Addicted Approach:} 6th level} While you are raging or experiencing the high of a substance, when you hit a creature with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, you can expend a Hit Die to deal additional damage to the target. Roll the Hit Die, adding the result of the die to the damage roll. If you are both raging and experiencing the high of a substance, you also add your Constitution modifier to the damage roll.

entries.name: Seeing Sound
entries: {@i {@b Addicted Approach:} 10th level} While you are raging or experiencing the high of a substance, you have {@sense Blindsight|sw5e-phb|blindsight} with a range of 10 feet. If you are both raging and experiencing the high of a substance, you instead have {@sense Blindsight|sw5e-phb|blindsight} with a range of 30 feet. If you would already have {@sense Blindsight|sw5e-phb|blindsight}, it instead increases by 5 feet or 15 feet, respectively.

entries.name: Fuel the Rampage
entries: {@i {@b Addicted Approach:} 14th level} While you are both raging and experiencing the high of a substance, having 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} doesn't knock you {@condition Unconscious|sw5e-phb|unconscious}. You still must make {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throws}, and you suffer the normal effects of taking damage while at 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}. However, if you would die due to failing {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throws}, you don't die until your rage ends, and you die then only if you still have 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}.

entries.name: Armored Approach
entries: Many berserkers forgo armor and rely on their own fortitude. Berserkers of the Armored Approach, however, embrace the use of armor. Each one customizes their own suit of armor to be used both defensively and offensively, so that the suit becomes an extension of the berserker's own might and fury.

entries.name: Spiked Armor
entries: {@i {@b Armored Approach:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency in {@item Armormech's implements|sw5e-phb|armormech's implements}. Over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can customize a suit of light or {@filter medium armor|items|type=medium armor} into spiked armor. You must have the armor and {@item Armormech's implements|sw5e-phb|armormech's implements} in order to perform this modification. You can only have one suit of spiked armor at a time.

This armor gains the barbed (1d4) property. If the armor already has the barbed property, the barbed damage increases by one step (from {@dice d4} to {@dice d6}, or from {@dice d6} to {@dice d8}). Additionally, while raging, you add your rage damage bonus to your barbed damage when you successfully initiate or maintain a grapple.
While wearing your spiked armor, you can use your Constitution modifier instead of your Dexterity modifier when determining your AC.

Additionally, while wearing your spiked armor, you can use your spiked armor as an improvised weapon. When you do so, you are considered proficient with it, and if your armor's barbed damage would be higher than your damage with improvised weapons, you use the barbed damage instead. If you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn and make at least one attack with your spiked armor, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to make an additional attack with your spiked armor against the same target.

entries.name: Environmental Shielding
entries: {@i {@b Armored Approach:} 6th level} You customize your spiked armor to better protect you. Choose one of the following damage types: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or sonic. While wearing your spiked armor, you have resistance to damage of the chosen type. Over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can select a different damage type, provided you have the armor and {@item Armormech's implements|sw5e-phb|armormech's implements} with you.

Additionally, while wearing your spiked armor, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} made to avoid {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion} due to extreme heat or cold.

entries.name: Customized Armor
entries: {@i {@b Armored Approach:} 10th level} You learn new ways to customize your spiked armor. Choose one of the following options. While wearing your spiked armor, you gain the effects of the chosen option. Over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can select a different option, provided you have the armor and {@item Armormech's implements|sw5e-phb|armormech's implements} with you.

entries.name: Defensive Field
entries: On your turn, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to gain temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to 1d12 + your berserker level. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Deflective Layer
entries: Your {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb|armor class} increases by 1.

entries.name: Grappling Line
entries: You can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to launch a grappling line at one creature of your choice that you can see within 15 feet. The target must succeed on a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Strength modifier) or be pulled up to 10 feet in a straight line towards you. If it ends this movement within 5 feet of you, it takes kinetic damage from your armor spikes equal to your Strength modifier.

entries.name: Integrated Sonar
entries: You can use an action to give yourself the benefits of the {@i true sight} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} for 1 hour. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Neural Interface
entries: You are immune to all effects that would cause you to be {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} or {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened}.

entries.name: Spiked Retribution
entries: {@i {@b Armored Approach:} 14th level} When a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with a melee attack, the attacker takes kinetic damage equal to your Strength modifier, as long as you are wearing your spiked armor and you aren't {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated}.
If you are raging, you add your rage damage bonus            to this damage.

entries.name: Beastmaster Approach
entries: Many berserkers feel a primal attunement to nature. For berserkers of the Beastmaster Approach, that attunement manifests itself in bestial marks and manifestations that grant the berserker newfound abilities.

entries.name: Bestial Fury
entries: {@i {@b Beastmaster Approach:} 3rd level} While raging, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on any Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|sw5e-phb}) checks.

Additionally, once on each of your turns while raging, you can mark a creature you can see as your prey for the duration of your rage (no action required). When you do so, once per turn when you deal damage to the creature with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}, you deal an additional 1d4 damage of the same type. Once per turn when the creature deals damage to you with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}, you take an additional 1d4 damage of the same type. This die increases to {@dice d6} at 5th level, {@dice d8} at 9th level, {@dice d10} at 13th level, and {@dice d12} at 17th level. You can only have one creature marked in this way at a time.

entries.name: Pack Tactics
entries: {@i {@b Beastmaster Approach:} 3rd level} When you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against a creature, another enemy of the creature is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn't {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated}, you can reroll one of the dice once.

entries.name: Animalistic Momentum
entries: {@i {@b Beastmaster Approach:} 6th level} You gain a your choice of a climbing or swimming {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}. Additionally, you gain an effect while raging based on your choice of {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}:

items: If you chose a climbing {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}, you can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}.
If you chose a swimming {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to Dash or Disengage while in water.

entries.name: Lick Wounds
entries: {@i {@b Beastmaster Approach:} 10th level} Whenever you reduce a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} while raging, you gain a number of temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to your berserker level, which last for the duration of your rage.

entries.name: Hunter's Call
entries: {@i {@b Beastmaster Approach:} 14th and 17th level} When you enter your rage, you can choose up to 5 allies that you can see within 30 feet of you. You gain 5 temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} for each creature. For the duration of your rage, once on each of their turns, an affected ally can add your rage damage bonus to a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}'s damage roll.
You can use this feature five times. You gain an additional use at 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Beastmaster Approach (Companion)
entries: Many berserkers feel a primal attunement to nature. For berserkers of the Beastmaster Approach, that attunement manifests itself in a bond with a beast companion that accompanies a berserker on his journey.

entries.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: {@i {@b Beastmaster Approach:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency in {@skill Animal Handling|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Beast Companion
entries: {@i {@b Beastmaster Approach:} 3rd, 11th, and 17th level} You learn to capitalize on a primal attunement to nature to forge a powerful bond with your own beast companion.
Create your beast companion as detailed in the Companions section of the Customization Options document for Expanded Content.
In addition to its traits and features, your beast companion gains additional benefits while it is bonded to you:

items: Your beast gains two additional traits. It gains one more additional trait when you reach 11th level in this class. For each beast trait in excess of your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, your number of available Hit Dice that can be spend to restore {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} is reduced by 1.

entries: Lastly, while bonded and within 10 feet of you, your beast companion gains the benefits of one of your chosen instincts. If that instinct relies on raging, your beast companion gains the benefits of that instinct while you are raging.
At 11th level, your companion must be within 30 feet of you to benefit from this feature. At 17th level, your companion must be within 60 feet.

entries.name: Pack Tactics
entries: {@i {@b Beastmaster Approach:} 3rd level} When you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against a creature your companion has dealt damage since the start of your last turn, you can reroll one of the dice once. When your companion has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against a creature you've dealt damage since the start of your last turn, it can reroll one of the dice once.

entries.name: Animalistic Momentum
entries: {@i {@b Beastmaster Approach:} 6th, 11th, and 17th level} Your bond with your beast companion strengthens, granting the following benefits while your beast companion is within 10 feet of you:

items: If you or your beast have a climbing or swimming {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} and the other doesn't, the other gains it with the same {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}. If you both have the a climbing or swimming {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}, you both use the larger {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} of the two, which then increases by 5 feet.
Whenever your beast deals damage to a hostile creature you can see on your turn, it counts as you taking a hostile action for the purposes of maintaining your rage.

entries: This radius increases to 30 feet at 11th level 60 feet at 17th level.

entries.name: Lick Wounds
entries: {@i {@b Beastmaster Approach:} 10th level} Whenever your companion reduces a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} while you are raging, it gains a number of temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to your berserker level, which last for the duration of your rage.

entries.name: Hunter's Call
entries: {@i {@b Beastmaster Approach:} 14th and 17th level} When you enter your rage, you can choose up to 5 allies that you can see within 30 feet of you. You gain 5 temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} for each creature. For the duration of your rage, once on each of their turns, an affected ally can add your rage damage bonus to a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}'s damage roll.
You can use this feature five times. You gain an additional use at 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Bloodstorm Approach
entries: The Bloodstorm Approach is said to have originated from the ancient wookiee Hroufrasnooohn clan (which loosely translates to Bloodstorm in {@language Galactic Basic|sw5e-phb}), whose warriors performed gravity-defying feats with their flying vibroaxes through a combination of unorthodox techniques and a mystical belief in their own abilities. A berserker who follows this approach can hurl their devastating weapons at enemies with such power and skill that it completely blurs the line between melee and ranged combat.

entries.name: Furious Throw
entries: {@i {@b Bloodstorm Approach:} 3rd level} Your throwing techniques have become a perfect extension of your melee prowess. When you throw a weapon with which you are proficient, you can benefit from your class features that only apply to melee weapon attacks, such as Rage or Reckless Attack.

entries.name: Returning Attacks
entries: {@i {@b Bloodstorm Approach:} 3rd level} Any weapon you throw can ricochet back to you at your command. When you make a thrown {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}, you may have the weapon fly back to your hand immediately after the attack.

entries.name: Throw Anything
entries: {@i {@b Bloodstorm Approach:} 6th level} Your strength and mastery of throwing techniques has allowed you to throw vibroaxes as easily as others hurl {@item Vibrodagger|sw5e-phb|vibrodaggers}. When you are wielding a light- or vibro-weapon with which you are proficient, it gains the thrown property (range 20/60).

entries.name: Fling People
entries: {@i {@b Bloodstorm Approach:} 10th level} You learn to throw creatures as easily as you throw your weapons. When you successfully grapple a creature, you may immediately throw the creature.

entries.name: Throw Friend
entries: If the creature is a willing ally and volunteers to be {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled}, you throw the target into any unoccupied space within 60 feet. That creature may immediately use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, adding your Strength modifier to the attack's damage roll.

entries.name: Throw Foe
entries: If the creature is an opponent, you throw the target into any unoccupied space within 30 feet, where it takes damage equal to your Strength modifier and falls {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}.

entries.name: Raging Whirlwind
entries: {@i {@b Bloodstorm Approach:} 14th level} You can send your weapon spinning into a gravity-defying whirlwind of pain. Once per rage as an action, you may throw a weapon with the thrown property to a point you choose within 60 feet. The weapon fills the air as a cyclone in a 10 foot radius sphere centered on that point. A creature takes damage equal to the thrown weapon's damage + your Strength modifier + your Rage Damage when it enter's the whirlwind's area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there. This effect ends when you command the weapon to return to you (no action required) or your rage ends.

entries.name: Brawling Approach
entries: Most berserkers require weapons. For berserkers of the Brawling Approach, however, everything is their weapon.

entries.name: Fists of Fury
entries: {@i {@b Brawling Approach:} 3rd level} You've learned to hone your rage through your fists. Your unarmed strike damage increases by one step (from 1 to {@dice d4}, {@dice d4} to {@dice d6}, or {@dice d6} to {@dice d8}).

entries.name: Reckless Strikes
entries: {@i {@b Brawling Approach:} 3rd level} While you are raging, not wearing {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor}, and not wielding a shield, when you hit a creature with an unarmed strike or improvised weapon, you can choose to forgo your rage damage to make the attack a reckless strike.

Some of your reckless strikes require your target to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the reckless strike's effects. The {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC is calculated as follows:
{@b Reckless Strike save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Strength modifier

You can use these features a combined number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, as shown in the berserker table. You regain all expended uses when you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Bracing Strike
entries: You gain temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to your rage damage bonus. If the target is {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} by you, you instead gain temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to twice your rage damage bonus.

entries.name: Punishing Strike
entries: Your target must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the creature is {@condition Deafened|sw5e-phb|deafened} until the start of its next turn. If the target is {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} by you, it is instead {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Staggering Strike
entries: Your target must make a Strength or Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (the target chooses the ability score to use). On a failed save, your target is pushed back 5 feet. If the target is {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} by you, it is instead knocked {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}.

entries.name: Shattering Strikes
entries: {@i {@b Brawling Approach:} 6th level} Your rage causes your strikes to overcome the hardest of materials. While raging, you gain the following benefits:

items: Your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes} and improved weapons count as enhanced for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to unenhanced attacks and damage.
Your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes} deal double damage against structures.

entries.name: Stop Hitting Each Other
entries: {@i {@b Brawling Approach:} 10th level} You can grapple creatures two sizes larger than you, instead of one.

Additionally, you can use creatures you have {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} that are at least one size smaller than you as improvised weapons. When you do so, when you hit with an attack using a creature as a weapon, it takes damage equal to your Strength modifier. While raging, you can instead use creatures your size or smaller as improvised weapons.

entries.name: Enforcer
entries: {@i {@b Brawling Approach:} 14th level} When you would make an unarmed strike or attack with an improvised weapon with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}, you can choose to forgo the {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}. If you do so, your {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} range increases by 1 for that attack, and on a hit, you deal maximum damage instead of rolling.

entries.name: Champion Approach
entries: Some berserkers revel in battle for battle's sake. For berserkers of the Champion Approach, this revelry is the goal to which they constantly strive.

entries.name: Champion Superiority
entries: {@i {@b Champion Approach:} 3rd level} You learn maneuvers that are fueled by special dice called {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}. See {@book chapter 13|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} for the {@book maneuvers list|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers}.

entries.name: Maneuvers Known
entries: You learn two maneuvers of your choice, and you earn more at higher levels, as shown in the Maneuvers Known column of the Champion Superiority table. Many maneuvers enhance an attack in some way. You can use only one maneuver per attack, and you may only use each maneuver once per turn.
Each time you learn new maneuvers, you can also replace one maneuver you know with a different one.

entries.name: Superiority Dice
entries: You have two {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}, which are d4s, and you earn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Superiority Dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} Quantity column of the Champion Superiority table. This die changes as you gain berserker levels, as shown in the {@book Superiority Dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} Size column of the Champion Superiority table. A superiority die is expended when you use it.
You regain all of your expended {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Maneuver Ability
entries: Your {@book maneuver ability|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} varies based on the type of the maneuver you use. You use Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution for {@book physical maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Physical} (your choice), Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma for {@book mental maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Mental} (your choice), and an ability of your choice for {@book general maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|General}. You use this ability whenever a maneuver refers to your {@book maneuver ability|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}. Additionally, you use this ability modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a maneuver you use.
{@b Maneuver save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your {@book maneuver ability|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} modifier

entries.name: Reckless Maneuvers
entries: {@i {@b Champion Approach:} 3rd level} When you use your Reckless Attack feature, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on superiority die rolls that would be added to the attack or damage rolls of your affected attacks.

entries.name: The Thrill
entries: {@i {@b Champion Approach:} 6th level} You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid being {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} or {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened}, and creatures can't have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid being {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} or {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} by effects that you control.

entries.name: Battlefield Euphoria
entries: {@i {@b Champion Approach:} 10th level} While raging, when you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, and when you reduce a hostile creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, you recover an expended superiority die.

entries.name: Furious Influence
entries: {@i {@b Champion Approach:} 14th level} While raging, you gain the following benefits:

items: You are resistant to psychic damage.
When you affect an ally with a maneuver, they gain the benefit of one of your damage resistances until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Frenzied Approach
entries: For some berserkers, rage is a means to an end—that end being violence. The Frenzied Approach is that of untrammeled fury, slick with blood. As you enter the berserker's rage, you thrill in the chaos of battle, heedless of your own health or well-being.

entries.name: Frenzy
entries: {@i {@b Frenzied Approach:} 3rd level} You can go into a frenzy when you enter your rage. If you do so, for the duration of your rage you can make a single {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on each of your turns after this one.

The first time you use this feature, you suffer no ill effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you suffer one level of {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion} when your rage ends each time you use it.

When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you reduce your {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion} level by 2, instead of 1. Additionally, any effect that removes {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion} reduces your {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion} by 1 additional level.

entries.name: Maniacal Rage
entries: {@i {@b Frenzied Approach:} 3rd level} While raging, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb}) checks.

entries.name: Mindless Rage
entries: {@i {@b Frenzied Approach:} 6th level} You can't be {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} or {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} while raging. If you are {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} or {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} when you enter your rage, the effect is suspended for the duration of the rage.

entries.name: Intimidating Presence
entries: {@i {@b Frenzied Approach:} 10th level} You can use your action to frighten someone with your menacing presence. When you do so, choose one creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. If the creature can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Charisma modifier) or be {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} of you until the end of your next turn. On subsequent turns, you can use your action to extend the duration of this effect on the {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} creature until the end of your next turn. This effect ends if the creature ends its turn out of line of sight or more than 60 feet away from you. While raging, you add double your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} to the save DC, instead of your normal {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}.
If the creature succeeds on its {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, it becomes immune to this feature for 24 hours.

entries.name: Retaliation
entries: {@i {@b Frenzied Approach:} 14th level} When you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} against that creature.

entries.name: Industrial Approach
entries: While some berserkers are content to surrender to their rage, others prefer a more tactful approach. Berserkers of the Industrial Approach augment their rage with the versatility of technology, adding elemental explosions to their already fearsome arsenal.

entries.name: Techcasting
entries: {@i {@b Industrial Approach:} 3rd level} You have derived powers from schematics with the aid of your {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}. See {@book chapter 10|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} for the general rules of {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} and {@book chapter 12|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} for the {@book tech powers list|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

entries.name: Tech Powers Known
entries: You learn 3 {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of your choice, and you learn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Tech Powers Known|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} column of the Industrial Approach {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table. You may not learn a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of a level higher than your Max Power Level.

entries.name: Tech Points
entries: You have a number of tech points equal to half of your berserker level, as shown in the Tech Points column of the Industrial Approach {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table, + your Intelligence modifier. You use these tech points to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. You regain all expended tech points when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Max Power Level
entries: Many {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} can be overcharged, consuming more tech points to create a greater effect. You can overcharge these powers to a maximum level, which increases at higher levels, as shown in the Max Power Level column of the Industrial Approach {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting}         table.
You may only cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} at            4th-level once. You regain the          ability to do so after a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Techcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence is your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} for your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. You use your Intelligence whenever a power refers to your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability}. Additionally, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you cast and when making an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with one.
{@b Tech save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence modifier
{@b Tech attack modifier} = your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence modifier

entries.name: Techcasting Focus
entries: You use a {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad} (found in {@book chapter 5|sw5e-phb|5} of the Player's Handbook) as a tech focus for your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

entries.name: Industrious Tech
entries: {@i {@b Industrial Approach:} 3rd level} You can cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} while raging as long as the power's casting time is no more than 1 action and the power does not require {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}. While raging, you add your rage damage to damage rolls from {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you cast that require a tech attack or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. If a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} damages more than one target, you may only apply your rage damage to one of them.

Casting {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} during rage counts as attacking for the purposes of maintaining rage, and you can use your Reckless Attack feature to gain {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} when casting a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} that requires a tech attack.

entries.name: Explosive Resilience
entries: {@i {@b Industrial Approach:} 6th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level} Once per round, when you deal damage that includes your rage damage, you can cause a localized explosion around the recipient of that damage. Each creature within 5 feet of the damaged creature other than you takes acid, cold, fire, ion, or lightning damage (your choice) equal to your rage damage bonus, and you gain resistance to the chosen damage type until the end of your next turn.
You can use this feature three times. You gain an additional use at 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Painkiller
entries: {@i {@b Industrial Approach:} 10th level} Whenever you cast a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of 1st-level or higher, or deal damage using your Explosive Resilience feature, you can cause a friendly creature you can see within 30 feet to gain temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to half your berserker level + your Intelligence modifier. Additionally, while they have these temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, they have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against effects that would cause them to be {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened}.

entries.name: Final Countdown
entries: {@i {@b Industrial Approach:} 14th level} When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} but not killed outright, and you have at least one tech point remaining, you can expend all your remaining tech points and instead to drop to one hit point (no action required). If you do so, each creature within 30 feet of you must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC. On a failed save, they take 1d12 acid, cold, fire, ion, or lightning damage (your choice) damage for each tech point spent in this way, or half as much on a successful one.

entries.name: Precision Approach
entries: Some berserkers have learned to channel their rage into a method of increasing their focus and precision to supernatural levels. Those berserkers who choose the Precision Approach hone their rage to a fine point, becoming agile warriors who ruthlessly dispatch their foes.

entries.name: Careful Steps
entries: {@i {@b Precision Approach:} 3rd level} You gain skills that represent your precise movement. You gain proficiency in your choice of {@skill Acrobatics|sw5e-phb} or {@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}. While raging, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on checks you make with the chosen skill.

entries.name: Focused Rage
entries: {@i {@b Precision Approach:} 3rd level} You hone your rage to a razor sharp focus. While raging, when you make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} using Dexterity, you add your rage damage to the damage roll. Additionally, you can use your Reckless Attack feature to give you {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on melee weapon attacks using Dexterity during your turn.

entries.name: Battle Anticipation
entries: {@i {@b Precision Approach:} 6th level} While raging, your {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} range with melee weapon attacks using Dexterity increases by 1.

entries.name: Improved Danger Sense
entries: {@i {@b Precision Approach:} 10th level} While raging, when you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to take only half damage against effects that you can see, such as traps and powers, you are treated as proficient in the save, and you instead take no damage if you succeed on a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and only half damage if you fail.

entries.name: Calm Within the Storm
entries: {@i {@b Precision Approach:} 14th level} The precision with which you act during your rage causes you to become a storm of reactive lethality. When you use your Reckless Attack feature, you can make a number of {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} without using your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}, and when a creature within 5 feet of you misses you with an attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} using Dexterity against that creature.

entries.name: Warchief Approach
entries: For some berserkers, it is their duty or birthright to lead their tribe and kin to battle and victory. The Warchief Approach is one forged from alliances, bonds, and strategy. In combat, your rages are less mindless, and more focused. Ignoring the distractions of unimportant events, your attention hones in on the battlefield and how best to direct and control it. You guide your allies' strikes, and your presence is enough to wash away their fatigue.

entries.name: Savage Diplomat
entries: {@i {@b Warchief Approach:} 3rd level} Your path necessitates that you build relationships with others, for the betterment of your tribe or yourself. You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb} or {@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb}. You can choose to learn one language in place of the skill proficiency.

entries.name: Commanding Rage
entries: {@i {@b Warchief Approach:} 3rd level} You become more aware of your allies, and their intent when fighting at your side. While you are raging, when an ally within 10 feet of you makes an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against an enemy, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to grant {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} to that attack and add your rage damage bonus to the damage roll, if the attack hits.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Inspiring Presence
entries: {@i {@b Warchief Approach:} 6th level} Your mere presence on the battlefield rallies your allies. When you rage, choose up to 3 allies that you can see within 30 feet of you. Each creature gains temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to half your berserker level + your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1).

entries.name: Raid Planning
entries: {@i {@b Warchief Approach:} 10th level} You learn to flare up your allies' drive for combat, urging them to follow you into the fray. During a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you tell sagas, sing battle songs, and give inspiring speeches. At the end of the {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} choose up to 5 creatures that can hear and understand you (which can include yourself) to add your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1) to their next {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb} check, and a 10 foot bonus to their {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} on their first turn of combat.

entries.name: War Chant
entries: {@i {@b Warchief Approach:} 14th level} You have memorized the litanies, songs, and chants of your people and their dedication to war. When you enter a rage on your turn, you can enter a commanding rage for one minute. When you do so, during this turn and at the start of each of your turns, you have a number of special reactions equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} you can only use for your Commanding Rage feature. When you use Commanding Rage with these special reactions, they do not count against your uses of that feature. You can only use one {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} per turn. Additionally, during this rage, when an enemy within 10 feet of you makes an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against an ally, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to reduce the attack by an amount equal to your Charisma modifier.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Way of Confluence
entries: The Force binds us, creating an intangible bridge connecting all living things. Those consulars who follow the Way of Confluence master this power, manipulating those connections to both sustain and torment.

entries.name: Manipulate Life Force
entries: {@i {@b Way of Confluence:} 3rd level} When you reduce a hostile creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} with a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, or restore {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} to a creature with 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} with a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, you gain temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to half your consular level + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one).

entries.name: Empowered Connection
entries: {@i {@b Way of Confluence:} 6th level} While you have temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, you can add half your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one) to any damage or healing you do with {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} that doesn't already include that modifier.

entries.name: Life Eternal
entries: {@i {@b Way of Confluence:} 10th level} You can use your powerful connection to the Force to keep fighting when others would fall. When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} but not killed outright, you can spend 5 force points to drop to 1 hit point instead.

entries.name: Interconnectedness
entries: {@i {@b Way of Confluence:} 14th and 17th level} When you cast a 5th level or lower {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} that deals damage or restores {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} and targets only one creature, the power can instead target two creatures within range and within 5 feet of each other.
You can use this feature five times. You gain an additional use at 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Dynamic Attachment
entries: {@i {@b Way of Confluence:} 18th level} While you have temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, you have resistance against the damage of {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, and your {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} ignore resistances.

entries.name: Way of Endurance
entries: The Force manifests in myriad ways; while some use the Force to manipulate the world around them, others use it to enhance themselves. Those consulars who follow the Way of Endurance channel the Force to allow them to overcome and reflect the most grievous of injuries.

entries.name: Upheld by the Force
entries: {@i {@b Way of Endurance:} 3rd level} The Force flowing through your body strengthens you, granting the following benefits:

items: Your hit point maximum increases by 3, and it increases by 1 again whenever you gain a level in this class.
Your base AC becomes 13 + your Constitution modifier.

When you make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} as a part of a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} you cast, you can use Wisdom or Charisma (your choice) instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls.

entries: Additionally, as an action, you can gain resistance to kinetic and energy damage for 1 minute. This effect lasts until you end it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated}, or you don armor other than a shield. You can use this feature twice. You regain all expended uses of it when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Retaliation Strike
entries: {@i {@b Way of Endurance:} 6th, 9th,  13th, and 17th level} You learn to turn an opponent's aggression back on them. When you deal damage with a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} or a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, if you took damage since the start of your last turn, you deal an extra 1d6 damage. The damage is the same type as the power or weapon's damage.
This die increases when you reach certain levels in this class: to 1d8 at 9th level, to 1d10 at 13th level, and to 1d12 at 17th level.

entries.name: Boundless Vitality
entries: {@i {@b Way of Endurance:} 10th level} When you take damage, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and expend a force point to regain health equal to 1d8 + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one) as long as the damage would not reduce your {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} to 0.
This die increases when you reach certain levels in this class: to 1d10 at 13th level, and to 1d12 at 17th level.

entries.name: Unrelenting Resilience
entries: {@i {@b Way of Endurance:} 14th level} When you use your Boundless Vitality feature while concentrating on a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, you can add the result of the roll to the Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} made to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}.

Additionally, when you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} but not killed outright while Upheld by the Force is active, you can drop to 1 hit point instead. You can't use this feature again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: The Force Unleashed
entries: {@i {@b Way of Endurance:} 18th level} As an action, you can choose a point within 60 feet. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of that point must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your universal force save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes 5d10 force damage and suffers 1 level of {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion}. On a successful save, a creature takes half damage and does not suffer {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion}.

For each creature that fails this {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, a friendly creature within 30 feet of them can regain {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to the amount of damage dealt. A friendly creature can only gain this benefit once per turn.
You can use this feature six times. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Way of Manipulation
entries: The power of the Force is both vast and diverse, with uses varying drastically based on their wielder. Those consulars who follow the Way of Manipulation learn to control their weapons with the Force, maneuvering them across the battlefield.

entries.name: Saber Storm
entries: {@i {@b Way of Manipulation:} 3rd, 5th, 11th, and 17th level} You learn to deftly control your weapons utilizing the Force. As an action, you can initiate your Saber Storm. When you do so, select a light- or vibro-weapon within 5 feet that is not worn or carried by a conscious creature other than you, and use the Force to cause it to levitate, acting as an extension of your will for 1 minute. When you activate this feature, you can cause the weapon to move up to 10 feet and make a melee force attack against a creature within 5 feet of it. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 + your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} modifier damage. The type is of the normal damage dealt by the weapon. The weapon then returns to your side.

Your weapon moves with you, and while Saber Storm is active and you have a weapon animated, on each of your turns you can use an action to move a weapon up to 10 feet and repeat the attack against a creature within 5 feet of it. The weapon then returns to your side. Your Saber Storm ends early if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated}. At any time, you can end this feature and return the animated weapon to your hand.
Additionally, while your Saber Storm is active, and at least one animated weapon is within 5 feet of you, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a bonus to your AC equal to your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of +1) if it doesn't already include that modifier.

You gain a bonus to any Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} you make to maintain your {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} on a power. The bonus equals your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of +1).

entries: This feature can animate more than one weapon when you reach higher levels: two weapons at 5th level, three weapons at 11th level, and four weapons at 17th level. When you use your action to attack with your weapons, you can direct them at the same target or at different ones. Make a separate {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} for each weapon.
At 5th level, the distance your weapon can travel increases to 20 feet. This distance increases to 30 feet at 11th level, and 40 feet at 17th level.
You can use this feature twice. You regain all expended uses of it when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Deceptive Strike
entries: {@i {@b Way of Manipulation:} 6th level} When you cast a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} with a range of touch while Saber Storm is active, your animated weapon can move up to its range and deliver the power as if it had cast it.

entries.name: Guarding Weapon
entries: {@i {@b Way of Manipulation:} 10th level} You can direct your animated weapons to absorb damage while your Saber Storm is activate. When you take damage, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to expend a number of force points up to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} to have your animated weapon intercept it, and reduce that damage to you by an amount equal to five times the number of points spent.

entries.name: Isolate
entries: {@i {@b Way of Manipulation:} 14th level} When you deal damage to a creature while Saber Storm is active, and that creature fails a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} on a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, you can steal and redirect the power. Until the end of your next turn, either you or the creature who failed the Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} gain the effects of the power (your choice).

entries.name: Sapping Storm
entries: {@i {@b Way of Manipulation:} 18th level} When you reduce a hostile creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} while Saber Storm is active, you gain temporary force points equal to your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one). These temporary force points can not exceed your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice), and when you would spend a force point while you have temporary force points, the temporary force points are spent first. When Saber Storm ends, you lose any remaining temporary force points.

entries.name: Way of Negation
entries: Some force users seek mastery over the fundamentals of energy manipulation, known as tutaminis. Those consulars who follow the Way of Negation harness this power to limit the havoc that other force-wielders might wreak.

entries.name: Force Deflection
entries: {@i {@b Way of Negation:} 3rd, 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level} When you fail a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to gain a bonus to that {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} equal to your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of +1).
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Power Surge
entries: {@i {@b Way of Negation:} 6th level} You learn to simultaneously limit a creature's {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} and store that power within yourself to later strengthen your damaging {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

You can store a maximum number of power surges equal to your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one). Whenever you successfully end a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} with a power such as {@i force suppression} or {@i sever force}, or use your Force shield or Force Deflection features to successfully avoid an attack or succeed on a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you gain one power surge, as you redirect the flow of the Force into yourself.

Once per turn, when you deal damage to a creature or object with a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, you can spend one power surge to deal extra damage to that target. The extra damage is of the same type as the power's damage, and it equals half your consular level.

Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, your number of power surges resets to one. If you end a {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest} with no power surges, you gain one power surge.

entries.name: Enduring Focus
entries: {@i {@b Way of Negation:} 10th level} You can casually deflect attacks while channeling your power. While you are concentrating on a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, you have a +2 bonus to your AC and all {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}.
Additionally, you can extend your Force Deflection to a creature within 5 feet of you when they fail a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

entries.name: Conflux
entries: {@i {@b Way of Negation:} 14th level} When you use your Force Deflection feature, you can cause a ripple in the Force to expand from you. Up to three creatures of your choice that you can see within 60 feet of you each take force damage equal to half your consular level.

entries.name: Tutaminis Mastery
entries: {@i {@b Way of Negation:} 18th level} When you use a Force-Empowered Casting option, you can spend a power surge to use it without spending additional force points.

entries.name: Way of the Seer
entries: The Force guides us in innumerable ways, often manifesting as visions. Those consulars who follow the Way of Seer attempt to harness these visions in an attempt to work towards the best possible future, as they see it.

entries.name: Force Visions
entries: {@i {@b Way of the Seer:} 3rd level} Glimpses of the future begin to press in on your awareness. When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, roll two d20s and record the numbers rolled. You can replace any {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, or {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} made by you or a creature that you can see with one of these foretelling rolls. You must choose to do so before the roll, and you can replace a roll in this way only once per turn. Each foretelling roll can be used only once. When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you lose any unused foretelling rolls.

entries.name: Powerful Mind
entries: {@i {@b Way of the Seer:} 6th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level} You can use your force abilities to read a creature's thoughts. You can then use your access to the creature's mind to command it.

As an action, choose one creature that you can see within 60 feet of you. That creature must make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your universal force save DC. If the creature succeeds on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can't use this feature on it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. If the creature fails its save, you can read its surface thoughts (those foremost in its mind, reflecting its current emotions and what it is actively thinking about) when it is within 60 feet of you. This effect lasts for 1 minute. During that time, you can use your action to end this effect and cast the {@i coerce mind} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} at its base level on the creature without expending force points. The target automatically fails its {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against the power.
You can use this feature three times. You gain an additional use at 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Visions of the Past
entries: {@i {@b Way of the Seer:} 10th level} You can call up visions of the past that relate to an object you hold or your immediate surroundings. You spend at least 1 minute in meditation, then receive dreamlike, shadowy glimpses of recent events. You can meditate in this way for a number of minutes equal to your Wisdom score and must maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} during that time, as if you were casting a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}. Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

{@b {@i Object Reading.}} Holding an object as you meditate, you can see visions of the object's previous owner. After meditating for 1 minute, you learn how the owner acquired and lost the object, as well as the most recent significant event involving the object and that owner. If the object was owned by another creature in the recent past (within a number of days equal to your Wisdom score), you can spend 1 additional minute for each owner to learn the same information about that creature.

{@b {@i Area Reading.}} As you meditate, you see visions of recent events in your immediate vicinity (a room, street, tunnel, clearing, or the like, up to a 50-foot cube), going back a number of days equal to your Wisdom score. For each minute you meditate, you learn about one significant event, beginning with the most recent. Significant events typically involve powerful emotions, such as battles and betrayals, marriages and murders, births and funerals. However, they might also include more mundane events that are nevertheless important in your current situation.

entries.name: Shielded Thoughts
entries: {@i {@b Way of the Seer:} 14th level} Your thoughts can't be read by telepathy or other means unless you allow it. You also have resistance to psychic damage, and whenever a creature deals psychic damage to you, that creature takes the same amount of damage that you do.

entries.name: Clarity of Vision
entries: {@i {@b Way of the Seer:} 18th level} The visions in your dreams intensify and paint a more    accurate picture in your mind of what is to come.    You roll three d20s for your Force Visions feature, rather than two.

entries.name: Way of Technology
entries: While many Forcewielders eschew the use of technology, other choose to embrace it. Those consulars who follow the Way of {@skill Technology|sw5e-phb} pair their mastery of the Force with the versatility of technology, applying the knowledge in tandem to perform unseen feats.

entries.name: Fundamentals of Mechu-deru
entries: {@i {@b Way of Technology:} 3rd, 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level} You've dabbled in adapting your use of the Force, melding it with technology. You gain proficiency in the {@skill Technology|sw5e-phb} skill, as well as {@filter simple blasters|items|firearm=true|weaponcategory=simple}. When you cast a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} that calls for a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, and you are wielding a {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} with which you are proficient, you can instead make a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}.

Additionally, you've learned to manipulate the Force to be able to manipulate technology when it couldn't previously. When you cast a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} that could not affect droids or constructs, you can choose to have it affect droids or constructs. If it would affect multiple targets, you must expend additional uses of this feature for each additional target. You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Techcasting Secrets
entries: {@i {@b Way of Technology:} 6th, 7th, 13th, and 17th level} You've learned to mimic technological effects. Choose two {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of 1st level. The chosen powers count as universal {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} for you, but are not included in the number in the Powers Known column of the consular table.

At 7th level, you learn two additional {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of 1st or 2nd level. At 13th level, you learn two {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of 1st-3rd level, and at 17th level, you learn two {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of 1st-4th level. Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you know and replace it with another {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of the same level.

entries.name: Ionized Weave
entries: {@i {@b Way of Technology:} 10th level} When you cast a damage-dealing {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} that requires a force attack or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can spend force points to cause that power to instead deal ion damage. The number of force points equals half the power's level (round down, minimum of one). If the power would call for a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} other than Dexterity, it instead calls for a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

entries.name: Force Circuitry
entries: {@i {@b Way of Technology:} 14th level} When you use your action to cast a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, and you use your Fundamentals of Mechu-deru feature as a part of that casting, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to cast one of the {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you know, as long as that power has a casting time of 1 action or {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Mechu-deru Mastery
entries: {@i {@b Way of Technology:} 18th level} You can cast one 5th-level {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of your choice at its base level. The power counts as a universal {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} for you, and you do not require force points to cast this power. Once you've done so, you can't do so again until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Way of Telekinetics
entries: The consular knows how to manipulate the essence of the surrounding elements with the power of the Force. Those consulars who follow the Way of Telekinetics create torrential gusts of telekinetic energy, forming a potent combination that can pummel even the toughest adversaries into submission.

entries.name: Staggering Stratagem
entries: {@i {@b Way of Telekinetics:} 3rd level} Your potency with the telekinetic power of the Force heightens. You can manipulate creatures of Large size or smaller with your {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} and Way of Telekinetics features. Additionally, once per turn, when you deal force or kinetic damage to a Large or smaller creature with a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} or class feature, you can choose to either push it up to 10 feet away from you or pull it up to 10 feet closer to you.

entries.name: Mighty Blast
entries: {@i {@b Way of Telekinetics:} 6th, 11th, and 17th level} Your {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} batter and blast your enemies with the strength of a hurricane. When you cast a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of 1st level or higher that deals force or kinetic damage, one creature of your choice damaged by that power must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your universal force save DC or be knocked {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}.
This feature can affect additional creatures when you reach higher levels: two creatures at 11th level and three creatures at 17th level.

entries.name: Size Matters Not
entries: {@i {@b Way of Telekinetics:} 10th level} You can manipulate creatures of Huge size or smaller with your {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} and Way of Telekinetics features.

Additionally, when you use your action to cast a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to fly up to 10 feet without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}.

entries.name: Repulsing Wave
entries: {@i {@b Way of Telekinetics:} 14th and 17th level} When you are dealt damage by a creature within 5 feet of you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to deal force damage to the creature equal to your consular level + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of +1). If the attacker is Huge or smaller, it must also make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your universal force save DC. On a failed save, the attacker is pushed in a straight line up to 20 feet away from you.
You can use this feature five times. You gain an additional use at 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: My Ally is the Force
entries: {@i {@b Way of Telekinetics:} 18th level} You can manipulate creatures of Gargantuan size or smaller with your {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} and Way of Telekinetics features.
Additionally, whenever a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} you cast pushes or pulls a creature, you can increase the distance of that push or pull by an additional 20 feet.

entries.name: Way of Tutelage
entries: With the Force, knowledge is most often passed from a master to an apprentice. Those consulars who follow the Way of Tutelage know the strength of working together exceeds that of working alone.

entries.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: {@i {@b Way of Tutelage:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency in your choice of {@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb} or {@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Humanoid Companion
entries: {@i {@b Way of Tutelage:} 3rd level} You've taken an apprentice, gaining the services of your own humanoid companion.
Create your humanoid companion as detailed in the Companions section of the Customization Options document for Expanded Content.
In addition to its traits and features, your companion gains additional benefits while it is bonded to you:

items: Your companion gains two additional traits. It gains one more additional trait when you reach 11th level in this class. For each trait in excess of your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, your force point maximum is reduced by 2.

entries: Lastly, while bonded and within 10 feet of you, when your companion is hit by an attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and expend a use of your Force shield feature to shroud it in Force energy. If you do so, until the start of your next turn, both you and your companion gain the benefits of your Force shield. This includes the triggering attack.
At 11th level, your companion must be within 30 feet of you to benefit from this feature. At 17th level, your companion must be within 60 feet.

entries.name: Strength Flows from the Force
entries: {@i {@b Way of Tutelage:} 6th level} When you cast a power that affects only your companion, you can choose to treat the power as if cast at your Max Power Level.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, as shown in the consular table. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: You Have That Power Too
entries: {@i {@b Way of Tutelage:} 10th, 11th, and 17th level} The bond between you and your companion has strengthened. When your companion is within 10 feet of you, and either you or your companion casts a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} that would affect only one of you, you can instead have it affect both.
At 11th level, your companion must be within 30 feet of you to benefit from this feature. At 17th level, your companion must be within 60 feet.

entries.name: Got Your Back
entries: {@i {@b Way of Tutelage:} 14th and 17th level} Once per turn, when your companion is within 10 feet of you, and both you and your companion have to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the same effect, either you or your companion can choose to have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the save. If either of you do so, the other of the two of you gains {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the save. You can use this feature before or after you both make the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, but you must do so before the GM says whether the save succeeds or fails.
At 17th level, your companion must be within 60 feet of you to benefit from this feature.

entries.name: Now I Am The Master
entries: {@i {@b Way of Tutelage:} 18th level} Your companion has learned almost all that it can from you. As an action on its turn, your companion can take the lead, gaining the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: It gains temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to twice its level.
Once per turn, when it deals damage or restores {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, it can roll an additional die.
It gains resistance to kinetic and energy damage.

entries: This effect ends early if your           companion is {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or dies.           Once your companion has used            this feature, it can't use it again             until it finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Artificer Engineering
entries: Those engineers who choose the Artificer Engineering discipline focus on building and modifying lightsabers, while tapping into the latent presence of the Force in these lightsaber crystals.

entries.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: {@i {@b Artificer Engineering:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency in {@item Artificer's implements|sw5e-phb|artificer's implements}, and with the lightsaber simple {@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}. Additionally, when you engage in crafting with {@item Artificer's implements|sw5e-phb|artificer's implements}, the rate at which you craft doubles.

entries.name: Modified Lightsaber
entries: {@i {@b Artificer Engineering:} 3rd and 9th level} You learn to modify an unenhanced lightsaber utilizing your artificer knowledge. Over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can modify your lightsaber. You must have the lightsaber and {@item Artificer's implements|sw5e-phb|artificer's implements} in order to perform this modification.

Your modified lightsaber is enhanced, requires attunement, can only be used by you, and counts as a tech focus for your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} while you are attuned to it. Your modified lightsaber has 4 modification slots, and it gains more at higher levels, as shown in the Modification Slots column of the engineer table. For each modification installed in excess of your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, your tech point maximum is reduced by 1. Over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can install, replace, or remove a number of modifications up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one).
Some modification effects require {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. When you use such an effect from this class, the DC equals your tech save DC.
At 9th level, you can maintain two different modified lightsabers. The total modification slots are split across the two items.

entries.name: Force Resonance
entries: {@i {@b Artificer Engineering:} 3rd level} Once per round, when you hit a creature with your modified lightsaber, you can expend one use of your Potent Aptitude to deal an extra 2d6 damage to that target. The damage is the same type as your modified lightsaber's damage.
The damage increases when you reach certain levels in this class, increasing to 3d6 at 5th level, 5d6 at 11th level, and 8d6 at 17th level.

entries.name: Forcecasting Secrets
entries: {@i {@b Artificer Engineering:} 6th, 7th, 13th, and 17th level} Your study of kyber crystals has awakened a latent force sensitivity. Choose two {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of 1st level. The chosen powers count as {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} for you, but are not included in the number in the Powers Known column of the engineer table.

At 7th level, you learn two additional {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of 1st or 2nd level. At 13th level, you learn two {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of 1st-3rd level, and at 17th level, you learn two {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of 1st-4th level. Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} you know and replace it with another {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of the same level.

entries.name: Disruptive Resonance
entries: {@i {@b Artificer Engineering:} 14th level} When you hit a creature that is concentrating on a power with your modified lightsaber, the creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}. Additionally, on a failed save, the creature immediately takes psychic damage equal to your engineer level + your Intelligence modifier.

entries.name: Resonating Recovery
entries: {@i {@b Artificer Engineering:} 18th level} Once per turn, when you reduce a hostile creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, you regain a use of your Potent Aptitude. Your number of Potent Aptitude uses can not exceed your Intelligence modifier.

entries.name: Artificer Modifications
entries: If a modification has prerequisites, you must meet them to install it. You can install the modification at the same time that you meet its prerequisites.

entries.name: Additonal Beam Port
entries: You install a second beam port into your modified lightsaber. Your modified lightsaber gains the double (1d8) property. You can only benefit from this property while wielding your modified lightsaber with two hands.

entries.name: Adegan Crystal
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 5th level} You gain a +1 bonus to damage rolls made with this weapon. This bonus increases to +2 at 9th level and +3 at 13th level.

entries.name: Advanced Blastsaber
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 15th level, Prototype Blastsaber} You further fine tune your blastsaber. As an action, you can disable a single electronic device not being worn or held by another creature within 5 feet of you. The device is then disabled until it is rebooted.

Additionally, when you activate this conversion to alter the properties of your {@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}, you create a projected barrier of ion energy in a 10-foot-radius sphere around you until the start of your next turn. Hostile creatures treat this area as {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain}. When a hostile creature enters the shielded area or starts its turn there, that creature takes 3d4 ion damage. Any electronics not being worn or held within the barrier's radius are disabled until rebooted.

entries.name: Advanced Brightsaber
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 15th level, Prototype Brightsaber} You further fine tune your brightsaber. While activated, your modified lightsaber's bright light now automatically dispels illusions and can detect invisibility, as with {@sense Truesight|sw5e-phb|truesight}.

Additionally, when you activate this conversion to alter the properties of your {@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} and use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to attempt to blind your target, it makes the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} with {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.

entries.name: Advanced Disruptorsaber
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 15th level, Prototype Disruptorsaber} You further fine tune your disruptorsaber. While activated, your modified lightsaber lightly obscures the area within 5 feet of it.

Additionally, when you activate this conversion to alter the properties of your {@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} and use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to attempt to knock your target prone, the next {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} you make before the end of your next turn has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}.

entries.name: Barrier
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 5th level} On your turn, when you make an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with your modified lightsaber, you can choose to forgo your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. If you do, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to erect a temporary barrier that lasts until the start of your next turn. While the barrier is activated, you have a bonus to AC against the first {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} made against you equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Beam Gem Lens
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 5th level} You gain a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} made with this weapon. This bonus increases to +2 at 9th level and +3 at 13th level.

entries.name: Biometric Safety Measures
entries: A security system is installed into the hilt of your {@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}. When a creature other than you attempts to activate your {@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}, the activation fails.
