entries: {@i {@b Kage Order:} 6th level} Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} when you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}, or it fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against an effect that you control, you can choose to roll a Martial Arts die and deal additional psychic damage equal to the amount rolled.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, as shown in the monk table. You regain any expended uses when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: One With Darkness
entries: {@i {@b Kage Order:} 11th level} You have learned to become one with the shadows. When you are in an area of dim light or darkness, you can use your action to become {@condition Invisible|sw5e-phb|invisible}. You remain {@condition Invisible|sw5e-phb|invisible} until you make an attack, cast a power, otherwise take a hostile action, or are in an area of bright light.

entries.name: Opportunist
entries: {@i {@b Kage Order:} 17th level} You can exploit a creature's momentary distraction when it is hit by an attack. Whenever a creature within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack made by a creature other than you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make a melee attack against that creature.

entries.name: Kyuzo Order
entries: Monks of the Kyuzo Order turn weapon throwing into a true art form. Inspired by the skill of native kyuzo wielding their war helmets as both shield and weapon, these monks utilize any thrown object they can find to defend themselves and others while they attack enemies from angles both surprising and devastating.

entries.name: Intercept
entries: {@i {@b Kyuzo Order:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency in {@filter vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon} with the thrown property and they become monk weapons for you. Additionally, when you throw an improvised weapon, you are considered proficient in it, and it uses your Martial Arts die instead of its 1d4.

Additionally, you've learned to use thrown weapons to intercept projectiles traveling towards your allies. When you are wielding a weapon with which you are proficient, and a creature within your weapon's normal thrown range is hit by a ranged attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to throw your weapon to intercept the projectile. When you do so, the damage the creature takes from the attack is reduced by 1d10 + your Dexterity modifier + your monk level. If the weapon has the returning property, it then returns to your hand.

entries.name: Scattering Stance
entries: {@i {@b Kyuzo Order:} 6th level} When you take the {@action Dodge|sw5e-phb} action, until the start of your next turn you gain a number of special reactions equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} that you can only use for your Intercept feature. You can only take one {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} per turn.

entries.name: Curved Throw
entries: {@i {@b Kyuzo Order:} 11th level} You can curve your throws behind {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}. When you make an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with a weapon with the thrown property, you can spend 1 focus point to cause the target to gain no benefit from shields or {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}, unless that {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} is full {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}.

entries.name: Relentless Assault
entries: {@i {@b Kyuzo Order:} 17th level} When you make multiple weapon attacks with thrown weapons against the same target on your turn, each attack after the first gains a +1 bonus to its {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, cumulatively, to a maximum bonus of +6.

entries.name: Kro Var Order
entries: Monks of the Kro Var Order—known as shapers—utilize a unique power to bend the four elements to their will, creating effects as small as a floating flame to quakes that sunder the earth.

entries.name: Elemental Attunement
entries: {@i {@b Kro Var Order:} 3rd, 11th, and 17th level} You gain the ability to bend the elements to your will. As an action, you can manipulate these forces to create one of the following effects of your choice at a space within 10 feet of you:

items: Create a harmless, instantaneous sensory effect related to air, earth, fire, or water, such as a shower of sparks, a puff of wind, a spray of light mist, or a gentle rumbling of stone.
Instantaneously light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a small campfire.
Chill or warm up to 1 pound of nonliving material for up to 1 hour.
Cause earth, fire, water, or mist that can fit within a 1-foot cube to shape itself into a crude form you designate for 1 minute.

entries: This range increases to 30 feet at 11th level and 60 feet at 17th level.

Additionally, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on your turn, you can spend 1 focus point to conjure a weapon made of one of the four elements—air, earth, fire, or water—which lasts for 1 minute. Your weapon takes an appearance of your choice, it can only be used by you, and you can't be disarmed of it while you are conscious. You are proficient in this weapon, which counts as a monk weapon for you and uses your Martial Arts die for its damage rolls. You can only have one of these weapons at a time, and if you summon a new one the old one immediately disappears.

entries.name: Air
entries: Your whistling weapon has the returning property, the thrown property with a range of 20/60, and deals sonic damage on a hit. Additionally, when you hit a creature with the weapon, it is {@condition Deafened|sw5e-phb|deafened} until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Earth
entries: Your earthen weapon takes the form of stone, and deals kinetic damage on a hit. Additionally, when you hit a creature with it, you can force the target to make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the target is pushed back 5 feet. Lastly, while active, you can use Strength instead of Dexterity when determining your AC, as long as it doesn't already include that modifier.

entries.name: Fire
entries: Your flaming weapon sheds bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet, deals fire damage, and when you hit a creature with it, the creature takes additional damage equal to half your focus ability modifier (minimum of one).

entries.name: Water
entries: Your watery weapon has the reach property, deals cold damage on a hit, and you can use your focus ability modifier instead of Dexterity or Strength for its attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls. Additionally, when you would make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, you can instead use your weapon to wet a 5-foot square within your weapon's reach. The affected area is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain}. Each creature who starts its turn in the square or enters it for the first time must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, falling {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone} on a failed save.

entries.name: Elemental Adept
entries: {@i {@b Kro Var Order:} 6th, 11th, and 17th level} You gain two of the following features. You gain an additional option at 11th and 17th level.

You can use these features a combined number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, as shown in the monk table. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

While you have no remaining uses of this feature, you can instead expend 2 focus points to use it. When you do so, your maximum focus points are reduced by 2 until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Burning Ember Flourish
entries: You can use your action to choose an area of flame that you can see and that fits within a 5-foot cube within 60 feet. You can {@spell Extinguish|sw5e-phb|extinguish} the fire in that area, and you create either fireworks or smoke when you do so.

{@b {@i Fireworks.}} The target explodes with a dazzling display of colors. Each creature within 10 feet of the target must succeed on a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or become {@condition Blinded|sw5e-phb|blinded} until the end of your next turn.

{@b {@i Smoke.}} Thick black smoke spreads out from the target in a 20-foot radius, moving around corners. The area of the smoke is heavily obscured. The smoke persists for 1 minute or until a strong wind disperses it.

entries.name: Curtain of Unyielding Wind
entries: As an action, you call up a mighty gale, which swirls around you in a 10-foot radius and moves with you, remaining centered on you. The wind lasts for 10 minutes. The wind deafens both you and other creatures in its area. It extinguishes unprotected flames in its area that are torch-sized or smaller and hedges out vapor, gas, and fog that can be dispersed by strong wind. The area is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain} for creatures other than you and the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} of ranged weapon attacks have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} if the attacks pass in or out of the wind.

entries.name: Crushing Hand of the Mountain
entries: As an action, you can choose a 5-foot-square unoccupied space on the ground that you can see within 30 feet. A Medium hand made from soil and stone, which lasts for 1 minute, rises in that space and reaches for one Large or smaller creature you can see within 5 feet of it. The target must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the target takes 2d6 kinetic damage and is {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained} for the duration. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on each of your turns, you can cause the hand to crush the {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained} target, which must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. It takes 2d6 kinetic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. To break out, the {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained} creature can use its action to make a Strength check against your focus save DC. On a success, the target escapes and is no longer {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained} by the hand. As an action, you can cause the hand to reach for a different creature or to move to a different unoccupied space within range. The hand releases a {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained} target if you do either.

entries.name: Hatchling's Flame
entries: As an action, you focus your energy into a torrent of fire that streaks away from you. A line of roaring flame 30 feet long and 5 feet wide emanates from you in a direction you choose. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A creature takes 3d8 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Patient Bantha Listens
entries: You reach out to the ground beneath you. You can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to gain {@sense Tremorsense|sw5e-phb|tremorsense} with a range of 30 feet and a burrow {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} for up to 1 minute. Your movement leaves behind a tunnel that remains for as long as this ability is active, after which it collapses.

entries.name: Rush of the Shyrack
entries: As an action, you form a line of strong wind 60 feet long and 10 feet wide that blasts from you in a direction you choose for one minute or until you lose {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} or dismiss the effect (no action required). Each Large or smaller creature that starts its turn in the line must succeed on a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be pushed 15 feet away from you in a direction following the line. Any creature in the line must spend 2 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves when moving closer to you. The gust disperses gas or vapor, and it extinguishes candles, torches, and similar unprotected flames in the area. It causes protected flames, such as those of lanterns, to dance wildly and has a 50 percent chance to {@spell Extinguish|sw5e-phb|extinguish} them. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on each of your turns before the effect ends, you can change the direction in which the line blasts from you.

entries.name: Shape the Raincloud
entries: You can use your action pull water from air, and return it to the atmosphere. In an open container, you can create up to 20 gallons of drinkable water. You may also produce a rain that falls within a 30-foot cube and extinguishes open-air flames. You can destroy the same amount of water in an open container, or destroy a 30-foot cube of fog.

entries.name: Swarming Ice Rabbit
entries: As an action, you can cause a flurry of ice crystals to erupt from a point you can see within 90 feet. Each creature in a 5-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, a creature takes 3d6 cold damage, and gains 1 {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed}.

entries.name: Elemental Master
entries: {@i {@b Kro Var Order:} 11th and 17th level} At 11th level, you gain one of the following features. You gain an additional option at 17th level.

You can use these features a combined number of times equal to half your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, as shown in the monk table. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

While you have no remaining uses of this feature, you can instead expend 3 focus points to use it. When you do so, your maximum focus points are reduced by 3 until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Earth Reaches for Sky
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Crushing Hand of the Mountain}  or {@i Patient Bantha Listens} As an action, you can choose a point you can see on the ground within 120 feet. A fountain of churned earth and stone erupts in a 20-foot cube centered on that point. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A creature takes 3d12 kinetic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Additionally, the ground in that area becomes {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain} until cleared. Each 5-foot-square portion of the area requires at least 1 minute to clear by hand.

entries.name: Ride the Wind
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Curtain of Unyielding Wind}  or {@i Rush of the Shyrack} As an action, you can gain a flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your movement {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} for 10 minutes. You can hover while this technique is active, but when it ends, you fall if you are still aloft, unless you can stop the fall.

entries.name: River of Hungry Flame
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Burning Ember {@optfeature Flourish|sw5e-phb}}  or {@i Hatchling's Flame} As an action, you can create a wall of fire on a solid surface within 120 feet. You can make the wall up to 60 feet long, 20 feet high, and 1 foot thick, or a ringed wall up to 20 feet in diameter, 20 feet high, and 1 foot thick. The wall is opaque and lasts for 1 minute.

When the wall appears, each creature within its area must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, a creature takes 5d8 fire damage, or half as much damage on a successful save.

One side of the wall, chosen by you when you use this feature, deals 5d8 fire damage to each creature that ends its turn within 10 feet of that side of the wall. A creature takes the same damage when it enters the wall for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there. The other side of the wall deals no damage.

entries.name: Shape the Flowing River
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Shape the Rainclud}  or {@i Swarming Ice Rabbit} As an action, you can control any freestanding water within 300 feet of you inside an area you choose that is a cube up to 100 feet on a side. You can choose from any of the following effects when you use this feature. As an action on your turn, you can repeat the same effect or choose a different one.{@b {@i Flood.}} You cause the water level of all standing water in the area to rise by as much as 20 feet. If the area includes a shore, the flooding water spills over onto dry land. If you choose an area in a large body of water, you instead create a 20-foot tall wave that travels from one side of the area to the other and then crashes down. Any Huge or smaller creatures in the wave's path are carried with it to the other side. Any Huge or smaller creatures struck by the wave have a 25 percent chance of being knocked {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}. The water level remains elevated until the feature ends or you choose a different effect. If this effect produced a wave, the wave repeats on the start of your next turn while the flood effect lasts.

{@b {@i Part Water.}} You cause water in the area to move apart and create a trench. The trench extends across the feature's area, and the separated water forms a wall to either side. The trench remains until the feature ends or you choose a different effect. The water then slowly fills in the trench over the course of the next round until the normal water level is restored.

{@b {@i Redirect Flow.}} You cause flowing water in the area to move in a direction you choose, even if the water has to flow over obstacles, up walls, or in other unlikely directions. The water in the area moves as you direct it, but once it moves beyond the feature's area, it resumes its flow based on the terrain conditions. The water continues to move in the direction you chose until the feature ends or you choose a different effect.

{@b {@i Whirlpool.}} This effect requires a body of water at least 50 feet square and 25 feet deep. You cause a whirlpool to form in the center of the area. The whirlpool forms a vortex that is 5 feet wide at the base, up to 50 feet wide at the top, and 25 feet tall. Any creature or object in the water and within 25 feet of the vortex is pulled 10 feet toward it. A creature can swim away from the vortex by making a Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) check against your feature save DC. When a creature enters the vortex for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the creature takes 2d8 kinetic damage and is caught in the vortex until the feature ends. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage, and isn't caught in the vortex. A creature caught in the vortex can use its action to try to swim away from the vortex as described above, but has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) check to do so. The first time each turn that an object enters the vortex, the object takes 2d8 kinetic damage; this damage occurs each round it remains in the vortex.

entries.name: Elemental Paragon
entries: {@i {@b Kro Var Order:} 17th level} You gain one of the following features.
Once you've used the chosen feature, you must complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

While you have no remaining uses of this feature, you can instead expend 4 focus points to use it. When you do so, your maximum focus points are reduced by 4 until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Archetype of Air
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Ride the Wind} As an action, you conjure a whirlwind around you, granting the following benefits until the start of your next turn:

items: Ranged attacks made against you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.
You gain a flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} of 60 feet. If you are still flying when the technique ends, you fall, unless you can somehow prevent it.

You can use your action to create a 15-foot cube of swirling wind centered on a point you can see within 60 feet of you. Each creature in that area must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A creature takes 2d10 kinetic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. If a Large or smaller creature fails the save, that creature is also pushed up to 10 feet away from the center of the cube.

entries: At the start of each of your turns, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to extend the benefits of this feature until the start of your next turn, to a maximum duration of 1 minute. This effect ends immediately if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die.

entries.name: Figure of Flame
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} River of Hungry Flame} As an action, you cause flames to race across your body, granting the following benefits until the start of your next turn:

items: You have resistance to fire damage.
The flames shed bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet.
Any creature that moves within 5 feet of you for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there takes 1d10 fire damage.

You can use your action to create a line of fire 15 feet long and 5 feet wide extending from you in a direction you choose. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, taking 4d8 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.

entries: At the start of each of your turns, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to extend the benefits of this feature until the start of your next turn, to a maximum duration of 1 minute. This effect ends immediately if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die.

entries.name: Icon of Ice
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Shape the Flowing River} As an action, you cause frost to chill the area around you, granting the following benefits until the start of your next turn:

items: You have resistance to cold damage.
You can move across {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain} created by ice or snow without spending extra movement.
The ground in a 10-foot radius around you is icy and is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain} for creatures other than you. The radius moves with you.

You can use your action to create a 15-foot cone of freezing ice extending from your outstretched hand in a direction you choose. Each creature in the cone must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A creature takes 4d6 cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that fails its save against this effect gains 1 {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level until the start of your next turn.

entries: At the start of each of your turns, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to extend the benefits of this feature until the start of your next turn, to a maximum duration of 1 minute. This effect ends immediately if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die.

entries.name: Embodiment of Earth
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Earth Reaches for Sky} As an action, you cause rock to envelop you, granting the following benefits until the start of your next turn:

items: You have resistance to kinetic and energy damage.

You can move across {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain} made of earth or stone without spending extra movement. You can move through solid earth or stone as if it was air without destabilizing it, but you can't end your movement there. If you do so, you are immediately shunted to the nearest unoccupied space that you can occupy and take force damage equal to twice the number of feet you are moved.

You can use your action to create a small earthquake on the ground in a 15-foot radius centered on you. Other creatures on that ground must succeed on a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be knocked {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}.

entries: At the start of each of your turns, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to extend the benefits of this feature until the start of your next turn, to a maximum duration of 1 minute. This effect ends immediately if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die.

entries.name: Avatar
entries: {@i {@b Kro Var Order:} 17th level} As an ultimate display of your mastery of the elements, you can spend 5 focus points as an action to have the elements of water, earth, fire, and air form a protective sphere around your body, gaining multiple benefits for 1 minute. While this ability is active, you have resistance to cold, energy, fire, kinetic, lightning, and sonic damage. You also gain a burrow, fly, and swim {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your movement {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}. Lastly, you can use any of the following abilities as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}:

items: You create a small earthquake on the ground in a 15-foot radius around you. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, a creature takes 1d6 kinetic damage and is knocked {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}.

You create a line of fire 15 feet long and 5 feet wide extending from you in a direction you choose. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A creature takes 3d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

You create a 15-foot cube of swirling wind centered on a point you can see within 60 feet of you. Each creature in that area must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A creature takes 1d10 kinetic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. If a Large or smaller creature fails the save, that creature is also pushed up to 10 feet away from the center of the cube.

You create a 15-foot cone of ice shards extending from your outstretched hand in a direction you choose. Each creature in the cone must make a Constitution save throw. A creature takes 2d6 cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that fails its save against this effect has its {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} halved until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Rakatan Order
entries: Monks of the Rakatan Order believe in the harmony of self with technology. They use tech to push themselves beyond their body's natural limits.

entries.name: Techcasting
entries: {@i {@b Rakatan Order:} 3rd level} You have derived powers from schematics with the aid of your {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}. See {@book chapter 10|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} for the general rules of {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} and {@book chapter 12|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} for the {@book tech powers list|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

entries.name: Tech Powers Known
entries: You learn 3 {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of your choice, and you learn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Tech Powers Known|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} column of the Rakatan Order {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table. You may not learn a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of a level higher than your Max Power Level.

entries.name: Tech Points
entries: You have a number of tech points equal to half of your monk level (rounded up), as shown in the Tech Points column of the Rakatan Order {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table, + your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier (your choice). You use these tech points to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. You regain all expended tech points when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Max Power Level
entries: Many {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} can be overcharged, consuming more tech points to create a greater effect. You can overcharge these powers to a maximum level, which increases at higher levels, as shown in the Max Power Level column of the Rakatan Order {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table.
You may only cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} at 4th-level once. You regain the ability to do so after a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Techcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} for your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} (your choice). You use this ability whenever a power refers to your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability}. Additionally, you use this ability modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you cast and when making an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with one.
{@b Tech save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} modifer
{@b Tech attack modifier} = your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} modifer

entries.name: Techcasting Focus
entries: You use a {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad} (found in {@book chapter 5|sw5e-phb|5}) as a {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} focus for your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

entries.name: Focused Tech
entries: {@i {@b Rakatan Order:} 6th level} You can cast your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} using your focus points. When you do so, your maximum focus points are reduced by 1 until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
Additionally, when you use a Focus feature, you gain the following tech enhancements. Each effect costs 1 tech point.
{@b {@i Flurry of Blows.}} When you hit with an attack with Flurry of Blows, you can deal an additional 1d8 damage of the same type.

entries.name: Rakatan Techcasting
entries: {@b {@i Patient Defense.}} While under the effects of your Patient Defense, when you are hit by an attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and roll your Martial Arts die to increase your AC against the attack.

{@b {@i Step of the Wind.}} While under the effects of your Step of the Wind, you can become immune to the {@condition Shocked|sw5e-phb|shocked} condition, and have each {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level only reduce your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} by 5 feet, unless it would reduce your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} to 0.

entries.name: Harmonious Rakatan
entries: {@i {@b Rakatan Order:} 11th level} You can use your Focus features using your tech points. When you do so, your maximum tech points are reduced by 1 until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

Additionally, you are constantly under the effects of the {@i detect enhancement} {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. As an action, you can cast the {@i analyze} {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} without expending tech points. When you do so, {@i detect enhancement} is suppressed and you can't do so again until you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Tech Mastery
entries: {@i {@b Rakatan Order:} 17th level} You learn and can cast one 5th-level {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} once per {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} without expending tech points.

entries.name: Teras Kasi Order
entries: Monks of the Teras Kasi Order are the ultimate masters of unarmed martial arts combat. They learn techniques to draw focus from the defeat of their enemies, resist the mental assaults of the Force, and unleash powerful rushes of strikes to subdue their foes.

entries.name: Forredari Stance
entries: {@i {@b Teras Kasi Order:} 3rd level} Your honed focus allows you to enter a stance of mental fortification and power. You can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to enter this stance. When you do so, you unleash a flurry of blows on creatures of your choice that you can see within 10 feet of you. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon) or take the weapon's normal damage.
This stance lasts for 1 minute. While you are in this stance, you gain the following benefits:

items: {@b Death Weave.} When you reduce a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, you gain temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to your focus ability modifier + half your monk level.
{@b Gundark Slap.} Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with an unarmed strike or a monk weapon, you can choose to make it unable to take reactions until the end of your next turn.

{@b Sleeping Krayt.} You can use your focus ability modifier instead of Strength whenever you would make a Strength check or a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. Additionally, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against being {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} or {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened}.

entries: These effects end early if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die. Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

While you have no remaining uses of this feature, you can instead expend 1 focus point to use it. When you do so, your maximum focus points are reduced by 1 until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Steel Hands Form
entries: {@i {@b Teras Kasi Order:} 6th level} You can draw upon your focus to utilize an array of {@feat Practiced|sw5e-phb|practiced} techniques to strike your opponents with precision and power. You can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to enter this stance, and when you do so, you can also enter your Forredari Stance as a part of this same {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}. This form lasts for 1 minute. While you are in this stance, you gain the following benefits:

items: {@b Charging Wampa.} Once per round, when you are forced to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, your movement {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} increases by 10 feet until the end of your next turn.

{@b Nexu Grin.} When a creature you can see within 10 feet of you casts a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} that requires a force {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against you or an an allied creature, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and expend 1 focus point to impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}. If the attack misses, and the higher of the two {@dice d20} rolls would also miss, the creature cannot cast that {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} again until it completes a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

{@b Screaming Squill.} Once per turn, when you hit a creature that is concentrating on a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} and it makes a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}, the DC for the check equals your focus save DC, unless the DC for the Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} would be higher.

entries: These effects end early if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die. Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

While you have no remaining uses of this feature, you can instead expend 1 focus point to use it. When you do so, your maximum focus points are reduced by 1 until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Matter Over Mind
entries: {@i {@b Teras Kasi Order:} 11th level} You tap into the greater power of your focus. While both your Forredari Stance and your Steel Hands Form are active, you gain the following benefits:

items: {@b Dancing Dragonsnake.} When you take force, lightning, or necrotic damage, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to deflect it. When you do so, the damage you take is reduced by 1d10 + your focus ability modifier + your monk level.

{@b Aryx Slash.} Once on each of your turns, when you hit a target with an unarmed strike or monk weapon, you can roll a Martial Arts die and deal additional psychic damage equal to the amount rolled.

{@b Piercing Gaze.} When you would make an {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb} check against a creature you know to wield the Force, you can use your focus ability modifier for the roll, and you are considered to have {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in the {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb} skill. If you would already have {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in the check, you instead have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the roll.

entries.name: Spitting Rawl
entries: {@i {@b Teras Kasi Order:} 17th level} You have learned to harness your strikes in a blistering fury. On your turn, when a creature takes damage from you three times, you can make up to three additional {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes} against the creature (no action required). The first additional unarmed strike costs 1 focus point and deals 1d12 additional psychic damage on a hit, and each unarmed strike after the first costs 1 additional focus point and deals 1d12 additional psychic damage on a hit, cumulatively.

entries.name: Trickster Order
entries: Monks of the Trickster Order embody the archetypal role of the "trickster"— one who seemingly bumbles their way into good fortune. They employ a unique fighting style composed of slips, trips, and falls to confuse and frustrate their enemies to no end. Whether your movements are actual foibles on your part or calculated strokes, they will surely leave others guessing long after your time is past.

entries.name: Bumbling Technique
entries: {@i {@b Trickster Order:} 3rd level} Your martial arts technique mixes combat training with the precision of a dancer and the antics of a jester. You gain proficiency in {@skill Performance|sw5e-phb}.

Additionally, you learn how to twist and turn quickly. Whenever you use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to make an unarmed strike, creatures you hit can't make {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks} against you, and your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} increases by 10 feet until the end of your turn.

entries.name: Clumsy Sway
entries: {@i {@b Trickster Order:} 6th level} You can move in sudden, swaying ways. You gain the following benefits.
{@b {@i Leap to Your Feet.}} When you're prone, you can stand up by spending 5 feet of movement, rather than half your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}.

{@b {@i Redirect Attack.}} When a creature misses you with a melee {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, you can spend 1 focus point as a {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to cause that attack to hit one creature of your choice, other than the attacker, that you can see within 5 feet of you.

entries.name: Luck of the Fool
entries: {@i {@b Trickster Order:} 11th level} You always seem to get a lucky bounce at the right moment. When you make an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} and have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}, you can spend 2 focus points to instead have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} for that roll.

entries.name: Comic Frenzy
entries: {@i {@b Trickster Order:} 17th level} You gain the ability to make an overwhelming number of attacks against a group of enemies. When you use your Flurry of Blows, you can make up to three additional attacks with it (up to a total of five Flurry of Blows attacks), provided that each Flurry of Blows attack targets a different creature this turn.

entries.name: Whills Order
entries: Monks of the Whills Order hold the secrets of the Force sacred, and dedicate their lives to defending ancient  knowledge of the Force and its artifacts. They master the use of ranged weapons, often crafting their own weapons in respectful admiration of the Jedi tradition of crafting {@filter lightweapons|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}.

entries.name: Flurry of Light
entries: {@i {@b Whills Order:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency in {@item Blaster pistol|sw5e-phb|blaster pistols}, {@item Blaster rifle|sw5e-phb|blaster rifles}, ion pistols, ion rifles, and the lightbow, which are your Whills weapons and are monk weapons for you. When you are wielding a Whills weapon, you gain the following benefits:

items: Your Whills weapons count as melee weapons for you, and when you make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} with them, you deal kinetic damage equal to your Martial Arts Damage Die.

When you would make an unarmed strike using your Martial Arts {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} or as a part of your Flurry of Blows, you can instead attack with a Whills weapon you are wielding. You roll a {@dice d4} in place of the normal damage of your Whills weapon when attacking in this way. This die changes as you gain monk levels, as shown in the Martial Arts column of the monk table.
When you would make a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} with a Whills weapon, you can instead reload the weapon.

entries.name: The Force is With You
entries: {@i {@b Whills Order:} 6th level} As you channel the Force through you, you gain the following benefits:

items: You can use your Stunning Strike feature when you hit with a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} while you are wielding a Whills weapon.

You can spend up to 3 focus points to reduce partial {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} by one step (from three-quarters to half or half to one-quarter). If you reduce the target below one-quarter {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}, you ignore {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} bonuses entirely. At 17th level, you can spend 3 focus points to ignore {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|total cover}, as long as your target is not hidden from you.

When you hit a creature with a Whills weapon, that creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks} against you until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: One With the Force
entries: {@i {@b Whills Order:} 11th level} You learn how to enter a trance, preparing to unleash yourself upon your enemy. While in this trance, you can still talk and move. If you stay in the trance for at least one minute, when you roll {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative}, you can make a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} on a number of creatures up to your focus ability modifier (a minimum of one) within 30 feet of you when you were in this trance.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Guided Strikes
entries: {@i {@b Whills Order:} 17th level} Your first ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} and your first {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} each turn deal additional damage equal to your focus ability modifier (a minimum of +1).

entries.name: Bolstering Practice
entries: Those operatives who choose the Bolstering Practice use precise strikes and brilliant use of small unit tactics to overwhelm enemies through superior teamwork.

entries.name: Articulate Authority
entries: {@i {@b Bolstering Practice:} 3rd, 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level} When you use your Cunning Action feature to take the {@action Dash|sw5e-phb}, {@action Disengage|sw5e-phb}, or {@action Hide|sw5e-phb} actions, a number of friendly creatures up to your Charisma modifier within 30 feet of you who can hear you and who can understand you can use their {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to gain an effect, determined by the action you took:

items: {@b Dash:} The creature can move up to half their {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}. They must end this movement within 30 feet of you.

{@b Disengage:} The creature can move up to 5 feet. If this movement would provoke an {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attack}, the {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attack} is made with {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.

{@b Hide:} The creature has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the first {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} they make before the end of their next turn against a creature you successfully hide from.

entries: You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Fireteam Commander
entries: {@i {@b Bolstering Practice:} 3rd level} You learn a number of squad maneuvers you can use to assist allies or exploit enemies. When you deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature, you may choose to forgo two of your Sneak Attack dice to make the attack a squad maneuver.

entries.name: Fortifying Strike
entries: You inspire a friendly creature within 60 feet of you who can see or hear you and roll two Sneak Attack dice. That ally immediately gains temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to the amount of rolled.

entries.name: Reaffirming Strike
entries: You use the authority your attacks carry to help your ally focus on the task at hand. Choose a creature within 60 feet of you who can see or hear you and that is currently {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} or {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} by the creature you would deal Sneak Attack damage to. The condition immediately ends on that creature.

entries.name: Bolstering Strike
entries: You choose a friendly creature within 60 feet of you who can see or hear you. Once before the start of your next turn, if that creature hits the creature against which you forwent two Sneak Attack damage dice, they deal additional damage to the target equal to the maximum of the two Sneak Attack dice.

entries.name: Open Opportunity
entries: {@i {@b Bolstering Practice:} 9th level} Once per turn, when you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action and hit a creature without applying your Sneak Attack damage to it, you can forgo your Sneak Attack damage for the turn and use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to throw the creature off balance. The next ally to hit that creature before the start of your next turn may add your Sneak Attack dice to the damage of their attack.

entries.name: Ambush Tactics
entries: {@i {@b Bolstering Practice:} 13th level} When attempting to move stealthily as a group, you may choose a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier. Those creatures may add their proficiency to any Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) checks they make as long as they remain within 60 feet of you and they do not already add their {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}.

Additionally, each ally other than you that surprises a creature and hits it with an attack on their first turn in combat rolls two dice equal to the size of your Sneak Attack dice, dealing additional damage of the same type to the creature.

entries.name: Squad Goals
entries: {@i {@b Bolstering Practice:} 17th level} You have such skill at maintaining the faith of your allies that the very sight of you in danger can spur them into action. When you are hit by an attack, up to six allies within 60 feet of you that can see or hear you and see the creature that hit you can make one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} against that creature (no action required).
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Disabling Practice
entries: Those operatives who choose the Disabling Practice utilize a variety of pushes, pulls, weight shifts, and joint locks to immobilize their opponent. They use these techniques to manipulate their opponent, moving them across the battlefield before incapacitating them.

entries.name: Clinch Strike
entries: {@i {@b Disabling Practice:} 3rd level} You learn how to discourage, debilitate, and harm your enemies. You gain the following benefits while you aren't wearing {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor} or wielding a medium or heavy shield:

items: Your damage die for your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes} and natural weapons increases by one step (from 1 to {@dice d4}, {@dice d4} to {@dice d6}, or {@dice d6} to {@dice d8}), and you can apply your Sneak Attack damage when you hit with an unarmed strike even if it doesn't have {@itemProperty SWF|sw5e-phb|the finesse property}.

You don't need {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} to use your Sneak Attack if the target of your Sneak Attack is a creature {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} by you. All the other rules for the Sneak Attack class feature still apply to you.
You can use the {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} granted by your Cunning Action to make an unarmed strike against a creature you are grappling.

entries.name: Skilled Grappler
entries: {@i {@b Disabling Practice:} 3rd level} You learn a number of grappling techniques to subdue your opponents. When you hit a creature {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} by you with an unarmed strike and deal Sneak Attack damage, you may choose to forgo two of your Sneak Attack dice to make the attack a grappling technique.

Some of your grappling techniques require your target to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the grappling technique's effects. The {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC is calculated as follows:
{@b Grapple Technique save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Strength modifier

entries.name: Constrict
entries: You attempt to choke the target into unconsciousness. The target must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained} until the end of your following turn.

If you maintain this technique for 1 minute, the target falls {@condition Unconscious|sw5e-phb|unconscious} for 1 hour. Droids and constructs can not be knocked {@condition Unconscious|sw5e-phb|unconscious} in this way.

entries.name: Disarm
entries: You attempt to disarm a weapon or other object the target is holding. The target must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, it releases the object. If you have a free hand, you can catch the object. Otherwise, it lands at your feet.

entries.name: Hip Toss
entries: You attempt to throw your target to the ground. The target must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the target is pushed back 5 feet, knocked {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}, and {@condition Stunned|sw5e-phb|stunned} until the start of your next turn. This ends the grapple.

entries.name: Human Shield
entries: {@i {@b Disabling Practice:} 9th level} You learn to manipulate the body of a {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} target to make attacks against you more difficult to land. Moving a {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} creature the same size as you or smaller no longer halves your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}, and when a creature {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} by you would grant you {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|half cover}, you instead have three-quarters {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}. Additionally, when you are hit by an attack while grappling a creature, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to force that attack to instead hit the {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} creature.

entries.name: Kiss the Wall
entries: {@i {@b Disabling Practice:} 13th level} You can use your surroundings to further punish the target of your grapple. When you roll a 1 or 2 on a Sneak Attack damage die for an unarmed strike you make against a creature {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} by you, you can treat the result of the die as a 3.

entries.name: Neck Snap
entries: {@i {@b Disabling Practice:} 17th level} You learn how to immediately remove your {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} opponent from the fight. As an action, you can force a creature {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} by you to make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, if the creature has 100 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} or fewer, it dies. If the target has more than 100 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, it immediately takes 10d10 true damage.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Gunslinger Practice
entries: Those operatives who choose the Gunslinger Practice are the masters of the trick shot. The Gunslinger and his {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} are the perfect team, utilizing knowledge of their enemies' vulnerabilities to take {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} of every opportunity.

entries.name: Dive For Cover
entries: {@i {@b Gunslinger Practice:} 3rd, 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level} You learn to quickly move into {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} when under fire. Once per round, when you are the target of a ranged attack, or you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and there is {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} within 10 feet of you, you can move up to 10 feet (no action required). You must end this movement in {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Trick Shooter
entries: {@i {@b Gunslinger Practice:} 3rd level} You learn a number of trick shots you can use to debilitate enemies and impress allies. When you deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature, you may choose to forgo two of your Sneak Attack dice to make the attack a trick shot.

Some of your trick shots require your target to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the trick shot's effects. The {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC is calculated as follows:
{@b Trick Shot save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Dexterity modifier

entries.name: Blinding Shot
entries: You attempt to blind the target. The target must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be {@condition Blinded|sw5e-phb|blinded} until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Brutal Shot
entries: You attempt to knock the target prone. The target must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be knocked {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}.

entries.name: Hampering Shot
entries: You attempt to hobble the enemy's movement. The target must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. If it fails, it gains 1 {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level and it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Spinning Flourish
entries: {@i {@b Gunslinger Practice:} 9th level} You can flourish your weapon in an intimidating or charming manner. As an action, you can cause one creature within 60 feet to make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Dexterity modifier). On a failed save, the target is {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} or {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} by you (your choice) until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Ricochet Shot
entries: {@i {@b Gunslinger Practice:} 13th level} You learn how to work all the angles. Once per turn, when you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action and miss with a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}, you can repeat the attack against a different target within 10 feet of the original target (no action required).

entries.name: Quickdraw
entries: {@i {@b Gunslinger Practice:} 17th level} You learn to perform miracles with just a {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} and some nerve. On your first turn in combat, if you aren't surprised, you can use your action to attack creatures that have not yet acted. Choose up to six such creatures that you can see, making a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} against each. On a hit, you deal normal weapon damage and can apply a single trick shot to each attack made this way.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Maverick Practice
entries: There are those who, when thrust into danger, use unexpected methods to achieve victory. Those operatives who choose the Maverick Practice draw on a wide array of skills, learning new ways to apply them, as their strongest asset.

entries.name: Maverick Superiority
entries: {@i {@b Maverick Practice:} 3rd level} You learn maneuvers that are fueled by special dice called {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}. See {@book chapter 13|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} for the {@book maneuvers list|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers}.

entries.name: Maneuvers Known
entries: You learn two maneuvers of your choice, and you earn more at higher levels, as shown in the Maneuvers Known column of the Maverick Superiority table. Many maneuvers enhance an attack in some way. You can use only one maneuver per attack, and you may only use each maneuver once per turn.
Each time you learn new maneuvers, you can also replace one maneuver you know with a different one.

entries.name: Superiority Dice
entries: You have two {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}, which are d4s, and you earn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Superiority Dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} Quantity column of the Maverick Superiority table. This die changes as you gain operative levels, as shown in the {@book Superiority Dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} Size column of the Maverick Superiority table. A superiority die is expended when you use it.
You regain all of your expended {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Maneuver Ability
entries: Your {@book maneuver ability|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} varies based on the type of the maneuver you use. You use Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution for {@book physical maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Physical} (your choice), Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma for {@book mental maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Mental} (your choice), and an ability of your choice for {@book general maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|General}. You use this ability whenever a maneuver refers to your {@book maneuver ability|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}. Additionally, you use this ability modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a maneuver you use.
{@b Maneuver save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your {@book maneuver ability|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} modifier

entries.name: Know a Bit
entries: {@i {@b Maverick Practice:} 3rd level} You can add half your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} to any {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} you make that doesn't already include your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Outplayed
entries: {@i {@b Maverick Practice:} 9th level} When a creature fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} against you or an effect you control, you don't need {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} to use Sneak Attack, you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against that creature, and that creature can't have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against effects you control. These effects last until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Practice Makes Perfect
entries: {@i {@b Maverick Practice:} 13th and 17th level} When you make an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} as part of or that is affected by a maneuver you use, you can choose to increase your level of proficiency in that check by one step (from trained to proficient, from proficient to {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise}, from {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} to mastery, from mastery to high mastery, or from high mastery to grand mastery).
You can use this feature five times. You gain an additional use at 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Flow State
entries: {@i {@b Maverick Practice:} 17th level} As an action, you can choose to intensely focus for one minute, gaining the following benefits:

items: Once on each of your turns, when you use a maneuver, you can use a {@dice d4} instead of expending a superiority die.
You can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}.
Creatures can't have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against you.

entries: Once you've used this feature, you must complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Performance Practice
entries: Some operatives choose to master finesse and timing through performance art. Those operatives who choose the {@skill Performance|sw5e-phb} Practice become skilled performers who prove especially deadly in close combat, able to find the rhythm of an attacker's strikes as easily as any song.

entries.name: Artful Dancer
entries: {@i {@b Performance Practice:} 3rd level} Your training with music and dancing grants you certain benefits. You gain proficiency in the {@skill Performance|sw5e-phb} skill and one musical instrument of your choice.
Additionally, while you are not wearing armor or wielding a medium or heavy shield, you can add half your Charisma modifier to your AC as long as it doesn't already include that modifier.

entries.name: Dazzling Steps
entries: {@i {@b Performance Practice:} 3rd level} You learn to conduct impressive displays of grace and {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} in combat. While you aren't wearing medium or {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor} or wielding a medium or heavy shield, and you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn and attack with a weapon with either the light or finesse properties, your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} increases by 10 feet until the end of the turn, and if you deal Sneak Attack damage, you may choose to forgo two of your Sneak Attack dice to make the attack a dazzling step.

Some of your dazzling steps require your target to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the dazzling step's effects. The {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC is calculated as follows:
{@b Dazzling Step save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Charisma modifier

entries.name: Defensive Step
entries: You defend yourself from further attack. Roll two Sneak Attack dice. You gain temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} that last until the start of your next turn equal to the amount rolled.

entries.name: Mobile Step
entries: You twist and twirl around the target. The target must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A Huge or larger creature automatically succeeds. On a failed save, it is pushed back 5 feet, and you can immediately move into the space it just vacated without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}.

entries.name: Offensive Step
entries: Choose another creature that you can see within your reach. The creature must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, roll two Sneak Attack dice. The creature takes damage equal to the amount rolled. This damage is of the same as your weapon's damage.

entries.name: Flexible Body
entries: {@i {@b Performance Practice:} 9th level} You are able to use your acrobatic talent to gain the upper hand in combat. You can use the {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} granted by your Cunning Action to shove or trip a creature. When you do so, you can make a Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|sw5e-phb}) check instead of a Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) check.

Additionally, you now ignore {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain}, you can move through space occupied by hostile creatures, and you can squeeze through smaller spaces without expending extra movement.

entries.name: Dance of Death
entries: {@i {@b Performance Practice:} 13th level} You can use your action to make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} against any number of creatures within 5 feet of you, with a separate {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} for each target. You can choose to deal Sneak Attack damage to each creature you hit, but you can only roll half your number of Sneak Attack dice per creature.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Master of Dance
entries: {@i {@b Performance Practice:} 17th level} Your confidence when putting on a show has extended into combat. You add your Charisma modifier to {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} checks. Additionally, any creature who fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your Dazzling Step save DC has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the first {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} they make against you each turn until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Pugnacity Practice
entries: Those operatives who choose the Pugnacity Practice apply an atypical versatility to their actions, comfortably dispatching foes from afar or face to face.

entries.name: Tools of the Trade
entries: {@i {@b Pugnacity Practice:} 3rd level} You've learned to move swiftly while wielding larger armaments. You gain proficiency with {@filter medium armor|items|type=medium armor} and martial {@filter vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon}. If you are already proficient in {@filter medium armor|items|type=medium armor}, you instead gain proficiency in {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor}. Additionally, you can deal Sneak Attack damage with any weapon, as long as it does not have the heavy or special properties.

Lastly, you don't need {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} to use your Sneak Attack if no creature other than your target is within 5 feet of you, as long as the target of the attack is below its hit point maximum. All the other rules for the Sneak Attack class feature still apply to you.

entries.name: Blitz Attack
entries: {@i {@b Pugnacity Practice:} 3rd level} You've learned ways to use your martial ability to boost your combat performance. When you deal Sneak Attack damage, you may choose to forgo two of your Sneak Attack dice to make the attack a blitz attack.

Some of your blitz attacks require your target to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the attack's effects. The {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC is as follows:
{@b Blitz Attack save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice)

entries.name: Demoralizing Attack
entries: The target must make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, it is {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} of you until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Diverting Attack
entries: Roll two of your Sneak Attack dice. The first time the target would deal damage before the start of your next turn, that damage is reduced by an amount equal to the resulting roll.

entries.name: Warmonger's Attack
entries: If the target makes an attack against you or an allied creature within 5 feet of you before the start of your next turn, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} against it.

entries.name: Extra Attack
entries: {@i {@b Pugnacity Practice:} 9th level} When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn, you can choose to attack twice, instead of once. Additionally, you can deal Sneak Attack damage any number of times on your turn. Each time you deal Sneak Attack damage, you can choose how many Sneak Attack dice you apply. You can't apply more than your total Sneak Attack dice each turn.

entries.name: Unrelenting Advance
entries: {@i {@b Pugnacity Practice:} 13th level} You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against effects that would grapple or restrain you. Additionally, if you are {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} or {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained}, and you could use your action to attempt to end the effect, you can instead use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Razor Focus
entries: {@i {@b Pugnacity Practice:} 17th level} You can enter a hyper-focused state of mind for 1 minute as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}. You must maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}, as if concentrating on a power. For the duration, each time you successfully deal Sneak Attack damage against a creature, you gain two additional Sneak Attack dice, cumulatively, as your attacks become increasingly precise. These additional dice are lost when your focus ends, whether through failing to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} or after 1 minute.

The first time you use this feature, you suffer no ill effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you suffer one level of {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion} each time you use it.

entries.name: Ruffian Practice
entries: Those operatives who choose the Ruffian Practice use rough-and-{@optfeature Tumble|sw5e-phb|tumble} tactics to handle any fight, big or small. They {@optfeature Incite|sw5e-phb|incite} chaos and make devious moves that keep their enemies reeling.

entries.name: Rakish Audacity
entries: {@i {@b Ruffian Practice:} 3rd level} Your unmistakable confidence propels you into battle. You can add your Charisma modifier to your {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} rolls.

Additionally, you don't need {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} to use your Sneak Attack if no creature other than your target is within 5 feet of you, as long as the target of the attack is within 5 feet of you. All the other rules for the Sneak Attack class feature still apply to you.
Finally, during your turn, if you make a melee attack against a creature, that creature can't make {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks} against you for the rest of your turn.

entries.name: Nimble Step
entries: {@i {@b Ruffian Practice:} 3rd level} You learn to fluidly strike and maneuver through combat. When you deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature, you may choose to forgo two of your Sneak Attack Dice in order to maneuver across the battlefield.

Some of your fancy footworks require your target to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the debilitating strike's effects. The {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC is calculated as follows:
{@b Nimble Step save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Dexterity modifier.

entries.name: Blade Defense
entries: You attempt to determine your target's next strike. Roll two Sneak Attack dice, and the target must make a Charisma {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, your AC increases by the higher amount rolled on the dice against the first attack it makes against you before the start of your next turn. On a successful save, your AC instead increases by the lower amount.

entries.name: Disarming Strike
entries: You attempt to disarm a creature with your attack. The target must succeed on a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be forced to drop one item of your choice that it's holding. If you have a free hand, you can catch the item. Otherwise, it lands at your feet.

entries.name: Fancy Footwork
entries: Roll two Sneak Attack dice. Your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} increases by 5 x the greater result of the two dice, and you ignore {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain} until the end of your current turn.

entries.name: Panache
entries: {@i {@b Ruffian Practice:} 9th level} Your charm becomes extraordinarily beguiling. As an action, you can make a Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}) check contested by a creature's Wisdom ({@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}) check. The creature must be able to hear you, and the two of you must share a language.

If you succeed on the check and the creature is hostile to you, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against targets other than you and can't make {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks} against targets other than you. This effect lasts for 1 minute, until one of your companions attacks the target or affects it with a power, or until you and the target are more than 60 feet apart.

If you succeed on the check and the creature isn't hostile to you, it is {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} by you for 1 minute. While {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed}, it regards you as a friendly acquaintance. This effect ends immediately if you or your companions do anything harmful to it.

entries.name: Elegant Maneuver
entries: {@i {@b Ruffian Practice:} 13th level} You can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on your turn to gain {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the next Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|sw5e-phb}) or Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) check you make during the same turn.

entries.name: Master Duelist
entries: {@i {@b Ruffian Practice:} 17th level} Your mastery of the blade lets you turn failure into success in combat. If you miss with an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, you can roll it again with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}. Once you do so, you can't use this feature again until you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Saboteur Practice
entries: Those operatives who choose the Saboteur Practice enhance their fine-honed skills of stealth and agility with tech, using advanced technology with the aid of a tracker droid to sustain a longer assault.

entries.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: {@i {@b Saboteur Practice:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency in {@item Astrotech's implements|sw5e-phb|astrotech's implements}.

entries.name: Techcasting
entries: {@i {@b Saboteur Practice:} 3rd level} You have derived powers from schematics with the aid of your {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}. See {@book chapter 10|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} for the general rules of {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} and {@book chapter 12|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} for the {@book tech powers list|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

entries.name: Tech Powers Known
entries: You learn 3 {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of your choice, and you learn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Tech Powers Known|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} column of the Saboteur Practice {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table. You may not learn a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of a level higher than your Max Power Level.

entries.name: Tech Points
entries: You have a number of tech points equal to half of your operative level, as shown in the Tech Points column of the Saboteur Practice {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table, + your Intelligence modifier. You use these tech points to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. You regain all expended tech points when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Max Power Level
entries: Many {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} can be overcharged, consuming more tech points to create a greater effect. You can overcharge these powers to a maximum level, which increases at higher levels, as shown in the Max Power Level column of the Saboteur Practice {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table.
You may only cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} at 4th-level once. You regain the ability to do so after a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Techcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence is your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} for your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. You use your Intelligence whenever a power refers to your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability}. Additionally, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you cast and when making an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with one.
{@b Tech save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence modifier
{@b Tech attack modifier} = your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence modifier

entries.name: Techcasting Focus
entries: You use a {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad} (found in {@book chapter 5|sw5e-phb|5}) as a {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} focus for your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

entries.name: Tracker Droid Companion
