entries: {@i {@b Saboteur Practice:} 3rd, 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level} You learn to employ all the knowledge you've accumulated to create and customize your own tracker droid companion.

Create your tracker droid companion as detailed in the Companions section of the Customization Options document for Expanded Content. You must have {@item Astrotech's implements|sw5e-phb|astrotech's implements} in order to create your droid.
In addition to its traits and features, your tracker droid companion gains an additional benefit while it is bonded to you:

items: Your tracker droid gains two additional traits. It gains one more additional trait when you reach 11th level in this class. For each droid trait in excess of your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, your tech point maximum is reduced by 1. Over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can install, replace, or remove a number of tracker droid traits equal to half your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one).

entries: Lastly, when you cast a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of 1st-level or higher that would affect only one target, and your tracker droid companion is bonded and within 10 feet of you or your target, your tracker droid companion can use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to increase the level at which you are casting your power by 1. This feature can increase a power's level above your Max Power Level, and using this feature does not cost additional tech points.
At 11th level, your tracker droid companion must be within 30 feet of you or your target to benefit from this feature. At 17th level, your tracker droid companion must be within 60 feet.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Powered Ambush
entries: {@i {@b Saboteur Practice:} 9th level} If you are hidden from a creature when you cast a power on it, the creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on any {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} it makes against the power this turn.

entries.name: Ion Pulse
entries: {@i {@b Saboteur Practice:} 13th level} As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on your turn, you can expend one or more of your tracker droid's Hit Dice to have it emit an pulse of ion energy. Each creature within 5 feet of your tracker droid must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC. A creature takes ion damage for each Hit Die expended in this way on a failed save, or half as much as on a successful one. The size of the damage die equals the size of your tracker droid's Hit Die. Any electronics not being worn or carried within the blast radius are disabled until rebooted.

entries.name: Sabotage
entries: {@i {@b Saboteur Practice:} 17th level} You gain the ability to sabotage a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} in the process of being cast. When a hostile creature casts a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, and you are the target of the {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} or within its area of effect, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to force that creature to make an Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC. On a successful save, the power is cast as normal.

On a failed save, you negate the power's effects, and the caster takes 1d6 lightning damage per level of the power it was casting. Additionally, on a failed save, the caster's tech focus used to cast the {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} is overloaded and can't be used to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} for 1 minute.

At the end of each of the caster's turns, it can repeat the Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a success, it can use the tech focus to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} again.
Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Sawbones Practice
entries: Those operatives who choose the Sawbones Practice have studied the humanoid body on a more intimate level than other operatives. While others may know where best to stab in order to kill, you also know how to repair the wounds you inflict, as well as how to make them even deeper. You delve into the secrets of the body, learning as much medical knowledge as you can get your hands on, regardless of how dirty the work becomes.

entries.name: General Practice
entries: {@i {@b Sawbones Practice:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency in {@skill Medicine|sw5e-phb}, and you can use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Wisdom modifier for checks made with it.

Additionally, you can expend one use of a {@item Traumakit|sw5e-phb|traumakit} to help {@spell Revitalize|sw5e-phb|revitalize} your wounded allies during a {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest}. If you or any friendly creatures within 30 feet of you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} at the end of the {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest} by spending one or more Hit Dice, each of those creatures regains an extra 1d6 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}.
The extra {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} increase when you reach certain levels in this class: to 1d8 at 9th level, to 1d10 at 13th level, and to 1d12 at 17th level.

entries.name: Debilitating Strike
entries: {@i {@b Sawbones Practice:} 3rd level} You learn to apply your anatomical knowledge in direct combat, in order to hinder your targets. When you deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature, you may choose to forgo two of your Sneak Attack Dice in order to hinder the creature, provided they have the appropiate physiology.

Some of your debilitating strikes require your target to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the debilitating strike's effects. The {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC is calculated as follows:
{@b Debilitating Strike save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence modifier.

entries.name: Bleeding Wound
entries: You attempt to create a lingering wound in the target for one minute. The target must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, at the start of each of the target's turns, it takes true damage equal to one Sneak Attack die and repeats this {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, ending the effect on a success.

entries.name: Crippling Pain
entries: You attempt to cause distracting pain in the target. The target must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Hampering Shot
entries: You attempt to hamper the target's movement. The target must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, it gains 1 {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level and it makes Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} with {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Swift Surgery
entries: {@i {@b Sawbones Practice:} 9th level} You know how to quickly patch up wounds, given the right tools. You are able to use a {@item Traumakit|sw5e-phb|traumakit} or administer a {@item Medpac|sw5e-phb|medpac} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, and when you use a {@item Traumakit|sw5e-phb|traumakit} to stabilize a dying creature, that creature also regains a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to your Intelligence modifier.

entries.name: Dosage Control
entries: {@i {@b Sawbones Practice:} 13th level} Your knowledge of medicine allows you to partition and ration healing supplies very effectively, without impacting its potency. Over the course of 1 hour, which can be done during a rest, you can carefully measure and mark out dosages of a {@item Medpac|sw5e-phb|medpac} within reach. The {@item Medpac|sw5e-phb|medpac} can now be used twice before it is consumed.
At your DM's discretion, you may be able to use this feature on other pacs, stims, or adrenals, most likely involving an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} to succeed.

entries.name: Self-Sustain
entries: {@i {@b Sawbones Practice:} 17th level} You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throws}.
Additionally, when you are stabilized, you regain 1 hit point. Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Scrapper Practice
entries: Those operatives who choose the Scrapper Practice don't have the time or patience for the fair fight. They utilize close-quarters {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} combat blended with underhanded tactics to surprise and disable their foes.

entries.name: Back Blast
entries: {@i {@b Scrapper Practice:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency in {@filter all blasters|items|firearm=true} with the burst or rapid property that lack the two-handed property. Additionally, when a creature fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against the burst or rapid property of a weapon you control and with which you are proficient, you can apply your Sneak Attack damage to one creature dealt damage in this way as long as that creature didn't have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the save.

When you reach 9th level in this class, when multiple creatures fail a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against the burst property of a weapon you control and with which you are proficient, you can divide your Sneak Attack dice amongst the targets as you see fit.

entries.name: Upper Hand
entries: {@i {@b Scrapper Practice:} 3rd level} You learn to use underhanded tactics to gain the upper hand. When you deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature, you may choose to forgo two of your Sneak Attack Dice in order to perform an upper hand technique.

Some of your upper hand techniques require your target to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the technique's effects. The {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC is calculated as follows:
{@b Upper Hand save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Charisma modifier

entries.name: Brutal Hit
entries: You attempt to knock the target prone while within 15 feet of it. The target must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be knocked {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}.

entries.name: Low Blow
entries: You attempt to stun the target while within 15 feet of it. The target must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be {@condition Stunned|sw5e-phb|stunned} until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Shank Shot
entries: You attempt to hamper the target while within 15 feet of it. The target must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. If it fails, it gains 1 {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level and makes Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} with {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Sleight of Foot
entries: {@i {@b Scrapper Practice:} 9th level} When a creature moves to within 5 feet of you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} away from the creature without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}. You must end this movement further from the creature than you started.

entries.name: Hostile Negotiations
entries: {@i {@b Scrapper Practice:} 13th level} You gain proficiency in {@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb} or {@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}. Additionally, while you are wielding a weapon with which you are proficient, you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb}) and Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}) checks, and if the target would make a contested check, they can't have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on it.

entries.name: Double Tap
entries: {@i {@b Scrapper Practice:} 17th level} You can deal Sneak Attack damage twice per turn, but you can't deal more than your total Sneak Attack dice to a single target per turn.

entries.name: Shadow Killer Practice
entries: Those operatives who choose the Shadow Killer Practice are master assassins, the spiritual practitioners who combine their finely honed skills with mystical aid to vanish from sight and neutralize their targets with poison-coated weapons.

entries.name: Venomous
entries: {@i {@b Shadow Killer Practice:} 3rd, 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th  level} You gain proficiency with the {@item Poisoner's kit|sw5e-phb|poisoner's kit}, and you can apply a poison as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

Additionally, you learn to create a number of special poison vials. Over the course of a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can create two doses of poison. You must have a {@item Poisoner's kit|sw5e-phb|poisoner's kit} in order to create these doses. Your doses can only be used by you, and they lose their potency at the end of your next short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

As an action, you can use one of your doses to coat one {@filter vibroweapon|items|type=martial weapon}, one {@item Slug cartridge|sw5e-phb|slug cartridge}, or one {@item Wrist launcher|sw5e-phb|wrist launcher} dart. A creature hit by the coated weapon must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence modifier), taking 1d4 + your Intelligence modifier poison damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one. Once applied, the poison retains potency for 1 minute before drying.
The quantity and damage of your doses increases at higher levels, to three and 2d4 at 5th level, four and 3d4 at 9th level, five and 4d4 at 13th level, and six and 5d4 at 17th level.

entries.name: Dark Arts
entries: {@i {@b Shadow Killer Practice:} 3rd level} You learn to combine poison and stealth to perform assassination techniques. When you deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature you may choose to forgo two of your Sneak Attack dice to make the attack a dark art.
{@b Dark Arts save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence modifier

entries.name: Envenomed Art
entries: You attempt to poison the target. The target must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be {@condition Poisoned|sw5e-phb|poisoned} until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Hallucinatory Art
entries: You attempt to blind the target. The target must make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be {@condition Blinded|sw5e-phb|blinded} until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Vanishing Art
entries: You feint to momentarily disappear from your target's purview. The target must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failure, you can move up to 10 feet without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks} from the target.

entries.name: Poisoner
entries: {@i {@b Shadow Killer Practice:} 9th level} You are a master of poisons. Targets of your poisons cannot have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} made to resist your poison, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Dexterity ({@skill Sleight Of Hand|sw5e-phb}) checks made to conceal the application of poisons.

Additionally, when you apply poison to a weapon or its ammunition, that poison can affect an additional hit or an additional piece of ammunition, and when you deal Sneak Attack damage with an attack that would include poison damage, you can change your Sneak Attack damage to poison damage.

entries.name: One With the Dark
entries: {@i {@b Shadow Killer Practice:} 13th level} You learn to partially enter the spirit realm. As an action, you can become {@condition Invisible|sw5e-phb|invisible} as an enhanced effect, along with anything you are wearing or carrying, for 1 hour or until you dismiss this effect (no action required). This invisibility ends early immediately after you deal damage to a creature or you force a creature to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. While you have no remaining uses of this feature, you can expend one of your poison doses from your Venomous feature to use this feature again. When you do so, your maximum doses decreases by 1 until the end of your next {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Shades of Night
entries: {@i {@b Shadow Killer Practice:} 17th level} Your familiarity with poisons and the spirit realm has opened up new paths of life and death for you. Your Evasion feature now applies to Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} as well as Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}.

Additionally, whenever you create poison using your Venomous feature, you can change the damage type to acid, cold, fire, lightning or necrotic. When you do so, and you deal Sneak Attack damage with a weapon coated with your poison, you can also change your Sneak Attack damage to the chosen type.

entries.name: Archaeologist Pursuit
entries: Archaeologists are those who study the remnants of historical civilizations. Those scholars who choose the Archaeologist Pursuit are driven by a desire to uncover the past, forming a connection to the lives of those that came before, and unlocking within themselves a connection not just to history, but to the Force itself.

entries.name: Studious Excavator
entries: {@i {@b Archaeologist Pursuit:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency with archaeologist kits and in the {@skill Lore|sw5e-phb} skill. Additionally, you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on checks you make with them.

entries.name: Forcecasting
entries: {@i {@b Archaeologist Pursuit:} 3rd level} You have learned powers from your studies of civilizations that were also once close to the Force. See {@book chapter 10|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} for the general rules of {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} and {@book chapter 11|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} for the {@book force powers list|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

entries.name: Force Powers Known
entries: You learn 4 {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of your choice, and you learn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Force Powers Known|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} column of the Archaeologist Pursuit {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table. You may not learn a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of a level higher than your Max Power Level, and you may learn a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} at the same time you learn its prerequisite.

entries.name: Force Points
entries: You have a number of force points equal to your scholar level, as shown in the Force Points column of the Archaeologist Pursuit {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table, + your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier (your choice). You use these force points to cast {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}. You regain all expended force points when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Max Power Level
entries: Many {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} can be overpowered, consuming more force points to create a greater effect. You can overpower these abilities to a maximum level, which increases at higher levels, as shown in the Max Power Level column of the Archaeologist Pursuit {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table.
You may only cast {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} at 4th-level once. You regain the ability to do so after a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Forcecasting Ability
entries: Your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} varies based on the alignment of the powers you cast. You use your Intelligence or Wisdom for {@book light side powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} (your choice), Intelligence or Charisma for {@book dark side powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} (your choice), and Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma for {@book universal powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} (your choice). You use this ability whenever a power refers to your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability}. Additionally, you use this ability modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} you cast and when making an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with one.
{@b Force save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} modifier
{@b Force attack modifier} = your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} modifier

entries.name: Archaic Diagnostics
entries: {@i {@b Archaeologist Pursuit:} 3rd level} When you {@spell Analyze|sw5e-phb|analyze} a hostile creature, you can use maneuvers that require a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} when you cast a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} that requires a force attack and you can use maneuvers that require a hit with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} when a creature fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} you cast.

entries.name: Force Carving
entries: {@i {@b Archaeologist Pursuit:} 6th level} You have unlocked more control over the Force, allowing you to choose wisely who it affects. When you cast a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 + the power's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against the power, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

entries.name: Psychometric Analysis
entries: {@i {@b Archaeologist Pursuit:} 9th level} Your strength in the Force and your ability to read the objects around you intensifies. You can use your Critical Analysis to {@spell Analyze|sw5e-phb|analyze} an object of Huge size or smaller that you can see within range. When you do so, you learn whether or not the object is enhanced, cursed, and how old it is.

Additionally, you can end your Critical Analysis on the object (no action required) to ask it a single question and receive an answer, usually in the form of an auditory or visual {@spell Hallucination|sw5e-phb|hallucination}. For example, touching the rusted, broken remains of a lightsaber and asking how it got there may result in a brief vision of a disgruntled Jedi Knight casting it to the ground on that spot. An object —questioned— in this way can only provide information relating to its past. The GM has the final say on what objects can be questioned, and to what extent.
You can use this feature four times. You gain an additional use at 13th and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Knowledge is Power
entries: {@i {@b Archaeologist Pursuit:} 17th level} You gain the ability to steal the knowledge of how to cast a power from another forcecaster. When a hostile creature casts a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} that affects a friendly creature within range of your Critical Analysis feature, and you use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} target that friendly creature with your Critical Analysis feature, you can force the creature casting the power to make a Wisdom or Charisma {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (your choice) against your universal force save DC. On a successful save, the power is cast as normal.

On a failed save, you negate the power's effects, and you steal the knowledge of that power if it is at least 1st level and of a level you can cast. For the next 8 hours, you know the power and can cast it using your force points. The creature cannot cast that power again until the 8 hours have passed.
Once you've used this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Archaeologist Discoveries
entries: When you select this pursuit, you gain access to new discoveries which reflect your studies into historical civilations. Whenever you learn a new discovery, you can choose from any of the following as well. The discoveries are listed in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Archive Research
entries: Your expeditions have turned up a bevy of knowledge on the force. You learn three at-will {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of your choice, which don't count against your number of {@book Force Powers Known|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

entries.name: Force Combat Knowledge
entries: Your research into Jedi and Sith combat techniques has allowed you to gain proficiency in {@filter simple lightweapons|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}. Additionally, you gain knowledge of one {@book lightsaber form|sw5e-phb|6|Lightsaber Forms} of your choice.

entries.name: It Belongs in a Museum
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 9th level} Your knowledge of antiquities is unparalleled. When you make an Intelligence ({@skill Lore|sw5e-phb}) check or an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} with your archaeologist kit, you may treat any roll of a 9 or lower as a 10.

entries.name: Localized Survey
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 13th level} Your affinity for the force allows you to key in to the recent past of an area you enter. When you would expend a use of your Psychometric Analysis, you can instead choose to target your immediate vicinity (up to a 50-foot cube) and investigate for at least 1 minute. For each minute you investigate, you see visions of recent events in the area going back a number of days equal to your scholar level, you learn about one significant event, beginning with the most recent.

You can investigate in this way for a number of minutes equal to your scholar level and must maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} during that time, as if you were concentrating on a power.
Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Making This Up As You Go
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 17th level} You may now cast {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} at 4th-level twice between rests.

entries.name: Telekinetic Ministrations
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 9th level} You can cast the {@i telekinesis} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} at 5th level without spending force points.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: The Years and the Mileage
entries: Your archaeological studies have taken you all across the galaxy. While you are the target of your Critical Analysis feature, you can use your universal {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} instead of Wisdom when making {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb} or {@skill Survival|sw5e-phb} checks.

entries.name: Tomb of the Ancients
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 5th level} As a {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} when you take damage, you can entomb yourself in the Force until the end of your next turn. For the duration, you have resistance to the triggering damage, you gain temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to 1d10 + your universal {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} modifier + your scholar level to potentially absorb the attack, and your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is reduced to 0.
Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Chef Pursuit
entries: Without it empires fall, armies dissolve into nothingness, and species are forgotten with the passage of time. A favored tool of assassins, crime lords, and moguls: food. Those scholars who choose the Chef Pursuit know the importance and power that food carries.

entries.name: Culinary Knowledge
entries: {@i {@b Chef Pursuit:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency with chef's kits and your choice of the {@skill Nature|sw5e-phb} or {@skill Survival|sw5e-phb} skills. Additionally, you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on checks you make with them.

entries.name: Emergency Supplements
entries: {@i {@b Chef Pursuit:} 3rd level} You are prepared to assist allies with specially prepared, instantly effective supplements. When an ally is the target of your Critical Analysis feature and within 5 feet of you, you may expend a superiority die and give that ally the benefits of any discovery that utilizes a superiority die and is exclusive to the Chef Pursuit, regardless of whether or not you've chosen it.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Balanced Diet
entries: {@i {@b Chef Pursuit:} 6th level} Your cooking is so nutritionally balanced that it allows allies to stave off the effects of continued rigorous activity. Creatures of your choice who eat food prepared by you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion}, as described in chapter 8, until the end of their next {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Comfort Food
entries: {@i {@b Chef Pursuit:} 9th level} If you or any friendly creatures who have consumed food you prepared during a {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest} regain {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} by spending hit dice at the end of the {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest}, each of those creatures regains an extra 1d8 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}.
The extra {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} increase when you reach certain levels in this class: to 1d10 at 11th level, and to 1d12 at 15th level.

entries.name: Heroes' Feast
entries: {@i {@b Chef Pursuit:} 17th level} You have developed a signature feast that is the purest distillation of your knowledge and talent as a chef.

Over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can expend rare culinary supplies worth 1,000 cr to create your feast, which can feed a number of creatures equal to twice your Critical Analysis ability modifer. Any creature partaking in the feast gains the following benefits:

items: It is cured of all poisons and disease, and becomes immune to poison and disease.
It makes Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid being {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}.
Its hit point maximum and current {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} increase by 2d10.

entries: These benefits last until the end of the creature's next {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} or 24 hours have passed. This feature has no effect on droids or constructs.

entries.name: Chef Discoveries
entries: When you select this pursuit, you gain access to new discoveries which reflect the progress of your studies into the culinary arts. Whenever you learn a new discovery, you can choose from any of the following as well. The discoveries are listed in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Allergens
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} while preparing or touching food, you may expend a superiority die and add to it an irritating allergen. At the start of each of its turns, a creature that consumes this food must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, it subtracts half the result of your superiority die (minimum of one) from the first {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} it makes before the start of its next turn. The effect of this maneuver ends when the creature completes its next {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} or 24 hours have passed. This maneuver has no effect on droids or constructs.

entries.name: Alternative Fuel
entries: Any of your chef features, maneuvers, or discoveries can now affect droids and constructs.

entries.name: Banquet
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 17th level, Full Course} Over the course of a long or {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest}, you may utilize an additional maneuver from this archetype (total of four).

entries.name: Brain Food
entries: At the end of a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} you may expend a superiority die and choose a number of friendly creatures up to your maneuver modifier (minimum of one), if they ate food you prepared. Each creature gains a number of temporary force or tech points (their choice) equal to the number you roll on the superiority die. When an affected creature casts a force or {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, the temporary force or tech points are spent first. An affected target can only benefit from one source of temporary force or tech points at a time, and they last until they're depleted or until the affected target completes their next short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. This maneuver has no effect on droids or constructs.

entries.name: Debilitants
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} when preparing or touching food, you may expend a superiority die and add to it a subtle poison. Any creature that consumes this food must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, their hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to twice the number rolled on your superiority die + your maneuver modifier. The effect of this maneuver ends when the creature completes its next {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} or 24 hours have passed. This maneuver has no effect on droids or constructs.

entries.name: Energizers
entries: At the end of a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} you may expend a superiority die and choose a number of friendly creatures up to your maneuver modifier (minimum of one), if they ate food you prepared. Each creature has their walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} increased by 10 until the end of their next short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. This maneuver has no effect on droids or constructs.

entries.name: Enhancers
entries: At the end of a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} you may expend a superiority die and choose a number of friendly creatures up to your maneuver modifier (minimum of one), if they ate food you prepared. Once before the end of their next short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, affected targets may add the result of the superiority die to a damage roll that would affect only one target. This maneuver has no effect on droids or constructs.

entries.name: Filling Meal
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 7th level} Over the course of a long or {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest}, you may utilize up to two different maneuvers from this archetype, rather than one.

entries.name: Full Course
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 12th level, Filling Meal} Over the course of a long or {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest}, you may utilize an additional maneuver from this archetype (total of three).

entries.name: Health Food
entries: At the end of a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} you may expend a superiority die and choose a number of friendly creatures up to your maneuver modifier (minimum of one), if they ate food you prepared. Each creature gains a number of temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to twice the number you roll on the superiority die. This maneuver has no effect on droids or constructs.

entries.name: Muscle Relaxants
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} while preparing or touching food, you may expend a superiority die and add to it a fast acting muscle relaxant. At the start of each of its turns, a creature that consumes this food must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, it subtracts the result of your superiority die from the first damage roll it makes before the start of its next turn. The effect of this maneuver ends when the creature completes its next {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} or 24 hours have passed. This maneuver has no effect on droids or constructs.

entries.name: On the Rocks
entries: Any food you prepare over a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} carries with it an additional cooling effect. Creatures that consume it are considered adapted to hot climates, as described in {@book chapter 5|sw5e-phb|5} of the Dungeon Master's Guide, until the end of the creature's next {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} or 24 hours have passed. Additionally, the first time a creature who eats your food takes fire damage before the end of their next short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, they are considered resistant to the damage.

entries.name: Secret Ingredient
entries: If you or any friendly creature that has consumed food made by you during their last short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} gains temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, the number of temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} they gain increases by an amount equal to your Critical Analysis ability modifer.

entries.name: Spice of Life
entries: Any food you prepare over a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} carries with it an additional warming effect. Creatures that consume it are considered adapted to cold climates, as described in {@book chapter 5|sw5e-phb|5} of the Dungeon Master's Guide, until the end of the creature's next {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} or 24 hours have passed. Additionally, the first time a creature who eats your food takes cold damage before the end of their next short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, they are considered resistant to the damage.

entries.name: Supplements
entries: At the end of a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} you may expend a superiority die and choose a number of friendly creatures up to your maneuver modifier (minimum of one), if they ate food you prepared. Once before the end of their next short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, affected targets may add the result of the superiority die to one {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. The creature can wait until after it rolls the {@dice d20} before deciding to use this feature, but must decide before the DM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. This maneuver has no effect on droids or constructs.

entries.name: Vitamins
entries: At the end of a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} you may expend a superiority die and choose a number of friendly creatures up to your maneuver modifier (minimum of one), if they ate food you prepared. Each creature gains proficiency in Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} until the end of their next short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. If a creature was already proficient in Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}, they instead become proficient in a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} of your choice. This maneuver has no effect on droids or constructs.

entries.name: Detective Pursuit
entries: Some individuals learn to hone their instincts to investigate and discover that which others can't see. Those scholars who choose the Detective Pursuit train themselves to see the things that others miss, gaining a unique—and powerful—perspective.

entries.name: Martial Training
entries: {@i {@b Detective Pursuit:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency in martial {@filter vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon} and the {@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb} skill. Additionally, you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on checks you make with it.

entries.name: Intelligent Applications
entries: {@i {@b Detective Pursuit:} 3rd level} When you {@spell Analyze|sw5e-phb|analyze} a hostile creature with your Critical Analysis, you can use your Critical Analysis ability modifer with any weapon, as long as it does not have the heavy or special properties.

entries.name: Extra Attack
entries: {@i {@b Detective Pursuit:} 6th level} You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn.

entries.name: Sharp Instincts
entries: {@i {@b Detective Pursuit:} 9th level} Once on each of your turns, when you hit the target of your Critical Analysis with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, you can make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}) check contested by the target's Charisma ({@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}) check. If you win the contest, you deal an additional 1d8 damage to the target, which is the same type as the weapon's damage This die increases to {@dice d10} at 13th level and {@dice d12} at 17th level.

entries.name: Discombobulate
entries: {@i {@b Detective Pursuit:} 17th level} When you use a scholar maneuver on a hostile creature, you can force that target to make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your maneuver save DC. On a failed save, the target is {@condition Stunned|sw5e-phb|stunned} for 1 minute. The target can repeat the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Detective Discoveries
entries: When you select this pursuit, you gain access to new discoveries which reflect your investigative prowess. Whenever you learn a new discovery, you can choose from any of the following as well. The discoveries are listed in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Athletic
entries: You gain your choice of a climbing, crawling, or swimming {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}.

entries.name: Brawler Adept
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 5th level} Your unarmed strike damage increases by one step (from 1 to {@dice d4}, {@dice d4} to {@dice d6}, or {@dice d6} to {@dice d8}). Additionally, your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes} and count as enhanced for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to unenhanced attacks and damage.

entries.name: Eye for Attire
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 5th level} As an action, you can touch a suit of armor that isn't being worn or carried by a hostile creature and instantly don it, provided you aren't wearing armor already.

entries.name: Eye for Detail
entries: You take the {@action Search|sw5e-phb} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Ear for Deceit
entries: Whenever you make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}) check to determine whether a creature is lying, treat a roll of 7 or lower on the {@dice d20} as an 8.

entries.name: Fighting Style
entries: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the {@book fighting style options, detailed in chapter 6|sw5e-phb|6|Fighting Styles} of the Player's Handbook.

entries.name: Scrapper's Armor
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 5th level} You gain proficiency in {@filter medium armor|items|type=medium armor}. If you are already proficient in {@filter medium armor|items|type=medium armor}, you instead gain proficiency in {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor}.

entries.name: Steady Eye
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 9th level} On your turn, you can reduce your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} by half to gain {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}) checks until the end of the turn. You can not use this feature if you have moved more than half your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} this turn.

entries.name: Thirst for Justice
entries: When you reduce a hostile creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, but don't kill it outright, you gain temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to your scholar level, which last for 1 minute.

entries.name: Unerring Eye
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 15th level} You can see the true form of any shapechanger or creature concealed by illusion while the creature is within 30 feet of you and within line of sight.

entries.name: Explorer Pursuit
entries: The explorer strives to navigate past the known to discover new planets, forgotten ruins, or forbidden locations. Those scholars who choose the Explorer Pursuit spend their time studying maps, landmarks, architecture blue prints, or even history books, using them to effectively lead the way for their companions.

entries.name: Focused Navigator
entries: {@i {@b Explorer Pursuit:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency in two of the {@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Piloting|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Survival|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Acrobatics|sw5e-phb} skills. Additionally, you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on checks you make with them.

entries.name: Surveyed Area
entries: {@i {@b Explorer Pursuit:} 3rd level} You can now use your Critical Analysis feature on a 15-foot cube area within 60 feet of you that you can see. You can treat any creatures inside this cube as if they are the target of your Critical Analysis feature, and when a creature ends your Critical Analysis feature on themself, it does not end this effect for other creatures in your Surveyed Area.

entries.name: Field Advantage
entries: {@i {@b Explorer Pursuit:} 6th level} You learn to quickly convey spatial information in the midst of combat about the area you analyzed, giving them an edge at maneuvering in the area. While moving through your Surveyed Area, you and friendly creatures of your choice ignore unenhanced {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain}, and {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks} against them are made with {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.

entries.name: Unstoppable Adventurer
entries: {@i {@b Explorer Pursuit:} 9th level} You learn to swim and scale vertical surfaces with ease. You gain swimming and climbing {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}.

Additionally, your Sage Advice feature can be used to give friendly creatures knowledge on how to swim or climb, provided you have a swimming or climbing {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}. Chosen creatures have a swimming {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} or climbing {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} for the entire duration.

entries.name: Survey Master
entries: {@i {@b Explorer Pursuit:} 17th level} When you use the Surveyed Area feature, the area affected is a 30-foot cube instead of a 15-foot cube.

entries.name: Explorer Discoveries
entries: When you select this pursuit, you gain access to new discoveries which reflect your studies in maps and hidden routes. Whenever you learn a new discovery, you can choose from any of the following as well. The discoveries are listed in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Cover Adept
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 12th level} You treat one-quarter {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} as {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|half cover}, {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|half cover} as three-quarters {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}, and three-quarters {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} as full {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}. Additionally, while you are in {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}, Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) checks you make gain a bonus equal to your Critical Analysis ability modifer (minimum of +1).

entries.name: Dungeon Explorer
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) checks and Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}) checks to locate any secret doors or traps, and you have resistance to damage dealt by traps.

Additionally, you can use your Sage Advice feature to teach friendly creatures about various types of traps, following the same rules of that feature. When you do so, the chosen creatures have resistance to damage dealt by traps.

entries.name: Galactic Explorer
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 9th level} When you make an Intelligence ({@skill Piloting|sw5e-phb}) check and add your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} to the check, treat any roll of 9 or lower as if you had rolled a 10.

entries.name: Grappling Hunter
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 5th level} Attack rolls that you make against creatures that you are grappling have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}.

entries.name: High Ground
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 5th level} Once per turn, when you or a friendly creature hits a creature that is a target of your Critical Analysis feature, it takes additional damage equal to half your Critical Analysis ability modifer (minimum of +1).

entries.name: No Stone Left Unturned
entries: When you make a Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}) check to find a hidden creature that is inside the area that is targeted by your Critical Analysis feature, you do so with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}.

entries.name: Versatile Explorer
entries: You can hold your breath twice as long as you are normally able to, and take half as much damage from fall damage.

entries.name: Geneticist Pursuit
entries: Throughout the galaxy there exists scientists who focus on unraveling the mysteries contained within the bodies of the divese sentients of the galaxy. Those scholars who choose the Geneticist Pursuit put their knowledge into practice, splicing their own genetic material to become superior beings... or monsters.

entries.name: Genesplicer's Methods
entries: {@i {@b Geneticist Pursuit:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency with geneticist's implements and your choice of {@skill Medicine|sw5e-phb} or {@skill Survival|sw5e-phb} skills. Additionally, you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on checks you make with them.

entries.name: Mutagenic Analysis
entries: {@i {@b Geneticist Pursuit:} 3rd level} While you are the target of your Critical Analysis feature, you can add half your Critical Analysis ability modifer (minimum of one) to any {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} you make that doesn't already include that modifier.

entries.name: Mutagenic Transformation
entries: {@i {@b Geneticist Pursuit:} 6th level} When you target yourself with your Critical Analysis feature, you can choose to undergo a mutagenic transformation. Your form shifts, exaggerating and strengthening your geneticist discoveries for 1 hour. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn.
Your Strength score becomes equal to your Critical Analysis score.
You gain a bonus to your AC equal to half your Critical Analysis ability modifer (minimum of +1) if it doesn't already include that modifier.

entries: You can end this effect early on your turn as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}. This effect ends early if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die. You can use this feature twice. You regain all expended uses of it when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Geneticist's Resilience
entries: {@i {@b Geneticist Pursuit:} 9th level} Your genetic alterations make you immune to poison and disease. Additionally, you have resistance to poison damage.

entries.name: Chimeric Adaptation
entries: {@i {@b Geneticist Pursuit:} 17th level} Your genetic modifications have reached new heights. When you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can choose one of the following features. When you undergo your mutagenic transformation, you also gain the benefits of the chosen feature for the duration. You can only have one of these features at a time.

entries.name: Aspect of the Terentatek
entries: You gain proficiency in Wisdom and Charisma {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. Additionally, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, and when a creature within 30 feet of you casts a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} towards the creature. You must end this movement closer to the creature than you started. If you end this movement within 5 feet of the creature, you can make one melee attack against the creature (no action required).

entries.name: Aspect of the Rancor
entries: You gain proficiency in Strength and Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. Additionally, you gain immunity to the {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} condition, and when you deal damage with a weapon or unarmed strike, you can deal an additional 1d8 damage of the same type as the weapon's damage.

entries.name: Aspect of the Varactyl
entries: You gain proficiency in Dexterity and Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. Additionally, your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} increases by 10 feet, your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} can't suffer from {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}, creatures can't have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against you, and each {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level only reduces your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} by 5 feet, unless it would reduce your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} to 0.

entries.name: Geneticist Discoveries
entries: When you select this pursuit, you gain access to new discoveries which reflect the changes you have caused your own body to undergo. Whenever you learn a new discovery, you can choose from any of the following as well. The discoveries are listed in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Adapted Hide
entries: When you aren't wearing armor, your AC is 13 + your Dexterity modifier. Additionally, you are adapted to hot or cold climates (your choice), as described in {@book chapter 5|sw5e-phb|5} of the Dungeon Master's Guide. When you undergo your mutagenic transformation, you add your full Critical Analysis ability modifer, instead of half, to your AC for the duration.

entries.name: Atmospheric Adaptation
entries: You can breathe air and water. When you undergo your mutagenic transformation, you no longer need to breathe, and you can survive up to one hour within the vacuum of space for the duration.

entries.name: Enhanced Musculature
entries: Your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift doubles. If it would already double, it instead triples. Additionally, when you make a long jump, you can {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} a number of feet up to twice your Strength score. When you make a high jump, you can leap a number of feet up into the air equal to 3 + twice your Strength modifier. When you undergo your mutagenic transformation, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Strength checks and Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} for the duration.

entries.name: Icarian Mutation
entries: You sprout a pair of winged arms. You gain a flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to half your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}. You can only gain the benefit of items held by two of your arms at any given time, and once per round you can switch which arms you are benefiting from (no action required). When you undergo your mutagenic transformation, your flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} increases to your full walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}, and you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to take the {@action Dash|sw5e-phb} action for the duration.

entries.name: Mutagenic Hardiness
entries: Your hit point maximum increases by a number equal to your level, and it increases by 1 every time you gain a level. When you undergo your mutagenic transformation, and at the beginning of each of your turns, you gain temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to your half your scholar level + your Critical Analysis ability modifer for the duration.

entries.name: Predatory Senses
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|sw5e-phb|darkvision} out to 60 feet. If you already have {@sense Darkvision|sw5e-phb|darkvision}, its range instead increases by 30 feet. When you undergo your mutagenic transformation, you gain {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) checks that rely on smell for the duration. Additionally, you can track creatures that have left a scent in the last 24 hours.

entries.name: Underground Adaptation
entries: You gain a burrowing {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} and you can tunnel through solid rock at a rate of 1 foot per round. In order to use this {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}, you must have two free hands. When you undergo your mutagenic transformation, you gain {@sense Tremorsense|sw5e-phb|tremorsense} out to 30 feet for the duration. You can detect and pinpoint the origin of vibrations within a specific radius, provided that monster and the source of the vibrations are in contact with the same ground or substance. {@sense Tremorsense|sw5e-phb} can't be used to detect flying or incorporeal creatures.

entries.name: Unnatural Weaponry
entries: You sprout claws or some other natural weapon. Your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes} deal 1d4 kinetic damage, and you can use your choice of your Strength, Dexterity, or Critical Analysis ability modifer for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls. When you undergo your mutagenic transformation, your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes} increase to a {@dice d6} and are considered enhanced for the duration. Additionally, you deal an additional 1d4 acid, lightning, or poison damage when you hit with them.

entries.name: Occultist Pursuit
entries: Occultists research the obscure practitioners of mystical arts, from witches to shamans to sorcerers. Those scholars who choose the Occultist Pursuit learn to harness these magics to bewitch and confound their enemies.

entries.name: Theurgic Research
entries: {@i {@b Occultist Pursuit:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency in the {@skill Lore|sw5e-phb} and {@skill Nature|sw5e-phb} skills. Additionally, you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on checks you make with them.

entries.name: Curse of Objurgation
entries: {@i {@b Occultist Pursuit:} 3rd, 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level} When you target a creature with your Critical Analysis, you can choose one ability. While it can see you, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} made with the chosen ability.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Heightened Hex
entries: {@i {@b Occultist Pursuit:} 6th level} When you use your Curse of Objurgation feature, each time the cursed creature deals damage to you or an allied creature you can see within 5 feet of you, the creature takes psychic damage equal to twice your Critical Analysis ability modifer (minimum of 2).

entries.name: Voodoo Doll
entries: {@i {@b Occultist Pursuit:} 9th level} Over the course of an hour, which can be done during a {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest}, you can perform a ritual to construct an effigy of a creature. In order to do so, you must have at least heard of or seen the creature before, and the target must be in the same system as you. At the end of the hour, the creature must make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your maneuver save DC. This {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} is modified by how well you know the target and the sort of physical connection you have to it, as shown in the Knowledge Save Modifier and Connection Save Modifier tables below.

rows: Secondhand (you have heard of the target)

entries.name: Connection Save Modifier

rows: Body part, lock of hair, bit of nail, or the like

entries: On a successful save, the target isn't affected, and you can't use this ritual against it again for 24 hours. On a failed save, the ritual creates a Tiny doll that is linked to the target. The doll remains linked for 24 hours, or for 10 minutes after you first use it. It disintegrates at the end of this duration. For the duration, you can see and hear the target through the doll as if you were within 5 feet of the creature.
Additionally, as action while the doll is in your possession, you can expend a Hit Die to torment the target, choosing an effect from the following options:

items: {@b Burn:} The target must succeed on a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the target believes it is burning. While burning in this way, the target has has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} made with Strength or Dexterity. This effect lasts for 1 hour.

{@b Pain:} The target must succeed on a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be wracked with pain for 1 hour. While in pain in this way, the target takes an additional 1d4 psychic damage whenever it takes damage.

{@b Stab:} The target must succeed on a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or gain 2 {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} levels and fall {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}. The {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} levels effect lasts for 1 hour.

entries: The target can only be under 1 effect at a time. When you use a new effect, any existing effects end. Placing an effect on a target requires maintaining your {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}, as if concentrating on a power.
You can use this feature twice. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Toil and Trouble
entries: {@i {@b Occultist Pursuit:} 17th level} You perfect your control of your curses, granting them unmatched potency. When the target of your Curse of Objurgation fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against one of your maneuvers, you can choose to amplify that maneuver by expending a number of Hit Dice of your choice. The target immediately takes 1d8 psychic damage for every Hit Die spent in this way.

Additionally, when a creature attempts to use a power like {@i remove curse} or other similar abilities to remove a curse you set, they must roll a Wisdom or Charisma check (their choice) against your maneuver save DC. On a failed save, their attempt fails, and any force or tech points spent in this way are wasted.

entries.name: Occultist Discoveries
entries: When you select this pursuit, you gain access to new discoveries which reflect your research on the occult. Whenever you learn a new discovery, you can choose from any of the following as well. The discoveries are listed in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Arcane Membrane
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Intelligence ({@skill Lore|sw5e-phb}) or Intelligence ({@skill Nature|sw5e-phb}) checks.

entries.name: Evil Eye
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 5th level} You can cast the {@i bestow curse} and {@i remove curse} {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} without spending force points. Wisdom or Charisma (your choice) is your {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} modifier for these powers.
Once you've cast a power using this feature, you must complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can cast it again.

entries.name: Exsanguination
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 9th level} When a creature marked by your Curse of Objurgation is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, you can use a {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and expend a Hit Die to immediately regain a use of your Curse of Objurgation.

entries.name: Hexes and Superstitions
entries: When you roll a 13 on an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, you treat it as if you rolled a 20.

entries.name: Natural Karma
entries: Before you use a maneuver or power to set a curse on a target you can see, you can make a contested Dexterity ({@skill Sleight Of Hand|sw5e-phb}) check against the target's Wisdom ({@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}) check. On a success, the target is unaware you set the curse on them.

entries.name: Savage Sortilege
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 13th level} You ignore resistance to psychic damage, and you have resistance to psychic damage.

entries.name: Supernatural Vigor
entries: At the end of a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can choose one creature you can see within 30 feet (this includes you) to imbue with unnatural power. The creature's hit point maximum and current {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} increase by an amount equal to your scholar level, and it has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} made to avoid {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion}. Both effects end after 8 hours.

entries.name: Slicer Pursuit
entries: Across the galaxy one can find numerous pseudonyms and false identities belonging to the hackers and cyber-infiltrators that call the world of electronics home. Those scholars who choose the Slicer Pursuit put their impressive intellectual prowess to work in the field of technology, to ends both benevolent and malicious.

entries.name: Hacker's Disposition
entries: {@i {@b Slicer Pursuit:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency with slicer's kits and in the {@skill Technology|sw5e-phb} skill. Additionally, you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on checks you make with them.

entries.name: Techcasting
entries: {@i {@b Slicer Pursuit:} 3rd level} You have derived powers from schematics with the aid of your {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}. See {@book chapter 10|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} for the general rules of {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} and {@book chapter 12|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} for the {@book tech powers list|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

entries.name: Tech Powers Known
entries: You learn 3 {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of your choice, and you learn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Tech Powers Known|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} column of the Slicer Pursuit {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table. You may not learn a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of a level higher than your Max Power Level.

entries.name: Tech Points
entries: You have a number of tech points equal to half of your scholar level, as shown in the Tech Points column of the Slicer Pursuit {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table, + your Intelligence modifier. You use these tech points to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. You regain all expended tech points when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Max Power Level
entries: Many {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} can be overcharged, consuming more tech points to create a greater effect. You can overcharge these powers to a maximum level, which increases at higher levels, as shown in the Max Power Level column of the Slicer Pursuit {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table.
You may only cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} at 4th-level once. You regain the ability to do so after a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Techcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence is your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} for your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. You use your Intelligence whenever a power refers to your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability}. Additionally, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you cast and when making an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with one.
{@b Tech save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence modifier
{@b Tech attack modifier} = your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence modifier

entries.name: Techcasting Focus
entries: You use a {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad} (found in {@book chapter 5|sw5e-phb|5} of the Player's Handbook) as a tech focus for your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

entries.name: Systems Hijack
entries: Also at 3rd level, when the target of your Critical Analysis is a droid or construct, or wearing or holding a {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} focus, that creature is a viable target for any {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} with you cast with a range of touch.

Additionally, when the target of your Critical Analysis casts a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to identify the {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} being cast, and at what level.

entries.name: Potent Programming
entries: {@i {@b Slicer Pursuit:} 6th level} When a creature succeeds on a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against an at-will {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you cast that deals damage, the creature takes half the power's damage, but suffers no additional effects of the power.

entries.name: Redirect Error
entries: {@i {@b Slicer Pursuit:} 9th level} When the target of your Critical Analysis feature casts a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} that affects an area, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to cause that power to instead affect an area in a 10-foot-radius sphere centered on the caster.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: System Override
entries: {@i {@b Slicer Pursuit:} 17th level} You know how to quickly activate anti-tech subroutines you have encoded into your {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}. You can cast the {@i diminish tech} and {@i tech override} powers at 3rd level without expending tech points. If the target is the target of your Critical Analysis, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} check for these powers.
You can use this feature three times. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Slicer Discoveries
entries: When you select this pursuit, you gain access to new discoveries which reflect your understanding of tech casting. Whenever you learn a new discovery, you can choose from any of the following as well. The discoveries are listed in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Administrator's Log
entries: If you spend at least 10 minutes working on a computer or terminal, you can get a full list of users who have accessed the machine within the past 24 hours. Over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you may then form a facsimile of identification that would allow you to pass yourself off as that person when accessing machines.

entries.name: Backdoor Egress
entries: When you cast a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} that affects an area and requires a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and you are inside that power's area, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}. If you end this movement outside the area affected by the {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, you do not have to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to avoid its effects.

entries.name: Intelligence Core Override
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 9th level} You can cast the {@i override interface} {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} at 5th level without spending tech points.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Resource Appropriation
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 11th level} If you reduce the target of your Critical Analysis feature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, and it has tech point remaining, you may choose to gain any tech points it had remaining. Your current tech points cannot exceed your tech point maximum.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Skillful Casting
entries: When you hit a creature with an at-will {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} that requires an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, you may treat that {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} as a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} for the purpose of using maneuvers.

entries.name: Sleeper Program
entries: Whenever you cast a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} with a casting time of 1 action, you can choose to delay the power's activation up to a minute. When you do so, you cast the power as normal, but holds its energy for the duration of the delay. Holding onto the power's effect requires {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}. If your {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} is broken before the delay ends, the power dissipates without taking effect. You can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to activate the power at any time.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses  when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Zoologist Pursuit
entries: Many academics develop an affinity for nature, studying the vast fauna that inhabit the different planets throughout the galaxy. Those scholars who choose the Zoologist Pursuit capitalize on their knowledge of animals, developing a strong bond with a companion with whom they gain an {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the battlefield.

entries.name: Wilderness Expert
entries: {@i {@b Zoologist Pursuit:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency in {@skill Animal Handling|sw5e-phb}, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling|sw5e-phb}) checks. Additionally, you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling|sw5e-phb}) checks.

entries.name: Beast Companion
entries: {@i {@b Zoologist Pursuit:} 3rd, 11th, and 17th level} You learn to employ all the knowledge you've accumulated to forge a powerful bond with your own beast companion.
Create your beast companion as detailed in the Companions section of the Customization Options document for Expanded Content.
In addition to its traits and features, your beast companion gains additional benefits while it is bonded to you:

items: Your beast gains two additional traits. It gains one more additional trait when you reach 11th level in this class. For each beast trait in excess of your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, your number of available Hit Dice that can be spend to restore {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} is reduced by 1.

entries: Lastly, while bonded and within 10 feet of you, your beast companion gains a bonus to {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks}, {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb|armor class}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls}, damage rolls, and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} equal to half your Critical Analysis ability modifer (minimum of +1).
This radius increases to 30 feet at 11th level, and 60 feet at 17th level.

entries.name: Vicious Hunting
entries: {@i {@b Zoologist Pursuit:} 6th level} Your beast companion's strikes count as enhanced for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to unenhanced attacks and damage. Additionally, when your beast makes an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you may expend a superiority die and apply the benefits of a maneuver you know from this class, as if you had taken the action yourself.

entries.name: Bestial Agility
entries: {@i {@b Zoologist Pursuit:} 9th level} Your beast's reflexes and agility allow it to move with a burst of {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}. When your beast moves on its turn in combat, it can double its {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} until the end of the turn. Once its used this feature, it can't use it again until it moves 0 feet on one of its turns.

entries.name: Feral Ferocity
entries: {@i {@b Zoologist Pursuit:} 17th level} You have learned how to push your beast beyond its limits. If your beast is within 30 feet of you and can see or hear you, you can command it to enter a furious state. While raging, your beast gains the following benefits:

items: Your beast has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Strength checks and Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} if it is size Medium or larger.
Your beast has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Dexterity checks and Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} if it is size Small or smaller.
When your beast hits with an attack, it deals bonus damage equal to your Critical Analysis ability modifer.
Your beast has resistance to kinetic and energy damage.
