entries: Your beast's furious state lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if your beast is knocked {@condition Unconscious|sw5e-phb|unconscious}. You can end your beast's furious state as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.
Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Zoologist Discoveries
entries: When you select this pursuit, you gain access to new discoveries which reflect your studies in biology and behaviour of alien lifeforms. Whenever you learn a new discovery, you can choose from any of the following as well. The discoveries are listed in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Advantageous Companion
entries: When you make a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb}) check against a creature that can see your beast companion, and your companion is size Medium or larger, you make the check with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}.

When you make a Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}) check against a creature that can see your beast companion, and your companion is size Small or Tiny, you make the check with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}.

entries.name: Holocam Attachment
entries: You have learned how to safely attach a holocam on the head of the companion. You learn the {@i tracker droid interface} {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, your beast becomes a valid target of this power, and when you cast this power targeting your beast, you do so without spending tech points. You require use of a {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad} for this power.

entries.name: Neat Tricks
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 5th level} Your beast gains proficiency in one Strength or Dexterity skill of your choice. If your beast's size is Medium or larger and the chosen skill uses Strength, it has {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in the chosen skill. If your beast's size is Small or smaller and the chosen skill uses Dexterity, it has {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in the chosen skill.

entries.name: One Big Baddie
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Size Medium or larger beast} Your beast companion gains the following benefits:

items: It deals double damage against structures.
It can take the {@action Guard|sw5e-phb} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, but it can only guard you in this way.
It can spend a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to spend one of its Hit Dice to recover {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}.

When it rolls a Hit Die to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, the minimum number of {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} it can regain from the roll equals twice its Constitution modifier (minimum of 2).

entries.name: Protective Friend
entries: If a creature makes a melee attack against you or your companion, and your companion is within 5 feet of you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}.

entries.name: The More the Merrier
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Size Small or smaller beast} Rather than a single beast companion, you instead control multiple beasts that function as a swarm. Your beast companion gains the following benefits:

items: Its effective size increases by two categories (from Tiny to Medium or Small to Large).
Its {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} increase by an amount equal to twice its level + 2.
It can only be mounted by creatures at least three size categories smaller than it, instead of one.
It can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and it can move through any opening large enough for a creature two size categories smaller than it.

While it is above half its hit point maximum, when it takes the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, it can make an additional attack. If the creature has the Extra Attack feature, this attack is in addition to the attack granted by that feature.

entries.name: Artillerist Technique
entries: Some scouts choose to navigate around defenses, while others choose to go through them. Followers of the Artillerist Technique learn to exert greater control of their {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, causing delayed—and often empowered—effects.

entries.name: Modular Munitions
entries: {@i {@b Artillerist Technique:} 3rd level} When you cast a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, rather than having it take effect instantly, you can choose to delay the effect to occur on {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} count 20 (losing all {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} ties). When you do so, any creature that leaves the affected area of your {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} is unaffected when the {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} occurs. If the power would only target one creature, and that creature moves from the space it was in when you cast the power, the {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} automatically misses if it would call for an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, as if you had rolled a 1 on the attack, and the creature automatically succeeds on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against the power if it calls for a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, as if it had rolled a 20 on the save.

Additionally, when you cast a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} and choose to delay it in this way, and that {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} would deal damage, you can apply one of the following additional empowerment effects:

items: {@b Flashbang}: Each creature damaged by this power must succeed on a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be {@condition Blinded|sw5e-phb|blinded} and {@condition Deafened|sw5e-phb|deafened} until the start of your next turn.

{@b Mire:} Each creature damaged by this power must succeed on a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or gain one {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level until the start of your next turn.

{@b Psyche:} Each creature damaged by this power must succeed on a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or become {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} until the start of your next turn.

entries: If an empowerment effect calls for a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, the DC equals your tech save DC.

You can use these features a combined number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, as shown in the scout table. You regain all expended uses when you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

While you have no remaining uses of this feature, you can instead expend 1 tech point to use it. When you do so, your maximum tech points are reduced by 1 until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Mark of the Artillerist
entries: {@i {@b Artillerist Technique:} 3rd and 11th level} You can now use your Ranger's Quarry feature on a 10-foot cube area within 60 feet of you that you can see. You can treat any creatures inside this cube as if they are the target of your Ranger's Quarry feature, and when a creature is hit by a tech attack or fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you cast that deals damage, you can apply your Ranger's Quarry damage to that creature.
At 11th level, you can now use your Ranger's Quarry feature on a 15-foot cube area, instead of a 10-foot cube.

entries.name: Sundered Defenses
entries: {@i {@b Artillerist Technique:} 7th level} Your precise bombardments make even the most hardened defenses crumble. When you cast a power that calls for a tech attack or a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, it reduces partial {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} by one step (from three-quarters to half or half to one-quarter) against creatures affected by it. If an affected creature has one-quarter {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}, your power ignores it entirely.

entries.name: Target Masking
entries: {@i {@b Artillerist Technique:} 11th level} You are familiar with various turrets and defensive emplacements, and their operation.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can activate a masking effect to confuse the targeting of constructs for 1 minute. Any construct who targets you with an attack, a harmful power, or a hostile action must first make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC. On a failed save, the construct must choose a new target or lose the attack or power. This power doesn't protect you from area effects.

You can use this feature a combined number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, as shown in the scout table. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Master of Ordnance
entries: {@i {@b Artillerist Technique:} 15th level} You can now expend two uses of your Modular Munitions feature when you cast a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} to apply two empowerment effects, instead of only one. Additionally, you gain three additional empowerment effects:

items: {@b Confusion:} Each creature damaged by this power must make a Charisma {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failure, on its next turn, a creature must use its action to make a melee attack against a randomly determined creature within its reach. If there is no creature within its reach, the creature does nothing this turn.
{@b Knockout:} Each creature damaged by this power must succeed on a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be knocked {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}.

{@b Static:} Each creature damaged by this power must succeed on an Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or become {@condition Shocked|sw5e-phb|shocked} until the start of your next turn.

entries: Additionally, when you would spend 1 tech point to apply an empowerment effect, it no longer reduces your maximum tech points.

entries.name: Artillerist Technique (Companion)
entries: While some scouts choose to foray alone, others like to have support. Followers of the Artillerist Technique master control of militant constructs, laying waste to the battlefield with their {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise}

entries.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: {@i {@b Artillerist Technique:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency in artillerist's implements.

entries.name: Turret Companion
entries: {@i {@b Artillerist Technique:} 3rd, 11th, and 17th level} You learn to apply your knowledge to construct and bond with your own portable turret.
Create your turret companion as detailed in the Companions section of the Customization Options document for Expanded Content. You must have artillerist's implements in order to create your turret.
In addition to its traits and features, your turret companion gains additional benefits while it is bonded to you:

items: Your turret is a valid target of the {@i tracker droid interface} {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

Your turret gains two additional traits. It gains one more additional trait when you reach 11th level in this class. For each turret trait in excess of your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, your tech point maximum is reduced by 1. Over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can install, replace, or remove a number of turret traits equal to half your Intelligence modifier (rounded up, minimum of one).
When you would make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}, you can let your turret make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} instead.

entries: Lastly, while your turret is bonded, within 10 feet of you, and the target of your {@i tracker droid interface} {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, when you cast a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} with a range of 5 feet or greater, you can cast it as if you were in your turret's space, and the range increases to 10 feet if it isn't greater.
Both the range and radius increase to 30 feet at 11th level, and 60 feet at 17th level.

entries.name: Mark of the Artillerist
entries: {@i {@b Artillerist Technique:} 3rd level} Once per round, when your turret deals damage to the target of your Ranger's Quarry, you can roll your Ranger's Quarry die and add it to the damage roll.

entries.name: Crisis Management
entries: {@i {@b Artillerist Technique:} 7th level} While you can see your turret, it can add half its {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} to any {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} it makes that doesn't already include it.

entries.name: Double Up
entries: {@i {@b Artillerist Technique:} 11th level} When you deal damage to a creature with a weapon or {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, your turret has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the next {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} it makes against the creature or it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the first {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} it makes against an effect your turret controls before the start of your next turn. When your turret deals damage to a creature, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your next {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against the creature or it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the first {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} it makes against an effect you control before the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Battlefront
entries: {@i {@b Artillerist Technique:} 15th level} When you use your Combat Tech feature, both you and your turret can each make one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} as part of the same {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Deadeye Technique
entries: Some scouts become legends written in {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} burns. Followers of the Deadeye Technique perfect the art of the {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} shot and utilize their incredible focus to make shots that most would deem impossible. When everything depends on one shot, you want a Deadeye pulling the trigger.

Due to their uncanny focus, Deadeyes can make shots that other marksmen would never dare to attempt. Deadeyes know how to make the most of ranged weapons and can use them to greater effect than other Scouts.

entries.name: Deadeye Superiority
entries: {@i {@b Deadeye Technique:} 3rd level} You learn maneuvers that are fueled by special dice called {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}. See {@book chapter 13|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} for the {@book maneuvers list|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers}.

entries.name: Maneuvers Known
entries: You learn two maneuvers of your choice, and you earn more at higher levels, as shown in the Maneuvers Known column of the Deadeye Superiority table. Many maneuvers enhance an attack in some way. You can use only one maneuver per attack, and you may only use each maneuver once per turn.
Each time you learn new maneuvers, you can also replace one maneuver you know with a different one.

entries.name: Superiority Dice
entries: You have two {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}, which are d4s, and you earn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Superiority Dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} Quantity column of the Deadeye Superiority table. This die changes as you gain scout levels, as shown in the {@book Superiority Dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} Size column of the Deadeye Superiority table. A superiority die is expended when you use it.
You regain all of your expended {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Maneuver Ability
entries: Your {@book maneuver ability|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} varies based on the type of the maneuver you use. You use Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution for {@book physical maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Physical} (your choice), Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma for {@book mental maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Mental} (your choice), and an ability of your choice for {@book general maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|General}. You use this ability whenever a maneuver refers to your {@book maneuver ability|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}. Additionally, you use this ability modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a maneuver you use.
{@b Maneuver save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your {@book maneuver ability|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} modifier

entries.name: Mark of the Deadeye
entries: {@i {@b Deadeye Technique:} 3rd level} The range of your Ranger's Quarry feature doubles. Additionally, when making ranged weapon attacks against the target of your Ranger's Quarry, the normal and long range of your {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} weapons double.

entries.name: Cover to Cover
entries: {@i {@b Deadeye Technique:} 7th level} Attack rolls made against you on your turn are made with {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.

entries.name: Shoot First
entries: {@i {@b Deadeye Technique:} 11th, 13th, and 17th level} You have learned that the person who shoots first is often the one who walks out alive. When you make a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} against a creature that has not yet acted during your first turn in combat and you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the roll, you can reroll one of the dice once. Additionally, on a hit, you deal an extra 1d8 damage of the same type as the weapon. This damage increases to 1d10 at 13th level and 1d12 at 17th level.

entries.name: Overwatch
entries: {@i {@b Deadeye Technique:} 15th level} You have become a master at protecting your allies from afar. When a creature attempts to make an {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attack} against an allied creature, or forces your ally to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against the enemy creature.

If your attack hits, either impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the enemy creature's {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attack} roll or grant {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} to any allies making the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

entries.name: Illusionist Technique
entries: Among the galaxy you may find the various infiltrators and agents who make ample use of holographic technology to get themselves in and out of danger. Followers of the Illusionist Technique make use of this holographic technology to give themselves an illusory edge in combat.

entries.name: Holographic Decoy
entries: {@i {@b Illusionist Technique:} 3rd, 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level} As an action, you can create a perfect illusion of yourself that lasts for 10 minutes, or until you lose your {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} (as if you were concentrating on a power). The decoy appears in an unoccupied space that you can see within 30 feet of you. The decoy is purely visual. If anything passes through it, it is revealed to be an illusion. For the duration, you can cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} as though you were in the decoy's space. Both your decoy and the target of your {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} must be within your line of sight.

You can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to cause the decoy to move up to 30 feet. As your decoy changes location, you can alter its appearance so that its movements appear natural for the decoy. If your decoy is ever more than 120 feet away from you, it immediately disappears.

Additionally, when both you and your decoy are within 5 feet of a creature that can see the decoy, but is not aware it is an illusion, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against that creature.

A creature that uses its action to examine your decoy can determine that it is an illusion with a successful Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}) check against your tech save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the creature can see through the image.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Mark of the Illusionist
entries: {@i {@b Illusionist Technique:} 3rd level} The target of your Ranger's Quarry feature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on all checks made to discern the nature of your illusions. Additionally, when the target of your Ranger's Quarry is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to immediately cause an active illusion, or your Holographic Decoy, to take the form of the creature as long as the creature's dimensions fall within the power's capacity restrictions.

entries.name: Charged Illusions
entries: {@i {@b Illusionist Technique:} 7th level} When a creature discerns the nature of an illusion you have created using a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} or class feature while within 5 feet of it, you can dispel the illusion (no action required) to have the creature take energy damage equal to 1d10 + half your scout level.

entries.name: Quick Escape
entries: {@i {@b Illusionist Technique:} 11th level} Whenever you take damage, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to swap places with an illusion of yourself that you have created using a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} or class feature. The illusion must be within 60 feet of you, and you must be able to see it.

entries.name: Improved Decoys
entries: {@i {@b Illusionist Technique:} 15th level} You can create up to four duplicates of yourself, instead of one, when you use your Holographic Decoy feature. When you use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to move a decoy, you can move any number of them with the same {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Inquisitor Technique
entries: Across history, there have been those who live to hunt those who wield the Force, be they Jedi or Sith. Followers of the Inquisitor Technique combine technology with force techniques to track down and eliminate force-wielders. For those practitioners of the Force, they are the greatest adversary.

entries.name: Forcecasting Secrets
entries: {@i {@b Inquisitor Technique:} 3rd, 5th, 9th, 13th,  and 17th level} You have learned secrets from a subtle attunement to the force. Choose two {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of no higher level than your Max Power Level, as shown in the scout table. The chosen powers count as {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} for you, but are not included in the number in the Powers Known column of the scout table.

You learn two additional powers at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} you know and replace it with another {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of no higher level than your Max Power Level.

entries.name: Mark of the Inquisitor
entries: {@i {@b Inquisitor Technique:} 3rd, 11th, and 17th level} When the target of your Ranger's Quarry feature is within 15 feet of you, you gain the following benefits:

items: Whenever the creature casts a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, it must first succeed on a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}. On a failed save, the casting is disrupted, the {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} fails, and the force points are wasted.

Whenever the creature starts its turn while concentrating on a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, it must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}. On a failed save, it loses {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} on the power.

entries: The radius of this feature increases to 30 feet at 11th level and 60 feet at 17th level.

entries.name: Sense Force
entries: {@i {@b Inquisitor Technique:} 7th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level} You can use your action to gain the benefits of the {@i force sight} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} until the end of your next turn.
You can use this feature three times. You gain an additional use at 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Force Resistance
entries: {@i {@b Inquisitor Technique:} 11th and 17th level} While the target of your Ranger's Quarry feature is within 30 feet of you, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} they cast.
You have resistance to damage dealt by {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} they cast.

entries: The radius of this feature increases to 60 feet at 17th level.

entries.name: Inquisitor's Wrath
entries: {@i {@b Inquisitor Technique:} 15th and 17th level} You can cast the {@i force suppression} and {@i sever force} {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} at 3rd level against the target of your Ranger's Quarry without expending tech points. If they are within 30 feet of you, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} check for these powers.
You can use this feature five times. You gain an additional use at 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
The radius of this feature increases to 60 feet at 17th level.

entries.name: Mastermind Technique
entries: Preparation, preparation, preparation. Some scouts are serious students of battle and any creatures they might encounter. Followers of the Mastermind Technique focus on being prepared for any eventuality, and using their breadth of knowledge to gain insights into their enemies.

entries.name: Instinctive Combatant
entries: {@i {@b Mastermind Technique:} 3rd level} You have learned to use your wits to help you survive. While you are wearing light or {@filter medium armor|items|type=medium armor}, you can use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Dexterity modifier when determining your AC.

entries.name: Mark of the Meticulous
entries: {@i {@b Mastermind Technique:} 3rd level} You can use Intelligence instead of Dexterity for the attack and damage rolls made with weapons with {@itemProperty SWF|sw5e-phb|the finesse property} or {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} weapons against the target of your Ranger's Quarry.

Additionally, once per round, when you hit the target of your Ranger's Quarry with a tech attack, or it fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you cast that deals damage, you can deal additional damage equal to your Ranger's Quarry damage die of the same type as the {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}'s damage.

entries.name: Adaptive Techie
entries: {@i {@b Mastermind Technique:} 7th level} When you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can choose up to a number of {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you know equal to half your Intelligence modifier and replace them with another {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, as long as that power is not of a higher level than your Max Power Level.

entries.name: Emergency Planning
entries: {@i {@b Mastermind Technique:} 11th level} You've learned to formulate and execute a plan. As an action, you can choose up to six creatures (including yourself) that you can see within 60 feet of you. For each creature, choose one of the following: {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. Each creature gains an Emergency Planning die, which is a {@dice d8}.

Once within the next 10 minutes, each creature can roll the die and add the number rolled to one {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, as determined when you use this feature. The creature can wait until after it rolls the {@dice d20} before deciding to use the Emergency Planning die, but must decide before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. Once the Emergency Planning die is rolled, it is lost.
A creature can have only one Emergency Planning die at a time.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.
Your Emergency Planning die changes when you reach certain levels in this class. to 1d10 at 13th level, and to 1d12 at 17th level.

entries.name: Exploit Weakness
entries: {@i {@b Mastermind Technique:} 15th level} Your training has taught you to find and exploit weaknesses in your prey. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the next {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} the target of your Ranger's Quarry makes against an effect you control before the end of your next turn. Once you've done so, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can do so again.

entries.name: Mechanist Technique
entries: Some scouts are peerless inventors, skilled at working with droids and other forms of technology. Followers of the Mechanist Technique make up for the weakness of organics with the strength and purity of their creations.

entries.name: Improved Techcasting
entries: {@i {@b Mechanist Technique:} 3rd level} Your command of {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} improves.

entries.name: Improved Tech Powers Known
entries: You know 7 {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of your choice, instead of 5, and you learn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Tech Powers Known|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} column of the Mechanist Technique {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table. You may not learn a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of a level higher than your Max Power Level.

entries.name: Improved Tech Points
entries: You have a number of tech points equal to one and a half times your scout level, instead of your scout level, as shown in the Tech Points column of the Mechanist Technique {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table, + your Intelligence modifier. You use these tech points to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. You regain all expended tech points when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Improved Max Power Level
entries: Your Max Power Level becomes 2nd, instead of 1st, and it increases at higher levels, as shown in the Mechanist Technique {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table.

You may only cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} at 5th, 6th, and 7th-level once, instead of 4th and 5th. You regain the ability to do so after a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Mark of the Mechanist
entries: {@i {@b Mechanist Technique:} 3rd level} As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can cause the target of your Ranger's Quarry to emit an ion pulse, as long as the target is within 60 feet of you. The target, and any creatures within 5 feet of it, must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC. On a failed save, roll your Ranger's Quarry die; each creature takes ion damage equal to the amount rolled.

entries.name: Potent Tech
entries: {@i {@b Mechanist Technique:} 7th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level} You can use your ingenuity to bolster yourself or an ally. As an action, you can touch one creature (which can be yourself) and confer one of the following benefits of your choice to that creature:

items: For 10 minutes, the creature can roll a d3 whenever making an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} or an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} and add the number rolled to the {@dice d20} roll. Once a creature receives this benefit, that creature can't receive it again until it finishes a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

Roll a {@dice d4}. The creature regains a number of tech points equal to the result. Once a creature receives this benefit, that creature can't receive it again until it finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries: You can use this feature three times. You gain an additional use at 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: High Voltage
entries: {@i {@b Mechanist Technique:} 11th level} You are used to working with electronics and have learned to increase their potency, while becoming inured to their dangers. You gain resistance to ion and lightning damage.

Additionally, whenever you deal ion damage to a creature, you can spend a tech point to force the creature to make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, it is {@condition Stunned|sw5e-phb|stunned} until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Command Droid
entries: {@i {@b Mechanist Technique:} 15th level} You can reprogram a droid and bring it under your control. As an action, you can touch one droid that you can see that is the target of your Ranger's Quarry. That creature must make a Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC. If it succeeds, you can't use this feature on it again for 24 hours. If it fails, it becomes friendly to you and obeys your commands until you use this feature again.

Intelligent droids are harder to control in this way. If the target has an Intelligence of 8 or higher, it has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. If it fails the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} and has an Intelligence of 12 or higher, it can repeat the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} at the end of every hour until it succeeds and breaks free.

entries.name: Mechanist Technique (Companion)
entries: Some scouts are peerless inventors, skilled at working with droids and other forms of technology. Followers of the Mechanist Technique utilize the assistance of a tracker droid companion to make up for the weakness of organics with the strength and purity of their creations.

entries.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: {@i {@b Mechanist Technique:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency in astrotech—s implements.

entries.name: Improved Techcasting
entries: {@i {@b Mechanist Technique:} 3rd level} Your command of {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} improves.

entries.name: Improved Tech Powers Known
entries: You know 7 {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of your choice, instead of 5, and you learn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Tech Powers Known|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} column of the Mechanist Technique {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table. You may not learn a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of a level higher than your Max Power Level.

entries.name: Improved Tech Points
entries: You have a number of tech points equal to one and a half times your scout level, instead of your scout level, as shown in the Tech Points column of the Mechanist Technique {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table, + your Intelligence modifier. You use these tech points to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. You regain all expended tech points when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Improved Max Power Level
entries: Your Max Power Level becomes 2nd, instead of 1st, and it increases at higher levels, as shown in the Mechanist Technique {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table.

You may only cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} at 5th, 6th, and 7th-level once, instead of 4th and 5th. You regain the ability to do so after a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Tracker Droid Companion
entries: {@i {@b Mechanist Technique:} 3rd, 5th, 9th, 11th, 13th, and 17th level} You learn to employ all the knowledge you've accumulated to create and customize your own tracker droid companion.

Create your tracker droid companion as detailed in the Companions section of the Customization Options document for Expanded Content. You must have {@item Astrotech's implements|sw5e-phb|astrotech's implements} in order to create your droid.
In addition to its traits and features, your tracker droid companion gains an additional benefit while it is bonded to you:

items: Your tracker droid gains two additional traits. It gains one more additional trait when you reach 11th level in this class. For each droid trait in excess of your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, your tech point maximum is reduced by 1. Over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can install, replace, or remove a number of droid traits equal to half your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one).

entries: Lastly, while your tracker droid companion is bonded and within 10 feet of you, you can use your action to learn the location of any droid or construct, tech focus, {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} or enhanced item within 60 feet of you or your tracker droid that isn't behind {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|total cover}. When you sense a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} in this way, you learn what the power is. At 11th level, your tracker droid companion must be within 30 feet of you or your target to benefit from this feature. At 17th level, your tracker droid companion must be within 60 feet. You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Mark of the Mechanist
entries: {@i {@b Mechanist Technique:} 7th level} As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can cause the target of your Ranger's Quarry to emit an ion pulse, as long as the target is within 60 feet of you. The target, and any creatures within 5 feet of it, must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC. On a failed save, roll your Ranger's Quarry die; each creature takes ion damage equal to the amount rolled.

entries.name: High Voltage
entries: {@i {@b Mechanist Technique:} 11th level} You are used to working with electronics and have learned to increase their potency, while becoming inured to their dangers. You gain resistance to ion and lightning damage.

Additionally, whenever you deal ion damage to a creature, you can spend a tech point to force the creature to make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, it is {@condition Stunned|sw5e-phb|stunned} until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Command Droid
entries: {@i {@b Mechanist Technique:} 15th level} You can reprogram a droid and bring it under your control. As an action, you can touch one droid that you can see that is the target of your Ranger's Quarry. That creature must make a Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC. If it succeeds, you can't use this feature on it again for 24 hours. If it fails, it becomes friendly to you and obeys your commands until you use this feature again.

Intelligent droids are harder to control in this way. If the target has an Intelligence of 8 or higher, it has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. If it fails the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} and has an Intelligence of 12 or higher, it can repeat the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} at the end of every hour until it succeeds and breaks free.

entries.name: Predator Technique
entries: Some scouts work in solitude, while others prefer the strength of a group. Followers of the Predator Technique find power lies with the pack; they distract their prey, while their allies go for the kill.

entries.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: {@i {@b Predator Technique:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency in {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor}.

entries.name: Hunting Party
entries: {@i {@b Predator Technique:} 3rd, 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level} When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to direct one of your companions to strike. When you do so, choose a friendly creature who can see or hear you. That creature can immediately use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses of it when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Mark of the Predator
entries: {@i {@b Predator Technique:} 3rd level} If the target of your Ranger's Quarry feature can see you, a number of friendly creatures you choose up to your Intelligence modifier have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) checks made to hide from it.

entries.name: Predator's Resolve
entries: {@i {@b Predator Technique:} 7th level} You can use your action to gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}.
At the start of each of your turns, you gain temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of one).
When you use your Hunting Party feature and the target of the attack is your Ranger's Quarry, your ally gains a bonus to damage on the attack equal to your Ranger's Quarry Damage Die.

entries: Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Prey on the Weak
entries: {@i {@b Predator Technique:} 11th level} When you hit a creature with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}, and the creature is below its hit point maximum, the next {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} made against that creature before the end of your next turn by someone other than you has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}.

entries.name: On the Hunt
entries: {@i {@b Predator Technique:} 15th level} When you use your Predator's Resolve feature, a number of friendly creatures you choose up to your Intelligence modifier that you can see within 30 feet of you also gain the benefits of the feature.

entries.name: Teleportation Technique
entries: Whether through experimentation or discovery of    an ancient technology, followers of the    Teleportation Technique have learned to create    brief teleportation portals, allowing them to    maneuver and attack both quickly and    unpredictably throughout the battlefield.

entries.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: {@i {@b Teleportation Technique:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency in {@item Tinker's implements|sw5e-phb|tinker's implements}.

entries.name: Personal Teleporter
entries: {@i {@b Teleportation Technique:} 3rd, 5th, 9th, 13th, 17th, and 20th level} You can use portable teleporters as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, instead of an action.

Additionally, while you are wielding a tech focus, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to create a pair of linked portals: one portal appears in a space within 5 feet of you, and the other portal appears in an unoccupied space you can see up to 30 feet away. These portals last until the start of your next turn, and they are large enough to accommodate Medium and smaller creatures and objects. Portals take the appearance of an elongated, shimmering {@item Mirror|sw5e-phb|mirror}, and looking through a portal, a creature can see through the linked portal as if looking through a window. A creature or object who passes through a portal immediately appears in a space within 5 feet of the linked portal. You can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to end your portals early. If a creature is partially within your portals, it is shunted back to the space it previously occupied and it must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your a tech save DC. On a failed save, it takes energy damage equal to your scout level + your Intelligence modifier. You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. At the beginning of each of your turns while you have a pair of portals active, you can expend a use of this feature to extend the duration of the portals until the start of your next turn (no action required). The distance at which you can create portals increases at higher levels. It increases to 60 feet at 5th level, 90 feet at 9th level, 150 feet at 13th level, 300 feet at 17th level, and 1,000 feet at 20th level.

entries.name: Mark of the Teleporter
entries: {@i {@b Teleportation Technique:} 3rd level} On your turn, when you deal damage to the target of your Ranger's Quarry, and either you, your weapon, or the source of your damage have passed through your portals on this turn, when you roll below half the maximum on a damage die, you can treat the roll as if you'd rolled half the maximum on the damage die. You can only affect a number of dice up to half your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one) in this way.

entries.name: Residual Warp
entries: {@i {@b Teleportation Technique:} 7th level} When you use your Personal Teleporter feature, you can place your portal in a place you've visited in the last 10 minutes, provided you can remember it, as opposed to a place you can see. That place must still be within range of your teleporter.

entries.name: Quantum Entanglement
entries: {@i {@b Teleportation Technique:} 11th level} When you use your Personal Teleporter feature, you can place the portal that you would normally place within 5 feet of you in a place you can see within your Personal Teleporter's range. If that space is occupied by a Huge or smaller creature or a Medium or smaller unsecured object, it must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC. An object automatically fails this {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and a creature can choose to fail. On a failed save, a Medium or smaller creature or object falls through the portal, immediately appearing in a space within 5 feet of the linked portal and falling {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}. A Large or Huge creature instead falls {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone} without moving.

entries.name: Reprisal
entries: {@i {@b Teleportation Technique:} 15th level} When you would be affected by a weapon or {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} that requires a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} and would affect only you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to instantaneously create a pair of portals to redirect that power to another target within 30 feet. If the weapon or power required a melee or ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, make a melee or ranged tech {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against the new target, as appropriate. If it required a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, the new target must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Triage Technique
entries: With every conflict comes death and destruction. Followers of the Triage Technique excel at keeping their comrades in the fight with quick thinking and fast-acting medicine.

entries.name: Triage Training
entries: {@i {@b Triage Technique:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency in the {@skill Medicine|sw5e-phb} skill.

Additionally, when you would use your action to make an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} to stabilize a creature, expend a use of a {@item Traumakit|sw5e-phb|traumakit}, or use a {@item Medpac|sw5e-phb|medpac}, you can instead use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Mark of Triage
entries: {@i {@b Triage Technique:} 3rd level} You learn new ways to use your Ranger's Quarry.

items: While a hostile creature is the target of your Ranger's Quarry, you always know any conditions it is suffering from, and you know at roughly what percentage its current {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} is relative to its maximum. Additionally, if the target is within 60 feet of you, when it is forced to make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to force it to make the roll with {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}. Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

While a friendly creature is the target of your Ranger's Quarry, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Medicine|sw5e-phb}) checks made to stabilize it. Additionally, if the target is within 60 feet of you, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} and roll your Ranger's Quarry and either restore {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to the amount rolled, or grant temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to the amount rolled. Once a friendly creature has benefited from this ability, they can not do so again until they complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Double Dose
entries: {@i {@b Triage Technique:} 7th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level} Your application of medicine does not interfere with your own ability to recover from injuries. When you restore {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} or grant temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} to another creature with a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} or class feature, you recover the same amount of {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} or gain the same number of temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}.
You can use this feature three times. You gain an additional use at 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Experimental Infusion
entries: {@i {@b Triage Technique:} 11th level} When you target a creature with your Ranger's Quarry, you can grant one of the following additional effects of your choice:

items: {@b {@i Adrenaline/Tranquilizer.}} The creature's movement {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is doubled until the end of its next turn. Alternatively, it gains a level of {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} until the end of its next turn.

{@b {@i Focus/Dizziness.}} The creature has either {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} or {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} (your choice) on the first {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} it makes within the next minute.

{@b {@i Toughen/Weaken.}} The creature gains temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to your scout level, which last for 1 minute. Alternatively, the creature must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC. On a failure, it takes psychic damage equal to your scout level and it can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} until the start of your next turn.

entries: You can use each feature once. You regain any expended uses when you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Cure-All
entries: {@i {@b Triage Technique:} 15th level} Your healing becomes even more potent. When you restore {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} or grant temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} to a creature as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} using your Mark of Triage feature, you can also end one of the following conditions afflicting it: {@condition Blinded|sw5e-phb|blinded}, {@condition Deafened|sw5e-phb|deafened}, {@condition Diseased|sw5e-phb|diseased}, {@condition Paralyzed|sw5e-phb|paralyzed}, or {@condition Poisoned|sw5e-phb|poisoned}.

entries.name: Path of Aggression
entries: From the murky depths of the dark side comes seething fury. Those sentinels who follow the Path of Aggression charge their weapon with lightning, culminating in a massive discharge that can ravage their opponents.

entries.name: Voltaic Slash
entries: {@i {@b Path of Aggression:} 3rd level} Starting when you choose this calling at 3rd level, you learn the {@i lightning charge} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, which does not count against your total powers known. Additionally, you can use Wisdom or Charisma as your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} for it, and when you deal lightning damage with the {@i lightning charge} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, you deal additional lightning damage equal to half your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one) if it doesn't already include that modifier.

entries.name: Thunderous Momentum
entries: {@i {@b Path of Aggression:} 3rd level} Your stride becomes nigh unbreakable. You are immune to the {@condition Shocked|sw5e-phb|shocked} condition, and each {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level only reduces your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} by 5 feet, unless it would reduce your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} to 0.

entries.name: Entropic Rush
entries: {@i {@b Path of Aggression:} 7th level} You've learned to move with {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} and precision, discharging your lightning in a massive burst. When you move at least half your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} before casting {@i lightning charge}, you make the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}. Additionally, on a hit, the lightning can leap a second time, to a third creature within range or back to the first creature.

entries.name: Living Current
entries: {@i {@b Path of Aggression:} 13th level} You've learned to channel the damage done to you to enhance your strikes. The first time you deal damage on your turn, if you took damage since the start of your last turn, you can deal additional lightning damage equal to your Kinetic Combat die + half the amount of damage taken.
You can use this feature five times. You gain an additional use at 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Retaliatory Strike
entries: {@i {@b Path of Aggression:} 18th level} When a creature hits you with an attack while within 5 feet of you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to cast the {@i lightning charge} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, targeting them.

entries.name: Path of Communion
entries: Those who master the Force can transcend death, persisting beyond their natural experation. Those sentinels who follow the Path of Communion bond with a Force ghost, developing a symbiotic relationship which alters the way they perceive their surroundings.

entries.name: Mystical Connection
entries: {@i {@b Path of Communion:} 3rd level} You learn the {@i feedback} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, which does not count against your total powers known. Additionally, you can use Wisdom or Charisma as your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} for it, and you can use the Double Strike Force-Empowered Self option when you cast it as your action and the target fails its {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. Finally, when you deal psychic damage with the {@i feedback} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, you deal additional psychic damage equal to your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one) if it doesn't already include that modifier.

entries.name: Symbiot Spirit
entries: {@i {@b Path of Communion:} 3rd, 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level} You attract the attention of the spirit of a Force ghost. Over the course of one hour, you can attune to the spirit, forging a lasting connection. While attuned to a spirit, you gain the following benefits:

items: Your spirit is always audible and visible to you. Your spirit can choose to make itself audible and visible or inaudible and {@condition Invisible|sw5e-phb|invisible} to other creatures (no action required), but it is always visible to beings with {@sense Truesight|sw5e-phb|truesight}.
Your spirit can not interact with the corporeal world, but it is also not impeded by unenhanced walls or barriers.

Your spirit acts independently of you, and it only obeys your commands if it chooses to. In combat, it rolls its own {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} and acts on its own turn. Your spirit can't attack, but it can take other actions as normal.

While your spirit is within 100 feet of you, you can telepathically communicate with it. Additionally, as an action, you can see through your spirit's vision and hear what it hears until the start of your next turn. During this time, you are deaf and blind with regard to your own senses.

When you cast a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} with a range of touch, your spirit can deliver the power as if it had cast it. Your spirit must be within 100 feet of you, and it must use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to deliver the power when you cast it. If the power requires an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, you use your attack modifier for the roll.

entries: You can only attune to one spirit at a time. If you attempt to attune to another spirit, you immediately break the bond with your current spirit.

entries.name: Generating
entries: Your Spirit

Your spirit might be the ghost of a benevolent Jedi, discovered in the ruins of a Jedi temple, or a powerful Sith spirit lingering in an ancient artifact. It might be the spirit of a Nightsister sorceress, or a paragon of a long-forgotten monastic order. Work with your GM to determine the nature of your spirit.

Additionally, your spirit can briefly interact with the physical world. When you would make a melee attack, your spirit can deliver the attack as if it had made it. Your spirit must be within 100 feet of you, and it must use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to deliver the attack. It uses your modifiers for the attack and damage rolls. You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Invasive Presence
entries: {@i {@b Path of Communion:} 7th level} Your spirit can invade another creature's being. As an action, your spirit can touch a creature within 5 feet of it, forcing it to make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your universal force save DC. If you or creatures that are friendly to you are fighting it, it has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

On a failed save, your spirit moves into that creatures space, inhabiting its body, for 1 minute. The affected creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the first {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} it makes each turn. At the end of each its turns, the creature repeats this save. On a success, it repels the spirit from its body, and it becomes immune to this feature for 24 hours.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Ethereal Vision
entries: {@i {@b Path of Communion:} 13th level} You and your guiding spirit both gain {@sense Truesight|sw5e-phb|truesight} out to 60 feet as long as your spirit is within 100 feet of you.

Additionally, when you use your action to see through your spirit's senses, you are no longer deaf and blind with regard to your own senses, able to comprehend what happens in both perspectives simultaneously.

entries.name: Assuming Direct Control
entries: {@i {@b Path of Communion:} 18th level} When a creature fails its {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your Invasive Presence feature, the target becomes {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} by you for as long as Invasive Presence is active.

While the target is {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed}, you and your spirit have a telepathic link with it as long as you are within 100 feet of it. You and your spirit can use this telepathic link to issue commands to the creature while you are conscious (no action required), which it does its best to obey. You can specify a simple and general course of action, such as "Attack that creature," "Run over there," or "Fetch that object." If the creature completes the order and doesn't receive further direction from you, it defends and preserves itself to the best of its ability.

You can use your action to take total and precise control of the target. Until the end of your next turn, the creature takes only the actions you choose, and doesn't do anything that you don't allow it to do. During this time you can also cause the creature to use a {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}, but this requires you to use your own {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} as well.

entries.name: Path of Ethereality
entries: In the distant reaches of the galaxy obscure knowledge and forgotten secrets of the Force can sometimes be found. While other Force-sensitive may find themselves touched by this secret knowledge of the Force, those sentinels who follow the Path of Ethereality instead find themselves grabbed. Held onto by mysterious aspects of the Force that refuse to let go, these sentinels find themselves able to manipulate the universe around them.

entries.name: Aberrant Resilience
entries: {@i {@b Path of Ethereality:} 3rd level} You learn the {@i resistance} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, which does not count against your total powers known. Additionally, this power no longer requires {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} for you when you target yourself with it.

entries.name: Force-Empowered Kinesis
entries: {@i {@b Path of Ethereality:} 3rd level} Your connection to the Force allows you to briefly become incorporeal. When you use a Force-Empowered Self option, until the end of your turn, you can move through other creatures and objects as if they are {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain}. If you end this movement inside a solid object or creature, you are immediately shunted to the nearest unoccupied space that you can occupy and take true damage equal to twice the number of feet you are moved.

entries.name: Out of Touch
entries: {@i {@b Path of Ethereality:} 7th level} As an action, you can step out of sync with the rest of the universe for 1 minute. At the start of each of your turns, roll a {@dice d20}. If you roll 11 or higher, you and everything your are wearing or carrying are completely {@condition Invisible|sw5e-phb|invisible} to all beings, except for those with {@sense Truesight|sw5e-phb|truesight}. On a roll of 10 or lower, you instead appear as an indistinguishably blurred form roughly your normal height and weight, though a being with {@sense Truesight|sw5e-phb|truesight} sees you normally. Regardless of your appearance, for the duration, your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} doubles, you gain a flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}, and you can move through creatures and objects willingly though you can not affect them and they can not affect you. You can end this feature early on your turn (no action required). When this effect ends, if you are inside a solid object or creature, you are immediately shunted to the nearest unoccupied space that you can occupy and take force damage equal to twice the number of feet you are moved.

This effect ends early if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die. Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Event Cascade
entries: {@i {@b Path of Ethereality:} 13th level} You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} you make against creatures if you haven't dealt damage to them or affected them with a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} since the start of your previous turn.

entries.name: Aberrant Self
entries: {@i {@b Path of Ethereality:} 18th level} You no longer suffer the frailty of old age, and you can't be aged abnormally. You can still die of old age, however. Additionally, you no longer need food or water, and you no longer need to sleep. Lastly, the first time you take damage on each of your turns, you can roll your Kinetic Combat die and reduce the damage by that amount.

entries.name: Path of Iron
entries: Many sentinels choose to focus on a discipline that demands physical strength, reflexes, and fortitude. Those sentinels who follow the Path of Iron train their bodies to their physical peak, able to withstand nigh intolerable punishment and bolster their physical combat capabilities.

entries.name: Form Combat Training
entries: {@i {@b Path of Iron:} 3rd level} You learn one {@book lightsaber form|sw5e-phb|6|Lightsaber Forms}, as detailed in the Customization Options document for Expanded Content.
Additionally, you gain proficiency in all martial light- and vibro- weapons.

entries.name: Physical Conditioning
entries: {@i {@b Path of Iron:} 3rd level} You've undergone special training, increasing your physical capabilities. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in {@filter medium armor|items|type=medium armor}. If you are already proficient in {@filter medium armor|items|type=medium armor}, you then gain proficiency in {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor}. While you are wearing light or {@filter medium armor|items|type=medium armor}, you can use your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice) instead of your Dexterity modifier when determining your AC.
Your hit point maximum increases by 3, and it increases by 1 again whenever you gain a level in this class.

entries.name: Enhanced Force-Empowered Self
entries: {@i {@b Path of Iron:} 7th level} Through intense physical training, you've improved your body's ability to access and channel the force flowing within you.
When you would use a Force-Empowered Self option, you can choose to bolster the option, gaining an additional effect as listed below. You can only bolster a Force-Empowered Self option once per turn.

You can use these features a combined three times. You gain an additional use at 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain any expended uses when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
While you have no remaining uses of this feature, you can instead expend 1 force point to use it.

entries.name: Aegis
entries: When you bolster Deflection, when an attack would hit you before the start of your next turn, you subtract the same value rolled for Deflection from the damage taken.

entries.name: Cleave
entries: When you bolster Double Strike, you choose another creature within 5 feet of your target. They take damage of the same type equal to the result of the die rolled for Double Strike.

entries.name: Momentum
entries: When you bolster Slow Time, until the end of your turn you ignore {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain}, and can move along vertical surfaces and across liquids without falling during the move.

entries.name: Follow Through
entries: {@i {@b Path of Iron:} 13th level} When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn, you can spend 2 force points and forgo one of your attacks to cast an at-will {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} which requires you to make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}.

entries.name: Kinetic Mastery
entries: {@i {@b Path of Iron:} 18th level} Choose a {@book lightsaber form|sw5e-phb|6|Lightsaber Forms} you know. Once on each of your turns, you can use the chosen form without using your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.
You can do so six times. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
While you have no remaining uses of this feature, you can instead expend 1 force point to use it.

entries.name: Path of Meditation
entries: Throughout the Force, there is both symphonic harmony, and discordant chaos. Those sentinels who follow the Path of Meditation embody these concepts, empowering their allies and hindering their enemies through the use of the ancient {@spell Force Technique|sw5e-phb|Force technique} of {@spell Battle Meditation|sw5e-phb|battle meditation}.

entries.name: Sage Counsel
entries: {@i {@b Path of Meditation:} 3rd level} You learn the {@i guidance} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, which does not count against your total powers known. Additionally, this power's die increases by one step (from {@dice d4} to {@dice d6}, {@dice d6} to {@dice d8}, {@dice d8} to {@dice d10}, or {@dice d10} to {@dice d12}).

entries.name: Force-Empowered Allies
entries: {@i {@b Path of Meditation:} 3rd level} While you are concentrating on a power that benefits a friendly creature other than you, you gain new ways to utilize your Force-Empowered Self features. Each option costs 1 force point, and you can only target a creature that is benefiting from a power you cast.

entries.name: Deflection
entries: When an ally is hit with an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and roll a Kinetic Combat die to add it to your ally's AC, potentially causing the attack to miss.

entries.name: Double Strike
entries: When an ally hits with an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and roll a Kinetic Combat die to deal additional damage of the same type as the attack.

entries.name: Slow Time
entries: When an ally moves on their turn, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and roll a Kinetic Combat die to increase their {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} by 5 x the amount rolled until the end of the turn.

entries.name: Unbreakable Focus
entries: {@i {@b Path of Meditation:} 7th level} Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can cast the {@i battle meditation} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} at its base level without expending force points. While concentrating on {@i battle meditation}, at the start of each of your turns, the power's die increases by one step (from {@dice d4} to {@dice d6}, {@dice d6} to {@dice d8}, {@dice d8} to {@dice d10}, or {@dice d10} to {@dice d12}).

Additionally, whenever you make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} on a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, you can treat a {@dice d20} roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

entries.name: Turbulent Presence
entries: {@i {@b Path of Meditation:} 13th level} Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can cast the {@i improved battle meditation} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} at its base level without expending force points. While concentrating on {@i improved battle meditation}, at the start of each of your turns, the power's die increases by one step (from {@dice d6} to {@dice d8}, {@dice d8} to {@dice d10}, or {@dice d10} to {@dice d12}).

Additionally, once per round, when a creature rolls a bonus or penalty die from an effect you control, you can have them roll the die with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} or {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} (your choice).

entries.name: Legendary Battle Meditation
entries: {@i {@b Path of Meditation:} 18th level} Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can cast the {@i master battle meditation} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} without expending force points. While concentrating on {@i master battle meditation}, at the start of each of your turns, the power's die increases by one step (from {@dice d8} to {@dice d10}, or {@dice d10} to {@dice d12}).

Additionally, you gain a second {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} each round that you can only use for your Force-Empowered Allies feature. You can only take one {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} per turn.

entries.name: Path of Synthesis
entries: There is power in diversity unknown to those of narrow mind. Those sentinels who follow the Path of Synthesis blend their intricate mastery of the Force with their understanding of technology, creating unique effects to overcome their obstacles.

entries.name: Techcasting Secrets
entries: {@i {@b Path of Synthesis:} 3rd level} You have learned to intersperse your training with an aptitude for technology. Choose two {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of 1st level or lower. The chosen powers count as universal {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} for you, but are not included in the number in the Powers Known column of the sentinel table.

At 7th level, you learn two {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of 2nd level or lower. At 13th level, you learn two {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of 3rd level or lower. At 17th level, you learn two {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of 4th level or lower. Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you know and replace it with another {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of no higher than the level determined by this feature.

entries.name: Synthetic Understanding
entries: {@i {@b Path of Synthesis:} 3rd level} You've applied your newfound knowledge to broader pursuits. You gain proficiency in {@skill Technology|sw5e-phb} or one tool of your choice.

Additionally, when you make an Intelligence ({@skill Technology|sw5e-phb}) check, or a check with a tool, you may use your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice) instead of your Intelligence modifier.
Finally, when you deal damage with a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} or your Double Strike Force Empowered Self option, you can choose to substitute the damage dealt as ion.

entries.name: Force-Empowered Tech
entries: {@i {@b Path of Synthesis:} 7th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level} You learn to fully blend your technological aptitude with your use of the Force. You have three such effects: Disruption Pulse, Force Override, and {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}. When you use your Force-Empowered Tech, you choose which effect to create.
You can use this feature three times. You gain an additional use at 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Disruption Pulse
entries: As an action, you can send out a 30 foot cone of electromagnetically-charged energy to overload enemy weapons. Each creature within the cone that is wearing or carrying a weapon with electric components must make an Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. If the weapon is being worn, this save is made with {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}. On a failed save, the first attack they attempt to make with that weapon has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}. A creature with multiple weapons must make a separate save for each weapon.

entries.name: Forced Override
entries: When you cast a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} that requires a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the save (no action required).

entries.name: Techcasting Insight
entries: As an action, you can attempt to determine another creature's experience with {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting}. When you do so, you make an Intelligence ({@skill Technology|sw5e-phb}) check contested by the target's Intelligence ({@skill Technology|sw5e-phb}) check. If you succeed, you immediately learn the target's {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} Max Power Level, as well as any {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} currently affecting the target.

entries.name: Improved Force-Empowered Tech
entries: {@i {@b Path of Synthesis:} 13th level} You've gained access to two additional Force-Empowered Tech effects: Harmonic Synthesis and Conservation of Energy.

entries.name: Harmonic Synthesis
entries: When you use your action to cast a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to gain resistance to damage dealt by {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} until the start of your next turn. If you use your action to cast a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, you can instead gain resistance to damage dealt by {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

entries.name: Conservation of Energy
entries: When you reduce a hostile creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} with a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, you can reduce the force point cost of the {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} to 0 (no action required).

entries.name: Reflective Shield
entries: {@i {@b Path of Synthesis:} 18th level} When you use your Force-Empowered Tech features, a barrier for energy shimmers into existence, surrounding you until the end of your next turn. When you take damage, you can mitigate the incoming energy and potentially reflect it back at your attacker. You use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to have resistance against the triggering damage, and if the source of the damage is within 5 feet of you, they take half of the total damage dealt as ion.

entries.name: Path of Tenacity
