entries: The tenacious are ever mindful that the Force ebbs and flows, and uses this knowledge to great {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}. Those sentinels who follow the Path of {@optfeature Tenacity|sw5e-phb} use their connection to the Force to draw the opposition's attention while also warding off their attacks, serving as an effective bulwark against even the most implacable of foes.

entries.name: Protector
entries: {@i {@b Path of Tenacity:} 3rd level} You learn the {@i saber ward} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, which does not count against your total powers known. Additionally, when you cast it, you can spend 2 force points to extend the benefits to creatures of your choice within 5 feet of you while the power is active. The creatures immediately lose this benefit if they move more than 5 feet away from you.

entries.name: Kinetic Ward
entries: {@i {@b Path of Tenacity:} 3rd level} You can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to deflect a strike when you are dealt damage by a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}. When you do so, the damage you take from the attack is reduced by 1d10 + your Dexterity modifier + your sentinel level. If you reduce the damage to 0, you can redirect it at another target if you have a weapon capable of doing so. You can spend 1 force point to make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} at a target within 5 feet of you with the weapon, as part of the same {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}. You make this attack with proficiency, regardless of your weapon proficiencies, and if the attack hits it uses your Kinetic Combat die for its damage roll. If {@i saber ward} is active, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}.

entries.name: Kinetic Bulwark
entries: {@i {@b Path of Tenacity:} 7th level} You can extend your Kinetic Ward to a creature within 5 feet of you when they are hit by a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}. If this damage is not reduced to 0, the warded creature takes any remaining damage.

entries.name: Indomitable
entries: {@i {@b Path of Tenacity:} 13th level} The Force flowing through you makes it harder for movement to be forced upon you. You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid being {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} or moved. If you fail the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, you can spend 1 force point to reroll one of the dice once. You must use the new roll.
Additionally, if allies within 5 feet of you are gaining the benefit of your {@i saber ward} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, they also gain the benefit of this feature.

entries.name: Kinetic Bastion
entries: {@i {@b Path of Tenacity:} 18th level} You can protect allies even further from you. When a creature within 30 feet of you is hit by a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to teleport to them and extend your Kinetic Ward. If this damage is not reduced to 0, the warded creature takes any remaining damage.
You can use this feature six times. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Path of Witchcraft
entries: The Force connects all living things. Those sentinels who follow the Path of Witchcraft use that connection to summon the aid of nature, both spirits and the elements, adapting them to their will.

entries.name: Wild Power
entries: {@i {@b Path of Witchcraft:} 3rd level} You learn the {@i enfeeble} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, which does not count against your total powers known. Additionally, you can use Wisdom or Charisma as your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} for it, and you can use the Double Strike Force-Empowered Self option when you cast it as your action and the target fails its save. Finally, you add your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one) to damage rolls with it.

entries.name: Ichor Conjuring
entries: {@i {@b Path of Witchcraft:} 3rd and 11th level} You learn to call on the spirits of beasts and grant them ichorous form. Once on each of your turns, when you cast a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} and deal necrotic damage to a creature, you can conjure a familiar within 5 feet of it (no action required). The familiar takes the form of a humanoid or beast made of green, glowing smoke, and it lasts for 1 minute, until you dismiss it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, until you manifest another spirit, or until you're {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die.

Your familiar has an AC equal to your universal force save DC, 1 hit point, and immunity to all conditions. If it has to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, it uses your {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} bonus for the roll. It is the same size as you regardless of its appearance, and it occupies its own space. On your turn, you can mentally command the familiar to move up to 30 feet in any direction (no action required). If your familiar is ever more than 30 feet from you at the end of your turn, it is destroyed. While you have a familiar, you gain the following benefits:

items: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can use your magicks to teleport, swapping places with your familiar at a cost of 15 feet of your movement, regardless of the distance between the two of you.
When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn, any attack you make with that action can originate from your space or the familiar's space. You make this choice for each attack.

When a creature that you can see within 5 feet of your familiar moves at least 5 feet away from it, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make an {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attack} against that creature as if you were in the familiar's space.

entries: Starting at 11th level, you can summon your familiar when you deal damage with any {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, instead of just necrotic. Additionally, you can summon your familiar when you use a Force-Empowered Self option on your turn.

entries.name: Nature's Vigor
entries: {@i {@b Path of Witchcraft:} 7th level} You've learned to attune your senses with nature. If you spend at least 1 minute meditating while in nature, you gain the following benefits for 1 hour:

items: You ignore {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain} caused by nature.
You can understand plants within 30 feet of you. They can telepathically communicate simple ideas to you, including memories from within the past day.
You can command plants within 30 feet of you to create {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain}, or other tasks at the GM's discretion (no action required).

entries: Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Waters of Life
entries: {@i {@b Path of Witchcraft:} 13th and 17th level} You've learned to absorb the fleeting magicks of your familiar. When your familiar is destroyed by taking damage, you can choose to grant temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to 2d8 + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice) to one friendly creature of your choice you can see within 30 feet.
You can use this feature five times. You gain an additional use at 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Stormcaller
entries: {@i {@b Path of Witchcraft:} 18th level} You've learned to command the elements to summon a fierce storm in a 30-foot radius around you. As an action, you can gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: You gain a flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}.
You have resistance to energy, lightning, and necrotic damage.
Whenever a hostile creature enters this radius for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it takes 10 lightning damage.

entries: This effect ends early if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die. Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Path of Witchcraft (Companion)
entries: The Force connects all living things. Those sentinels who follow the Path of Witchcraft use that connection to summon the aid of nature, both beasts and the elements, adapting them to their will.

entries.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: {@i {@b Path of Witchcraft:} 3rd level} You gain proficiency in {@skill Animal Handling|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Wild Power
entries: {@i {@b Path of Witchcraft:} 3rd level} You learn the {@i enfeeble} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, which does not count against your total powers known. Additionally, you can use Wisdom or Charisma as your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} for it, and you can use the Double Strike Force-Empowered Self option when you cast it as your action and the target fails its save. Finally, you add your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one) to damage rolls with it.

entries.name: Beast Companion
entries: {@i {@b Path of Witchcraft:} 3rd, 11th, and 17th level} You learn to create a powerful bond through the Force with your own  beast companion.
Create your beast companion as detailed in the Companions section of the Customization Options document for Expanded Content.
In addition to its traits and features, your beast companion gains an additional benefit while it is bonded to you:

items: Your beast gains two additional traits. It gains one more additional trait when you reach 11th level in this class. For each beast trait in excess of your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, your force point maximum is reduced by 2.

entries: Lastly, while bonded and within 10 feet of you, your beast companion gains the following benefits:

items: When you use a Force-Empowered Self option to increase your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} or {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb|armor class}, you can instead grant this bonus to your beast companion.
You and your beast companion can communicate telepathically, though your beast companion can only communicate in and understand simple concepts.

entries: This radius increases to 30 feet at 11th level, and 60 feet at 17th level.

entries.name: Nature's Vigor
entries: {@i {@b Path of Witchcraft:} 7th level} You've learned to attune your senses with nature. If you spend at least 1 minute meditating while in nature, you gain the following benefits for 1 hour:

items: You ignore {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain} caused by nature.
You can understand plants within 30 feet of you. They can telepathically communicate simple ideas to you, including memories from within the past day.
You can command plants within 30 feet of you to create {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain}, or other tasks at the GM's discretion (no action required).

entries: Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Beastwarden
entries: {@i {@b Path of Witchcraft:} 13th and 17th level} Your bond with your beast companion strengthens, granting the following benefits while your beast companion is within 30 feet of you:

items: When you cast a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} that targets only yourself, and your beast companion is within range, you can also target your beast companion with that power.

If you or your beast have {@sense Darkvision|sw5e-phb|darkvision} and the other doesn't, the other gains it with the same radius. If you both have {@sense Darkvision|sw5e-phb|darkvision}, you both use the larger radius of the two, which then increases by 30 feet.

If you or your beast have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@skill Perception|sw5e-phb} checks and the other doesn't, the other gains {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@skill Perception|sw5e-phb} checks. If you both have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@skill Perception|sw5e-phb} checks, when either of you makes a {@skill Perception|sw5e-phb} check with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}, you can reroll one of the dice once.

entries: This radius increases to 60 feet at 17th level.

entries.name: Stormcaller
entries: {@i {@b Path of Witchcraft:} 18th level} You've learned to command the elements to summon a fierce storm in a 30-foot radius around you. As an action, you can gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: You gain a flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}.
You have resistance to energy, lightning, and necrotic damage.
Whenever a hostile creature enters this radius for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it takes 10 lightning damage.

entries: This effect ends early if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die. Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Addict
entries: You hammer down your fifth {@item Bottle|sw5e-phb|bottle} of the night, do your last bit of snuff, and bid farewell to the seedy cantina barman. You stagger onto the streets and find a nearby alley in which you empty the night's contents. To many, the next morning's hangovers would be hell. To you, they're a ritual.

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Performance|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}, and Sleight of Hand
{@b Tool Proficiencies:} Your choice of any gaming set, brewer's kit, or spicer's kit

{@b Equipment:} A chance cube set, a sabaac deck, 2 days field rations, a flask or belt pouch containing your addiction, a set of common clothes, a {@item Bedroll|sw5e-phb|bedroll}, and a belt pouch containing 25 cr

entries.name: Pick Your Poison
entries: While most addicts are willing to try everything once, they typically have a drug of choice. You can determine what the source of your addiction or determine it randomly below.

entries.name: Feature: Addicted
entries: You've been abusing substances for a long time. You always know who to talk to and where to find substances, and you can often identify them in their raw form.

entries.name: Background Feat
entries: As a further embodiment of the experience and training of your background, you can choose from the following feats:

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Addicts can be rude and uncouth, wearing their addiction visibly, or they might hide that addiction and appear to function normally. Importantly, and varying with every addict, why are you addicted? To forget the past? To drown your sorrows? Or are you simply chasing the dragon?

rows: I am guaranteed to fight someone if I'm drunk/high enough.
Life is pain. All I want is to drink/smoke myself into nothingness.
I have a simple rule; life's a party, so grab the deathsticks!
The only thing keeping me from burning down this village is the fact that you make some damn good spice.
I'm quite reserved until the moment I fulfill my addictive needs.
This stuff is a bit weak, do you have anything higher than 60% in the back?
I take pride in my addiction and am often snobbish when talking about it.
I blow up at the slightest insult.
{@b Hope.} I hope to one day be free of my addiction. (Light)
{@b Carelessness.} I don't care what I have to do, just let me feed my addiction. (Dark)
{@b Isolation.} Just let me deal with my demons in peace. (Neutral)
{@b Caution.} I will never let my addiction harm others. (Lawful)
{@b Comradery.} Hey, some of my favorite people are addicts! (Any)
I use my addiction as a tool to wash away my past sins.
My family never wanted to be forgotten. I take drugs in the hopes they will be.
I hope to start a drug business myself and give people the same happiness I've found.
Everything I do is in the hopes of getting my hands on my drug.
I traded my former self to my addiction. Now I need to find a way to get him back.
To be addicted is to be truly alive.
This could be rough, let's take something before we go.
Hopefully this will be the one to end it.
The mission can wait, we should find some dealers first.
What? I don't have a problem. You're the one with the problem!
It looks like my drug, so it should be safe to take right?
I'm never myself when I'm on it.

entries.name: Amnesiac
entries: One day you awoke, perhaps in a forest or on a sandy beach, with no recollection of what happened to you. How did you get here? Who were you? These questions elude and boggle your mind. Some people wish for a fresh start, but you never even got a choice.

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Survival|sw5e-phb}
{@b Tool Proficiencies:} Choose one from {@item Disguise kit|sw5e-phb|disguise kit}, {@item Forgery kit|sw5e-phb|forgery kit}, or {@item Tinker's implements|sw5e-phb|tinker's implements}
{@b Equipment:} A set of common clothes, a relic of your past which you do not remember, and a belt pouch containing 200 cr

entries.name: Variant: Randomized Proficiencies
entries: Rather than taking the proficiencies provided by this background, you can choose to take no proficiencies, instead waiting to gain a proficiency during a story moment. When you do so, you must succeed on a DC 15 check. You add your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} to this check, but no additional modifiers. On a success, you gain the chosen skill, tool, or language proficiency. On a failure, you do not gain a proficiency, and you can't attempt again for 24 hours. You can gain no more than two skill proficiencies and two tool or language proficiencies in this way.

entries.name: Feature: A Life Once Lived
entries: You once had a home, a family, relationships, possessions, but now you are left with nothing but the ability to start anew. You are unfamiliar with the world around you as well as the people in it. You may often need to ask for clarification on things other adventurers may know intrinsically. Some events, locations, names, phrases, or objects may also trigger you to recall small details which could relate to the life you once had, at the discretion of the GM.

entries.name: Background Feat
entries: As a further embodiment of the experience and training of your background, you can choose from the following feats:

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: The important things to consider when choosing this background are how your character has dealt with starting life anew and what have they done to set down that path.

rows: I don't know who you are but I'll try to help you.
I will let nothing stop my quest for answers.
Even if I never find out who I was before, I will know who I am now.
I am sometimes clumsy when speaking. I must've not been very eloquent.
I shy away from forging new relationships. I don't want to leave anyone behind again.
Having no memories of the past has left me feeling free and happy.
I am eager to learn and devour any knowledge I can.
I am insightful and can often see things from other peoples point of view.
{@b Conscience.} I've forgotten before, I can forget again.  I don't let my conscience get in the way of my actions. (Lawful)
{@b Freedom.} With no past to tie me down I do was I will. (Chaotic)
{@b Respect.} People deserve to be treated with respect. (Light)
{@b Past.} I will destroy whatever I have to in order to reclaim what I once had. (Dark)
{@b Live and Let Live.} Ideals aren't worth killing over or going to war for. (Neutral)
{@b Memory.} Finding out my history drives every action I do. (Any)
I will never rest until I find out what happened to me.
I have a family out there who's looking for me. I can't let them down.
I was given a chance to start fresh, and I'm not taking it for granted.
My entire life was lost in the blink of an eye. What's the point of all this?
I've already lost everything. Now I do as I please.
I will become something great so that even if I forget, others won't.
I've lost all hope since I woke up.
I'm obsessed with the life I left behind.
Sometimes I crack under the stress of starting new.
I get tunnel vision when investigating my past life.
I no longer care about anything. It could all be gone in an instant.
I am constantly angry about forgetting everything.

entries.name: Archaeologist
entries: An archaeologist learns about the long-lost and fallen cultures of the past by studying their remains — their bones, their ruins, their surviving masterworks, and their tombs. Those who practice archaeology travel to the far corners of the world to root through crumbled cities and lost dungeons, digging in search of artifacts that might tell the stories of monarchs and high priests, wars and cataclysms.

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Lore|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}, or {@skill Survival|sw5e-phb}
{@b Tool Proficiencies:} Surveyor's implements or scavenging kit

{@b Equipment:} A case containing a physical or digital map to a ruin or dungeon, a lantern, a vibropick, a set of traveler's clothes, a {@item Shovel|sw5e-phb|shovel}, a two-person tent, a trinket recovered from a dig site, and a pouch containing 250 cr

entries.name: Dust Digger
entries: Prior to becoming an adventurer, you spent most of your young life crawling around in the dust, pilfering relics of questionable value from crypts and ruins. Though you managed to sell a few of your discoveries and earn enough credits to buy proper adventuring gear, you have held onto an item that has great emotional value to you. You can determine your signature item or determine it randomly below.

entries.name: Feature: Historical Knowledge
entries: When you enter a ruin or dungeon, you can correctly ascertain its original purpose and determine its builders, whether those were jedi, sith, hutts, rakata, or some other known species or civilization. Additionally, you can readily determine the value of ancient art.

entries.name: Background Feat
entries: As a further embodiment of the experience and training of your background, you can choose from the following feats:

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Few archaeologists can resist the lure of an unexplored ruin or dungeon, particularly if such a site is the source of legends or is rumored to contain noteworthy relics. Whatever their motivations, they combine the likes of a dutiful historian with those of a dogged scoundrel.

rows: I love a good puzzle or mystery.
I'm a pack rat who never throws anything away.
Fame is more important to me than money.
I have no qualms about stealing from the dead.
I'm happier in a dusty old tomb than I am in the centers of civilization.
Traps don't make me nervous. Idiots who trigger traps make me nervous.
I might fail, but I will never give up.
You might think I'm a scholar, but I love a good brawl. These fists were made for punching.
{@b Preservation.} That artifact belongs in a museum. (Light)
{@b Greed.} I won't risk my life for nothing. I expect some kind of payment. (Any)
{@b Death Wish.} Nothing is more exhilarating than a narrow escape from the jaws of death. (Chaotic)
{@b Dignity.} The dead and their belongings deserve to be treated with respect. (Lawful)
{@b Immortality.} All my exploring is part of a plan to find the secret of everlasting life. (Any)
{@b Danger.} With every great discovery comes grave danger. The two walk hand in hand. (Any)
Ever since I was a child, I've heard stories about a lost city. I aim to find it, learn its secrets, and earn my place in the history books.
I want to find my mentor, who disappeared on an expedition some time ago.
I have a friendly rival. Only one of us can be the best, and I aim to prove it's me.
I won't sell an art object or other treasure that has historical significance or is one of a kind.
I'm secretly in love with the wealthy patron who sponsors my archaeological exploits.
I hope to bring prestige to an library, a museum, or a university.
I have a secret fear of some common wild animal, and in my work, I see them everywhere.
I can't leave a room without searching it for secret doors.
When I'm not exploring dungeons or ruins, I get jittery and impatient.
I have no time for friends or family. I spend every waking moment thinking about and preparing for my next expedition.
When given the choice of going left or right, I always go left.
I can't sleep except in total darkness.

entries.name: Barbarian
entries: Though you might have only recently arrived in civilized lands, you are no stranger to the values of cooperation and group effort when striving for supremacy. You learned these principles, and much more, as a member of your tribe.

Your people have always tried to hold to the old ways. Tradition and taboo have kept your tribe strong while the kingdoms of others have collapsed into chaos and ruin. But for the last few generations, some bands among the tribes were tempted to settle, make peace, trade, and even to build towns. Perhaps this is why your tribe chose to raise up the totems among the people as living embodiments of his power. Perhaps they needed a reminder of who they were and from whence they came. The Chosen of your tribe led bands back to the old ways, and most of your people abandoned the soft ways of civilization.

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Animal Handling|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Nature|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Survival|sw5e-phb}
{@b Tool Proficiencies}: One type of musical instrument or artisan's implements
{@b Equipment:} A hunting trap, a totemic token or set of tattoos marking your loyalty to your tribe, a set of traveler's clothes, and a pouch containing 100 cr

entries.name: Feature: Barbarian Heritage
entries: You have an excellent knowledge of not only your tribe's territory, but also the terrain and natural resources of the rest of the worlds. You are familiar enough with any wilderness area that you find twice as much food and water as you normally would when you forage there.
Additionally, you can call upon the hospitality of other tribes in times of need.

entries.name: Background Feat
entries: As a further embodiment of the experience and training of your background, you can choose from the following feats:

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Often considered rude and uncouth among civilized folk, barbarians have little respect for the niceties of life in the cities. The ties of tribe, clan, family, and the natural world of which they are a part are the most important bonds to most outlanders.

rows: I'm driven by a wanderlust that led me away from home.
I watch over my friends as if they were a litter of newborn pups.
I once ran twenty-five miles without stopping to warn my clan of an approaching horde. I'd do it again if I had to.
I have a lesson for every situation, drawn from observing nature.
I place no stock in wealthy or well-mannered folk. Money and manners won't save you from a hungry rancor.
I'm always picking things up, absently fiddling with them, and sometimes accidentally breaking them.
I feel far more comfortable around animals than people.
I was, in fact, raised by wampas.
{@b Change.} Life is like the seasons, in constant change, and we must change with it. (Chaotic)
{@b Greater Good.} It is each person's responsibility to make the most happiness for the whole tribe. (Light)
{@b Honor.} If I dishonor myself, I dishonor my whole clan. (Lawful)
{@b Might.} The strongest are meant to rule. (Dark)
{@b Nature.} The natural world is more important than all the constructs of civilization. (Neutral)
{@b Glory.} I must earn glory in battle, for myself and my clan. (Any)
My family, clan, or tribe is the most important thing in my life, even when they are far from me.
An injury to the unspoiled wilderness of my home is an injury to me.
I will bring terrible wrath down on the Darkdoers who destroyed my homeland.
I am the last of my tribe, and it is up to me to ensure their names enter legend.
I suffer awful visions of a coming disaster and will do anything to prevent it.
It is my duty to provide children to sustain my tribe.
I am too enamored of ale, wine, and other intoxicants.
There's no room for caution in a life lived to the fullest.
I remember every insult I've received and nurse a silent resentment toward anyone who's ever wronged me.
I am slow to trust members of other species, tribes, and societies.
Violence is my answer to almost any challenge.
Don't expect me to save those who can't save themselves. It is nature's way that the strong thrive and the weak perish.

entries.name: Bartender
entries: Sometimes you want to go where everybody knows your name and they're always glad you came. As a bartender, you're a charismatic fellow that knows how to deal with people. Whether you're the life of the party or simply an ear for someone who needs advice, people from all walks of life are drawn to your trustworthy nature.

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Medicine|sw5e-phb}, or {@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}
{@b Equipment:} A set of common clothes, a brewer's kit, and a belt pouch containing 150 cr

entries.name: Feature: Social Lubricant
entries: You have no trouble finding and getting into places that serve drinks. While drinking in a social establishment, strangers take a liking to you and feel comfortable enough to share gossip.

entries.name: Background Feat
entries: As a further embodiment of the experience and training of your background, you can choose from the following feats:

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: A bartender's demeanor ranges from jovial to downright rude. Regardless, all bartenders know how to take care of business—they break up fights, kick out drunk patrons, and offer honest counsel to people down on their luck.

rows: I'm always looking for a good time with good company.
Even in a social atmosphere, I always feel alone.
I live vicariously through the people I meet and the stories I hear.
I'm everyone's outlet but sometimes I just want to punch them in their thoughtless face.
If you're looking for a fight, I'll give you one.
TI know how to calm people down, but I also know how to rile them up.
It's not all fun and games. Business needs to run smoothly, whatever that might be.
{@b Cheer}. Spreading joy is my passion. (Light)
{@b Guidance}. It's our duty to help others. (Lawful)
{@b Legacy}. We have only one chance to write our story. Do what you will and make it count. (Chaotic)
{@b Manipulation}. Drunk people are the most vulnerable and can easily be taken {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} of. (Dark)
{@b People}. It's always good to meet and connect with new people. (Any)
{@b Honesty}. If I call you a nerf herder, it means I like you. (Any)
My cantina means everything to me. It brings back important memories from my past.
Brewing is my craft. My art brings people together.
The regular patrons of my cantina are like family to me.
I want to be successful. Whatever it takes.
Alcohol is all I ened, and sometimes all I want.
I've met so many people while staying in the same place. I need my own story to tell.
I can always go for another round. The gutter is my second home.
I judge people that don't drink to be antisocial and untrustworthy.
Party animals and depressed people make me feel bitter about my life.
Whenever life gets hard, I drink my problems away.
I need to know everyone's story.
I curse more than a kriffing sailor.

entries.name: Blackguard
entries: You are a member of the Blackguard: a reclusive sect of Force users from the planet of Mustafar. Rather than being determined by the Force, the Blackguard believe that the light or dark dwell within the user, and that to truly increase one's knowledge and strength in the Force, one must understand and seek out the philosophies and abilities of other Force traditions around the galaxy.

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Lore|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Survival|sw5e-phb}
{@b Equipment:} A copy of a Force-wielder organization's text, a trinket from your travels around the galaxy, a set of common clothes including a robe, and a belt pouch containing 150 cr

entries.name: Feature: Student of the Force
entries: You often know where to find information on Force-sensitive organizations, or where to find someone who would know, and can readily decipher more common lore about them. Your GM might rule that the knowledge you seek is secreted away in an almost inaccessible place, that it simply cannot be found, or is too difficult to decipher.

entries.name: Background Feat
entries: As a further embodiment of the experience and training of your background, you can choose from the following feats:

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: The Blackguard are galactic travelers and students, looking to expand their horizons and knowledge of the Force by learning from others.

rows: I let my actions speak for themselves.
I've left emotion behind me, I'm now perfectly placid.
I question every Force user I meet, trying to acquire every piece of knowledge I can.
I'm willing to listen to every side of an argument before I make my own judgment.
I spend every free moment training in lightsaber techniques.
I judge people by their actions, not their words.
When I set my mind to something, I follow through no matter what gets in my way.
I face problems head-on. A simple, direct solution is the best path to success.
{@b Knowledge.} The path to true understanding of the Force is through knowledge. (Neutral)
{@b Might.} Knowledge is the path to power and domination. (Dark)
{@b Defense.} The Blackguard protect that which others would seek to destroy. (Lawful)
{@b Loyalty.} The Blackguard Order watches its own. (Any)
{@b Balance.} There is no light or dark. There is only the Force. (Balanced)
{@b Freedom.} True freedom rejects the restrictions of the Jedi and Sith. (Chaos)
Nothing is more important than the other members of the Blackguard.
I would die to recover an ancient relic that was lost long ago.
I will do anything to protect the temple where I served.
I seek to preserve a sacred text that my enemies consider heretical and seek to destroy.
I'm still seeking the enlightenment I pursued in joining the Blackguard, and it still eludes me.
I would do anything for the Wilder that trained me.
I believe that everyone is beneath me.
I am easily distracted by the promise of information.
I have little respect for anyone who is not a proven warrior.
I find those who believe in the Dark and Light of the Force childish simpletons.
My rejection of Light and Dark has drained me of any real moral compass.
My focus on gaining knowledge has left me with little attachment to people or their feelings.

entries.name: Bodyguard
entries: You are a licensed bodyguard, standing by your charge ready to protect them from any threat.

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}
{@b Tool Proficiencies:} Your choice of {@item Demolitions kit|sw5e-phb|demolitions kit}, {@item Disguise kit|sw5e-phb|disguise kit}, or {@item Security kit|sw5e-phb|security kit}
{@b Equipment:} A set of clandestine clothes, the kit for your chosen tool proficiency, a {@item Traumakit|sw5e-phb|traumakit}, and a belt pouch containing 75 cr

entries.name: Feature: Authorized Violence
entries: As a licensed professional, most law enforcement tend to turn a blind eye when you are involved in altercations. You are rarely detained due to wearing armor and wielding weaponry; in fact, while accompanying your client, it is typically socially acceptable for you to go both armed and armored.

entries.name: Background Feat
entries: As a further embodiment of the experience and training of your background, you can choose from the following feats:

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: There are many reasons as to why you may be guarding someone. It could be that you and your family are in the service of a powerful individual, or that you owe a friend a life debt after they rescued you from some perilous encounter. You may be friends with the ones you protect: You may not. But in any case, your loyalties are unwavering, and your courage speaks for itself.

rows: I am overly cautious of all food and drink that either my client or I consume.
I find it hard to leave my client to themselves.
I try to take the safest routes through cities, roads, or passes: I am not a fan of dark alley shortcuts.
If my client's legs were weary in a dangerous area, I would carry them every step of the way.
Even though I am constantly by my client's side, I cannot help but feel alone sometimes.
I often try to make situations sound better than they are to make my client feel more comfortable.
I may be a stick in the mud while I am sober, but I am wilder than a rancor when I am intoxicated.
I form attachments to those I care about, and often find myself going above and beyond to make them happy.
{@b Guardian.} I dedicate my life to defending those who cannot defend themselves (Light)
{@b Indifferent.} I do not have personal connections with my charge. They are merely part of the job. (Neutral)
{@b Determined.} I will protect those who I must... by any means necessary. (Chaotic)
{@b Underhanded.} I will learn my clients' weaknesses so that I may take {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} of them. (Dark)
{@b Resolute.} I follow the law laid down for me to protect those whom I am ordered to. (Lawful)
{@b Flexible.} I take into account my past experiences to help prepare for the future endeavors. (Any)
I have a home I love somewhere, though I rarely see it.
I am part of an order dedicated to protecting others.
The one who I look after saved me from something horrible once: I owe them everything.
I have other friends in this business who don't perform their duties exactly how I do.
While that time is behind me now, the faces from my past still linger.
My client isn't the only one who I should protect. There are many more out there without protection.
I have lost clients before. I now find myself detached to prevent future heartache.
I am often times forgetful, much to my client's dismay.
I am very stubborn. It is very nearly impossible to sway my opinions on how things should be handled.
Trust is a rare commodity in my line of work. As such, it is not something I often give to others.
My client and I don't get along in the slightest. It makes it quite difficult to want to look after them.
Although I am sworn to protect my client, I will abandon them in the face of certain death.

entries.name: City Watch
entries: You have served the community where you grew up, standing as its first line of defense against crime and wildlife. You aren't a soldier, directing your gaze outward at possible enemies. Instead, your service to your hometown was to help police its populace, protecting the citizenry from lawbreakers and malefactors of every stripe.
Even if you're not city-born or city-bred, this background can describe your early years as a member of law enforcement. Most settlements of any size have their own law enforcement forces.

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}
{@b Equipment:} A uniform in the style of your unit and indicative of your rank, a horn with which to summon help, a set of {@item Binders|sw5e-phb|binders}, and a pouch containing 100 cr

entries.name: Feature: Watcher's Eye
entries: Your experience in enforcing the law, and dealing with lawbreakers, gives you a feel for local laws and criminals. You can easily find the local outpost of the watch or a similar organization, and just as easily pick out the dens of criminal activity in a community, although you're more likely to be welcome in the former locations rather than the latter.

entries.name: Background Feat
entries: As a further embodiment of the experience and training of your background, you can choose from the following feats:

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Years of service in the City Watch have led to the rigid discipline most often seen in military service. Working with your comrades has created a strong family bond and pride in your community.

rows: I'm haunted by memories of war. I can't get the images of violence out of my mind.
I've lost too many friends, and I'm slow to make new ones.
I'm full of inspiring and cautionary tales from my guard service relevant to almost every combat situation.
I can stare down a hell hound without flinching.
I enjoy being strong and like breaking things.
I have a crude sense of humor.
I face problems head-on. A simple, direct solution is the best path to success.
{@b Greater Good.} Our lot is to lay down our lives in defense of others. (Light)
{@b Responsibility.} I do what I must and obey just authority. (Lawful)
{@b Independence.} When people follow orders blindly, they embrace a kind of tyranny. (Chaotic)
{@b Might.} In life as in war, the stronger force wins. (Dark)
{@b Live and Let Live.} Ideals aren't worth killing over or going to war for. (Neutral)
{@b Nation.} My city, nation, or people are all that matter. (Any)
I would still lay down my life for the people I served with.
Someone saved my life on the battlefield. To this day, I will never leave a friend behind.
I'll never forget the crushing defeat my company suffered or the enemies who dealt it.
Those who fight beside me are those worth dying for.
I fight for those who cannot fight for themselves.
The monstrous enemy we faced in battle still leaves me quivering with fear.
I have little respect for anyone who is not a proven warrior.
I made a terrible mistake in battle cost many lives— and I would do anything to keep that mistake secret.
My hatred of my enemies is blind and unreasoning.
I obey the law, even if the law causes misery.
I'd rather eat my armor than admit when I'm wrong.

entries.name: Clone
entries: You are a miracle of science. A creature born not from love or passion, but from logic and machinery. Created in a laboratory, you are a perfect genetic replica of your DNA-Donor, whomever that is.

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Lore|sw5e-phb}, Sleight of Hand and {@skill Survival|sw5e-phb}
{@b Tool Proficiencies:} Your choice of geneticist's implements, {@item Security kit|sw5e-phb|security kit}, or {@item Slicer's kit|sw5e-phb|slicer's kit}
{@b Equipment:} A set of clothes appropriate to your duties, a trinket related to your DNA-donor, and 150 credits

entries.name: DNA-Donor
entries: The background of your DNA-Donor often shapes a clone's path in life.

entries.name: Feature: A Life Not Lived
entries: Being a clone, you were born from the existence of another. Flashes of deeds you never did, of people you have never met and of information you have never learned sporadically appear. You may be confused with your DNA-Donor by others, being befriended by, or made enemies of, people you have never before met. The exact nature of these revelations depends on the nature of your DNA-Donor; they might lead to a site that only one other has ever seen, some long-forgotten fact, relic or weapon from the past that could reshape the present, or even information that would be damaging to the people who created you.

entries.name: Background Feat
entries: As a further embodiment of the experience and training of your background, you can choose from the following feats:

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: A clone's demeanor often, though not always, matches that of their DNA-Donor. Is it nature, or is it nurture?

rows: I speak rarely but mean every word I say.
I laugh loudly and see the humor in stressful situations.
I prefer to solve problems without violence, but I finish fights decisively.
I enjoy being out in nature; poor weather never sours my mood.
I am always working on some project or other.
I'm always picking things up, absently fiddling with them, and sometimes accidentally breaking them.
I bluntly say what others are hinting at or hiding.
{@b Charity.} I always try to help those in need, no matter what the personal cost. (Light)
{@b Logic.} Emotions must not cloud our sense of what is right and true, or our logical thinking. (Lawful)
{@b Live and Let Live.} Meddling in the affairs of others only causes trouble. (Balanced)
{@b Freedom.} Chains are meant to be broken, as are those who would forge them. (Chaotic)
{@b Pride.} I will do whatever it takes to be recognized as the best. (Dark)
{@b Aspiration.} I'm determined to make something of myself. (Any)
I am fiercely loyal to those with whom I work.
In my birth laboratory, I discovered something that could endanger the world.
I spend money freely and live life to the fullest, knowing that tomorrow I might die.
I live for the thrill of the hunt.
I owe my instructor a great debt for forging me into the person I am today.
One day I will return to my home planet and prove that I am their greatest creation.
I secretly believe that everyone is beneath me.
I write exceptionally bad poetry and recite it at inopportune times.
I struggle with individuality, those who see me as unique I would die for.
Every social situation I'm in seems to lead to my asking rude personal questions.
I have trouble trusting in my allies.
I invest so much time into planning that I can't bring myself to deviate from the plan, even when it is needed.

entries.name: Clone Trooper
entries: You are one of millions; genetically engineered, identical specimens designed to be the perfect soldier. Created from a template provided by the legendary bounty hunter Jango Fett, you represent the latest and greatest evolution in galactic warfare.

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Medicine|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Piloting|sw5e-phb}
{@b Tool Proficiencies:} Your choice of {@item Demolitions kit|sw5e-phb|demolitions kit}, {@item Security kit|sw5e-phb|security kit}, or {@item Slicer's kit|sw5e-phb|slicer's kit}
{@b Equipment:} Badge or emblem of your rank, your chosen tools, a set of common clothes, and a pouch containing 100 cr

entries.name: Clone Specialization
entries: While most clones serve as simple soldier, there are many specialized units. Roll a {@dice d8} or choose from the options in the table below to determine your specialization:

entries.name: Feature: Republic Rank
entries: You are a soldier of the Republic. Those loyal to the Republic will respect your status and defer to you if they don't outrank you. You can invoke your position to exert influence over other soldiers, requisition simple equipment, and gain access to military compounds affiliated with the Republic.

entries.name: Background Feat
entries: As a further embodiment of the experience and training of your background, you can choose from the following feats:

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Clones are trained from birth to be the perfect soldier; over time, they also develop their own personalities. They are universally loyal to the Republic. While clones share genetic coding, no two are completely identical.

rows: I can stare down a krayt dragon without flinching.
I face problems head-on. A simple, direct solution is the best path to success.
I have a sense of humor. This is rare among my brothers.
I judge people by their actions, not their words.
I've lost too many friends, and I'm slow to make new ones.
I ask a lot of questions.
I'll settle for nothing less than perfection.
{@b Responsibility.} I do what I must and obey just authority. (Lawful)
{@b Might.} Strength, not compassion, wins battles. (Dark)
{@b Republic.} My brothers, the Republic, or people are all that matter. (Any)
{@b Greater Good.} We fight not for ourselves, but for countless of others that can't fight for themselves. (Light)
{@b Freedom.} Tyrants must not be allowed to oppress the people. (Chaotic)
{@b Live and Let Live.} Ideals aren't worth killing or going to war over. (Neutral)
Someone saved my life on the battlefield. To this day, I will never leave a friend behind.
Those who fight beside me are those worth dying for.
I fight for those who cannot fight for themselves.
I would still lay down my life for the people I serve with.
A proud commander once gave me a horrible beating, and I will take my revenge on any bully I encounter.
I have little respect for anyone who is of a lesser rank.
I obey orders without question, even if the orders cause misery.
I'd rather eat my armor than admit when I'm wrong.
I judge others harshly, and myself even more severely.
I am inflexible in my thinking.
I can't tell a lie for the life of me.

entries.name: Companion
entries: You are experienced in the arts of companionship, and you provide these services for people who can afford to pay it. This may mean adult favors of the sensual variety, but it just as frequently means conversation, comfort, and company.

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Acrobatics|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Performance|sw5e-phb}
{@b Tool Proficiencies:} One instrument of your choice or a {@item Disguise kit|sw5e-phb|disguise kit}
{@b Equipment:} A set of common clothes, an instrument or {@item Disguise kit|sw5e-phb|disguise kit}, and a belt pouch containing 50 cr

entries.name: Feature: Sordid Knowledge
entries: You have or can gain compromising information about people of importance. You may be able to leverage this information in order to acquire lodging, information, or even money.  You may also become a target for having this information. Your GM may rule that any particular individual is either above reproach or is too careful in covering their tracks to provide such leverage.

entries.name: Background Feat
entries: As a further embodiment of the experience and training of your background, you can choose from the following feats:

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: You enjoy people and you enjoy your work and you enjoy the money it brings. There is no shame in your profession and it is often highly regulated and regimented by factions or the local government. It requires outgoing and adventurous personalities to be a success, and often these traits lead them to adventures of a different sort.

rows: People are often hurt and damaged. I try to heal them and leave them stronger than when I meet them.
I enjoy being in control and manipulating people. It's important that they like me so they do what I say.
I'm not a laser-brain, although I don't open my mouth to prove people wrong. I let them discover the truth after I have what I want.
I'm better than those who are more prim and proper, and I'm having more fun.
I don't really care what happens, it's an easy way to get money for my habit.
There are so many different kinds of people, and I want to meet them all.
I never thought this was the life for me, perhaps some brave person will rescue me.
I like what I do and I resent those who want to rescue me.
{@b Sacred.} My body is a temple I am duty-bound to share. (Lawful)
{@b Hedonism.} I fill my urges when and where I wish. (Chaotic)
{@b Loving.} Everyone needs attention and love. (Light)
{@b Exploitation.} I take pleasure in toying with people, and taking {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} of them. (Dark)
{@b Consent.}  I respect other's desires and wishes. (Neutral)
{@b Freedom.}  I want to have the independence to enjoy life. (Any)
I seek a relationship with the most powerful people in the land, desiring to be the power behind the throne.
If I can only collect enough credits, I'll be able to pay off my debts and be free.
I have a sick parent to whom I send all my money.
My independence is the most important thing in my world.
I bring happiness to the world one person at a time.
I have a young child who is my world.
I have an incurable disease I acquired from a client.
I am addicted to recreational drugs that dull the pain I feel.
I no longer practice my old profession, and I fear anyone discovering it.
I am suspicious of anyone who tries to be nice to me. They only want me to sleep with them.
I pretend to be tough, but am broken inside.

entries.name: Courtier
entries: In your earlier days, you were a personage of some significance in a noble court or a bureaucratic organization. You might or might not come from an upper-class family; your talents, rather than the circumstances of your birth, could have secured you this position.

You might have been one of the many functionaries, attendants, and other hangers-on in Coruscant's upper echelons, or perhaps you traveled in Nar Shaddaa's baroque and sometimes cutthroat conglomeration of factions, nobles, adventurers, and secret societies. You might have been one of the behind-the-scenes law-keepers or functionaries on Dromund Kaas, or you might have grown up on some other affluent planet.

Even if you are no longer a full-fledged member of the group that gave you your start in life, your relationships with your former fellows can be an {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} for you and your adventuring comrades. You might undertake missions with your new companions that further the interest of the organization that gave you your start in life. In any event, the abilities that you honed while serving as a courtier will stand you in good stead as an adventurer.

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Performance|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Survival|sw5e-phb}
{@b Equipment:} A set of fine clothes and a pouch containing 150 cr

entries.name: Feature: Court Functionality
entries: Your knowledge of how bureaucracies function lets you gain access to the records and inner workings of any noble court or government you encounter. You know who the movers and shakers are, whom to go to for the favors you seek, and what the current intrigues of interest in the group are.

entries.name: Background Feat
entries: As a further embodiment of the experience and training of your background, you can choose from the following feats:

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: The noble court or bureaucratic organization where you got your start is directly or indirectly associated with your bond (which could pertain to certain individuals in the group, such as your sponsor or mentor). Your ideal might be concerned with the prevailing philosophy of your court or organization.

rows: I believe that anything worth doing is worth doing right. I can't help it— I'm a perfectionist.
I'm a snob who looks down on those who can't appreciate fine art.
I always want to know how things work and what makes people tick.
I'm full of witty aphorisms and have a proverb for every occasion.
I'm rude to people who lack my commitment to hard work and fair play.
I like to talk at length about my profession.
I don't part with my money easily and will haggle tirelessly to get the best deal possible.
I'm well known for my work, so I'm always taken aback when people haven't heard of me.
{@b Community.} It is the duty of all civilized people to strengthen the bonds of community and the security of civilization. (Lawful)
{@b Generosity.} My talents were given to me so that I could use them to benefit the world. (Light)
{@b Freedom.} Everyone should be free to pursue his or her own livelihood. (Chaotic)
{@b Greed.} I'm only in it for the money. (Dark)
{@b People.} I'm committed to the people I care about, not to ideals. (Neutral)
{@b Aspiration.} I work hard to be the best there is at my craft. (Any)
The location where I learned my trade is the most important place in the world to me.
I created a great work for someone unworthy to receive it. I'm still looking for someone worthy.
I owe someone a great debt for forging me into the person I am today.
I pursue wealth to secure someone's love.
One day I will return to my faction and prove that I am the greatest artisan of them all.
I will get revenge on the Dark forces that destroyed my place of business and ruined my livelihood.
I'll do anything to get my hands on something rare or priceless.
I'm quick to assume that someone is trying to cheat me.
No one must ever learn that I once stole money from faction coffers.
I'm never satisfied with what I have— I always want more.
I would kill to acquire a noble title.
I'm horribly jealous of anyone who can outshine my handiwork. Everywhere I go, I'm surrounded by rivals.

entries.name: Crime Lord
entries: Few societies manage to eradicate crime altogether. In the underworld, someone always rises to the top, either through vision, organisation, or sheer intimidation. The life of a crime lord isn't for the timid. After conquering an unseen empire, the crime lord wages a daily struggle not only to stay on top, but also to stay alive.

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}
{@b Tool Proficiencies:} One type of gaming set
{@b Equipment:} A fine set of clothes, a gaming set (one of your choice), and a purse containing 250 cr

entries.name: Criminal Motivation
entries: Not every crime lord is bent on corrupting society and making a profit. Some use their criminal connections to wage guerilla wars against tyrants and despots. Indeed, some historical heroes began as smugglers or pirates, rising through the ranks of their organization to provide a more noble direction for their group's activities. Although some did so to remove an obstacle to making more money, others recognized that ridding the galaxy of evil is a more important long-term goal. Choose the motivation behind your criminal enterprise, or roll on the table below.

entries.name: Feature: Criminal Network
entries: You have access to an extensive network of organised crime. You know how to get messages to and from local contacts, even over great distances; you know the local messengers, corrupt caravan masters, and seedy sailors who can deliver messages for you.

entries.name: Background Feat
entries: As a further embodiment of the experience and training of your background, you can choose from the following feats:

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Crime lords might seem like villains on the surface, and many of them are villainous to the core. But some have an abundance of endearing, if not redeeming, characteristics. Unlike common thieves, some crime lords even have some respect for law and authority, with whom they play a cat-and-mouse type game.

rows: I always have a plan for what to do when things go wrong.
I am always calm, no matter what the situation. I never raise my voice or let me emotions control me.
My eloquent flattery makes everyone I talk to feel like the most wonderful and important person in the world.
I would rather make a new friend than a new enemy.
I don't like to get my hands dirty, and I won't be caught dead in unsuitable accommodations.
My favor, once lost, is lost forever.
If you do me an injury, I will crush you, ruin your name, and salt your fields.
I blow up at the slightest insult.
{@b Honor.} I don't steal from others in the trade. (Lawful)
{@b Freedom.} Chains are meant to be broken, as are those who would forge them. (Chaotic)
{@b Charity.} I steal from the wealthy so that I can help people in need. (Light)
{@b Greed.} I will do whatever it takes to become wealthy. (Dark)
{@b People.} I'm loyal to my friends, not to any ideals, and everyone else can take a walk for all I care. (Neutral)
{@b Redemption.} There's a spark of good in everyone. (Light)
I'm trying to pay off an old debt I owe to a generous benefactor.
My ill-gotten gains go to support my family.
Something important was taken from me, and I aim to steal it back.
The common folk must see me as a hero of the people.
I'm guilty of a terrible crime. I hope I can redeem myself for it.
Someone I loved died because of a mistake I made. That will never happen again.
I secretly believe that everyone is beneath me.
When faced with a choice between money and my friends, I usually choose the money.
I too often hear veiled insults and threats in every word addressed to me, and I'm quick to anger.
I have a —tell— that reveals when I'm lying.
I turn tail and run when things look bad.
An innocent person is in prison for a crime that I committed. I'm okay with that.

entries.name: Dathomir Witch
entries: You are a part of one of the many Force-sensitive clans on Dathomir. You and your sisters, under the {@spell Guidance|sw5e-phb|guidance} of the Clan Mother, form powerful connections with one another and the untamed wilds of the planet. Your people are a matriarchal society of warriors who train in the art of war and the usage of both muscle and the Force in combat. While all clans have their own set of rules regarding Force usage, all the clans held one rule above all others: {@i "Never Concede to Evil."}

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Acrobatics|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Animal Handling|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Lore|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Nature|sw5e-phb}
{@b Equipment:} A copy of your clan's book of laws, a set of traveler's clothes, and a pouch containing 150 cr

entries.name: Witch Clans
entries: Dathomir culture is built on the backbone of various clans. The clan you are a part of has it's own history, allegiances, and feuds which shape your persepctive. Choose an option or roll on the table below to determine your clan.

entries.name: Feature: Matriarchal Society
entries: Other Dathomir Witches know, and will look out for you. If you're ever in need of a place to stay, or a meal to eat, other Dathomir Witches will help you as long as your clans aren't feuding. This could be in the form of shelters, meals, even healing. If the Dathomir Witches are of your clan or a clan friendly to you, they may be willing to help you even at cost to themselves.

entries.name: Background Feat
entries: As a further embodiment of the experience and training of your background, you can choose from the following feats:

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Dathomir Witches are shaped by their training. They study their book of laws and use it to uphold order and prevent one's turn to the dark side. Their clan and the people around them affects their mannerisms and ideals. Their flaws might be some hidden hypocrisy or heretical idea, or an ideal or bond taken to an extreme.

rows: I try and bring my culture to outsiders.
I always put my clan first.
I follow my clan's book of law to the letter.
I once ran twenty-five miles without stopping to warn my clan of an approaching rival clan. I'd do it again if I had to.
I place no stock in wealthy or well-mannered folk. Credits and manners won't save you from a hungry rancor.
I have a lesson for every situation, drawn from observing nature.
I feel far more comfortable around wildlife than I do society.
I'm always picking things up, absently fiddling with them, and sometimes accidentally breaking them.
{@b Change.} Life is like the seasons, in constant change, and we must change with it. (Chaotic)
{@b Greater Good.} It is each person's responsibility to make the most happiness for the whole clan. (Light)
{@b Honor.} If I dishonor myself, I dishonor my whole clan. (Lawful)
{@b Might.} The strongest are meant to rule. (Dark)
{@b Nature.} The natural world is more important than all the constructs of civilization. (Neutral)
{@b Glory.} I must earn glory in battle, for myself and my clan. (Any)
My family and clan is the most important thing in my life, even when they are far from me.
An injury to the unspoiled wilderness of my home is an injury to me.
I am the last of my clan, and it is up to me to keep the traditions of my ancestors alive.
It is my duty to provide children to sustain my clan.
I suffer awful visions of a coming disaster and will do anything to prevent it.
I will bring terrible wrath down on those who disrespect my clan.
I stick to my traditions no matter what, even at the cost of others.
There's no room for caution in a life lived to the fullest.
I remember every insult I've received and nurse a silent resentment toward anyone who's ever wronged me.
I am slow to trust members of other species, clans, and societies.
Violence is my answer to almost any challenge.
Don't expect me to save those who can't save themselves. It is nature's way that the strong thrive and the weak perish.

entries.name: Ex-Cultist
entries: Once you served alongside your fellow neophytes. You worshiped at altars to a deific entity, performed the sacraments and adorned yourself in the proper fashion. You basked in this dark glory with your fellows as you served this higher, malign power. But, something changed. Now, you wander the world outside of isolated circle of brethren, either unwillingly or of your own volition.

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}, or {@skill Lore|sw5e-phb}

{@b Equipment:} A set of common clothes including a robe, a symbol of devotion, a copy of a blasphemous holy text, a curved ritual knife, a {@item Poisoner's kit|sw5e-phb|poisoner's kit}, and a belt pouch containing 50 cr

entries.name: Change of Heart
entries: Why did you walk away from the world you knew? Was this a choice you made, or did fate separate you from your fellow devotees? Do you wish to undo the evil that your cult perpetuated, or would you rejoin your cult if given the chance?

rows: I witnessed a particularly gruesome rite and ran for my life.
I asked the wrong kind of questions. The others planned to sacrifice me to our dark lord, but I escaped.
The others took their own lives to ascend. I could not.
I no longer believed in what we were doing. It seemed wrong, somehow.

entries.name: Feature: Secret Signs
entries: You know the secret symbology of your cult, which can pop up in some surprising places. With a subtle gesture or knowing handshake you can discern who follows the ways of your dark lord. Cloisters of your cult may be hidden across the galaxy, identified by the secret signs and symbols designed to lead the faithful to places of dark worship. Such cloistered often contain enough lodging and food for at least ten people, for a week, and sometimes harbor eldritch treasures belonging to the cult.

entries.name: Background Feat
entries: As a further embodiment of the experience and training of your background, you can choose from the following feats:

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: A cult washes away all doubt and instills faith throughout a cultist's life. Even if a service is forsworn, members are still deeply affected by their old life.

rows: Everything is a sign of coming doom. Every. Single. Thing.
The world is so exciting! Now I can do things previously forbidden like drinking wine or wearing shoes.
The dark lord used to order us to do everything. It's a little hard for me to live without that.
If my friends will let me, I'll openly reminisce about my old days in the cult all day long.
I can't help but check the holy scriptures for advice about any given situation.
It's not the end of the world. That's not for another five years, three months, ten days, twelve hours...
I hate my cult for what they made me do and what they made me become.
I'll happily inform those I meet of the many ways in which they are being heretical.
{@b Loyalty}. My new companions are my new family, I will protect them. (Lawful)
{@b Redemption}. I must fix the evils my cult has done. (Light)
{@b Independence}. I'll never be bound in servitude again! (Chaotic)
{@b Power}. The dark lord was weak in the end. I will be stronger than they ever were. (Dark)
{@b Secrets}. The lore of my cult is historically important, and I should preserve it. (Neutral)
{@b Revision}. The cult failed because the holy book was wrong. I must learn about the outside world, and fix the book's errors. (Any)
I must discover the truth behind my dark lord, even if it kills me.
I need to reconnect with the people from my life before the cult, if I can ever find them.
I must free other people from unwitting service to dark masters.
A monstrous, immortal guardian of the cult is hunting me. I pray it never finds me.
I sacrificed my light in service to the dark lord, and now I seek to reclaim it.
The day of reckoning is coming, and my knowledge is the key to stopping it.
If I ever had the chance, I'd definitely rejoin my cult.
I'm a little too into blood sacrifice.
Knowledge is more important than sanity.
I'm often more interested in than {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} of abominable eldritch monsters.
I'm almost too willing to follow orders without thinking.
Murder was significantly less frowned upon by the cult than in the outside world.

entries.name: Faction Adventurer
entries: Adventuring is nothing new to you. Due to the circumstances of how you were raised, you have been involved with wandering heroes for most of your life. Maybe you were part of an adventuring band previously, but split with them after a disagreement or tragedy. Or, perhaps you worked around heroes in a lesser role for most of your young life, and you are now ready to graduate to the front lines.

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Nature|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Survival|sw5e-phb}
{@b Tool Proficiencies:} Your choice {@item Demolitions kit|sw5e-phb|demolitions kit}, {@item Security kit|sw5e-phb|security kit}, or {@item Slicer's kit|sw5e-phb|slicer's kit}
{@b Equipment:} 50 feet of rope, a small knife, a trophy, a set of traveler's clothes, and a belt pouch containing 100 cr.

entries.name: Adventuring Origin
entries: You have either been adventuring or assisting other in adventuring since a very young age. Perhaps your parents were famous adventurers, or a group of adventurers found and raised you as their own. Perhaps you were trained to be a professional monster hunter, or maybe another faction member saved your life so you swore loyalty to them. Work with your GM to determine the nature of your adventuring.

entries.name: Feature: Faction Membership
entries: You are an established and respected member of an adventurer's faction, allowing you to rely on certain benefits that membership provides. If you are in a town with a headquarters for your adventurer's faction and you are in good standing with the faction, you will be allowed to look at the job postings and find adventuring work to earn money.

factions often wield tremendous political power. If you are accused of a crime, your faction will support you if a good case can be made for your innocence or the crime is justifiable. You can also gain access to powerful political figures through the faction, if you are a member in good standing. You must pay dues of 50 cr per month to the faction. Your dues must be current to remain in the faction's good graces.

entries.name: Background Feat
entries: As a further embodiment of the experience and training of your background, you can choose from the following feats:

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Adventurers are well adjusted to life on the road. They are often comfortable doing dangerous things like dungeoneering and fighting and can stay level-headed in the face of danger, but they may not be so well adapted to other parts of life.

rows: I can't bring myself to ignore a cry for help.
I hold onto every mildly interesting item I find, in case it comes in handy someday.
After all the weirdness I've seen on my travels, nothing can surprise me.
I spit and laugh in the face of danger.
Giving up is never an option for me.
I feel more at home in monster-infested dungeons than in civilized society.
I fill silence with wacky stories about my past misadventures, which may or may not be exaggerated.
My sense of humor is as dark and grim as the dungeons I explore.
{@b Adventure.} All I want is to travel the world and see amazing things. (Any)
{@b Heroism.} I am dedicated to helping people in need. (Light)
{@b Order.} I use my power to save the world from the forces of destruction and chaos. (Lawful)
{@b Excitement.} An ordinary life is boring, I'd rather travel around and find trouble. (Chaotic)
{@b Power.} The more powerful enemies I defeat, the stronger I become. (Neutral)
{@b Aspiration.} I want to go down in history as a brave, powerful hero. (Any)
I carry with me a strange artifact that I found in a dungeon, but I don't know what it's for.
My adventuring party means the world to me.
I have sworn to hunt down the monster or villain who killed my former adventuring party.
I adventure in order to bring honor (or money) to my family.
There is a faraway place I've always wanted to visit, and I won't stop until I make it there.
All I want is to make the ones who trained me in the way of adventuring proud.
I default to solving problems with violence even when it's unwise or immoral.
I expect to be lavished with praise whenever I do my job, and I get mad when no one acknowledges me.
All members of "Dark" species must be Dark, so I will never trust them.
Waiting around makes me antsy. I'd rather do something stupid than do nothing at all.
My habit of looting dungeons makes me swipe things I shouldn't.
A monstrous enemy I faced in the past still leaves me quivering with fear.

entries.name: Faction Artisan
entries: You are a member of an artisan's faction, skilled in a particular field and closely associated with other artisans. You are a well-established part of the mercantile world, freed by talent and wealth from the constraints of a feudal social order. You learned your skills as an apprentice to a master artisan, under the sponsorship of your faction, until you became a master in your own right.

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Technology|sw5e-phb}
{@b Tool Proficiencies:} One type of artisan's implements, {@item Biochemist's kit|sw5e-phb|biochemist's kit}, or {@item Chef's kit|sw5e-phb|chef's kit}
{@b Equipment:} A set of tools (one of your choice), a letter of introduction from your faction, a set of traveler's clothes, and a belt pouch containing 150 cr

entries.name: Faction Business
entries: factions are generally found in cities large enough to support several artisans practicing the same trade. However, your faction might instead be a loose network of artisans who each work in a different village within a larger realm. Work with your GM to determine the nature of your faction.

entries.name: Feature: Faction Membership
entries: As an established and respected member of a faction, you can rely on certain benefits that membership provides. Your fellow faction members will provide you with lodging and food if necessary, and pay for your funeral if needed. In some cities and towns, a factionhall offers a central place to meet other members of your profession, which can be a good place to meet potential patrons, allies, or hirelings.

factions often wield tremendous political power. If you are accused of a crime, your faction will support you if a good case can be made for your innocence or the crime is justifiable. You can also gain access to powerful political figures through the faction, if you are a member in good standing. You must pay dues of 50 cr per month to the faction. Your dues must be current to remain in the faction's good graces.

entries.name: Background Feat
entries: As a further embodiment of the experience and training of your background, you can choose from the following feats:

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: faction artisans are among the most ordinary people in the world—until they set down their tools and take up an adventuring career. They understand the value of hard work and the importance of community, but they're vulnerable to sins of greed and covetousness.

rows: I believe that anything worth doing is worth doing right. I can't help it— I'm a perfectionist.
I'm a snob who looks down on those who can't appreciate fine art.
I always want to know how things work and what makes people tick.
I'm full of witty aphorisms and have a proverb for every occasion.
I'm rude to people who lack my commitment to hard work and fair play.
I like to talk at length about my profession.
I don't part with my money easily and will haggle tirelessly to get the best deal possible.
I believe I'm well known for my work, and I'm always taken aback when people haven't heard of me.
{@b Community.} It is the duty of all civilized people to strengthen the bonds of community and the security of civilization. (Lawful)
{@b Generosity.} My talents were given to me so that I could use them to benefit the world. (Light)
{@b Freedom.} Everyone should be free to pursue his or her own livelihood. (Chaotic)
{@b Greed.} I'm only in it for the money. (Dark)
{@b People.} I'm committed to the people I care about, not to ideals. (Neutral)
{@b Aspiration.} I work hard to be the best there is at my craft. (Any)
The workshop where I learned my trade is the most important place in the world to me.
I created a great work for someone, and then found them unworthy of it; I now search for someone worthy.
I owe my faction a great debt for forging me into the person I am today.
I pursue wealth to secure someone's love.
One day I will return to my faction and prove that I am the greatest artisan of them all.
I will get revenge on the Dark forces that destroyed my place of business and ruined my livelihood.
I'll do anything to get my hands on something rare or priceless.
I'm quick to assume that someone is trying to cheat me.
No one must ever learn that I once stole money from faction coffers.
I'm never satisfied with what I have— I always want more.
I would kill to acquire a noble title.
I'm horribly jealous of anyone who can outshine my handiwork. Everywhere I go, I'm surrounded by rivals.

entries.name: Faction Merchant
entries: Instead of an artisans' faction, you might belong to a faction of traders, caravan masters, or shopkeepers. You don't craft items yourself but earn a living by buying and selling the works of others. Your faction might be a large merchant consortium (or family) with interests across the galaxy. Perhaps you transported goods from one place to another, by ship, wagon, or caravan, or bought them from traveling traders and sold them in your own little shop. In some ways, the traveling merchant's life lends itself to adventure far more than the life of an artisan.

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Performance|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}
{@b Equipment:} A letter of introduction from your faction, a set of traveler's clothes, and a belt pouch containing 150 cr
