entries: You are an experienced teacher who knows how to best instruct others in an array of disciplines.  Although you have a vast amount of knowledge yourself, pedagogy is the most important tool in your toolbox because it allows the rest of your knowledge to spread most efficiently.

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Lore|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Nature|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Performance|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Technology|sw5e-phb}
{@b Tool Proficiencies:} One instrument or set of artisan's implements of your choice
{@b Equipment:} A set of common clothes, an instrument or set of tools with which you are proficient, a token from a former student, and a belt pouch containing 50 cr

entries.name: Feature: Knowledge
entries: If you need information on something, you know if there is a book containing that information and where to find it. Further, when you hear a creature speaking or when you see language written down, you can identify exactly what language is being used even if you are not proficient in the language.  Finally, when you hear music, you know which instruments are being used in the performance, even if you are not proficient in their use.

entries.name: Background Feat
entries: As a further embodiment of the experience and training of your background, you can choose from the following feats:

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: As a teacher you are devoted to educating others, as well as learning new information for yourself. It is up to you whether you are preachy or wise, a bookworm or more kinesthetic, a note taker or visual learner.  In any case, you are most likely underappreciated.

rows: Knowledge is the most important thing in the world.
I have quotes for every occasion.
My vocabulary is vast enough I sometimes use words that are larger than necessary.
Because I understand why people can make mistakes, I am also patient with them.
Sometimes I start explaining things at a level much to basic for the audience.
I reward hard work and good manners.
{@b Teach.} I must spread what I have learned. (Lawful)
{@b Insatiable.} When I find something new I must learn everything about it, no matter the cost. (Chaotic)
{@b Discovery.} Every single piece of information is waiting to be discovered. (Light)
{@b Greed.} Every piece of knowledge will be mine. (Dark)
{@b People.} I will teach anybody anything. (Neutral)
I was picked on while growing up for being a bookworm.
The world is such an open place, I feel like there is still so much to learn. I want to compile knowledge from different places.
I like reading books and writing, but I'm no poet yet. It is just a hobby I want to share with others, looking for exotic inspirations.
I will become the power behind the throne by controlling the information the throne receives.
Children are our future, and I will mold them.
I can't teach what I don't know. I will teach everything.
Someone showing bad manners does not exist to me. I will never talk to or acknowledge that person.
I overemphasize the importance of discipline.
I invest so much time into planning that I can't bring myself to deviate from the plan, even when it is needed.
I look down on uneducated adults.
I'd give up my companions for a piece of secret information.
I can't stand not reading at least one page of a book a day.

entries.name: (Un)Retired Adventurer
entries: "I'm getting too old for this stuff."

You spent your life as an adventurer, learning the use of many skills and basic survival techniques, including how to stay alive in a hostile area. You might have been part of a famous adventuring party or a less renowned one.

When you choose this background, work with your GM to determine the details of your previous adventuring party, and what kind of experiences you had in your adventuring career. How famous was your previous adventuring party and how well known are you? What did you learn? What was your group's specialty?

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Lore|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Survival|sw5e-phb}
{@b Tool Proficiencies}: One type of artisan's implements

{@b Equipment:} A {@item Grappling hook|sw5e-phb|grappling hook}, one tool with which you are proficient, a memento of an unsuccessful expedition (map to a never found treasure, lock of hair from a fallen companion, or another trinket),  and a pouch containing your last 50 cr

entries.name: Feature: Bridges Not Yet Burned
entries: Throughout your adventures you have established a multitude of contacts from all walks of life, but the intervening years have seen those relationships strained. You may use any feature of any other background, but once a particular feature is used, that feature can't be used again until one year has passed.

entries.name: Background Feat
entries: As a further embodiment of the experience and training of your background, you can choose from the following feats:

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: The trials and triumphs of retired adventurers have left an impact, shaping their ideals, creating strong bonds, and often leaving them scarred and vulnerable to fear, shame, and hatred.

rows: I'm haunted by memories of war. I can't get the images of violence out of my mind.
I've lost too many friends, and I'm slow to make new ones.
I'm full of inspiring and cautionary tales from my adventuring experience relevant to almost every combat situation.
I can stare down a rancor without flinching.
I enjoy being strong and like breaking things.
I have a crude sense of humor.
I face problems head-on. A simple, direct solution is the best path to success.
{@b Greater Good.} Our lot is to lay down our lives in defense of others. (Light)
{@b Responsibility.} I do what I must and obey just authority. (Lawful)
{@b Independence.} When people follow orders blindly, they embrace a kind of tyranny. (Chaotic)
{@b Might.} In life as in war, the stronger force wins. (Dark)
{@b Live and Let Live.} Ideals aren't worth killing over or going to war for. (Neutral)
{@b Nation.} My city, nation, or people are all that matter. (Any)
I would still lay down my life for the people I adventured with.
Someone saved my life when they could have left me. To this day, I will never leave a friend behind.
I'll never forget the crushing defeat my party suffered or the enemies who dealt it.
Those who fight beside me are those worth dying for.
I fight for those who cannot fight for themselves.
The monstrous enemy we faced in battle still leaves me quivering with fear.
I have little respect for anyone who is not a proven adventurer.
I made a terrible mistake in battle cost many lives— and I would do anything to keep that mistake secret.
My hatred of my enemies is blind and unreasoning.
I obey the law, even if the law causes misery.
I'd rather eat my armor than admit when I'm wrong.

entries.name: Urchin
entries: You grew up on the streets alone, orphaned, and poor. You had no one to watch over you or to provide for you, so you learned to provide for yourself. You fought fiercely over food and kept a constant watch out for other desperate souls who might steal from you. You slept on rooftops and in alleyways, exposed to the elements, and endured sickness without the {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} of medicine or a place to recuperate. You've survived despite all odds, and did so through cunning, strength, {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}, or some combination of each.

You begin your adventuring career with enough money to live modestly but securely for at least ten days. How did you come by that money? What allowed you to break free of your desperate circumstances and embark on a better life?

items: {@b Skill Proficiencies:} Choose two from {@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}, Sleight of Hand, and {@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}
{@b Tool Proficiencies:} {@item Disguise kit|sw5e-phb}, {@item Security kit|sw5e-phb|security kit}
{@b Equipment:} A small knife, a map of the city you grew up in, a pet mouse, a token to remember your parents by, a set of common clothes, and a belt pouch containing 100 cr

entries.name: Feature: City of Secrets
entries: You know the secret patterns and flows to cities and can find passages through the urban sprawl that others would miss. When you are not in combat, you (and companions you lead) can travel between any two locations in the city twice as fast as your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} would normally allow.

entries.name: Background Feat
entries: As a further embodiment of the experience and training of your background, you can choose from the following feats:

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Urchins are shaped by lives of desperate poverty, for good and for ill. They tend to be driven either by a commitment to the people with whom they shared life on the street or by a burning desire to find a better life— and maybe get some payback on all the rich people who treated them badly.

rows: I hide scraps of food and trinkets away in my pockets.
I ask a lot of questions.
I like to squeeze into small places where no one else can get to me.
I sleep with my back to a wall or tree, with everything I own wrapped in a bundle in my arms.
I eat like a pig and have bad manners.
I think anyone who's nice to me is hiding Dark intent.
I bluntly say what other people are hinting at or hiding.
{@b Respect.} All people, rich or poor, deserve respect. (Light)
{@b Community.} We have to take care of each other, because no one else is going to do it. (Lawful)
{@b Change.} The low are lifted up, and the high and mighty are brought down. Change is the nature of things. (Chaotic)
{@b Retribution.} The rich need to be shown what life and death are like in the gutters. (Dark)
{@b People.} I help the people who help me—that's what keeps us alive. (Neutral)
{@b Aspiration.} I'm going to prove that I'm worthy of a better life. (Any)
My town or city is my home, and I'll fight to defend it.
I sponsor an orphanage to keep others from enduring what I was forced to endure.
I owe my survival to another urchin who taught me to live on the streets.
I owe a debt I can never repay to the person who took pity on me.
I escaped my life of poverty by robbing an important person, and I'm wanted for it.
No one else should have to endure the hardships I've been through.
If I'm outnumbered, I will run away from a fight.
Gold seems like a lot of money to me, and I'll do just about anything for more of it.
I will never fully trust anyone other than myself.
I'd rather kill someone in their sleep then fight fair.
It's not stealing if I need it more than someone else.
People who can't take care of themselves get what they deserve.

data.name: Customization Options
entries: he combination of ability scores, species, class, and         background defines your character's capabilities in the game, and the personal details you create set your character apart from every other character. Even within your class and species, you have options to fine-tune what your character can do. But this chapter is for players who—with the GM's permission—want to go a step further.

This chapter expands on feats, which are special options you can choose instead of increasing your ability scores as you gain levels. Your GM decides whether these options are available in a campaign.

entries.name: Fighting Styles and Masteries
entries: Wretched Hives introduces new ammunition types, such as the specialized {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, or rockets. You'll want to extend the benefits of certain Fighting Styles and Fighting Masteries to these new munitions, as explained below.

entries.name: Explosives Style and Mastery
entries: You will want to extend the benefits of this pair to include charges.

entries.name: Feats
entries: A feat represents a talent or an area of {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} that gives character special capabilities. It embodies training, experience, and abilities beyond what a class provides. At certain levels, your class gives you the Ability Score Improvement feature. Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking that feature to take a feat of your choice instead. You can take each feat only once, unless the feat's description says otherwise.

You must meet any prerequisite specified in a feat to take that feat. If you ever lose a feat's prerequisite, you can't use that feat until you regain the prerequisite. For example, the {@feat Inspiring Leader|sw5e-phb} feat requires you to have a Charisma of 13 or higher. If your Charisma is reduced below 13 somehow—perhaps by a withering curse—you can't benefit from the {@feat Inspiring Leader|sw5e-phb} feat until your Charisma is restored.

entries.name: Spiritual Techcaster
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} The ability to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}} You've developed a transcendent approach to your tech prowess. Choose one from Wisdom or Charisma. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase the chosen ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You can use the chosen ability instead of Intelligence as your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability}.
You can add the chosen ability instead of Intelligence when determining your maximum tech points.

entries.name: Cunning Forcecaster
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} The ability to cast {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}} You've discovered a clever avenue to your study of the Force. Choose one from Wisdom or Charisma. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You can use Intelligence instead of the chosen ability as your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability}.
You can add Intelligence instead of the chosen ability when determining your maximum force points.

entries.name: Auditory Dampening
entries: You've developed resilience against debilitating noises, gaining the following benefits:

items: Increase your Constitution, Intelligence, or Wisdom score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

While you are {@condition Deafened|sw5e-phb|deafened}, you can make {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} that rely on hearing with {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}, instead of automatically failing them.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} made to avoid sonic damage.

entries.name: Chemical Buffer
entries: You're able to neutralize caustic chemicals, mitigating their worst effects. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Dexterity, Constitution, or Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You cannot be disintegrated, and you ignore the first {@condition Corroded|sw5e-phb|corroded} level you receive.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} made to avoid acid damage.

entries.name: Electrical Grounding
entries: You're able to avoid the brunt of electric shocks. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

At the start of each of your turns while {@condition Shocked|sw5e-phb|shocked}, you can choose to have a {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}, or you can choose to be able to take both an action and a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on your turn.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} made to avoid lightning damage.

entries.name: Force Frustrater
entries: You've {@feat Practiced|sw5e-phb|practiced} techniques to resist being manipulated by the Force. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Strength, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
When a creature attempts to move you against your will using a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, the maximum distance it can move you is halved.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} made to avoid force damage.

entries.name: Heat Shielded
entries: You can tolerate extremely hot temperatures. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Dexterity, Consitution, or Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} made to avoid {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion} due to extreme heat, and you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to end the {@condition Ignited|sw5e-phb|ignited} condition on yourself, instead of your action.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} made to avoid fire damage.

entries.name: Metabolic Tolerance
entries: You've developed resilience against many poisons, gaining the following benefits:

items: Increase your Constitution, Intelligence, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
As an action or {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can expend a Hit Die to end the {@condition Poisoned|sw5e-phb|poisoned} condition on yourself.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} made to avoid poison damage.

entries.name: Mindful Meditator
entries: You've learned meditation techniques to calm your mind. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

You only need 3 hours of sleep during a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} to gain its benefits, instead of 6. Additionally, if your {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} would be interrupted, you only need to complete the {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} instead of restarting it to gain its benefits.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} made to avoid psychic damage.

entries.name: Vigorous Virility
entries: Thanks to the strength of your vitality, you gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Constitution, Intelligence, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
As an action, you can expend a Hit Die to end the {@condition Weakened|sw5e-phb|weakened} condition on yourself.

Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, when you complete a {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest}, you can expend a Hit Die to remove 1 level of {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion}.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} made to avoid necrotic damage.

entries.name: Well-Insulated
entries: You can tolerate extremely cold temperatures. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Dexterity, Constitution, or Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} made to avoid {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion} due to extreme cold, and each {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level only reduces your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} by 5 feet, unless it would reduce your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} to 0.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} made to avoid cold damage.

entries.name: Exotic Weapon Training
entries: Mastery of simple and {@filter Martial weapons|items|type=martial weapon} has unlocked new potential for you. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

You gain proficiency in three exotic weapons. You must have proficiency in all simple and {@filter Martial weapons|items|type=martial weapon} in the exotic weapon's category to gain proficiency in it. If the exotic has modes that would fall in two different weapon categories, you require proficiency all simple and {@filter Martial weapons|items|type=martial weapon} in both categories in order to gain proficiency in that exotic.

entries.name: Total Reconstruction
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Type beast or humanoid} You are more machine than man. While repaired in a similar configuration as your own species, you are subject to the following changes:

items: Increase an ability score of your choice by 1, to a maximum of 20.
Choose one class of droid (class I-V or tracker). You count as the chosen creature type in addition to your other type.
You are resistant to necrotic and poison damage, and are immune to poison and disease.
You do not need to eat or drink. Additionally, you no longer require a tech focus to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

You are vulnerable to ion damage. Additionally, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against effects that would deal ion or lightning damage.
You can not sense the Force, use {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, or take levels in {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} classes.
You are no longer a valid target for cybernetic augmentations or genetic mutations. However, you are now a valid target for droid customizations.

entries.name: Double-Weapon Casting
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 4th level, the ability to cast force or tech  powers} You've learned to blend your prowess with twinblades with your casting. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

When you use your action to Cast a Power that calls for a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} and attack with a weapon with the light and double properties while wielding it in two hands, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to engage in Double-Weapon Fighting. All the rules of Double-Weapon Fighting still apply to you.

entries.name: Two-Weapon Casting
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 4th level, the ability to cast force or tech  powers} You've learned to better combine your dual wielding with your powers. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

When you use your action to Cast a Power that calls for a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} and attack with a light weapon that you're holding in one hand, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to engage in Two-Weapon Fighting. All the rules of Two-Weapon Fighting still apply to you.

entries.name: Dutifully Deployed
entries: You've developed an aptitude for a particular deployment on a starship. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase an ability score of your choice by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You gain 1 rank in a deployment of your choice. This rank does not count towards or affect your prestige.
The maximum number of ranks you can gain in deployments increases by 1. You can still only gain 5 ranks in a deployment.

entries.name: Adaptable Fading
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 4th level} You can easily overthrow an enemy's fortitude. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Strength or Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

When you make an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} using your Strength, you can choose to add half your Constitution modifier to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}. Alternatively, when you would make an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} using Constitution, you can add half your Strength modifier to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain all expended uses of this feature when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

When an effect you control would call for a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can instead have it call for a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. Alternatively, when an effect you control would call for a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can instead have it call for a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain all expended uses of this feature when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Flexible Rending
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 4th level} You are adept at overwhelming an opponent's reflexes. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Dexterity or Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

When you make an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} using your Dexterity, you can choose to add half your Intelligence modifier to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}. Alternatively, when you would make an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} using Intelligence, you can add half your Dexterity modifier to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain all expended uses of this feature when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

When an effect you control would call for a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can instead have it call for a Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. Alternatively, when an effect you control would call for a Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can instead have it call for a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain all expended uses of this feature when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Versatile Withering
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 4th level} You have learned to easily overcome an adversary's will. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Wisdom or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

When you make an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} using your Wisdom, you can choose to add half your Charisma modifier to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}. Alternatively, when you would make an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} using Charisma, you can add half your Wisdom modifier to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain all expended uses of this feature when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

When an effect you control would call for a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can instead have it call for a Charisma {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. Alternatively, when an effect you control would call for a Charisma {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can instead have it call for a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain all expended uses of this feature when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Improved Force-Sensitive
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} The ability to cast 2nd-level {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}} You know one at-will {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}. Additionally, you know one 3rd-level {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, which you can cast once per {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. Your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} is Wisdom or Charisma (depending on power alignment).

entries.name: Greater Force-Sensitive
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} The ability to cast 3rd-level {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}} You know one at-will {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}. Additionally, you know one 4th-level {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, which you can cast once per {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. Your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} is Wisdom or Charisma (depending on power alignment).

entries.name: Master Force-Sensitive
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} The ability to cast 4th-level {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}} You know one at-will {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}. Additionally, you know one 5th-level {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, which you can cast once per {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. Your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} is Wisdom or Charisma (depending on power alignment).

entries.name: Improved Tech Dabbler
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} The ability to cast 2nd-level {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}} You know one at-will {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. Additionally, you know one 3rd-level {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, which you can cast once per {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. Your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} is Intelligence. You require use of a {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad} for these powers.

entries.name: Greater Tech Dabbler
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} The ability to cast 3rd-level {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}} You know one at-will {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. Additionally, you know one 4th-level {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, which you can cast once per {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. Your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} is Intelligence. You require use of a {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad} for these powers.

entries.name: Master Tech Dabbler
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} The ability to cast 4th-level {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}} You know one at-will {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. Additionally, you know one 5th-level {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, which you can cast once per {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. Your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} is Intelligence. You require use of a {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad} for these powers.

entries.name: Companion Keeper
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 4th level} You gain the services of a companion. Choose one of the companion nature options, detailed later in this chapter.

entries.name: Close Quarters Caster
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 4th level, the ability to cast force or tech  powers} You've {@feat Practiced|sw5e-phb|practiced} utilizing powers in close quarters, learning techniques that grant you the following benefits:

items: When making a ranged force or tech attack while you are within 5 feet of a hostile creature, you do not have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}.
Your ranged force and tech attacks ignore {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|half cover} and three-quarters {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} against targets within 30 feet of you.

You learn one at-will power that requires an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}. Your casting ability for this at-will power depends on the power list you chose from: Wisdom or Charisma (depending on power alignment) for {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} or Intelligence for {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

entries.name: Combat Caster
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 4th level, the ability to cast force or tech  powers} You've {@feat Practiced|sw5e-phb|practiced} making your powers more difficult to avoid, learning techniques that grant you the following benefits:

items: When a creature rolls a 1 on the {@dice d20} roll of a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against a power you cast that deals damage, they instead take the highest number possible for the damage die.

You learn one at-will power that requires a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. Your casting ability for this at-will power depends on the power list you chose from: Wisdom or Charisma (depending on power alignment) for {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} or Intelligence for {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

entries.name: Dual Focused Caster
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 4th level, the ability to cast force or tech  powers} You have learned to bifurcate your attention while concentrating on powers, learning techniques that grant you the following benefits:

items: If you attempt to cast a power that requires {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} while already concentrating on an existing power, you can maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} on both powers simultaneously. You must spend your action each subsequent round on maintaining this {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}, or lose {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} for both powers.

At the end of each of your turns where you have two powers you are concentrating on, you must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC equals 10 + the number of complete rounds you've been concentrating on two powers). On a failure, you lose {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} for both powers. You can drop {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} on one of your powers during your turn as a free action to avoid this {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

Any time you would be forced to make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} due to taking damage, the DC equals 10 + both powers' levels combined, or half the damage you take, whichever number is higher. On a failure, you lose {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} on both powers.

entries.name: Mounted Caster
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 4th level, the ability to cast force or tech  powers} You are trained in the use of powers while mounted. While you are mounted and aren't {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated}, you gain the following benefits:

items: When you cast a power targeting yourself, you can also affect your mount with the power.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on melee force or tech {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against any unmounted creature that is smaller than your mount.

If your mount is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and only half damage if it fails.

entries.name: Quick Caster
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 4th level, the ability to cast force or tech  powers} You've {@feat Practiced|sw5e-phb|practiced} casting powers in quick succession, learning techniques that grant you the following benefits:

items: When you cast a power with a casting time of a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you may use your action to cast a power with a power level no higher than half your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} (rounded down).

When you cast a power with a casting time of a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can cast it without expending force or tech points as long as it is no higher level than your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. Once you've used this feature, you must complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Sniping Caster
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 4th level, the ability to cast force or tech  powers} You've {@feat Practiced|sw5e-phb|practiced} casting powers more accurately from long range, learning techniques that give you the following benefits:

items: When you cast a power that requires you to make an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, the power's range is doubled.
Your ranged force and tech attacks ignore one-quarter, half, and three-quarters {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}.

You learn one at-will power that requires an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}. Your casting ability for this at-will power depends on the power list you chose from: Wisdom or Charisma (depending on power alignment) for {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} or Intelligence for {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

entries.name: War Caster
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 4th level, the ability to cast force or tech  powers} You've {@feat Practiced|sw5e-phb|practiced} casting powers in the midst of combat, learning techniques that grant you the following benefits:

items: You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} that you make to maintain your {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} on a power when you take damage.

Once per round, when a hostile creature provokes an {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attack} from you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to cast a power at the creature, rather than making an {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attack}. The power must have a casting time of 1 action and must target only that creature.

entries.name: Casting Specialist
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 4th level, the ability to cast force or tech  powers} Choose one from force- or tech-casting. You've mastered your chosen casting type, gaining the following benefits:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to your force or tech save DC and your force or tech attack modifier.

Once per turn, when you cast a power that requires an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or you can force one creature affected by the power to have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} or {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (your choice). Once you've used this feature on a power, you can't affect that power again until you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. Once you've used this feature on a creature, you can't do so again until you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

Once per turn, when you cast a power that doesn't require an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, but requires a die roll, you can choose the maximum or minimum on the die (your choice). If the power requires rolling multiple dice, you can only affect a number of them equal to half your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} (rounded up) in this way. Once you've used this feature on a power, you can't affect that power again until you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries: You can select this feat twice. Each time you do so, you must choose a different casting type.

entries.name: Ability Capstone Feats
entries: At higher levels, character tend to reach the pinnacle of an ability score, representing their mastery of that aspect. These feats are designed to give those characters an edge greater than just the ability score.

entries.name: Titan's Power
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 12th level, Strength 20} You have the strength that legends tell of, granting the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. If you are already proficient in them, you instead gain {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in them.
You ignore the two-handed property of weapons with which you are proficient.
When you miss with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, the creature takes damage equal to your Strength modifier. This damage is of the same type as the weapon's damage.

entries.name: Blinding Agility
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 12th level, Dexterity 20} You have the reflexes one who can see things before they happen, granting the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. If you are already proficient in them, you instead gain {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in them.
Weapons that lack the two-handed or special properties are considered to have {@itemProperty SWF|sw5e-phb|the finesse property} for you.
Opportunity attacks made against you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.

entries.name: Unnatural Resilience
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 12th level, Constitution 20} You have the fortitude often attributed to gods, granting the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. If you are already proficient in them, you instead gain {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in them.

Enhanced effects, such as powers or medpacs, that would restore {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} to you can't restore an amount less than half your level + your Constitution modifier. If this amount would exceed that maximum amount of {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} that effect could restore, you instead take that effect's maximum.
You can add your Constitution modifier to {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throws} you make.

entries.name: Cunning Intellect
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 12th level, Intelligence 20} You have the cunning of the most prolific scholars, granting the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. If you are already proficient in them, you instead gain {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in them.

When you engage in the Training downtime activity, during resolution, you add your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} to the check. If you would already add your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, you instead add twice your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. If you would already add twice your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, you instead have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the check.

Whenever you make an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} that uses your Intelligence, you can add half your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} (rounded down) if it doesn't already include your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. Additionally, if you roll lower than half your level (rounded down) on an Intelligence check, you can instead use your level for the {@dice d20} roll.

entries.name: Exalted Awareness
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 12th level, Wisdom 20} You have the wisdom associated with the most renowned masters of the Force, granting the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. If you are already proficient in them, you instead gain {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in them.
Creatures within 60 feet of you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) checks made to hide from you.

As an action, you can sense the presence of illusions and other effects designed to {@optfeature Deceive|sw5e-phb|deceive} the senses within 30 feet of you, provided that you aren't {@condition Blinded|sw5e-phb|blinded} or {@condition Deafened|sw5e-phb|deafened}. You sense that an effect is trying to trick you, but you gain no insight into what is hidden or its true nature. Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Overwhelming Presence
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 12th level, Charisma 20} You have the presence of the most affluent of leaders, granting the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in Charisma {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. If you are already proficient in them, you instead gain {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in them.

While you are conscious, up to five friendly creatures within 30 feet of you who can see or hear you and who can understand you can gain a bonus to one Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} they make equal to your Charisma modifier. Once they've done so, they can't do so again until they finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

As an action, you can attempt to distract up to five creatures you can see within 30 feet of you. Each creature must make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Charisma modifier). Any creature immune to being {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} is unaffected. If you or your companions are fighting a creature, it has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, for the next minute, a creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) checks made to perceive any creature other than you until the effect ends or until the target can no longer see or hear you. This ends early if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die.

entries.name: Companions
entries: A companion is a creature who accompanies you on your adventures. It might take the form of a fearsome beast, a padawan learner, a droid sidekick, or a mischievous spirit. Some companions are an integral part of an archetype, while others are simple NPCs that characters encounter and adopt during their adventures.

entries.name: Companions
entries: In Your Game

Companions are not for the faint of heart. They add a significant power boost to a party, and can really bog down your game if their player's are not prepared. You might choose to allow your players to use the companion archetypes, but not the feats, vice versa, both options, or none. It's up to you. {@b {@i Starting Equipment.}} Companions generally don't start with any equipment, so it's up to the player to gear their companion. For the sake of modesty, humanoid companion should probably start with a set of basic clothing, as appropriate. {@b {@i Downtime Activities.}} Companions should not be able to perform downtime activities separately from their player's character. However, companions should be able to help others perform their downtime activities. Additionally, a player can choose to have their companion perform a downtime activity, though their character must spend their downtime helping the companion. {@b {@i Encounter Building and Experience Allocation.}} A companion's level matches that of their owner, so they do not need to gain experience. However, you should consider treating a companion as half a character when building encounters and distributing experience. For instance, if your party is three characters and one companion, you should generate encounters and divide experience gained 3.5 ways, instead of simply three ways. {@b {@i Enhanced Items.}} Companions should not count towards party size when allocating enhanced items. Additionally, while companion classes share names with their player character class counterparts, companions can not attune to items that require that class. {@b {@i Starships and Deployments.}} Companions can not deploy as pilots, though they can fill other deployments as normal. Additionally, companions can gain deployment ranks, though they accrue prestige at half the rate of player characters, and they can not exceed 4 ranks in a deployment.

entries.name: Gaining a Companion
entries: Certain archetypes, such as the Astrotech Engineer, Saboteur Operative, or Zoologist Scholar, have their companions as the focus of their archetype's features. Alternatively, a companion can be gained through taking the Companion Keeper feat, detailed later in this chapter.
Regardless of how a companion is obtained, each player may have no more than one companion at a given time.

entries.name: Generating Your Companion
entries: First, you should determine your companion's nature and appearance, as determined by your archetype feature or chosen from the list of companion natures if you take the Companion Keeper feat. Second, allocate your companion's ability scores, as determined by its nature. Finally, you should generate your companion from 1st level using the follower class, and increase its level one level at a time, until its level equals your own. Be sure to update your companion's {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, ability scores, {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, and any features it gains as it levels.

entries.name: Companion Nature
entries: Your companion's nature, discussed later in this chapter, is determined by your archetype feature or companion feat. Your companion's nature determines its type, its {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} and Hit Dice, its proficiencies and other features, and its companion traits. At 1st level, your companion starts with two traits. It gains additional traits when it reaches higher levels, as shown in the follower table.

entries.name: Class and Features
entries: Your companion gains features when it reaches certain levels, as shown in the follower table.

entries.name: Leveling Your Companion
entries: Your companion's level equals your own, and each time you gain a level, so does your companion.

entries.name: Proficiency Bonus
entries: Your companion's {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} is equal to that of a player character of the same level, as shown in the follower table.

entries.name: Starting Equipment
entries: Generally speaking, companions are not intended to start with any equipment; it is up to you to outfit them as you deem appropriate. Humanoid companions should probably at least have clothing, however.

entries.name: Companions in Combat
entries: In combat, companions generally behave as a player character would, with the following differences.

entries.name: Actions in Combat
entries: Unless you use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to direct your companion, your companion can only use its action to Dash, Dodge, Disengage, Guard, or Hide.

entries.name: Companion Initiative
entries: Both you and your companion roll {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative}, but you act together on the lesser of the two results. You act on one turn, and you can each move or take actions in any order.

entries.name: Companion Natures
entries: Certain class features grant a specific companion nature, while the Companion Keeper feat offers your choice of companion nature. You must meet a companion nature's requirement in order to choose that companion. You may only have one active companion at a time.

entries.name: Alternative Companion {@skill Nature|sw5e-phb}
entries: Your archetype feature may grant you one type of companion, whereas your character can be better realized utilizing a different companion. For instance, an astrotech engineer might prefer to have a tracker droid over one of the larger droid options. Work with your GM to determine if a different companion is better suited, and mechanically appropriate, to your character's identity.
You may choose your companion's nature from the following options or roll on the table below to determine it randomly.
If you determine your companion's nature randomly, and the result is a nature for which you are ineligible, simply reroll until you get a proper result.

If your companion is irreparably destroyed, or you want a different companion, you must first break the bond with your current companion. Bonding with a new companion takes 8 hours spent in an appropriate location. You may only have one companion at a time. If you want to change your companion nature, as with the Alternative Companions feature above.

entries.name: Aberrant Companion
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Proficient with alchemy kits}
Aberrant companions are part of a WIP scholar archetype.

entries.name: Beast Companion
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Proficiency in {@skill Animal Handling|sw5e-phb}} Through spending time in the wilderness or discovering a forlorn creature in a foreign environment, you gain the loyalty of a beast companion.

entries.name: Droid Companion
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Proficiency with {@item Astrotech's implements|sw5e-phb|astrotech's implements}} Through creation of your own or capture of another, you gain the services of a droid companion.

entries.name: Humanoid Companion
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Proficiency in {@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb} or {@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}} Through menacing or recruitment, you gain the fidelity of a humanoid companion.

entries.name: Spirit Companion
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Discovery of a spirit's essence} Through happenstance or misfortune, you gain the curiosity of a spirit companion.
Spirits don't exist yet, but they will as a part of the Path of Communion sentinel rework c. 2023.

entries.name: Thrall Companion
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} The ability to cast {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}}
Undead thralls are part of a WIP consular archetype.

entries.name: Tracker Droid Companion
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} The ability to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}} Through fabrication of your own or purchase from a vendor, you gain the assistance of a tracker droid companion.

entries.name: Turret Companion
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Proficiency with artillerist's kit} Through construction of your own or coopting someone else's, you gain the use of a turret companion.

entries.name: Beast Companion
entries: Your beast takes a form of your choosing. Alternatively, your GM can choose what form your beast takes based on your environment. Once you've chosen your beast's appearance, you assign your beast companion's ability scores. Your beast's Intelligence score is 6, and you assign its other ability scores using a standard array (16, 14, 12, 10, 8) as you see fit.

entries.name: Beast Features
entries: All beasts share the following traits.

items: {@b Hit Dice:} 1d4 per beast companion level
{@b Hit Points at 1st Level:} 4 + your beast's Constitution modifier
{@b Hit Points at Higher Levels:} 1d4 (or 3) + your beast's Constitution modifier per beast level after 1st
{@b Languages:} Your beast can understand simple commands spoken in two languages of your choice, as well as hand signals, but it can not speak
{@b Armor Class:} Your beast's {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb|armor class} equals 10 + its Dexterity modifier.
{@b Barding:} Your beast requires proficiency in armor in order to have it made into barding for them, and if the your beast's size increases, the barding must be upgraded accordingly.
{@b Natural Weapon:} Your beast companion attacks with a natural weapon, such as claws or a bite, with which it is proficient. On a hit, it deals 1d4 kinetic damage.

{@b Attitude:} The beast obeys your commands as best it can. It acts on your turn, and you determine its actions, decisions, attitudes, and so on. If you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or absent, your beast acts on its own.

entries.name: Bestial Traits
entries: The traits are presented in alphabetical order. If a trait has prerequisites, your companion must meet them to adopt it. Your companion can adopt a trait at the same time that it meets the trait's prerequisites. Whenever your companion gains a level, it can exchange one trait for another one.

entries.name: Aerial
entries: Your companion has a flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to its walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}, and {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks} made against it have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.

entries.name: Amphibious
entries: Your companion has a swimming {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to its walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}, and it can breathe air and water.

entries.name: Burrower
entries: Your companion has a burrowing {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to its walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}, and it has {@sense Blindsight|sw5e-phb|blindsight} out to 10 feet.

entries.name: Charger
entries: If your companion moves at least half its {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} straight towards a target before making a melee attack, it deals an additional 1d8 damage on a hit.

entries.name: Climber
entries: Your companion has a climbing {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to its walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}, and it has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} and Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) checks that involve climbing.

entries.name: Closed Mind
entries: Your companion has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Wisdom and Charisma {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: Your companion is accustomed to low-light environments. Your companion can see in dim light within 60 feet as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. Your companion can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

entries.name: Evasive
entries: Your companion can take the {@action Disengage|sw5e-phb} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Force Adept
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Force Sensitive} Your companion learns one 2nd-level {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of your choice, and once per {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} it can cast it at 2nd-level without expending force points. Your companion's {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} is Wisdom or Charisma (depending on power alignment).

entries.name: Force Contention
entries: Your companion has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Strength and Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

entries.name: Force-Sensitive
entries: Your companion learns one at-will {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} and one 1st-level {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, which it can cast at its lowest level once per {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. Your companion's {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} is Wisdom or Charisma (depending on power alignment). At-will powers chosen by your companion do not scale normally at higher levels. Instead, if they would scale at 5th level, they instead scale at 11th level, and if they would scale at 11th level, they instead scale at 17th level.

entries.name: Grappler
entries: When your companion hits with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, it can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to attempt to grapple the target. On a success, the target is both {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} and {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained}, and your companion can't attack again while it has a creature {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled}.

entries.name: Heavy Hide
entries: Your companion's {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb|armor class} becomes 14.

entries.name: Keen Hearing
entries: Your companion has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) checks that rely on hearing.

entries.name: Keen Sight
entries: Your companion has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) checks that rely on sight.

entries.name: Keen Smell
entries: Your companion has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) checks that rely on smell.

entries.name: Light Hide
entries: Your companion's {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb|armor class} becomes 11 + its Dexterity modifier.

entries.name: Medium Hide
entries: Your companion's {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb|armor class} becomes 13 + its Dexterity modifier, to a maximum of +2.

entries.name: Natural Camouflage
entries: When your companion attempts to hide, it can opt to not move on its turn. If it avoids moving, it is considered lightly obscured until it moves.

entries.name: Nimble Reflexes
entries: Your companion has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Dexterity and Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

entries.name: Nimble Weapon
entries: Your companion's natural weapon gains {@itemProperty SWF|sw5e-phb|the finesse property}.

entries.name: Pack Tactics
entries: Your companion has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against a creature if at least one ally of your companion is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated}.

entries.name: Pouncer
entries: If your companion moves at least half its {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} straight toward a creature and hits it with a melee attack, the creature must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your companion's {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + its Strength modifier). If the creature is larger than your companion, it makes this save with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}. On a failed save, the creature is knocked {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}, and your companion can make one additional attack against it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Powerful Build
entries: Your companion's carrying capacity and the weight it can push, drag, or lift doubles. If it would already double, it instead triples.

entries.name: Rampager
entries: If your companion reduces a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} with a melee attack on its turn, your companion can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to move up to half its {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} and make a melee attack.

entries.name: Ranged Weapon
entries: Your companion has a natural ranged weapon, such as a spitter or tail spikes. It has a normal range of 30 feet and a long range of 90 feet, and on a hit it deals kinetic damage equal to its natural weapon damage die.

entries.name: Reach Weapon
entries: Your companion has a natural weapon with reach, such as a tail or wings. It has the reach property, and on a hit it deals kinetic damage equal to its natural weapon damage die.

entries.name: Size: Huge
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 9th level} {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Size Large} Your companion's size is Huge. Its {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} increase by an amount equal to its level + 1, its Hit Die becomes a {@dice d12}, its natural weapon damage die becomes a {@dice d12}, and its walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} increases to 40.

entries.name: Size: Large
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Size Medium} Your companion's size is Large. Its {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} increase by an amount equal to its level + 1, its Hit Die becomes a {@dice d10}, its natural weapon damage die becomes a {@dice d10}, and its walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} increases to 35.

entries.name: Size: Medium
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Size Small} Your companion's size is Medium. Its {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} increase by an amount equal to its level + 1, its Hit Die becomes a {@dice d8}, its natural weapon damage die becomes a {@dice d8}, and its walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} increases to 30.

entries.name: Size: Small
entries: Your companion's size is Small. Its {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} increase by an amount equal to its level + 1, its Hit Die becomes a {@dice d6}, its natural weapon damage die becomes a {@dice d6}, and its walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} increases to 25.

entries.name: Sturdy-Legged
entries: Your companion's long jump is up to 20 feet and its high jump is up to 10 feet, with or without a running start, and it has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Strength and Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} made against effects that would knock it prone.

entries.name: Swift
entries: Your companion can take the {@action Dash|sw5e-phb} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Tremorsense
entries: Your companion gains {@sense Tremorsense|sw5e-phb|tremorsense} out to 30 feet.

entries.name: Venomous Weapon
entries: When your companion deals damage to a creature with its natural weapon, it must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your companion's {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your companion's Constitution modifier) or become {@condition Poisoned|sw5e-phb|poisoned} until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Droid Companion
entries: Your droid takes a form of your choosing. The class of droid you choose determines its features. Once you've selected your type of droid class, you assign your droid's ability scores using standard array (16, 14, 14, 12, 10, 8) as you see fit.

entries.name: Droid Features
entries: All droids share the following features.

items: {@b Droid Resistances:} Your droid is resistant to necrotic, poison, and psychic damage, and immune to poison and disease.

{@b Droid Vulnerabilities:} Your droid is vulnerable to ion damage. Additionally, your droid has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against effects that would deal ion or lightning damage.
{@b Armor Class:} Your droid's {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb|armor class} equals 10 + its Dexterity modifier.

{@b Armor Integration:} Your droid can not wear armor, but it can have the armor professionally integrated into its chassis over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. This work must be done by someone proficient with {@item Astrotech's implements|sw5e-phb|astrotech's implements}. Your droid must be proficient in armor in order to have it integrated.
{@b Droid Systems:} Your droid does not need to eat or drink. Additionally, your droid does not require a tech focus to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.
{@b Force Insensitive:} Your droid can not use {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} or take levels in {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} classes.

{@b Maintenance Mode:} Rather than sleep, your droid must spend 3 hours performing routine maintenance during a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} to gain its benefits, during which it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) checks. Additionally, if your droid's {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} would be interrupted, it only needs to complete the {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} instead of restarting it.

{@b Attitude:} The droid obeys your commands as best it can. It acts on your turn, and you determine its actions, decisions, attitudes, and so on. If you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or absent, your droid acts on its own.

entries.name: Class I Droid
entries: Class I droids, programmed for the mathematical, medical, or physical sciences, are subcategorized as medical droids, biological science droids, physical science droids, and mathematics droids.
As a class I droid, your droid companion has the following features.

items: {@b Hit Points at 1st Level:} 8 + your droid's Constitution modifier
{@b Hit Points at Higher Levels:} 1d8 (or 5) + your droid's Constitution modifier per droid level after 1st

{@b Languages:} Your droid can speak, read, and write {@language Galactic Basic|sw5e-phb} and one language of your choice. It can understand spoken and written {@language Binary|sw5e-phb|Binary}, but can not speak it.
{@b Skills:} One Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma skill of your choice

entries.name: Class II Droid
entries: Class II droids, programmed for the application of engineering and other technical sciences, are subcategorized as astromech droids, exploration droids, environmental droids, engineering droids, and maintenance droids.
As a class II droid, your droid companion has the following features.

items: {@b Hit Points at 1st Level:} 6 + your droid's Constitution modifier
{@b Hit Points at Higher Levels:} 1d6 (or 4) + your droid's Constitution modifier per droid level after 1st
{@b Tools:} One {@feat Specialist|sw5e-phb|specialist}'s kit of your choice

{@b Languages:} Your droid can speak, read, and write {@language Binary|sw5e-phb|Binary}. It can understand spoken and written {@language Galactic Basic|sw5e-phb} and one language of your choice, but can not speak it.

{@b Undersized:} Your droid's small stature makes it hard for it to wield bigger weapons. Your droid can't use heavy shields. Additionally, it can't use {@filter Martial weapons|items|type=martial weapon} with the two-handed property unless it also has the light property, and if a martial weapon has the versatile property, your droid can only wield it in two hands.

entries.name: Class III Droid
entries: Class III droids, programmed to interact with humans and said to be the most advanced droids ever invented, are subcategorized as protocol droids, servant droids, tutor droids, and child care droids.
As a class III droid, your droid companion has the following features.

items: {@b Hit Points at 1st Level:} 8 + your droid's Constitution modifier
{@b Hit Points at Higher Levels:} 1d8 (or 5) + your droid's Constitution modifier per droid level after 1st
{@b Languages:} Your droid can speak and understand all registered languages

entries.name: Class IV Droid
entries: Class IV droids, programmed for military and security purposes, are subcategorized as assassin droids, battle droids, gladiator droids, and security droids.
As a class IV droid, your droid companion has the following features.

items: {@b Hit Points at 1st Level:} 8 + your droid's Constitution modifier
{@b Hit Points at Higher Levels:} 1d8 (or 5) + your droid's Constitution modifier per droid level after 1st

{@b Languages:} Your droid can speak, read, and write {@language Galactic Basic|sw5e-phb} and one language of your choice. It can understand spoken and written {@language Binary|sw5e-phb|Binary}, but can not speak it.

{@b Armored:} Your droid has proficiency in {@filter light armor|items|type=light armor}. If it would already have proficiency in {@filter light armor|items|type=light armor}, it instead has proficiency in {@filter medium armor|items|type=medium armor}. If it would already have proficiency in light and {@filter medium armor|items|type=medium armor}, it instead has proficiency in {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor}. If it would already have proficiency in all armor, it instead has proficiency in a skill or tool of your choice.

entries.name: Class V Droid
entries: Class V droids, programmed for menial and low-skill tasks, are subcategorized as construction droids, lifting droids, mining droids, sanitation droids, and transportation droids.
As a class V droid, your droid companion has the following features.

items: {@b Hit Points at 1st Level:} 8 + your droid's Constitution modifier
{@b Hit Points at Higher Levels:} 1d8 (or 5) + your droid's Constitution modifier per droid level after 1st
{@b Tools:} One set of artisan's implements

{@b Languages:} Your droid can speak, read, and write {@language Binary|sw5e-phb|Binary}. It can understand spoken and written {@language Galactic Basic|sw5e-phb} and one language of your choice, but can not speak it.

entries.name: Droid Traits
entries: The traits are presented in alphabetical order. If a trait has prerequisites, your companion must meet them to adopt it. Your companion can adopt a trait at the same time that it meets the trait's prerequisites. Whenever your companion gains a level, it can exchange one trait for another one.

entries.name: Alarm Protocol
entries: You install an alarm module in your companion, granting it the following benefits:

items: Your companion gains a +5 bonus to {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative}.
You and your companion can't be surprised while your companion is conscious.

entries.name: Analysis Protocol
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 9th level, Class I Droid} Your companion can {@spell Analyze|sw5e-phb|analyze} a target, develop a plan on how to best overcome any potential obstacle, and execute that plan with ruthless efficiency. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on your companion's turn, your companion can {@spell Analyze|sw5e-phb|analyze} a target it can see within 60 feet of it. For the next minute, or until it analyzes another target, it gains the following benefits:

items: When it analyzes a hostile creature, its attack and damage rolls made with weapons with {@itemProperty SWF|sw5e-phb|the finesse property} or {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} weapons against that target may use its Intelligence modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity.

When it analyzes a friendly creature, the target can end your companion's Analysis Protocol on them (no action required) to add half your companion's Intelligence modifier (rounded down, minimum of +1) to one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. Once a friendly creature has benefited from this ability, they can not do so again until they complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Arm Cannons
entries: You install dual arm cannons in your companion. The arm cannons have 2 charges. As an action, your companion can use charges to cast the {@i overload} {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, using 1 charge per level. The {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} is made against your companion's tech save DC (8 + your companion's {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your companion's Intelligence modifier).

You can choose this trait multiple times. Each time you do so, the arm cannons gain another charge, to a maximum of 4. The arm cannons regain all charges after a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Back-Up Protocol
entries: You install an emergency protocol in your companion, prompting a quick {@spell Reboot|sw5e-phb|reboot} after critical damage is taken. If your companion would be reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, it instead is reduced to 1.
Once your companion uses this feature, it must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before it can use it again.

entries.name: Celerity Augment
entries: You augment your companion to move a little faster. Your companion's {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} increases by 10 feet.

entries.name: Charisma Chip
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Class III Droid} You install a charisma chip in your companion. When an ally your companion can see makes an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, your companion can use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to give them {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the roll. It can do so before or after they roll the {@dice d20}, but before the GM says the roll succeeds or fails. Once your companion uses this ability, it can't use it again until it finishes a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Darkvision Optics
entries: Your companion has {@sense Darkvision|sw5e-phb|darkvision} to a range of 60 feet. If your companion already has {@sense Darkvision|sw5e-phb|darkvision}, this trait increases its range by 30 feet.

entries.name: Durability Module
entries: You enhance your companion's durability, granting the following benefits:

items: When your companion rolls a Hit Die to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, the minimum number of {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} your companion can regain from the roll equals twice your companion's Constitution modifier (minimum of 2).

Your companion's hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to twice its level when you install this protocol. Whenever your companion gains a level thereafter, its hit point maximum increases by an additional 2 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}.

entries.name: Emergency Mode
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Back-Up Protocol} You modify your companion's back-up protocol. When your companion's back-up protocol is initiated, it can use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against a target within range. If the target is the source of the damage that reduced your companion to 0, the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}.

entries.name: Energy Shield
entries: You install an energy shield in your companion, which has 1 charge. As an action, your companion can use 1 charge to cast the {@i energy shield} {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

You can choose this trait multiple times. Each time you do so, the energy shield gains another charge, to a maximum of 3. The energy shield regains all expended charges after a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: False Combustion
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Class II Droid} As a {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} in response to taking damage, your companion can feign an explosion. For 1 minute, it appears to be destroyed to all outward inspection. A creature can use its action to inspect your companion and make an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}) check (DC = 8 + your companion's {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your companion's Intelligence modifier). If it succeeds, it becomes aware that your companion still functions.

entries.name: Fighting Style Protocol
entries: Your companion adopts a particular style of fighting as its specialty. Choose one of the Fighting Style options, detailed in {@book chapter 6|sw5e-phb|6} of the Player's Handbook. Your companion can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if it later gets to choose again.

entries.name: Flamethrower
entries: You install a flamethrower in your companion. The flamethrower has 1 charge. As an action, your companion can cast the {@i jet of flame} {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, though it does not scale with higher levels, or use 1 charge to cast the {@i flame sweep} {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} at 1st level. The {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} is made against your companion's tech save DC (8 + your companion's {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your companion's Intelligence modifier).

You can choose this trait multiple times. Each time you do so, the flamethrower gains another charge, to a maximum of 3. If the flamethrower has multiple charges, you can use multiple charges to cast {@i flame sweep} at a higher level, 1 point per charge.
