As a guardian, your companion gains the following class features.

items: {@b Armor:} {@filter light armor|items|type=light armor}, {@filter medium armor|items|type=medium armor}
{@b Weapons:} {@filter all lightweapons|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}, {@filter all vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon}

{@b Skills:} Choose two from {@skill Acrobatics|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Lore|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Piloting|sw5e-phb}

entries.name: Forcecasting
entries: Beginning when your companion chooses this class at 3rd level, it has learned powers, fragments of knowledge that imbue it with an abiding force ability. See {@book chapter 10|sw5e-phb|10} of the Player's Handbook for the general rules of {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} and {@book chapter 11|sw5e-phb|11} of the Player's Handbook for the {@book force powers list|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

entries.name: Force Powers Known
entries: Your companion learns three {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of its choice of no higher level than its Max Power Level. It may learn a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} at the same time it learns its prerequisite.

At-will powers chosen by your companion do not scale normally at higher levels. Instead, if they would scale at 5th level, they instead scale at 11th level, and if they would scale at 11th level, they instead scale at 17th level.

entries.name: Force Points
entries: Your companion does not require force points. Instead, it can only cast powers at 1st-level twice. It regains all expended uses after completing a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Max Power Level
entries: Your companion's Max Power Level is 1st.

entries.name: Forcecasting Ability
entries: Your companion's {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} varies based on the alignment of the powers you cast. It uses Wisdom for {@book light side powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, Charisma for {@book dark side powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, and Wisdom or Charisma for {@book universal powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} (its choice). It uses this ability score modifier whenever a power refers to its {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability}. Additionally, it uses this ability score modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} it casts and when making an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with one.
{@b Force save DC} = 8 + its {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + its {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} modifier
{@b Force attack modifier} = its {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + its {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} modifier

entries.name: Channel the Force
entries: Also at 3rd level, your companion knows how to channel the Force to create a unique effect. Your companion starts with its choice of one from two such effects: Cause Harm or Lend Aid.
Some Channel the Force effects require {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. When your companion uses such an effect from this class, the DC equals its universal force save DC.

Your companion can use this feature a number of times equal to its Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your companion's choice, minimum of once). Your companion regains all expended uses when it finishes a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Cause Harm
entries: As an action, your companion can expend a use of its Channel the Force to sap the life from a hostile creature it can see within 60 feet. That creature must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the creature takes necrotic damage equal to your companion's level + its Charisma modifier (minimum of one), or half as much on a successful one.

entries.name: Lend Aid
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, your companion can expend a use of its Channel the Force and touch a beast or humanoid within 5 feet of it. That creature regains {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to your companion's guardian level + its Wisdom modifier (minimum of one). Alternatively, if the beast or humanoid is {@condition Poisoned|sw5e-phb|poisoned} or {@condition Diseased|sw5e-phb|diseased}, your companion neutralizes the poison or disease. If more than one poison or disease afflicts the target, your companion neutralizes one poison or disease that it knows is present, or it neutralizes one at random.

entries.name: Apprentice Forcecasting
entries: At 7th level, your companion's Max Power Level increases to 2nd, and it learns three additional powers.
Additionally, your companion can cast powers at 2nd-level twice. It regains all expended uses after completing a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Extra Attack
entries: By 11th level, your companion can attack twice, instead of once, whenever it takes the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on its turn.

entries.name: Force Purity
entries: At 15th level, the Force flowing through your companion makes it immune to poison and disease.

entries.name: Journeyman Forcecasting
entries: As of 18th level, your companion's Max Power Level increases to 3rd, and it learns three additional powers.
Additionally, your companion can cast powers at 3rd-level once. It regains the ability to do so after completing a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Monk
entries: In order to become a monk, your companion must have a Dexterity, Wisdom, or Charisma score of 13 or higher.
As a monk, your companion gains the following class features.

items: {@b Weapons:} {@filter simple blasters|items|firearm=true|weaponcategory=simple}, {@filter simple vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon|weaponcategory=simple}, chakrams, {@item Techblade|sw5e-phb|techblades}
{@b Skills:} Choose two from {@skill Acrobatics|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Lore|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}

entries.name: Martial Arts
entries: Beginning when your companion chooses this class at 3rd level, your companion's practice of martial arts gives it mastery of combat styles that use {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes} and martial artist weapons, which are any {@filter simple vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon|weaponcategory=simple} that don't have the two-handed property.
Your companion gains the following benefits while it is unarmed or wielding only martial artist weapons and isn't wearing armor or wielding a shield:

items: Your companion can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of its {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes} and martial artist weapons.
Your companion can roll a {@dice d4} in place of the normal damage of its unarmed strike or martial artist weapons. This die becomes a {@dice d6} at 7th level and a {@dice d8} at 15th level.
Your companion can use Dexterity instead of Strength whenever it would make a Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) check to grapple, shove, or trip a creature.

When your companion takes the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action with an unarmed strike or a martial artist weapon on your turn, it can make one unarmed strike as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.
Your companion can take the Dash and Disengage actions as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Unarmored Defense
entries: Also at 3rd level, while your companion is wearing no armor and not wielding a shield, its AC equals 10 + its Dexterity modifier + its Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your companion's choice).

entries.name: Focus
entries: At 7th level, your companion's training allows it to harness the mystic energy of focus. Its access to this energy is represented by a number of focus points. Your companion has three focus points. It gains an additional focus point at 9th, 13th, and 17th level.
Your companion can spend these points to fuel various focus features. Your companion knows three such features: Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind.

When your companion spends a focus point, it is unavailable until your companion finishes a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, at the end of which it draws all of its expended focus back into itself. Your companion must spend at least 30 minutes of the rest meditating to regain its focus points.

Some of your companion's focus features require your target to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the feature's effects. The {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC is calculated as follows:
{@b Focus save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice)

entries.name: Flurry of Blows
entries: When your companion makes its Martial Arts {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} unarmed strike, it can spend 1 focus point to make an additional unarmed strike (no action required). At 18 level, it can instead spend 2 focus points to make two additional {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes}.

entries.name: Patient Defense
entries: When your companion uses its {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to Disengage, it can spend 1 focus point to also Dodge (no action required). At 18th level, it can instead spend 2 focus points to Dodge and gain an additional {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} until the start of its next turn. It can only take one {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} per turn.

entries.name: Step of the Wind
entries: When your companion uses its {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to Dash, it can spend 1 focus point to double its jump distance for the turn. At 18th level, it can instead spend 2 focus points to gain a flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to its walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} until the end of your turn, though it falls if it ends its {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} in the air and nothing else is holding it aloft.

entries.name: Enhanced Strikes
entries: Also at 7th level, your companion's {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes} count as enhanced for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to unenhanced attacks and damage.

entries.name: Extra Attack
entries: By 11th level, your companion can attack twice, instead of once, whenever it takes the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on its turn.

entries.name: Evasion
entries: At 15th level, when your companion is subjected to an effect, such as a consular's {@i force storm} or an engineer's {@i explosion}, that allows it to make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to take only half damage, it instead take no damage if it succeeds on a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and only half damage if it fails.

entries.name: Diamond Soul
entries: As of 18th level, your companion gains proficiency in all {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. Additionally, whenever your companion fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, it can spend 1 focus point to reroll it and take the second result.

entries.name: Operative
entries: In order to become an operative, your companion must have a Dexterity or Intelligence score of 13 or higher.
As an operative, your companion gains the following class features.

items: {@b Weapons:} {@filter simple blasters|items|firearm=true|weaponcategory=simple}, {@filter simple vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon|weaponcategory=simple}, {@item Blaster pistol|sw5e-phb}, {@item Hidden blade|sw5e-phb|hidden blade}, {@item Techblade|sw5e-phb}, {@item Vibrorapier|sw5e-phb|vibrorapier}
{@b Tools:} One {@feat Specialist|sw5e-phb|specialist}'s kit of your choice

entries.name: Sneak Attack
entries: Beginning when your companion chooses this class at 3rd level, your companion knows how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, it can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature it hits with an attack if it has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}. The attack must use a finesse or a ranged weapon.

Your companion doesn't need {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn't {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated}, and your companion doesn't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}.
The amount of extra damage increases to 2d6 at 7th level, 3d6 at 11th level, 4d6 at 15th level, and 5d6 at 17th level.

entries.name: Cunning Action
entries: Also at 3rd level, your companion's quick thinking and agility allow it to move and act quickly. Your companion can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on each of its turns in combat. This action can be used only to take the Dash, Disengage, or {@action Hide|sw5e-phb} action.

entries.name: Bad Feeling
entries: At 7th level, your companion has a wary eye, bordering on paranoia. When your companion rolls for {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative}, it can move up to its {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}. This movement happens before the {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} order is determined.
Once your companion has used this feature, it must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before it can use it again.

entries.name: Uncanny Dodge
entries: By 11th level, when an attacker that your companion can see hits it with an attack, your companion can use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to halve the attack's damage against it.

entries.name: Evasion
entries: At 15th level, when your companion is subjected to an effect, such as a consular's {@i force storm} or an engineer's {@i explosion}, that allows it to make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to take only half damage, it instead take no damage if it succeeds on a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and only half damage if it fails.

entries.name: Reliable Talent
entries: As of 18th level, your companion has refined its chosen skills until they approach perfection. Whenever your companion makes an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} that lets it add its {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, it can treat a {@dice d20} roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

entries.name: Scholar
entries: In order to become a scholar, your companion must have an Intelligence score of 13 or higher.
As a scholar, your companion gains the following class features.

items: {@b Weapons:} {@filter simple blasters|items|firearm=true|weaponcategory=simple}, {@filter simple vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon|weaponcategory=simple}, {@item Techblade|sw5e-phb|techblades}

{@b Skills:} Choose three from {@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Lore|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Medicine|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Nature|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Survival|sw5e-phb}

entries.name: Academic Superiority
entries: Beginning when your companion chooses this class at 3rd level, your companion has learned maneuvers that are fueled by special dice called {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}. See {@book chapter 13|sw5e-phb|13} of the Player's Handbook for the {@book maneuvers list|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers}.

entries.name: Maneuvers
entries: Your companion learns two maneuvers of its choice. Many maneuvers enhance an attack in some way. Your companion can use only one maneuver per attack, and it may only use each maneuver once per turn.

Your companion learns an additional maneuver at 5th, 7th, 9th, 11th, 13th, 15th, and 17th level. Each time your companion gains a level, it can also replace one maneuver it knows with a different one.

entries.name: Superiority Dice
entries: Your companion has two {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}, which are d4s. This die increases to a {@dice d6} at 9th level and a {@dice d8} at 17th level. A superiority die is expended when your companion uses it. Your companion regains all of its expended {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} when it finishes a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
Your companion gains an additional superiority die at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level.

entries.name: Maneuver Ability
entries: Your companion's {@book maneuver ability|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} varies based on the type of the maneuver it uses. It uses Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution for {@book physical maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Physical} (its choice), Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma for {@book mental maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Mental} (its choice), and an ability of its choice for {@book general maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|General}. It uses this ability whenever a maneuver refers to its {@book maneuver ability|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}. Additionally, it uses this ability modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a maneuver it uses.
{@b Maneuver save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your {@book maneuver ability|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} modifier

entries.name: Critical Analysis
entries: Also at 3rd level, it is able to {@spell Analyze|sw5e-phb|analyze} a target, develop a plan on how to best overcome any potential obstacle, and execute that plan with ruthless efficiency. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on its turn, your companion can {@spell Analyze|sw5e-phb|analyze} a target it can see within 60 feet of it. For the next minute, or until your companion analyzes another target, it gain the following benefits:

items: When your companion analyzes a hostile creature, its attack and damage rolls made with weapons with {@itemProperty SWF|sw5e-phb|the finesse property} or {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} weapons against that target may use its Intelligence modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity.

When your companion analyzes a friendly creature, the target can end your companion's Critical Analysis on them (no action required) to add your companion's Intelligence modifier to one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. Once a friendly creature has benefited from this ability, they can not do so again until they complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Discoveries
entries: At 7th level, your companion learns two discoveries from those available to the scholar class or any of the scholar's archetypes.

entries.name: Multitasker
entries: By 11th level, your companion can take a second {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} each round. It can only take one {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} per turn.

entries.name: Sage Advice
entries: At 15th level, your companion can spend 1 minute spread its knowledge and experience, advising those around it. When it does so, your companion chooses a skill or tool it is proficient with and a number of friendly creatures up to its Intelligence modifier with 30 feet of it who can hear it and understand it. Once within the next hour, the next time each creature would make an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} with the chosen skill or tool, they may add their {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} to the roll if they are not already proficient. A creature may only benefit from this feature once. If a creature is targeted by this feature again before using it, they can choose to retain the first benefit or replace it with the new skill or tool instead.
Once your companion has used this feature, it must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before it can use it again.

entries.name: Calm and Collected
entries: As of 18th level, when your companion makes a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} caused by an effect it can see, it may gain a bonus to the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} equal to its Intelligence modifier.
Once your companion has used this feature, it must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before it can use it again.

entries.name: Scout
entries: In order to become a scout, your companion must have a Strength, Dexterity, or Intelligence score of 13 or higher.
As a scout, your companion gains the following class features.

items: {@b Armor:} {@filter light armor|items|type=light armor}, {@filter medium armor|items|type=medium armor}
{@b Weapons:} {@filter all blasters|items|firearm=true}, {@filter all vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon}

{@b Skills:} Choose three from {@skill Animal Handling|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Piloting|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Survival|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Technology|sw5e-phb}

entries.name: Techcasting
entries: Beginning when your companion chooses this class at 3rd level, during its training it has derived powers from schematics with the aid of a {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}. See {@book chapter 10|sw5e-phb|10} of the Player's Handbook for the general rules of {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} and {@book chapter 12|sw5e-phb|12} of the Player's Handbook for the {@book tech powers list|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

entries.name: Tech Powers Known
entries: Your companion learns two {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of its choice of no higher level than its Max Power Level.

At-will powers chosen by your companion do not scale normally at higher levels. Instead, if they would scale at 5th level, they instead scale at 11th level, and if they would scale at 11th level, they instead scale at 17th level.

entries.name: Tech Points
entries: Your companion does not require tech points. Instead, it can only cast powers at 1st-level once. It regains the ability to do so after completing a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Max Power Level
entries: Your companion's Max Power Level is 1st.

entries.name: Techcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence is your companion's {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} for its {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. It uses Intelligence whenever a power refers to its {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability}. Additionally, it use its Intelligence modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} it casts and when making an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with one.
{@b Tech save DC} = 8 + its {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + its Intelligence modifier
{@b Tech attack modifier} = its {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + its Intelligence modifier

entries.name: Techcasting Focus
entries: Your companion uses a {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad} (found in {@book chapter 5|sw5e-phb|5} of the Player's Handbook) as a {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} focus for its {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

entries.name: Ranger's Quarry
entries: Also at 3rd level, your companion learns how to effectively read and track its prey. Once on each of its turns, your companion can choose a creature it can see within 120 feet and mark it as its quarry (no action required). For the next hour, your companion gains the following benefits:

items: Once per turn, when your companion hits the target with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}, it can deal 1d4 additional damage to it of the same type as the weapon's damage. This die increases to a {@dice d6} at 7th level and a {@dice d8} at 15th level.

Your companion has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on any Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|sw5e-phb}) check it makes to find the target while it's on the same planet as your companion.

entries: Your companion can only have one creature marked in this way at a time. Beginning at 11th level, your companion can use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to mark a creature when it enters its line of sight, provided it is within range of your companion's Ranger's Quarry.
The duration increases to 8 hours at 11th level.

entries.name: Techcasting, Mark II
entries: At 7th level, your companion's Max Power Level increases to 2nd, and it learns two additional powers.
Additionally, your companion can cast powers at 2nd-level once. It regains the ability to do so after completing a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Extra Attack
entries: By 11th level, your companion can attack twice, instead of once, whenever it takes the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on its turn.

entries.name: Commando
entries: At 15th level, your companion can take the Dash or Hide actions as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on each of its turns. Additionally, it can remain perfectly still for long periods of time to set up ambushes.

When your companion attempts to hide on its turn, it can opt to not move on that turn. If it avoids moving, creatures that attempt to detect it take a -10 penalty to their Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) checks until the start of your companion's next turn. Your companion loses this benefit if it moves or falls {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}, either voluntarily or because of some external effect. It is still automatically detected if any effect or action causes it to no longer be hidden.
If your companion is still hidden on its next turn, it can continue to remain motionless and gain this benefit until it is detected.
Additionally, your companion can no longer be tracked by unenhanced means, unless it chooses to leave a trail.

entries.name: Techcasting, Mark III
entries: As of 18th level, your companion's Max Power Level increases to 3rd, and it learns two additional powers.
Additionally, your companion can cast powers at 3rd-level once. It regains the ability to do so after completing a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Sentinel
entries: In order to become a sentinel, your companion must have a Dexterity, Wisdom, or Charisma score of 13 or higher.
As a sentinel, your companion gains the following class features.

items: {@b Weapons:} Simple {@filter vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon}, {@filter simple lightweapons|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}, {@item Chakram|sw5e-phb|chakram}, {@item Doubleblade|sw5e-phb|doubleblade}, {@item Doublesaber|sw5e-phb|doublesaber}, {@item Doubleshoto|sw5e-phb|doubleshoto}, {@item Doublesword|sw5e-phb|doublesword}, {@item Hidden blade|sw5e-phb|hidden blade}, {@item Lightfoil|sw5e-phb|lightfoil}, light ring, {@item Saberwhip|sw5e-phb|saberwhip}, {@item Vibrorapier|sw5e-phb|vibrorapier}, {@item Vibrowhip|sw5e-phb|vibrowhip}
{@b Tools:} One {@feat Specialist|sw5e-phb|specialist}'s kit of your choice

{@b Skills:} Choose three from {@skill Acrobatics|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Animal Handling|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Piloting|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}, and {@skill Technology|sw5e-phb}

entries.name: Forcecasting
entries: Beginning when your companion chooses this class at 3rd level, it has learned powers, fragments of knowledge that imbue it with an abiding force ability. See {@book chapter 10|sw5e-phb|10} of the Player's Handbook for the general rules of {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} and {@book chapter 11|sw5e-phb|11} of the Player's Handbook for the {@book force powers list|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

entries.name: Force Powers Known
entries: Your companion learns three {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of its choice of no higher level than its Max Power Level. It may learn a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} at the same time it learns its prerequisite.

At-will powers chosen by your companion do not scale normally at higher levels. Instead, if they would scale at 5th level, they instead scale at 11th level, and if they would scale at 11th level, they instead scale at 17th level.

entries.name: Force Points
entries: Your companion does not require force points. Instead, it can only cast powers at 1st-level twice. It regains all expended uses after completing a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Max Power Level
entries: Your companion's Max Power Level is 1st.

entries.name: Forcecasting Ability
entries: Your companion's {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} varies based on the alignment of the powers you cast. It uses Wisdom for {@book light side powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, Charisma for {@book dark side powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, and Wisdom or Charisma for {@book universal powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} (its choice). It uses this ability score modifier whenever a power refers to its {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability}. Additionally, it uses this ability score modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} it casts and when making an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with one.
{@b Force save DC} = 8 + its {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + its {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} modifier
{@b Force attack modifier} = its {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + its {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} modifier

entries.name: Led by the Force
entries: Also at 3rd level, your companion can add half its {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, rounded down, to any {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} it makes that doesn't already include its {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Apprentice Forcecasting
entries: At 7th level, your companion's Max Power Level increases to 2nd, and it learns three additional powers.
Additionally, your companion can cast powers at 2nd-level twice. It regains all expended uses after completing a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Extra Attack
entries: By 11th level, your companion can attack twice, instead of once, whenever it takes the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on its turn.

entries.name: Journeyman Forcecasting
entries: At 15th level, your companion's Max Power Level increases to 3rd, and it learns three additional powers.
Additionally, your companion can cast powers at 3rd-level twice. It regains all expended uses after completing a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Adept Forcecasting
entries: As of 18th level, your companion's Max Power Level increases to 4th, and it learns three additional powers.
Additionally, your companion can cast powers at 4th-level once. It regains the ability to do so after completing a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Torpedo Launcher (Fine)
entries: {@i {@b Weapon} (torpedo launcher), {@b premium}} You have a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} made with this enhanced weapon. Additionally, the damage of torpedoes fired by this weapon increases by one step (from {@dice d4} to {@dice d6}, {@dice d6} to {@dice d8}, {@dice d8} to {@dice d10}, {@dice d10} to {@dice d12}, or {@dice d12} to {@dice d20}). If this would increase the damage die above a {@dice d20}, instead add an additional five dice to the torpedo's damage for each step above a {@dice d20}.

entries.name: Torpedo Launcher (Improved)
entries: {@i {@b Weapon} (torpedo launcher), {@b prototype}} You have a +2 bonus to {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} made with this enhanced weapon. Additionally, the damage of torpedoes fired by this weapon increases by two steps (from {@dice d4} to {@dice d8}, {@dice d6} to {@dice d10}, {@dice d8} to {@dice d12}, or {@dice d10} to {@dice d20}). If this would increase the damage die above a {@dice d20}, instead add an additional five dice to the torpedo's damage for each step above a {@dice d20}.

entries.name: Torpedo Launcher (Superior)
entries: {@i {@b Weapon} (torpedo launcher), {@b advanced}} You have a +3 bonus to {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} made with this enhanced weapon. Additionally, the damage of torpedoes fired by this weapon increases by three steps (from {@dice d4} to {@dice d10}, {@dice d6} to {@dice d12}, or {@dice d8} to {@dice d20}). If this would increase the damage die above a {@dice d20}, instead add an additional five dice to the torpedo's damage for each step above a {@dice d20}.

entries.name: Torpedo, Fragmentation (Average)
entries: {@i {@b Consumable} (ammunition), {@b premium}} You have a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} made with this enhanced torpedo launcher ammunition, which deals 20d6 kinetic damage on a hit. This bonus is in addition to any bonuses granted by the weapon. Once the torpedo is depleted, it no longer gives a bonus.

entries.name: Torpedo, Fragmentation (Major)
entries: {@i {@b Consumable} (ammunition), {@b prototype}} You have a +2 bonus to {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} made with this enhanced torpedo launcher ammunition, which deals 20d8 kinetic damage on a hit. This bonus is in addition to any bonuses granted by the weapon. Once the torpedo is depleted, it no longer gives a bonus.

entries.name: Torpedo, Fragmentation (Deadly)
entries: {@i {@b Consumable} (ammunition), {@b advanced}} You have a +3 bonus to {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} made with this enhanced torpedo launcher ammunition, which deals 20d10 kinetic damage on a hit. This bonus is in addition to any bonuses granted by the weapon. Once the torpedo is depleted, it no longer gives a bonus.

entries.name: Torpedo, Fragmentation (Lethal)
entries: {@i {@b Consumable} (ammunition), {@b legendary}} You have a +3 bonus to {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} made with this enhanced torpedo launcher ammunition, which deals 20d12 kinetic damage on a hit. This bonus is in addition to any bonuses granted by the weapon. Once the torpedo is depleted, it no longer gives a bonus.

entries.name: Torpedo, Fragmentation (Devastating)
entries: {@i {@b Consumable} (ammunition), {@b artifact}} You have a +3 bonus to {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} made with this enhanced torpedo launcher ammunition, which deals 20d20 kinetic damage on a hit. This bonus is in addition to any bonuses granted by the weapon. Once the torpedo is depleted, it no longer gives a bonus.

entries.name: Torpedo, Plasma (Average)
entries: {@i {@b Consumable} (ammunition), {@b premium}} You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this enhanced torpedo launcher ammunition, which deals 20d6 energy damage on a hit. This bonus is in addition to any bonuses granted by the weapon. Once the torpedo is depleted, it no longer gives a bonus.

entries.name: Torpedo, Plasma (Major)
entries: {@i {@b Consumable} (ammunition), {@b prototype}} You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this enhanced torpedo launcher ammunition, which deals 20d8 energy damage on a hit. This bonus is in addition to any bonuses granted by the weapon. Once the torpedo is depleted, it no longer gives a bonus.

entries.name: Torpedo, Plasma (Deadly)
entries: {@i {@b Consumable} (ammunition), {@b advanced}} You have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this enhanced torpedo launcher ammunition, which deals 20d10 energy damage on a hit. This bonus is in addition to any bonuses granted by the weapon. Once the torpedo is depleted, it no longer gives a bonus.

entries.name: Torpedo, Plasma (Lethal)
entries: {@i {@b Consumable} (ammunition), {@b legendary}} You have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this enhanced torpedo launcher ammunition, which deals 20d12 energy damage on a hit. This bonus is in addition to any bonuses granted by the weapon. Once the torpedo is depleted, it no longer gives a bonus.

entries.name: Torpedo, Plasma (Devastating)
entries: {@i {@b Consumable} (ammunition), {@b artifact}} You have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this enhanced torpedo launcher ammunition, which deals 20d20 energy damage on a hit. This bonus is in addition to any bonuses granted by the weapon. Once the power generator is depleted, it no longer gives a bonus.

entries.name: Charge, Fragmentation (Average)
entries: {@i {@b Consumable} (explosive), {@b premium}} A device used to blow holes in larger constructs and structures, a charge creates a devastating explosion focused in a specific direction. Installing a charge takes 1 minute. The charge can be set with a 6-second timer, or detonated remotely using a {@item Remote detonator|sw5e-phb|remote detonator}.

When detonated, the charge explodes in a 15-foot cone. Each creature within the cone must make a DC 16 Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, taking 20d6 kinetic damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one. If affixed to a creature, that creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. Objects, structures, and other surfaces have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. If affixed to the object, structure, or surface, it instead automatically fails this {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

entries.name: Charge, Fragmentation (Major)
entries: {@i {@b Consumable} (explosive), {@b prototype}} A device used to blow holes in larger constructs and structures, a charge creates a devastating explosion focused in a specific direction. Installing a charge takes 1 minute. The charge can be set with a 6-second timer, or detonated remotely using a {@item Remote detonator|sw5e-phb|remote detonator}.

When detonated, the charge explodes in a 15-foot cone. Each creature within the cone must make a DC 18 Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, taking 20d8 kinetic damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one. If affixed to a creature, that creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. Objects, structures, and other surfaces have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. If affixed to the object, structure, or surface, it instead automatically fails this {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

entries.name: Binders (Fine)
entries: {@i {@b Adventuring gear}, {@b premium}} {@item Binders|sw5e-phb} can be used to restrain a Small or Medium creature with appropriate appendages. Applying {@item Binders|sw5e-phb|binders} takes an action, and the target must make a DC 16 Strength or Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (the target chooses the ability to use). A hostile creature makes this save with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}. A set of {@item Binders|sw5e-phb|binders} comes with one key. Breaking the {@item Binders|sw5e-phb|binders} requires a DC 22 Strength check. Escaping them requires a DC 22 Dexterity check. Without the key, unlocking the {@item Binders|sw5e-phb|binders} requires a DC 18 {@item Security kit|sw5e-phb|security kit} to force open. {@item Binders|sw5e-phb} have an AC of 11 and 30 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}. Destroying the {@item Binders|sw5e-phb|binders} frees the creature without harming it.

entries.name: Camtono (Fine)
entries: {@i {@b Adventuring gear}, {@b premium}} A camtono is a secured, handle container used for transporting valuable goods. A camtono comes with one key. Without the key, unlocking the camtono requires a DC 18 {@item Security kit|sw5e-phb|security kit} to force open. It stores 6 lb., not exceeding 1/4 cubic foot, has an AC of 11, and 30 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}. Destroying the camtono risks damaging any goods stored inside.

entries.name: Credit Chip (Fine)
entries: {@i {@b Adventuring gear}, {@b premium}} The {@item Credit|sw5e-phb|credit} chip is a small, flat card that features a security code and algorithm memory stripes. The chip can be preloaded with a specified number of credits, or it can draw directly from a specific account held by the user. The {@item Credit|sw5e-phb|credit} chip can be accessed with a pin, or by a DC 18 {@item Slicer's kit|sw5e-phb|slicer's kit} check.

entries.name: Restraining Bolt (Fine)
entries: {@i {@b Adventuring gear}, {@b premium}} Restraining bolts are small, cylindrical devices that can be affixed to a droid in order to limit its functions and enforce its obedience. When inserted, a {@item Restraining bolt|sw5e-phb|restraining bolt} restricts the droid from any movement its master does not desire, and also forced it to respond to signals produced by a hand-held control unit.

Installing a {@item Restraining bolt|sw5e-phb|restraining bolt} takes 1 minute. The droid must make a DC 16 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A hostile droid makes this save with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}. On a successful save, the {@item Restraining bolt|sw5e-phb|restraining bolt} overloads and is rendered useless. On a failed save, the {@item Restraining bolt|sw5e-phb|restraining bolt} is correctly installed, and the control unit can be used to actively control the droid. While the control unit is inactive, the droid can act freely but it can not attempt to remove the {@item Restraining bolt|sw5e-phb|restraining bolt}.

entries.name: Remote Detonator (Fine)
entries: {@i {@b Adventuring gear}, {@b premium}} A small handhold device with a single button, used to activate explosives. Over the course of 1 minute, you can pair the detonator with up to four mines within 10 feet. As an action, you can remotely detonate all of the paired mines. You must be within 60 feet of the mines to detonate them.

entries.name: Projector Canister, Corrosive (Average)
entries: {@i {@b Consumable} (ammunition), {@b premium}} When triggered, this enhanced {@item Wrist launcher|sw5e-phb|wrist launcher} ammunition produces a spray of acid in a line 15 feet long and 5 feet wide or a 15-foot cone. A single fuel canister holds enough fuel for three attacks in a line or a single attack in a cone. Each creature must make a DC 16 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, a creature takes 2d6 acid damage, and the first attack it makes before the end of its next turn has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}. On a successful save, a creature takes half damage and isn't disadvantaged. If this damage reduces a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, it must make a DC 13 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, it dies immediately without making {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throws}. A disintegrated creature and everything it is wearing and carrying are reduced to a pile of fine gray dust. entries: {@i {@b Consumable} (ammunition), {@b premium}} You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this enhanced corrosive cartridge. A disintegrated creature and everything unenhanced it is wearing and carrying are reduced to a pile of fine gray dust. A creature destroyed in this way can not be revitalized.

entries.name: Deafening Calibrator (Average)
entries: {@i {@b Consumable} (ammunition), {@b premium}} As an action, you can apply this calibrator to one {@filter vibroweapon|items|type=martial weapon} or pair of handwraps within 5 feet, granting it a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls for 1 minute. This bonus is in addition to any bonuses granted by the weapon. Additionally, for the duration, the weapon gains the sonorous 14 property. If it already has the sonorous property, its sonorous number increases by 2, to a maximum of 18. Lastly, if the weapon is not enhanced, it becomes enhanced for the duration.

entries.name: Grenade, Corrosive (Average)
entries: {@i {@b Consumable} (explosive), {@b premium}} Grenades can be set to detonate on impact or with a timer that causes them to explode on {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} count 20 (losing all {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} ties). As an action, you can prime and throw a grenade at a point you can see within 30 feet + your Strength modifier x 5. Each creature within 10 feet must make a DC 16 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A creature takes 4d8 acid damage on a failed save, or half as much as on a successful one. If this damage reduces a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, it must make a DC 13 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, it dies immediately without making {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throws}. A disintegrated creature and everything unenhanced it is wearing or carrying are reduced to a pile of fine gray dust. A creature destroyed in this way can not be revitalized.

entries.name: Mine, Corrosive (Average)
entries: {@i {@b Consumable} (explosive), {@b premium}} Mines can be set to detonate when a creature comes within up to 15 feet of it or paired with a {@item Remote detonator|sw5e-phb|remote detonator}. A disintegrated creature and everything unenhanced it is wearing or carrying are reduced to a pile of fine gray dust. A creature destroyed in this way can not be revitalized.

entries: {@i {@b Consumable} (explosive), {@b artifact}} Mines can be set to detonate when a creature comes within up to 15 feet of it or paired with a {@item Remote detonator|sw5e-phb|remote detonator}. As an action, you can prime and set a mine on a surface you can reach, which arms at the start of your next turn. When detonated, the mine fills the air in a 15-foot-radius sphere with yellow-green fog for 1 minute. The fog spreads around corners, and its area is heavily obscured. It lasts for 1 minute or until a wind of at least 10 miles per hour disperses it.

When a creature enters the fog or starts its turn there, it creature must make a DC 24 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. The creature takes 12d6 poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Additionally, on a failed save, the creature is {@condition Poisoned|sw5e-phb|poisoned} while it is in the cloud. Droids, constructs and humanoids wearing appropriate protective equipment are unaffected.

entries.name: Byrothsis Adept Cell
entries: {@i {@b Item modification} ({@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}), {@b advanced}} When this weapon is levitated by the Force to deal damage through a class feature or {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} you use, it deals additional damage equal to one of its weapon damage dice.

entries.name: Byrothsis Ancient Cell
entries: {@i {@b Item modification} ({@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}), {@b artifact}} When this weapon is levitated by the Force to deal damage through a class feature or {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} you use, it deals additional damage equal to two of its weapon damage dice.

entries.name: Telgorn Jolt Stabilizer (Improved)
entries: {@i {@b Item modification} ({@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}), {@b advanced}} When you cast a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} or use a class feature that requires a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, you can spend 1 force point to change the weapon's damage type to lightning and deal an additional 1d8 lightning damage.

entries.name: Ghostfire Crystal
entries: {@i {@b Item modification} ({@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}), {@b legendary}} This weapon loses the luminous property, if it has it. Additionally, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls made with this weapon, when you attack a creature with it, the creature can't take reactions until the end of the current turn.
{@i These crystals are so transparent that they are nigh invisible. The blade formed by this form of kyber makes no noise, is dim and may form illusory images as it is used.}

entries.name: Krayt Dragon Pearl (Regular)
entries: {@i {@b Item modification} ({@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}), {@b advanced}} You gain a +1 bonus to damage rolls made with this weapon. Additionally, you gain a +1 bonus to damage rolls you make with {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} when using this weapon as your focus. If the power would damage multiple targets, you can only apply this damage bonus to one of them.

entries.name: Krayt Dragon Pearl (Flawless)
entries: {@i {@b Item modification} ({@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}), {@b legendary}} You gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls made with this weapon. Additionally, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls you make with {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} when using this weapon as your focus. Additionally, you gain a +3 bonus to damage rolls you make with {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} when using this weapon as your focus. If the power would damage multiple targets, you can only apply this damage bonus to one of them.

entries.name: Ostrine Crystal (Regular)
entries: {@i {@b Item modification} ({@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}), {@b advanced}} When you deal damage with this weapon, you deal an additional 1d4 force, lightning, necrotic, poison, psychic, or sonic damage (chosen by the GM when generating this item).

entries.name: Ostrine Crystal (Flawless)
entries: {@i {@b Item modification} ({@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}), {@b legendary}} When you deal damage with this weapon, you deal an additional 1d6 force, lightning, necrotic, poison, psychic, or sonic damage (chosen by the GM when generating this item).

entries.name: Ostrine Crystal (Perfect)
entries: {@i {@b Item modification} ({@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}), {@b artifact}} When you deal damage with this weapon, you deal an additional 1d8 force, lightning, necrotic, poison, psychic, or sonic damage (chosen by the GM when generating this item).

entries.name: Careful Subroutine
entries: {@i {@b Item modification} ({@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}), {@b Premium}} When you cast a power that forces other creatures to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can protect some of those creatures from the power’s full force. To do so, you spend 1 additional tech point and choose a number of those creatures up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one). A chosen creature automatically succeeds on its {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against the power.

You can only spend a number of tech points in this way equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain the ability to do so when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
You can use only one Subroutine modification on a power when you cast it, unless otherwise noted.

entries.name: Distant Subroutine
entries: {@i {@b Item modification} ({@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}), {@b Premium}} When you cast a power that has a range of 5 feet or greater, you can spend 1 additional tech point to double the range of the power.
Alternatively, when you cast a power that has a range of touch, you can spend 1 additional tech point to make the range of the power 30 feet.

You can only spend a number of tech points in this way equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain the ability to do so when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
You can use only one Subroutine modification on a power when you cast it, unless otherwise noted.

entries.name: Extended Subroutine
entries: {@i {@b Item modification} ({@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}), {@b Premium}} When you cast a power that has a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can spend 1 additional tech point to double its duration, to a maximum duration of 24 hours.

You can only spend a number of tech points in this way equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain the ability to do so when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
You can use only one Subroutine modification on a power when you cast it, unless otherwise noted.

entries.name: Heightened Subroutine
entries: {@i {@b Item modification} ({@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}), {@b Prototype}} When you cast a power that forces a creature to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist its effects, you can spend 3 additional tech points to give one target of the power {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on its first {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} made against the power.

You can only spend a number of tech points in this way equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} (minimum of once). You regain the ability to do so when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
You can use only one Subroutine modification on a power when you cast it, unless otherwise noted.

entries.name: Improved Subroutine
entries: {@i {@b Item modification} ({@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}), {@b Premium}} When you roll damage for a power, you can spend 1 additional tech point to reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one). You must use the new rolls.

You can only spend a number of tech points in this way equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain the ability to do so when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
You can use Improved Subroutine even if you have already used a different Subroutine modification during the casting of the power.

entries.name: Lingering Subroutine
entries: {@i {@b Item modification} ({@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}), {@b Prototype}} WWhen you cast a power that requires {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} to maintain you can choose to spend 3 additional tech points. If you do, when you lose {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} on the power, the power will not end until the end of your next turn.

You can only spend a number of tech points in this way equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} (minimum of once). You regain the ability to do so when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
You can use only one Subroutine modification on a power when you cast it, unless otherwise noted.

entries.name: Pinpoint Subroutine
entries: {@i {@b Item modification} ({@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}), {@b Premium}} When you cast a power that allows you to force creatures in an area to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} you can instead spend 1 tech point and make a ranged tech attack against a single target that would be in the range. On a hit the target suffers the effects as though they failed their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

You can only spend a number of tech points in this way equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain the ability to do so when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
You can use only one Subroutine modification on a power when you cast it, unless otherwise noted.

entries.name: Quickened Subroutine
entries: {@i {@b Item modification} ({@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}), {@b Prototype}} When you cast a power that has a casting time of 1 action, you can spend 2 additional tech points to change the casting time to 1 {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} for this casting.

You can only spend a number of tech points in this way equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain the ability to do so when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
You can use only one Subroutine modification on a power when you cast it, unless otherwise noted.

entries.name: Refocused Subroutine
entries: {@i {@b Item modification} ({@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}), {@b Prototype}} When you are forced to make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} on a power you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and spend 2 tech points to automatically succeed on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

You can only spend a number of tech points in this way equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain the ability to do so when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
You can use Refocused Subroutine even if you have already used a different Subroutine modification during the casting of the power.

entries.name: Seeking Subroutine
entries: {@i {@b Item modification} ({@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}), {@b Prototype}} If you miss with a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} that calls for an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, you can spend 2 tech points to reroll the attack. You must use the new roll.

You can only spend a number of tech points in this way equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain the ability to do so when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
You can use Seeking Subroutine even if you have already used a different Subroutine modificatio during the casting of the power.

entries.name: Twinned Subroutine
entries: {@i {@b Item modification} ({@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}), {@b Prototype}} When you cast a power that can only have one target and doesn’t have a range of self, you can spend a number of additional tech points equal to the power’s level to choose a second target in range with the same power (1 tech point if the power is at-will).

You can only spend a number of tech points in this way equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain the ability to do so when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
You can use only one Subroutine modification on a power when you cast it, unless otherwise noted.

entries.name: Exotic Weapons
entries: A new weapon tier succeeding simple and {@filter Martial weapons|items|type=martial weapon}, exotic weapons introduce new special weapons with unique capacities that can not be achieved by simple or {@filter Martial weapons|items|type=martial weapon}.

entries.name: Proficiency
entries: In order to gain proficiency in an exotic weapon, you must first have proficiency in all simple and {@filter Martial weapons|items|type=martial weapon} within that category. For instance, before you can be come proficient with an exotic {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true}, you would first need to be proficient in all simple and martial {@filter blasters|items|firearm=true}. For modal exotics (discussed below), if the exotic has modes that would fall in two different weapon categories, you require proficiency all simple and {@filter Martial weapons|items|type=martial weapon} in both categories in order to gain proficiency in that exotic.

entries.name: Types of Exotic Weapons
entries: Exotic weapons come in two major types: modal and specialized.

entries.name: Modal Exotics
entries: Modal exotics have the capacity to switch between modes, with each mode utilizing the damage and properties of an existing weapon, as indicated by the weapons included with the property. Switching between each mode can be achieved by using a character's object interaction on their turn.

entries.name: Combination Weapons
entries: This rule allows characters to combine {@filter lightweapons|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} with other {@filter lightweapons|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} and {@filter vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon} with other {@filter vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon}, granting modes that can be switched between on a character's turn by using their object interaction. {@filter blasters|items|firearm=true}, on the other hand, can gain an attachment that lets them load {@item Wrist launcher|sw5e-phb|wrist launcher} ammunition in addition to their base ammunition, granting them some limited additional effects. Modal exotics instead allow a {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} to have multiple modes that a character can switch between using their object interaction. Modal {@filter lightweapons|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} and {@filter vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon} can grant a mode of a different weapon type, still using that object interaction to switch between. For instance, a modal exotic {@filter vibroweapon|items|type=martial weapon} could have a separate {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} or {@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} mode, instead of a {@filter vibroweapon|items|type=martial weapon} mode. Additionally, modal exotics count as a number of weapons equal to their modes when using the Combination Weapons rule. For instance, an IWS has three modes and thus would count as three weapons. Adding the {@item Wrist launcher|sw5e-phb|wrist launcher} attachment to it would require a DC 20 {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, as appropriate, and a {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} of +4. The attachment would only have a reload property of 1, in this instance, since the total reload number of this attachment combined with the number of weapon modes should not exceed what the total number of combined weapons could be, per the Combination/Separation DC by Weapons table.

entries.name: Specialized Exotics
entries: Specialized exotics, on the other hand, bypass the inherent base and cap to a weapon property. For instance, a weapon with the keen 1 property could not bypass keen 3, per the rules of weapon modifications. A specialized exotic, on the other hand, could potentially start with the keen 2 property, and have up to the keen 4 property. A specialized exotic weapon must have that property in order to bypass its base and cap, and a specialized exotic cannot bypass the base and cap of more than one property.
{@b {@i Biting.}} A specialized exotic {@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} with this property gains a +2 bonus to its base and cap.
{@b {@i Bright.}} A specialized exotic {@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} with this property gains a +2 bonus to its base and cap.
{@b {@i Brutal.}} A specialized exotic weapon with this property gains a +1 bonus to its base and cap.
{@b {@i Corrupting.}} A specialized exotic {@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} with this property gains a +2 bonus to its base and cap.
{@b {@i Defensive.}} A specialized exotic light- or vibro-weapon with this property gains a +1 bonus to its base and cap.
{@b {@i Dire.}} A specialized exotic weapon with this property gains a +1 bonus to its base and cap.
{@b {@i Disintegrate.}} A specialized exotic {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} with this property gains a +2 bonus to its base and cap.
{@b {@i Keen.}} A specialized exotic weapon with this property gains a +1 bonus to its base and cap.
{@b {@i Neuralizing.}} A specialized exotic {@filter vibroweapon|items|type=martial weapon} with this property gains a +2 bonus to its base and cap.
{@b {@i Piercing.}} A specialized exotic weapon with this property gains a +1 bonus to its base and cap.
{@b {@i Shocking.}} A specialized exotic {@filter vibroweapon|items|type=martial weapon} with this property gains a +2 bonus to its base and cap.
{@b {@i Smart.}} A specialized exotic {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} with this property gains a (+2, 0) bonus to its base and cap.
{@b {@i Sonorous.}} A specialized exotic {@filter vibroweapon|items|type=martial weapon} with this property gains a +2 bonus to its base and cap.
{@b {@i Vicious.}} A specialized exotic weapon with this property gains a +1 bonus to its base and cap.

entries.name: Generating Exotics
entries: Exotics can be generated just like weapons using the weapon calculator, with the following variations.

items: {@b 1.} Modal exotics take the highest weight of each its modes, and add half the weight of each of the other modes.
{@b 2.} Modal exotics combine the value of each of its modes.
{@b 1.} Specialized exotics use the framework of a martial weapon of the appropriate category with an appropriate property.
{@b 2.} Specialized exotics adds the specialized property value and weight a second time.

entries.name: Exotic Weapon Chassis
entries: For modal exotics, each mode has separate modification slots, with the exception of augments; augments are shared across all weapon modes. Specialized exotics function like non-exotic weapons.

entries.name: Weapon Properties
entries: Many weapons have special properties related to their use, as shown in the Weapons table.

entries.name: Modal
entries: A weapon with this property can switch between modes. A list of weapons in parentheses appears with the property-the weapons between which an exotic weapon can be switched by using an object interaction.

entries.name: Specialized
entries: A weapon with this property bypasses the base and cap of certain properties. Another weapon property in parentheses with the property-the weapon property that the exotic bypasses the base and cap for.

entries.name: Special Weapons
entries: Weapons with special rules are described below.

entries.name: Atlatl
entries: This specialized gungan club can be used to throw grenades or similar objects at long distances. If you are wielding this weapon, as part of the action to throw a grenade, you can instead throw it using an atlatl you are holding. The grenade can be thrown at a short distance of 30ft and a long distance of 120ft. When throwing a grenade at long range, creatures within the radius of the grenade’s explosion have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.  If you lack proficiency in the atlatl, you must roll the damage dice twice and take the lesser total.

entries.name: ARC Caster
entries: Whenever you deal damage with this weapon and roll the maximum on the weapon damage die, the creature hit becomes {@condition Shocked|sw5e-phb|shocked} until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Blaster Cannon
entries: Rather than traditional {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, the {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} cannon uses a specialized power generator that allows it to fire continuously for 10 minutes. Replacing a power generator takes an action.

Before firing the {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} cannon, you must deploy it using an action unless you meet its strength requirement. Alternatively, if you’re able to make multiple attacks with the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, this action replaces one of them.  While deployed in this way, you treat this weapon’s strength number as two steps less (from 19 to 15), your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is reduced by half, and you cannot fire this weapon at long range. You can collapse the {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} cannon as an action or {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Bolas
entries: A Large or smaller creature hit by a bolas is {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained} until it is freed. A bolas has no effect on formless or Huge or larger creatures. A creature can use its action to make a DC 13 Dexterity check, freeing itself or another creature within its reach on a success. The bolas has an AC of 10, 5 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, and immunity to all damage not dealt by melee weapons. Destroying the bolas frees the creature without harming it and immediately ends the bolas’s effects. While a creature is {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained} by a bolas, you can make no further attacks with it.

Due to their unwieldy nature, bolas make ineffective melee weapons. Melee {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} made with them are made at {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.

entries.name: Bolt-thrower
entries: Rather than traditional {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, the bolt-thrower fires specialized projectiles in the form of bolts.

entries.name: Cesta
entries: This specialized gungan staff can be used to throw grenades or similar objects at long distances. If you are wielding this weapon, as part of the action to throw a grenade, you can instead throw it using a cesta you are holding. The grenade can be thrown at a short distance of 60ft and a long distance of 240ft. When throwing a grenade at long range, creatures within the radius of the grenade’s explosion have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. If you lack proficiency in the cesta, you must roll the damage dice twice and take the lesser total.

entries.name: Compound Bow
entries: Rather than traditional {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, the compound bow fires specialized projectiles in the form of arrows. You can make a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} only if you have ammunition to fire from the weapon. Each time you attack with the weapon, you expend one arrow.

Drawing the ammunition from a quiver, case, or other container is part of the attack. At the end of the battle, you can recover half your expended ammunition by taking a minute to search the battlefield.

entries.name: Heavy blaster Cannon
entries: Rather than traditional {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, the heavy {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} cannon uses a specialized power generator that allows it to fire continuously for 10 minutes. Replacing a power generator takes an action.

Before firing the {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} cannon, you must deploy it using an action unless you meet its strength requirement. Alternatively, if you’re able to make multiple attacks with the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, this action replaces one of them.  While deployed in this way, you treat this weapon’s strength number as two steps less (from 19 to 15), your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is reduced by half, and you cannot fire this weapon at long range. You can collapse the heavy {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} cannon as an action or {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Lightning Cannon
entries: Whenever you deal damage with this weapon and roll the maximum on the weapon damage die, the creature hit becomes {@condition Shocked|sw5e-phb|shocked} until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Lightning Rifle
entries: Whenever you deal damage with this weapon and roll the maximum on the weapon damage die, the creature hit becomes {@condition Shocked|sw5e-phb|shocked} until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Mancatcher
entries: When you would make a Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) check to attempt to grapple a creature while wielding a weapon with the grappling property, you can instead make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} with it. If the attack hits, the creature becomes {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} by you, and it takes damage equal to your Strength modifier of the same type as the weapon’s damage.

entries.name: Mortar Launcher
entries: Rather than traditional {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, the mortar launcher fires grenades. If you lack proficiency in the mortar launcher, you must roll the damage dice twice and take the lesser total. A mortar launcher cannot fire on targets within its short range and when firing a grenade at long range, creatures within the radius of the grenade’s explosion do not have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. Additionally, when you launch a mortar at a target, you can treat the Weapon's point of origin as being 200ft in the air for the purposes of determining line of sight and {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}.

The mortar launcher requires the use of a {@item Tripod|sw5e-phb|tripod}, which is included in the price. Over the course of 1 minute, you can deploy or collapse the mortar launcher on the {@item Tripod|sw5e-phb|tripod}. While deployed, your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is reduced to 0.

entries.name: Needler
entries: The needler includes a specialized compartment for poison. One dose of poison, when installed in this compartment, retains its potency for 1 hour before drying. One dose of poison is effective for the next 10 shots fired by the weapon.

entries.name: Retrosaber
entries: The retrosaber is an ancient type of {@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} that requires a {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb} to function. Once four attacks have been made with a retrosaber, a character must replace the {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb} using an action or {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}. You must have one free hand to replace the {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Rocket Rifle
entries: Rather than traditional {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, the rocket rifle fires specialized projectiles in the form of small missiles.

entries.name: Sentry Gun
entries: Before firing the sentry gun, you must deploy it using an action unless you meet its strength requirement. Alternatively, if you’re able to make multiple attacks with the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, this action replaces one of them.  While deployed in this way, you treat this weapon’s strength number as two steps less (from 19 to 15), your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is reduced by half, and you cannot fire this weapon at long range. You can collapse the sentry gun as an action or {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Shortbow
entries: Rather than traditional {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, the shortbow fires specialized projectiles in the form of arrows. You can make a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} only if you have ammunition to fire from the weapon. Each time you attack with the weapon, you expend one arrow.

Drawing the ammunition from a quiver, case, or other container is part of the attack. At the end of the battle, you can recover half your expended ammunition by taking a minute to search the battlefield.

entries.name: Torpedo Launcher
entries: Rather than traditional {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, the torpedo launcher fires specialized projectiles in the form of torpedoes. Torpedo launchers have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against Gargantuan creatures and {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against Large and smaller creatures. Unlike other weapons, the torpedo launcher can only be loaded using an action, and you don’t add your Dexterity modifier to damage rolls you make with it.

The torpedo launcher requires the use of a {@item Tripod|sw5e-phb|tripod}, which is included in the price. Over the course of 1 minute, you can deploy or collapse the torpedo launcher on the {@item Tripod|sw5e-phb|tripod}. While deployed, your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is reduced to 0.

entries.name: Tranquilizer Rifle
entries: The {@spell Tranquilizer|sw5e-phb|tranquilizer} rifle includes a specialized compartment for poison. One dose of poison, when installed in this compartment, retains its potency for 1 hour before drying. One dose of poison is effective for the next 4 shots fired by the weapon. Additionally, creatures reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} by this weapon are immediately stabilized, unless that damage would instantly kill them.

entries.name: Vibro-lance
entries: You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} when you use a vibrolance to attack a target within 5 feet of you. Also, a lance requires two hands to wield when you aren’t mounted.

entries.name: Adventuring Gear
entries: This section describes items that have special rules or require further explanation.

entries.name: Arrow
entries: Arrows are ammunition used in bow weapons. When you would use poison to coat a weapon or {@item Slug cartridge|sw5e-phb|slug cartridge} you can instead coat an arrow with the poison. Once a {@condition Poisoned|sw5e-phb|poisoned} arrow hits a target, it no longer gives a bonus.

entries.name: Arrow, Combustive
entries: A combustive arrow is a specialized arrow for use with bow weapons. When the arrow hits another creature, object, or surface it detonates. Each creature within 5ft of the arrows detonation must make a DC 14 Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or take 1d8 fire damage. On a successful save, a creature takes half damage. Once the arrow hits a target, it no longer gives a bonus.

entries.name: Arrow, Noisemaker
entries: A noisemaker arrow is a specialized arrow for use with bow weapons. When the arrow hits another creature, object, or surface it generates an explosion of sound that can be heard up to 100 feet away. If the target of the attack is a creature, the creature must make a DC 14 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the creature takes 1d6 sonic damage and is {@condition Deafened|sw5e-phb|deafened} until the end of its next turn. Once the arrow hits a target, it no longer gives a bonus.

entries.name: Arrow, Electroshock
entries: An {@spell Electroshock|sw5e-phb|electroshock} arrow is a specialized arrow for use with bow weapons. When you hit a creature with this arrow, the creature must make a DC 14 Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the creature takes 1d3 ion damage and becomes {@condition Stunned|sw5e-phb|stunned} until the start of its next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half damage and isn’t {@condition Stunned|sw5e-phb|stunned}. Once the arrow hits a target, it no longer gives a bonus.

entries.name: Bolt
entries: This Bolt-thrower ammunition deals 2d6 kinetic damage on a hit. When you would use poison to coat a weapon or {@item Slug cartridge|sw5e-phb|slug cartridge} you can instead coat a bolt with the poison.

entries.name: Bolt, Deafening
entries: This bolt-thrower ammunition deals 2d6 kinetic damage on a hit. Also on a hit, the creature must make a DC 14 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, taking 2d4 sonic damage on a failed save. Additionally, on a failed save, a creature is {@condition Deafened|sw5e-phb|deafened} for 1 minute. At the end of an affected creature’s turn, it can repeat this save, ending the effect on a success.

entries.name: Bolt, Electrifying
entries: This bolt-thrower ammunition deals 2d6 kinetic damage on a hit.
