Also on a hit, the creature must make a DC 14 Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, taking 2d4 lightning damage on a failed save. Additionally, on a failed save, a creature is {@condition Shocked|sw5e-phb|shocked} for 1 minute. At the end of an affected creature’s turn, it can repeat this save, ending the effect on a success.

entries.name: Bolt, Panic
entries: This bolt-thrower ammunition deals 2d6 kinetic damage on a hit. Also on a hit, the creature must make a DC 14 Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, taking 2d4 psychic damage on a failed save. Additionally, on a failed save, a creature becomes {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} of you for 1 minute. At the start of an affected creature’s turn, it can repeat this save, ending the effect on a success.

entries.name: Fragmentation Torpedo
entries: This torpedo launcher ammunition deals 20d4 kinetic damage on a hit.

entries.name: Plasma Torpedo
entries: This torpedo launcher ammunition deals 20d4 energy damage on a hit.

entries.name: Charge, Fragmentation
entries: A device used to blow holes in larger constructs and structures, a breaching charge creates a devastating explosion focused in a specific direction. Installing a breaching charge takes 1 minute. The charge can be set with a 6-second timer, or detonated remotely using a {@item Remote detonator|sw5e-phb|remote detonator}.

When detonated, the breaching charge explodes in a 15-foot cone. Each creature within the cone must make a DC 14 Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, taking 20d4 kinetic damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one. If affixed to a creature, that creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. Objects, structures, and other surfaces have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. If affixed to the object, structure, or surface, it instead automatically fails this {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

entries.name: Charge, Plasma
entries: A device used to blow holes in larger constructs and structures, a breaching charge creates a devastating explosion focused in a specific direction. Installing a breaching charge takes 1 minute. The charge can be set with a 6-second timer, or detonated remotely using a {@item Remote detonator|sw5e-phb|remote detonator}.

When detonated, the breaching charge explodes in a 15-foot cone. Each creature within the cone must make a DC 14 Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, taking 20d4 energy damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one. If affixed to a creature, that creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. Objects, structures, and other surfaces have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. If affixed to the object, structure, or surface, it instead automatically fails this {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

entries.name: Emergency Raft
entries: This raft comes packed in a 2-foot-long tube. When activated, the raft quickly deploys, expanding to full size in six seconds. The raft is 6 feet long and 3 feet wide, and can hold up to four Medium creatures not exceeding 800 lb. It comes with two collapsible oars with which to row. The raft can be collapsed and restored over the course of 1 minute.

entries.name: Emergency Rations (One day's)
entries: Emergency rations come in small pill form, provide all the necessary nourishment for one person for one day, and take up roughly one-tenth the space of field rations.

entries.name: Environmental Suits
entries: Environmental suits are heavy duty completely sealed suits that can be worn over other clothing and armor. Each suit is tailored to a certain environment, and has no effect on environments to which it is not tailored. Due to their encompassing and cumbersome nature, while wearing an environmental suit, a creature's {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is reduced by 15. Environmental suits include 8 hours' capacity of oxygen, which can be replenished by an oxygen tank or directly connected to a source of oxygen such as a life support system on a vehicle or starship.

{@b {@i Chemical Suit.}} Chemical suits are sealed suits that repel corrosive acids. While wearing a chemical suit, you have resistance to acid damage, and you are immune to the {@condition Corroded|sw5e-phb|corroded} condition.

{@b {@i Conductive Suit.}} Conductive suits help prevent electrocution by grounding electrical sources. While wearing a conductive suit, you have resistance to lightning damage, and you are immune to the {@condition Shocked|sw5e-phb|shocked} condition.

{@b {@i Dampening Suit.}} Dampening suits modulate sounds that come from outside the suit. While wearing a dampening suit, you have resistance to sonic damage, you are immune to the {@condition Deafened|sw5e-phb|deafened} condition, and you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) and Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}) checks that rely on sound.

{@b {@i Diving Suit.}} Diving suits are sealed suits that help regulate body temperature while underwater. While wearing a diving suit, you have resistance to cold damage, and are protected from the hazards associated with high pressure environments.

{@b {@i Flame-Proof Suit.}} Flame-proof suits prevent flames from reaching the wearer's body. While wearing a flame-proof suit, you have resistance to fire damage, and you are immune to the {@condition Ignited|sw5e-phb|ignited} condition.

{@b {@i Hazard Suit.}} Hazard suits are made to seal the wearer away from noxious gases. While wearing a hazard suit, you have resistance to poison damage, and you are immune to the {@condition Poisoned|sw5e-phb|poisoned} condition.

{@b {@i Mind-Shielding Suit.}} Mind-shielding suits help protect the wearer's mind—and body—from outside influence. While wearing a mind-shielding suit, you have resistance to psychic damage, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid being {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened}, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid having your mind read or affected.

{@b {@i Stabilizer Suit.}} Stabilizer suits help to keep the bearer from being battered by powerful forces. While wearing a stabilizer suit, you have resistance to force damage, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid being moved.

{@b {@i Space Suit.}} Space suits are suits that enabled wearers to survive and operate in the vacuum of space. While wearing a space suit, you have resistance to necrotic damage, and are protected from the hazards associated with low pressure environments.

entries.name: Oxygen Tank
entries: Oxygen tanks include 8 hours' capacity of oxygen. They can be connected to an environmental suit or {@item Respirator|sw5e-phb|respirator} to feed it directly or replenish any reduced capacity at a rate of one hour's oxygen per ten minutes connected. Only one oxygen tank can be connected at a time.

entries.name: Bucket
entries: A bucket stores 3 gallons of liquid or 1/2 cubic foot of solids.

entries.name: Flask
entries: A flask stores 1 pint of liquid.

entries.name: Hovercart
entries: This repulsorcraft is designed to efficiently move large amounts of goods. It has a {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} of 30 feet and can store 2,000 lb., not exceeding 120 cubic feet.

entries.name: Jug
entries: A jug stores 1 gallon of liquid.

entries.name: Pot
entries: A pot stores 1 gallon of liquid.

entries.name: Sack
entries: A sack stores 30 ounces, not exceeding 1 cubic foot.

entries.name: Tankard
entries: A tankard stores 1 pint of liquid.

entries.name: Vial
entries: A vial stores 4 ounces of liquid.

entries.name: Fire Extinguisher
entries: As an action, you can expend a use of the extinguisher to create a 15 foot cone of misty air which lasts for 6 seconds, snuffing out any unenhanced fires within range. Additionally, each creature within range must make a DC 14 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, a creature is {@condition Blinded|sw5e-phb|blinded} until the start of their next turn. On a successful save, a creature becomes immune to this effect. An extinguisher can be used 5 times before it must be replenished at its original cost.

entries.name: Gravity Generator
entries: Gravity generators are special devices typically worn on belts that function as a portable, personal artificial gravity source. Activating or deactivating the belt requires a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} and, while active, you are able to move as if in a standard gravitational pull. The generator lasts for 10 minutes and can be recharged by a power source or replacing the {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Ammo Pouch
entries: An ammo pouch is a small pouch, usually worn around the waist or chest, which holds 20 slug cartridges. When you reload a weapon, you can draw as much ammunition needed from this pouch without using an object interaction to do so. Instead of slug cartridges, you can instead store a {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb} which takes up the space of 10 cartridges.

entries.name: Propulsion Pack
entries: Propulsion packs enhance underwater movement. Activating or deactivating the propulsion pack requires a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} and, while active, you have a swimming {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} of 30 feet. The propulsion pack lasts for 1 minute per {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb} (to a maximum of 10 minutes) and can be recharged by a power source or replacing the {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}.

entries.name: Quiver
entries: A quiver which can hold up to 20 arrows, 10 bolts, or 10 darts. Drawing an item from the quiver does not require an object interaction.

entries.name: Repulsor Pack
entries: Repulsor packs are used to {@spell Slow Descent|sw5e-phb|slow descent} from a high elevation. Activating or deactivating the repulsor pack requires a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} and, while active, your rate of descent slow to 60 feet per round, and you ignore the effects of wind of less than moderate {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} (no more than 10 mph). The repulsor pack lasts for 1 minute per {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb} (to a maximum of 10 minutes) and can be recharged by a power source or replacing the {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}.

entries.name: Shock Gloves
entries: A shock glove is a type of armored glove that is coated with a webbed lacing. When used for an attack, this webbing carries a charge that deals 1d4 lightning damage to any objects that the glove come in contact with. If you are engaged in combat with the target of the attack, you must make a grapple check instead of an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, using a Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) check contested by the target's Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|sw5e-phb}) check (the target chooses the ability to use).

entries.name: Droids
entries: One common way to spend wealth is to purchase droids. Some droids are built for scouting, while others offer advanced skillsets. Protocol droids help communicate with foreign bodies, and combat droids can help supplement a budding force. The Droids table offers some choices for purchase.

entries.name: Mounts and Vehicles
entries: Mounts and vehicles are the two most common types of on-planet transport.

entries.name: Mounts
entries: A good mount can help you move more quickly through the wilderness, but its primary purpose is to carry the gear that would otherwise slow you down. The Mounts and Other Animals table shows each animal's {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} and base carrying capacity.

An animal pulling a cart or wagon can move weight up to five times its base carrying capacity, including the weight of the vehicle. If multiple animals pull the same vehicle, they can add their carrying capacity together.

Mounts other than those listed here are available in the worlds of {@i Star Wars}, but they are rare and not normally available for purchase, like aiwhas from Kamino. Acquiring such a mount is often an adventure in-and-of itself.
Mounts are governed by {@skill Animal Handling|sw5e-phb} proficiency.

entries.name: Barding
entries: Barding is armor designed to protect an animal's head, neck, chest, and body. Any type of armor shown on the Armor table in this chapter can be purchased as barding. The cost and weight of barding varies based on the size of the creature, as shown in the Tack, Harness, and Drawn Vehicles table.

entries.name: Saddles
entries: A military saddle braces the rider, helping you keep your seat on an active mount in battle. It gives you {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on any check you make to remain mounted. An exotic saddle is required for riding an exotic mount.

entries.name: Vehicles
entries: Vehicles are more common on civilized planets than animal mounts. Vehicles do not have access to barding and do not require saddles. Vehicles vary greatly based on price, {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}, carrying capacity, personnel capacity, and armaments (if any). Below are some base costs for standard types of speeders. Vehicles are governed by {@skill Piloting|sw5e-phb} proficiency.

entries.name: Agile Defense
entries: {@i 1st-level universal power}
As part of the action of casting this power, you take the {@action Dodge|sw5e-phb} action.

entries.name: Art of Movement
entries: {@i 3rd-level universal power}
By letting the Force flow through you, you move with preternatural grace, leaping onto or over tall obstacles that impede others. Until the power ends, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have resistance to damage from falling.

You gain a climbing {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}, and you can move up, down, and across vertical surfaces and upside down along ceilings, while leaving your hands free. If you are on a vertical surface when you end your turn and are not using your hands to climb, you immediately fall unless you have some other means of remaining there.
Your movement is unaffected by {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain} or squeezing.
You ignore the effects of {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} levels under 3.

entries: Once before the power ends, you can give yourself {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} roll on your turn. That attack deals an extra 1d10 force damage on a hit. Whether you hit or miss, you gain a flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} until the end of that turn.

entries.name: Battlemind
entries: {@i 2nd-level universal power}

Through the Force, you gain a limited form of telepathy that enables you to anticipate the moves of your opponents in combat. While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a shield, you gain a +2 AC bonus against melee attacks and a +3 AC bonus against ranged attacks.
This AC bonus is not applied against attacks from droids, constructs, or creatures with resistance or immunity to psychic damage.

entries.name: Break
entries: {@i At-will universal power}

You inflict 10 force damage to an object you can see within range that is not being worn or carried, generating an explosion of sound that can be heard up to 100 feet away. Even if the object is not destroyed, small shards of shrapnel fly at creatures within 5 feet of it. Each creature must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, a creature takes 1d4 kinetic damage.
This power’s kinetic damage increases by 1d4 when you reach 5th level (2d4), 11th level (3d4), and 17th level (4d4), and the power’s force damage also increases by 10 at each of these levels.

entries.name: Defensive Technique
entries: {@i At-will light side power}

As part of the action used to cast this power, you must make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} against one creature within your reach, otherwise the power fails. On a hit, the target suffers the attack's normal effects, and you ward yourself from it through the Force.

If the target forces you to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} before the start of your next turn, the target takes an additional 1d6 psychic damage, and you can roll 1d4 and add the number rolled to your {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. The power then ends.

The power's damage increases when you reach higher levels. At 5th level, the melee attack deals an extra 1d6 psychic damage to the target, and the psychic damage the target takes for forcing you to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} increases to 2d6. Both damage rolls increase by 1d6 at 11th level and 17th level.

entries.name: Force Current
entries: {@i 1st-level universal power}

When you cast this power, you raise your hand and unleash a burst of Force energy. Each creature in a 15-foot cone must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, a creature takes 3d6 force damage and, if it is Large or smaller, is also pushed back 5 feet. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't pushed. All Medium or smaller objects that are not worn or carried within the area of effect are also pushed 5 feet.

{@b {@i Force Potency.}} When you cast this power using a force slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 1st. For each slot 2 levels higher than 1st, you can add an additional 5 feet to the push.

entries.name: Force Intuition
entries: {@i 1st-level universal power}

Your senses attune to your environment for the duration, allowing you to see things before they happen, and react even faster than normal. For the duration, you can use your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} modifier in place of your Dexterity modifier when you make {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} checks, if the check doesn't already include that modifier.

In addition, once during the duration of this power, if you are surprised at the start of combat, rather than being completely unable to act, you can still use a {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}, and take an action on your first turn in combat. This action can be used only to take one of the following actions: Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Hide, or Use an Object.

entries.name: Greater Kinetite
entries: {@i 5th-level dark side power}

A 5-foot diameter sphere of compressed lightning appears in an unoccupied space of your choice and lasts for the duration. Each creature within 5 feet of the sphere when the power is cast must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A creature takes 5d8 lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on each of your turns, you can move the ball of lightning up to 30 feet vertically or horizontally. If you ram the sphere into a creature, that creature must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or take 5d8 kinetic damage (or half as much damage on a success), and the sphere stops moving this turn. A creature takes half as damage on a successful Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.
{@b {@i Force Potency.}} When you cast this power with a force slot of 6th level or higher, both the lightning and kinetic damage increase by 1d8 for each slot level above 5th.

entries.name: Greater Pyrokinesis
entries: {@i 4th-level universal power}

You create a wall of Force-enhanced fire on a solid surface within range. You can make the wall up to 60 feet long, 20 feet high, and 1 foot thick, or a ringed wall up to 20 feet in diameter, 20 feet high, and 1 foot thick. The wall is opaque and lasts for the duration.

When the wall appears, each creature within its area must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, a creature takes 5d8 energy damage, or half as much damage on a successful save.

One side of the wall, selected by you when you cast this power, deals 5d8 energy damage to each creature that ends its turn within 10 feet of that side or inside the wall. A creature takes the same damage when it enters the wall for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there. The other side of the wall deals no damage.
{@b {@i Force Potency.}} When you cast this power using a force slot of 5th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 4th.

entries.name: Heighten Senses
entries: {@i 1st-level universal power}

items: {@b Casting Time:} 1 {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}, which you take when you would roll {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative}

entries: Through the Force, you sense a sudden shift in your environment, and can seize on it with great {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}. You gain {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} check, and until the end of your first turn in combat, your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} increases by 30 feet.

entries.name: Improved Force Intuition
entries: {@i 2nd-level universal power}

items: {@b Casting Time:} 1 {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}, which you take when you would roll {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative}

entries: You make your {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} check at {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}, and gain a +2 bonus to AC until the power ends. In addition, until the end of your first turn in the combat, your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} increases by 10 feet and you add 1d4 to your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls}. This power ends early if you fail a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or are hit by an attack.

entries.name: Improved Kinetite
entries: {@i 4th-level dark side power}

A 20-foot-radius sphere of compressed lightning springs into existence centered on a point you choose within range. The sphere remains for the power’s duration. Each creature in the sphere when it appears or that ends its turn there must succeed on a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or take 2d6 kinetic damage. The sphere’s space is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain}.

Until the power ends, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on each of your turns to cause a bolt of lightning to leap from the center of the sphere toward one creature you choose within 60 feet of the center. Make a ranged force attack. You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} if the target is in the sphere. On a hit, the target takes 4d6 lightning damage.
Creatures within 30 feet of the sphere have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) checks made to listen.
{@b {@i Force Potency.}} When you cast this power with a force slot of 5th level or higher, the damage increases for each of its effects by 1d6 for each slot level above 4th.

entries.name: Improved Pyrokinesis
entries: {@i 2nd-level universal power}

A line of roaring Force-enhanced flame 30 feet long and 5 feet wide emanates from you in a direction you choose. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A creature takes 3d8 energy damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
{@b {@i Force Potency.}} When you cast this power using a force slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd.

entries.name: Instinctive Movement
entries: {@i 1st-level universal power}

You enhance your movement with the Force, allowing you to traverse your environment with {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} and acrobatic grace. When you cast this power, you gain two {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} points. When you cast the power and as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on subsequent turns, you can expend a {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} point, granting yourself all of the following benefits until the end of that turn:

items: You have resistance to falling damage.
You have a climb {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}.
You add 10 feet to your long jump distance and 3 feet to your high jump distance.
You can move up, down, and across vertical surfaces and upside down along ceilings, while leaving your hands free.
You do not sink when moving over soft or brittle terrain, such as dust, silt, mud, snow, or thin ice. This effect does not allow you to move across liquid surfaces.

If you move at least 20 feet straight toward a creature and then hit it with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} for the first time on the same turn, you deal an extra 1d4 damage with that attack.

entries: At the end of the turn, the benefits fade entirely until you spend another {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} point. If these benefits end while you are still on a vertical surface, or anywhere else where you would normally fall or sink, you immediately fall or begin to sink unless you have some other means to remain there.

This power ends when its duration expires, when you cast this power again, or when you have spent all your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} points. When the power ends, any unspent {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} points are lost.

{@b {@i Force Potency.}} When you cast this power using a force slot of 2nd level or higher, the extra damage increases by 1d4 for each slot level above 1st. In addition, if you cast this power with a force slot of 3rd level or higher, you gain one additional {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} point for every two slot levels above 1st.

entries.name: Kinetite
entries: {@i 2nd-level dark side power}

A 5-foot-diameter sphere of compressed lightning appears in an unoccupied space of your choice within range and lasts for the duration. Any creature that ends its turn within 5 feet of the sphere must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. The creature takes 2d6 lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can move the sphere up to 30 feet. If you ram the sphere into a creature, that creature must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, taking 2d6 kinetic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one, and the sphere stops moving this turn.

When you move the sphere, you can direct it over barriers up to 5 feet tall and jump it across pits up to 10 feet wide. The sphere ignites flammable objects not being worn or carried, and it sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet.
{@b {@i Force Potency.}} When you cast this power with a force slot of 3rd level or higher, both the lightning and kinetic damage increase by 1d6 for each slot level above 2nd.

entries.name: Land Stride
entries: {@i 1st-level light side power}

You align yourself with nature, making traversing natural environments far easier. For the duration, your movement and that of creatures of your choice within 40 feet of you can't be {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} by natural terrain, such as mud, rocky ground, vines, or tall grass. Climbing still costs double normal movement. A creature that receives this bonus leaves behind no traces of its passage.

entries.name: Master Pyrokinesis
entries: {@i 7th-level universal power}

A storm made up of sheets of roaring, Force-enhanced flame appears in a location you choose within range. The area of the storm consists of up to ten 10-foot cubes, which you can arrange as you wish. Each cube must have at least one face adjacent to the face of another cube. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. It takes 7d10 energy damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature in the area of more than one cube is affected only once.
The flame damages objects in the area and ignites flammable objects that aren't being worn or carried.

entries.name: Phaseshift
entries: {@i At-will universal power}
Too quickly for untrained eyes to perceive, you shift in position. You can move up to 5 feet, and this movement does not provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}.

entries.name: Probe Mind
entries: {@i 2nd-level dark side power}

For the duration, you can read the thoughts of certain creatures. When you cast the power and as your action on each turn until the power ends, you can focus your mind on any one creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. If the creature you choose has an Intelligence of 3 or lower or doesn’t speak any language, the creature is unaffected.

You initially learn the surface thoughts of the creature—what is most on its mind in that moment. As an action, you can either shift your attention to another creature’s thoughts or attempt to probe deeper into the same creature’s mind. If you probe deeper, the target must make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. If it fails, it takes 1d6 psychic damage as you gain insight into its reasoning (if any), its emotional state, and something that looms large in its mind (such as something it worries over, loves, or hates). If it succeeds, the power ends. Either way, the target knows that you are probing into its mind, and unless you shift your attention to another creature’s thoughts, the creature can use its action on its turn to make an Intelligence check contested by your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} check; if it succeeds, the power ends.
On subsequent turns after probing deeper, you can use your action to deal 1d6 psychic damage to the target automatically.
Questions verbally directed at the target creature naturally shape the course of its thoughts, so this power is particularly effective as part of an interrogation.

You can also use this power to detect the presence of thinking creatures you can’t see. When you cast the power or as your action during the duration, you can search for thoughts within 30 feet of you. The power can penetrate barriers. You can’t detect a creature with an Intelligence of 3 or lower or one that doesn’t speak any language.
Once you detect the presence of a creature in this way, you can read its thoughts for the rest of the duration as described above, even if you can’t see it, but it must still be within range.
This power has no effect on droids or constructs.

{@b {@i Force Potency.}} When you cast this power using a force slot of 3rd level or higher, the initial psychic damage a target takes the first time you probe deeper into its mind increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 2nd.

entries.name: Pull Earthward
entries: {@i 2nd-level universal power}

Choose one creature you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or its flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} (if any) is reduced to 0 feet for the power’s duration. An airborne creature affected by this power descends at 60 feet per round until it reaches the ground or the power ends.

entries.name: Pyrokinesis
entries: {@i At-will universal power}

By stimulating air molecules, you create a zone of Force-enhanced fire on ground that you can see within range. Until the power ends, the enhanced fire fills a 5-foot cube. Any creature in the fire's space when you cast the power must succeed on a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or take 1d8 energy damage. A creature must also make the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} when it moves into the fire's space for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there.
The fire ignites flammable objects in its area that aren't being worn or carried.
The power's damage increases by 1d8 when you reach 5th level (2d8), 11th level (3d8), and 17th level (4d8).

entries.name: Reveal Shatterpoint
entries: {@i 5th-level universal power}

You focus on a creature you can see within range, and gain uncanny insight on its defenses and capabilities through the Force. The target must make a Charisma {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against that creature, and it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against you for the duration. On a successful save, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the next {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} you make against that creature, and it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on its next {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against you. Once both attacks have been made, the power ends.

entries.name: Saber Assault
entries: {@i 1st-level universal power}

The first time you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action during your turn, you can simultaneously cast this power to blend your melee weapon attacks with the use of the Force. For each successful hit you make with a melee weapon before the power ends, the target must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or have a new effect apply until the end of its next turn. Once you've made three weapon attacks, the power ends.

items: {@b 1st Hit:} If the target fails its {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, it gains 1 {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level until the end of its next turn.
{@b 2nd Hit:} If the target fails its {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, it takes 1d6 kinetic damage and cannot take reactions until after the end of its next turn.
{@b 3rd Hit:} If the target fails its {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, it takes 2d6 kinetic damage and cannot take bonus actions during its next turn.

entries: {@b {@i Force Potency.}} When you cast this power using a force slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage of the second and third hit each increase by 1d6 for every two slot levels above 1st.

entries.name: Saber Dance
entries: {@i 4th-level universal power}

A light- or vibro-weapon of your choice that you are wearing or carrying begins to animate, spinning around your body at high speeds in a 10-foot radius centered on you. For the duration, your movement {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is halved, and the weapon moves with you.

When a creature enters the affected area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, the creature must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or take 4d10 damage of the weapon's type, or half as much damage on a successful {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.
When this power ends, you can immediately recall the weapon to your hand.

{@b {@i Force Potency.}} When you cast this power using a force slot of 5th level or higher, the radius of the power increases to 15 feet, and the power's damage increases by 1d10 for each slot level above 4th.

entries.name: Saber Onslaught
entries: {@i 4th-level universal power}

You assume a battle stance. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}. Additionally, whenever you move, you can make one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} against each creature you move within 5 feet of for the first time this turn. On a hit, the attack deals an extra 1d6 damage of the weapon's type, and the target must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, you can choose to either knock the target prone, or push it 5 feet away from you.
{@b {@i Force Potency.}} When you cast this power using a force slot of 5th level or higher, the bonus weapon damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 4th.

entries.name: Saber Slash
entries: {@i 3rd-level universal power}

You move in a burst of {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} to deliver a deadly blow. When you cast this power, you must be wielding a melee weapon with which you are proficient, otherwise, the power fails. As part of the action used to cast this power, you move in a straight line to an unoccupied space within the power's range and strike a creature within your weapon's range. Opportunity attacks provoked by this movement have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}. The creature must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, it takes damage equal to three rolls of the weapon's damage dice + 4d4 force damage, or half as much damage on a successful one.
{@b {@i Force Potency.}} When you cast this power using a force slot of 4th level or higher, the force damage increases by 1d4 for each slot level above 3rd.

entries.name: Sense Shatterpoint
entries: {@i 2nd-level universal power}

You seek deeper insight into the defenses of a creature you can see within range. Until the end of your next turn, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your next two {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against the target.

entries.name: Saber Strike
entries: {@i 2nd-level universal power}

As part of the action used to cast the power, you can move up to your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} and make one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}. On a hit, the attack deals an extra 1d10 damage of the weapon's type. In addition, if you hit with the attack, the target must succeed on a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be knocked {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}.
{@b {@i Force Potency.}} When you cast this power using a force slot of 4th level or higher, the bonus weapon damage increases by 1d10 for every two slot levels above 2nd.

entries.name: Tapas
entries: {@i 1st-level universal power}
You use the Force to inure yourself to the elements. For the duration, you are considered adapted to hot and cold climates.

entries.name: Telepathic Link
entries: {@i 1st-level universal power}
You establish a telepathic link with one willing creature you touch. Until the power ends, whenever you and the target can see each other, each of you can communicate with the other via telepathy.

You don't need to share a language with a creature for it to understand your telepathic utterances, and the creature understands you even if it lacks a language. The creature can respond to you telepathically as well, but it must understand at least one language in order to communicate this way. This power has no effect on droids or constructs.

{@b {@i Force Potency.}} When you cast this power using a force slot of 3rd level or higher, the duration increases to {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}, up to 1 hour, and if either you or the creature you are linked to are surprised while the other isn't, and both of you can see each other, the surprised creature can still act normally on its first turn in combat, as if it were not surprised.

entries.name: Vitality Shield
entries: {@i 2nd-level universal power}

You siphon some of your own vitality to create a barrier in the Force around yourself. You take 2d8 true damage, and gain a number of temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to twice the amount of damage you took. If this damage would reduce your {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} to 0, the power fails. While you have these temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Strength, Dexterity and Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. Any remaining temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} are lost when this power ends.
{@b {@i Force Potency.}} When you cast this power using a force slot of 3rd level or higher, the true damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd.

entries.name: Wakefulness
entries: {@i 2nd-level universal power}
You use the Force to control your body's functions. For the duration, you gain the following benefits:

items: You ignore the effects of any levels of {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion} you have.

You do not need to eat, drink, or sleep. You can't be forced to sleep by any means. To gain the benefits of a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can spend all 8 hours doing light activity, such as reading and keeping watch.

entries: If you still have any levels of {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion} when this power ends, you must make a DC 15 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, you gain one additional level of {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion}.

entries.name: Wall Run
entries: {@i At-will universal power}

Until the end of the turn, you have a climbing {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} and you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|sw5e-phb}) and Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) checks that involve movement. For the same duration, you can move up, down, and across vertical surfaces while leaving your hands free. This does not allow you to move upside down along ceilings. If you are on a vertical surface when you no longer have a climbing {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}, you immediately fall unless you have some other means of remaining there.

entries.name: Agonizing Lethargy
entries: {@i {@b Mental maneuver}} You can use an action to expend a superiority die. When you do so, choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The target must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the target takes 1d6 necrotic damage for each attack it makes until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Assess the Situation
entries: {@i {@b General maneuver}} You can expend one superiority die to make a Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}) check as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, adding the superiority die to the check.

entries.name: Befogging Ichor
entries: {@i {@b Mental maneuver}} You can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to expend a superiority die. When you do so, choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The target must make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the target can't take reactions until the start of its next turn and on its turn must use its movement to move half its {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} in a random direction. Roll a {@dice d8} and assign a direction to each face. If the direction rolled is blocked, the target doesn't move.

entries.name: Chains of Transfixing
entries: {@i {@b Mental maneuver}} You can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to expend a superiority die. When you do so, choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you that is no more than one size larger than you. The target must succeed on a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or gain four {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} levels until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Daring Escape
entries: {@i {@b General maneuver}} You can expend one superiority die to take the {@action Disengage|sw5e-phb} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on your turn. Until the end of this turn, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to break effects that would grapple, restrain or slow you.

entries.name: Dark Transference
entries: {@i {@b Mental maneuver}} When you hit a creature with an attack, you can expend a superiority die and roll it to attempt to {@spell Siphon Life|sw5e-phb|siphon life} from it. The target must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, add the result to the damage roll, and you regain one expended Hit Die.

entries.name: Deathseek
entries: {@i {@b Mental maneuver}} When an attack made against a hostile creature that you can see would miss, you can use a {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and expend a superiority die and roll it to force the creature to instead take the hit. The creature must make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the target takes the minimum damage the attack could have dealt plus additional damage equal to the result of the superiority die.

entries.name: Deliberate Movement
entries: {@i {@b General maneuver}} You can expend one superiority die to take the {@action Dash|sw5e-phb} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} and ignore the effects of unenhanced {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain} until the end of your turn.

entries.name: Go Get 'Em
entries: {@i {@b General maneuver}} {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Companion} While your companion is moving, you can expend a superiority die and add 5 times the number rolled to its movement {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}.

entries.name: Loyal Bond
entries: {@i {@b General maneuver}} {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Companion} Whenever you are hit with an attack, you can expend one superiority die to command your companion to immediately use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and move up to its {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} directly towards you. If it ends this movement within 5 feet of you, roll the superiority die. Your companion takes the damage instead of you, subtracting the amount you rolled from the total.

entries.name: Pin Down
entries: {@i {@b General maneuver}} {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Companion} When your companion attempts to grapple or knock a creature prone, you can expend a superiority die to give it direction as long as it can see or hear you. Roll a superiority die and add it to your companion's Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) check.

entries.name: Primal Endurance
entries: {@i {@b General maneuver}} {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Companion} As an action, you can expend a superiority die to improve your companion's defense. Roll the die and add it to your companion's AC until the beginning of your next turn.

entries.name: Reverse Curse
entries: {@i {@b Mental maneuver}} When another creature attempts to charm or frighten you or an ally you can see within 15 feet of you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and expend a superiority die and roll it to attempt to turn the effect back on that creature. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be be {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} or {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} by you, dependent on the triggering ability, for a number of rounds equal to the die roll or until the creature takes any damage.

entries.name: Shadow Puppetry
entries: {@i {@b Mental maneuver}} When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and expend a superiority die to give that creature a final act of aggression. That creature can immediately move a number of feet equal to 5 times the result of the die and make a single {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} against a target of your choice within its attack range, adding the die to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}.

entries.name: Sic 'Em
entries: {@i {@b General maneuver}} {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Companion} As an action, you can expend a superiority die and command your companion to savage a nearby enemy. Your companion can use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to immediately move up to 10 feet and make one attack, adding the {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} to the damage roll on a hit.

entries.name: Spine-Chilling Howls
entries: {@i {@b General maneuver}} {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Companion} As an action, you can expend one superiority die to command your companion to frighten another creature. The target must then succeed on a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your maneuver save DC or become {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} of both you and your companion for 1 minute. The {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} target can repeat the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Water of Life
entries: {@i {@b Mental maneuver}} When an allied creature within 30 feet that you can see takes damage, you can use a {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to expend a superiority die and roll it. The ally regains a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to the roll + your maneuver modifier.

entries.name: Wild Senses
entries: {@i {@b General maneuver}} {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Companion} Whenever you make a Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) or a Wisdom ({@skill Survival|sw5e-phb}) check, you can request the aid of your companion by expending a superiority die, adding the number rolled to the check. You can use this maneuver before or after making the {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, but before the results of the {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} are determined.

entries.name: Wracking Torment
entries: {@i {@b Mental maneuver}} When a hostile creature you can see within 30 feet would take damage from an effect you or a friendly creature controls, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and expend a superiority die to temporarily weaken their resilience against it. Until the end of the turn, the target loses resistance to the damage types of the triggering attack or power.

entries.name: Biology and Appearance
entries: The hulking abyssin have long limbs and a single large eye that dominates their foreheads. Typically well-muscled, the abyssin's stooping gait results in a slightly hunched appearance.

A distinctive trait of the abyssin is their ability to heal quickly; their fast regeneration is believed to have been an adaptation to prevent fluid loss via bleeding on their desert homeworld. All cells in the abyssin body are replaced every 80 hours, and organs which typically were paired in other species appear singularly.

entries.name: Society and Culture
entries: A primitive tribal society, the abyssin of Byss are known as violent and brutish, and their planet is avoided by most beings in the civilized galaxy. Unstable resources on Byss do not allow for mass population growth or for the stabilization of a central government, economy or trade system.

Existing simply in nomadic tribes, abyssin groups can interact peacefully with one another, though only if both groups have plentiful water and food supplies. Otherwise, they began a 'Blooding', a brawl that ends only when one tribe's warriors are all killed, captured, or {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated}. Warriors who survive a Blooding are usually allowed to join the winning tribe once they finish their regeneration. This tradition led to some violent incidents when spacers tried to make first contact and trade with Abyssin tribes with scarce water resources, especially since the abyssin assumed the alien traders could regenerate as quickly as they did.

entries.name: Names
entries: There does not appear to be any distinction between male and female names for abyssin. Abyssin don't use surnames.
{@b Names.} Anami, Easym, Myo, Qawohl, Seh-run, Sidie

entries.name: Abyssin Traits
entries: As an abyssin, you have the following special traits.
{@b {@i Ability Score Increase.}} Your Constitution score increases by 2, and your Strength score increases by 1.
{@b {@i Age.}} Abyssin reach adulthood at age 30 and can live up to 300 years thanks to their regenerative abilities.
{@b {@i Alignment.}} Abyssin's violent and anarchic upbringing cause them to tend toward the dark side, though there are exceptions.
{@b {@i Size.}} Abyssin stand around 6 feet tall and weigh between 200 and 400 lbs. Regardless of your position in that range, your size is Medium.
{@b {@i Speed.}} Your base walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is 30 feet.

{@b {@i Rapidly Regenerative.}} You heal quickly, both at will and in response to danger. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can choose to spend one of your Hit Dice to recover {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}. Additionally, when you take damage, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and expend a Hit Die to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} as long as the damage would not reduce your {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} to 0.

{@b {@i Rugged Survivalist.}} You are proficient in the {@skill Survival|sw5e-phb} skill. Additionally, you are naturally adapted to hot climates, as described in {@book chapter 5|sw5e-phb|5} of the Dungeon Master's Guide.

{@b {@i Tech-Impaired.}} While abyssin can figure out basic technology, they experience difficulty using more complex equipment like wristpads. You can not use {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} or take levels in {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} classes.

{@b {@i Savage Attacks.}} When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, you can roll one of the weapon's damage dice one additional time and add it to the extra damage of the {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit}.

{@b {@i Languages.}} You can speak, read, and write {@language Galactic Basic|sw5e-phb} and Abyssin. Abyssin uses mainly growls and grunts that many species consider primitive. The written form of language uses only a small number of simple hieroglyphs.

rows: Green, brown, muddy yellow, or tan
Large eyes, single horn on head, pointed ears

entries.name: Biology and Appearance
entries: Advozsec evolved from herbivorous reptile-analogs which fed on the vegetation known to form around Riflor's hot springs. Evolving into a class of reptomammal, advozsec have a single horn at the crown of their heads, four digits on each hand and foot, pointed ears, and large eyes. Advozsec are strictly vegetarian, unable to properly digest meat. The geothermal hot springs that appear on their homeworld forced the species to evolve thick skin in order to survive. The large eyes of the advozsec are adaptations to the clouds of volcanic ash which darken Riflor's skies.

entries.name: Society and Culture
entries: Since so much of the sunlight on Riflor is blocked by volcanic eruptions, advozsec tend to settle near geothermal springs for heat. Unfortunately, these springs also tend to be in geologically unstable regions, and anything built near them is often destroyed or abandoned due to eruptions or groundquakes. As a result, the advozse people ended up having little attachment to material goods or long-term plans, and developed a pessimistic, selfish, and even paranoid outlook on life. This facet of their culture remained long after contact with the Galactic Republic gave them access to modern construction techniques allowing for more permanent buildings. Seeing financial stability as the only truly achievable stability one could find in life, the advozsec constantly strive to accumulate as much monetary wealth as they can in a lifetime in order to have the ability to rebuild when the worst happens.

entries.name: Names
entries: Advozsec have simple names that do not distinguish between genders, using familiar surnames.
{@b First Names.} Dleck, Fjemm, Gorde, Rollar, Xon {@b Surnames.} Ghantere, Leventraim, Timack, Vy, Zimda

entries.name: Advozse Traits
entries: As an advozse, you have the following special traits.
{@b {@i Ability Score Increase.}} Your Constitution score increases by 2, and your Wisdom score increases by 1.
{@b {@i Age.}} Advozsec reach adulthood in their late teens and typically live for over half a century.
{@b {@i Alignment.}} Advozsec's paranoid and pessimistic nature causes them to tend towards balanced alignments, particularly lawful balanced, though there are exceptions.
{@b {@i Size.}} Advozsec typically stand 5 to 6 feet tall and generally weigh about 130 lbs. Regardless of your position in that range, your size is Medium.
{@b {@i Speed.}} Your base walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is 30 feet.

{@b {@i Darkvision}} Your vision can easily cut through darkness. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.
{@b {@i Hide.}} You have a thick hide. While you are unarmored or wearing {@filter light armor|items|type=light armor}, your AC is 12 + your Dexterity modifier.

{@b {@i Horn.}} Your sharp horn is a natural weapon, which you can use to make {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes}. Additionally, your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes} deal 1d4 kinetic damage.
{@b {@i Lava Dweller.}} Your body is well accustomed to extreme heat, giving you resistance to fire damage.

{@b {@i Vigilant.}} When you would roll {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative}, you can choose to have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the roll. Once you've done so, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can do so again.

{@b {@i Languages.}} You can speak, read, and write {@language Galactic Basic|sw5e-phb} and Advb. Advb sounds quick and aggressive. It's incredibly rare to find a non-advozsec speaking Advb, some linguists even considering it all but a dead language.

rows: Force-sensitivity, unique technology, six green tongues
Aing-Tii homeworld in the Kathol Rift
Non-verbal communication  via taste, smell, and touch

entries.name: Biology and Appearance
entries: The aing-tii are a species of sentient, toothless mammals who stand on two clawed feet with two spindly arms, each with three large digits. Their bodies are covered in jointed white, bony plates covered in unique painted motifs. The aing-tii head is small and juts out perpendicularly from their chest, featuring two large eyes and six long, thin, green tongues extending from their mouths. They have a long, prehensile tail. The species is incapable of producing sound and conveys information via tasting, smelling and touching each other with their tongues.

entries.name: Society and Culture
entries: The aing-tii are native to a planet whose location in the Kathol Rift is a closely guarded secret. Although in a dangerous area of space, the majority of Aing-Tii never leave their homeworld nor have any contact with the outside world. Those who do—commonly called aing-tii warrior monks—are often xenophobic and reclusive. The monks spend their entire lives performing errands for their gods, in the hope that they will receive "an answer" from them. The aing-tii hate slavery, and often attack slavers who roam the Kathol Outback.

While the aing-tii are Force-sensitive, they avoid wielding the Force, which they see as sacred. The aing-tii believe that everything is somehow guided by the Force. They do not believe in the light or dark sides of the Force. Instead, they hold that there are many different aspects to the Force.

entries.name: Names
entries: Aing-tii names are, in reality, non-verbal and only truly understandable via taste, smell, and touch.  The few aing-tii who have been known to the outside world have used translators to convey an auditory identifier.
{@b Male Names.} Ben'Sur, Looshen'Fel, Tadar'Ro {@b Female Names.} Kulan'Pa, Laman'So, Te'Nuriel

entries.name: Aing-Tii Traits
entries: As an aing-tii, you have the following special traits.
{@b {@i Ability Score Increase.}} Your Wisdom score increases by 2, and your Constitution score increases by 1.
{@b {@i Age.}} Aing-tii reach adulthood in their late teens and live more than a century.
{@b {@i Alignment.}} Aing-tii's foreign nature causes them to be hard to understand. Most aing-tii tend toward neutral light side, though there are exceptions.
{@b {@i Size.}} Aing-tii typically stand 6 to 7 feet tall and generally weigh about 200 lbs. Regardless of your position in that range, your size is Medium.
{@b {@i Speed.}} Your base walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is 30 feet.
{@b {@i Armored Plates.}} You have thick armored plates. While you are unarmored or wearing {@filter light armor|items|type=light armor}, your AC is 13 + your Dexterity modifier.

{@b {@i Closed Mind.}} Aing-tii have a natural attunement for the Force, which makes them resistant to its powers. You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Wisdom and Charisma {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

{@b {@i Force-Sensitive.}} You know the {@i force push/pull} at-will {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}. Wisdom or Charisma (your choice) is your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} for this power.
{@b {@i Prehensile Tail.}} You have supreme control over your tail and can use it to manipulate objects as well as your hands.
{@b {@i Wisdom of the Elders.}} You are proficient in the {@skill Lore|sw5e-phb} skill.
{@b {@i Languages.}} You can understand, read, and write {@language Galactic Basic|sw5e-phb}, and the non-verbal communication of the aing-tii. However, you cannot speak or make noise verbally.

rows: Short stature, scaly skin, crested head

entries.name: Biology and Appearance
entries: Aleena are short, reptilian bipeds with large eyes and wide mouths full of small, sharp teeth. Aleena's bodies are long compared to their short arms and stubby legs. Warm-blooded reptiles, they possess exceptional reflexes as well as a fast metabolism which allow them to convert food into energy very rapidly in order to escape predators on their harsh home planet.

entries.name: Society and Culture
entries: Aleena are social and tend to thrive best in with close-knit teams if not with their own kind. They develop strong loyalties to friends and protect those they care about fiercely. Due to their inborn curiosity, the aleena are stereotypically galactic travelers, tourists in every sense. This, combined with their strong dedication to their relatives, results in aleena families traveling even to most unusual and dangerous locations just to see its sights. The appearance of aleena family walking through an intergalactic metropolis is a common sight on many planets. The aleena's love of sports and particularly, adventure and thrill sports, draw many into the galactic community. Most who enter professional classes are experts or diplomats.

Aleena settlements were small, and most individuals were part of a single lineage, or tahiko. The leader of each tahiko led the community, and represented their wishes to the planetary advisory body. The advisory body elected a king to govern the planet, and was generally revered as a religious figure as they led religious ceremonies.

entries.name: Names
entries: Aleena names are generally short and guttural, with longer names being saved for royalty. Surnames are based on their tahiko, or tribal lineage.
{@b Male Names.} Batts, Gratz, Wakka, Zakan, Zetts {@b Female Names.} Arkei, Harza, Sutci, Tsuon, Yenn, {@b Surnames.} Anares, Kylar, Ors, Practes, Targae

entries.name: Aleena Traits
entries: As an aleena, you have the following special traits.
{@b {@i Ability Score Increase.}} Your Dexterity score increases by 2, and your Charisma score increases by 1.
{@b {@i Age.}} Aleena reach adulthood in their late teens and live to be about 80.
{@b {@i Alignment.}} Aleena's benevolent yet curious nature causes them to tend toward chaotic light side, though there are exceptions.
{@b {@i Size.}} Aleena typically stand 2 and a half to 3 feet tall and generally weigh about 35 lbs. Regardless of your position in that range, your size is Small.
{@b {@i Speed.}} Your base walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is 25 feet.

{@b {@i Bite.}} Your sharp teeth are a natural weapon, which you can use to make {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes}. Additionally, your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes} deal 1d4 kinetic damage. Lastly, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can perform a special bite attack. On a hit, the target suffers the attack's normal effects, you gain temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1), and you can't use this trait again until you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
{@b {@i Cosmopolitan.}} You have proficiency in {@skill Lore|sw5e-phb}.
{@b {@i Nimble Escape.}} You can take the Disengage or {@action Hide|sw5e-phb} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on each of its turns.
{@b {@i Nimbleness.}} You can move through the space of any creature that is of a size larger than yours.

{@b {@i Racer's Reflexes.}} Whenever you make a Dexterity {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can choose to add 1d4 to the result. You can choose to do this after the check is rolled, but before the DM determines if you've passed or failed the check. You cannot do so again until you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

{@b {@i Undersized.}} Your small stature makes it hard for you to wield bigger weapons. You can't use heavy shields. Additionally, you can't use {@filter Martial weapons|items|type=martial weapon} with the two-handed property unless it also has the light property, and if a martial weapon has the versatile property, you can only wield it in two hands.

{@b {@i Languages.}} You can speak, read, and write {@language Galactic Basic|sw5e-phb} and Aleena. Aleena is characterized by its use of short syllables and energetic movements to convey urgency and emotion.

entries.name: Biology and Appearance
entries: Anomid are a species of humanoids with translucent, purple-hued skin that is smooth but wrinkles with age. They have large, slender hands with six fingers on each: two end fingers, two center fingers and two thumbs, with a sharp claw on each. The fingers are paired in twos and slightly spaced apart from the others. The eyes of the anomids are solid, with no visible irises or pupils and have been seen in varying shades of yellow or blue. The anomids have pointed, fin-like ears that protrude from the sides of their heads. Anomid hair is often long and well kept, and is always found in shades of black, gray or white.

entries.name: Society and Culture
entries: Anomids almost always wear elaborate masks which {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} most of their faces. These are not breath masks, but vocalizer units. Since anomids have no vocal cords, they rely on these vocalizer masks to communicate with other species. These masks are often elaborately customized to reflect an anomid's social status, family origin, or profession. Among themselves, anomids communicate using an elaborate sign language. Anomid sign language requires six-fingered hands, which makes it difficult for humans or human-programmed protocol droids to use.
Anomid civilization has a long history of pacifism and technical achievement. In fact, most Anomids are pacifists—historians believed that no major wars have ever been fought in the Yablari system.

entries.name: Names
entries: Anomid names are usually one or two syllables long, featuring hard consonants. Female names are often softer, with a greater flow to them. Surnames are familial.
{@b Male Names.} Arkis, Jarak, Magris, Vell {@b Female Names.} Apharis, Eralie, Siphanie, Ulaniye {@b Surnames.} Dekan, Krest, Narroc, Quill, Wode

entries.name: Anomid Traits
entries: As an anomid, you have the following special traits.
{@b {@i Ability Score Increase.}} Your Intelligence score increases by 2, and your Wisdom score increases by 1.
{@b {@i Age.}} Anomid reach adulthood in their late teens and live a little under a century.
{@b {@i Alignment.}} Anomid's pacifistic culture causes them to tend toward light alignments, though there are exceptions.
{@b {@i Size.}} Anomid typically stand 5 to 6 feet tall and generally weigh about 120 lbs. Regardless of your position in that range, your size is Medium.
{@b {@i Speed.}} Your base walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is 30 feet.

{@b {@i Agricultural Exports.}} Whenever you make an Intelligence ({@skill Nature|sw5e-phb}) or Intelligence ({@skill Technology|sw5e-phb}) check related to food, agriculture, or agricultural technology, you are considered to have {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in the skill.

{@b {@i Tech Dabbler.}} You know the {@i minor hologram} at-will {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. When you reach 3rd level, you learn and can cast the {@i repair droid} {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} once per {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. When you reach 5th level, you learn and can cast the {@i hold droid} {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} once per {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. Your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} is Intelligence. You require use of a {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad} for these powers.

{@b {@i Tech Resistance.}} Growing up around technology leaves an impact on anomid. You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Dexterity and Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.
{@b {@i Tech Savant.}} You have proficiency in the {@skill Technology|sw5e-phb} skill.
{@b {@i Vocalizer.}} Anomid have no vocal cords, and rely on a vocalizer to communicate with other species. If your vocalizer is removed or destroyed, you cannot speak.
{@b {@i Wealthy.}} During character creation, you start with additional credits equal to your level x your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} x 1,000 cr.

{@b {@i Languages.}} You can speak, read, and write {@language Galactic Basic|sw5e-phb} through the use of your vocalizer. You can also use Anomid Sign Language, which is an elaborate language requiring six-fingered hands.

rows: Hunched stature, mood sensitive crests, tails

entries.name: Biology and Appearance
entries: The anx are a bipedal, reptilian species discernible by their height, their tall crests, and their tails. Originating from a world with higher-than-average gravity, the anx possess a stooped stature. Their heads are tall and blade-shaped, with a soaring crest which acts as a sinus cavity. While their crests change color to reflect their moods, its primary function gives anx a low rumbling voice. An anx's large, muscular tail serves as a counterbalance for running.
Anx have long necks and limbs, and would appear taller if they didn't walk with their shoulders stooped and their crested heads held out in front of them.

entries.name: Society and Culture
entries: The anx are serene giants who assume many roles in the Republic. Evolving from herd animals, the anx are a placid, sociable race known for developing a near fanatical interest in groups they related to. Living in complicated clan structures, anx enjoy the company of their large families and are more comfortable in groups.

An innate trait among the anx is a formidable knowledge of anatomy, especially in regard to nerves, muscles and bone structures. Due to this extensive knowledge, even by species they have never encountered, the anx are considered dangerous unarmed combatants and skilled warriors, capable of incapacitating opponents with a single, well-placed strike.

entries.name: Names
entries: Anx names are less harsh-sounding compared to those of other reptilian species. Surnames are familial.
{@b Male Names.} Drexol, Graxol, Horox, Theen {@b Female Names.} Kendiula, Madurrin, Pipalidi, Quiyya {@b Surnames.} Fida, Jur, Kelvyyn, Ryyd

entries.name: Anx Traits
entries: As an anx, you have the following special traits: {@b {@i Ability Score Increase.}} Your Constitution score increases by 2, and your Wisdom score increases by 1.
{@b {@i Age.}} Anx reach adulthood in their late teens and live up to 120 years.
{@b {@i Alignment.}} The anx's social nature causes them to tend toward the light side, though there are exceptions.
{@b {@i Size.}} Anx stand at around 8 feet tall and weigh about 200 lbs. Regardless of your position in that range, your size is Medium.
{@b {@i Speed.}} Your base walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is 30 feet.

{@b {@i Acute Smell.}} Whenever you make a Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) check involving smell, you are considered to have {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in the {@skill Perception|sw5e-phb} skill.
{@b {@i Anatomical Knowledge.}} You have proficiency in the {@skill Medicine|sw5e-phb} skill.

{@b {@i Subsonic Bellow.}} As an action, you can violently expel air in a 15-foot cone. When you do so, each creature in the area of the exhalation must make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Constitution modifier). A creature takes 2d6 sonic damage on a failed save, and half as much damage on a successful one. The damage increases to 4d6 at 5th level, 6d6 at 11th level, and 8d6 at 17th level. This ability has no effect on constructs. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

{@b {@i Surgical Strikes.}} Your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes} deal 1d4 kinetic damage. Additionally, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can perform a special pressure point attack. On a hit, the target suffers the attack—s normal effects, and it must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Constitution modifier). On a failed save, the target is {@condition Stunned|sw5e-phb|stunned} until the end of its next turn, and you can—t use this feature again until you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

{@b {@i Languages.}} You can speak, read, and write {@language Galactic Basic|sw5e-phb} and Anx. Anx is mostly characterized by low, rumbling noises made by the throat, amplified by an anx's crest. Anx are able to communicate over long distances with each other by using loud low-frequency sounds.

entries.name: Biology and Appearance
entries: The anzellans are a diminutive species hailing from the secluded planet Anzella. Their eyes have floating corneal micro-lenses that allow them to see microscopic details. Anzellans are a bubbly and receptive people. They are a jovial and trusting people that tend to welcome strangers with open arms.
Due to their volcanic homeworld, anzellans are also adapted towards heat. This, coupled with their small size, make them well-suited to working in compact places.

entries.name: Society and Culture
entries: Anzella is a tropical planet covered in thousands of small volcanic islands. Many of these islands are developed as small villages, with the largest islands designed to accommodate larger species. Anzellan culture is generally based around tourism and crafting; in fact, anzellans are renowned craftsmen due to their discerning eyesight and ability to fit into small spaces.

Anzellan government is generally casual. Each village has its own governing council of rotating members; these villages act independently from one another unless their decisions would affect more than a single island. In that case, all of the councils work together to come to a planet-wide decision.

entries.name: Names
entries: Anzellan names are rarely longer than two syllables, with a bouncy intonation to them. Their surnames are familial.
{@b Male Names.} Babu, Gridel, Moru, Rano, Yodel {@b Female Names.} Dibi, Fing, Nooni, Teena, Zazi {@b Surnames.} E'ayoo, Frik, Meer, Tanni, Vrut

entries.name: Anzellan Traits
entries: As an anzellan, you have the following special traits.
{@b {@i Ability Score Increase.}} Your Intelligence score increases by 2, and two other ability scores of your choice increase by 1.
{@b {@i Age.}} Anzellans are considered adults at ten years old. They are a short-lived species, however, that rarely lives longer than 60 years.
{@b {@i Alignment.}} Anzellans are a friendly and respectful people, which causes them to tend toward lawful light side, though there are exceptions.
{@b {@i Size.}} Anzellans stand between 1 and 2 feet tall and weigh around 10 lbs. Regardless of your position in that range, your size is Tiny.
{@b {@i Speed.}} Your base walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is 20 feet.
{@b {@i Crafters.}} You have proficiency in one tool of your choice.

{@b {@i Detail Oriented.}} You are {@feat Practiced|sw5e-phb|practiced} at scouring for details. You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}) checks that rely on sight within 5 feet.

{@b {@i Pintsized.}} Your tiny stature makes it hard for you to wield bigger weapons. You can't use medium or heavy shields. Additionally, you can't wield weapons with the two-handed or versatile property, and you can only wield one-handed weapons in two hands unless they have the light property.

{@b {@i Puny.}} Anzellans are too small to pack much of a punch. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}, and when determining your bonus to attack and damage rolls for weapon attacks using Strength, you can't add more than +3.

{@b {@i Small and Nimble.}} You are too small and fast to effectively target. You have a +1 bonus to AC, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}.
{@b {@i Tanned.}} You are naturally adapted to hot climates, as described in {@book chapter 5|sw5e-phb|5} of the Dungeon Master's Guide.
{@b {@i Technician.}} You are proficient in the {@skill Technology|sw5e-phb} skill.

{@b {@i Tinker.}} You have proficiency with {@item Tinker's implements|sw5e-phb|tinker's implements}. You can use these and spend 1 hour and 100 cr worth of materials to construct a Tiny Device (AC 5, 1 hp). You can take the {@action Use an Object|sw5e-phb} action to have your device cause one of the following effects: create a small explosion, create a repeating loud noise for 1 minute, create smoke for 1 minute, create a soothing melody for 1 minute. You can maintain a number of these devices up to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} at once, and a device stops functioning after 24 hours away from you. You can dismantle the device to reclaim the materials used to create it.
