{@b {@i Aquatic Adaptation.}} You adapt your body to an aquatic environment. You can breathe underwater and gain a swimming {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}.

{@b {@i Change Appearance.}} You transform your appearance. You decide what you look like, including your height, weight, facial features, sound of your voice, hair length, coloration, and distinguishing characteristics, if any. You can make yourself appear as a member of another species (an organic species cannot appear as a droid, or vice versa), though none of your statistics change. You can also alter your vocal cords, enabling you to speak a language you know, but otherwise would be incapable of speaking. You also can’t appear as a creature of a different size than you, and your basic shape stays the same; if you’re bipedal, you can’t use this power to become quadrupedal, for instance. At any time for the duration of the power, you can use your action to change your appearance in this way again.

{@b {@i Natural Weapons.}} You grow claws, fangs, spines, horns, or a different natural weapon of your choice. Your damage die for your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes} increases by one step (from 1 to {@dice d4}, {@dice d4} to {@dice d6}, or {@dice d6} to {@dice d8}). Your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes} are considered enhanced and you have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls with them.

entries.name: Barrage
entries: {@i 1st-level tech power}

You launch 4d6 tiny projectiles at up to four creatures you can see within range. The projectiles can be divided between the targets as desired. Each target must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A target takes 1 kinetic damage per projectile, or half as much damage on a successful save.

{@b {@i Overcharge Tech.}} When you cast this power using a tech slot of 2nd level or higher, you launch an additional 1d6 projectiles and can target one additional creature for each slot level above 1st.

entries.name: Burst of Flame
entries: {@i 2nd-level tech power}

You expel a burst of flame in a line 30 feet long and 5 feet wide, originating from you. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A creature takes 3d8 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
{@b {@i Overcharge Tech.}} When you cast this power using a tech slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd.

entries.name: Construct Droid
entries: {@i 2nd-level tech power}

You construct a droid, which is deployed in an unoccupied space that you can see within range. This droid uses the Constructed Droid stat block. When you cast the power, choose a design: Probe, Pyro, or Battle. The droid resembles a Class IV droid, and the design determines certain traits in its stat block. The droid falls to pieces and disintegrates when it drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} or when the power ends.

The droid is an ally to you and your companions. In combat, the droid shares your {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It obeys your commands you issue through your tech focus (no action required). If you don’t issue any, it takes the {@action Dodge|sw5e-phb} action and uses its movement to avoid danger.
The droid is a valid target for the {@i tracker droid interface} power. If that power is cast targeting the constructed droid, it only takes 1 minute to synchronize with the droid.
{@b {@i Overcharge Tech.}} When you cast this power using a tech slot of 3rd level or higher, use the higher level wherever the power’s level appears in the stat block.

entries.name: Constructed Droid
entries: {@i Medium droid, unaligned} - {@b Armor Class} 11 + the level of the power (natural armor) - {@b Hit Points} 20 (Probe only) or 30 (Pyro and Battle only) + 10 for each slot level above 2nd - {@b Speed} 30 ft. (Pyro and Battle only); 0 ft. and fly 60 ft. (Probe only)

- {@b Damage Vulnerabilities} ion - {@b Damage Resistances} necrotic, poison, psychic - {@b Condition Immunities} disease, {@condition Poisoned|sw5e-phb|poisoned} - {@b Senses} {@sense Darkvision|sw5e-phb|darkvision} 60 ft, passive {@skill Perception|sw5e-phb} 12 - {@b Languages} {@language Galactic Basic|sw5e-phb}, {@language Binary|sw5e-phb|Binary}, understands the languages you speak - {@b Proficiency Bonus} equals your bonus {@b {@i Circuitry.}} The construct has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against effects that would deal ion or lightning damage. {@b {@i Surveillance (Probe Only).}} The probe is proficient in {@skill Perception|sw5e-phb} and one other skill or tool of your choice. ### Actions {@b {@i Multiattack.}} The droid makes a number of attacks equal to half this power’s level (rounded down). {@b {@i Blaster.}} {@i Ranged Weapon Attack:} your tech attack modifier to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit: 1d6 + 3 + the power's level energy damage. {@b {@i Vibroweapon. (Battle Only)}} {@i Melee Weapon Attack:} your tech attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 1d12 + 3 + the power's level kinetic damage. {@b {@i Flamethrower. (Pyro Only)}} The droid shoots a stream of flame from itself in a 15-foot cone. Creatures in the cone must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = your tech save DC). On a failure, the creature takes 1d8 fire damage + 1d8 fire damage for each power level above 2nd. On a success, the creature takes half as much damage. This cannot be used with Multiattack.

entries.name: Cryogenic Blow
entries: {@i 1st-level tech power}

The next time you hit a creature with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} during this power's duration, the attack deals an extra 1d6 cold damage to the target. The target must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, it gains a level of {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} for the duration. At the start of each of its turns, the target can repeat the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, ending the effect on itself on a success.
{@b {@i Overcharge Tech.}} If you cast this power using a tech slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 1st.

entries.name: Delayed Detonator
entries: {@i 1st-level tech power}

Choose a point you can see within range. You launch a detonator at that point, which remains there until the start of your next turn, when it explodes, ending the power. You can also use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} at any point during the power's duration to cause the detonator to explode early. When the detonator explodes, each creature within 5 feet of the point must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A creature takes 1d8 fire damage and 1d8 kinetic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

{@b {@i Overcharge Tech.}} When you cast this power using a tech slot of 2nd level or higher, you can launch an additional detonator at another point you can see within range for each slot level above 1st. The detonators all explode simultaneously. A creature in the area of more than one detonator when they explode is only affected once.

entries.name: Detonator
entries: {@i At-will tech power}

You launch a detonator at a creature. Make a ranged tech attack against a creature you can see within range. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 fire damage, and each creature within 5 feet of the target must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or take 1d4 fire damage.
This power's damage increases by one die when you reach 5th level (2d6/2d4), 11th level (3d6/3d4), and 17th level (4d6/4d4).

entries.name: Disassemble
entries: {@i 7th-level tech power}

One constructed object up to 100 lbs. in weight that you touch falls to pieces, separating into its component parts. For instance, a {@item Vibrosword|sw5e-phb|vibrosword} separates into a blade, handle, oscillator, and guard, while a hovercart collapses into a repulsor engine, bolts, and metal panels. If the object is being worn, carried, or operated by a creature, the creature can make an Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a successful save, the item is unaffected.

entries.name: Dismantle
entries: {@i At-will tech power}

You break or tear an unenhanced structure or object you touch that is not being worn or carried by a creature other than you. The break or tear can be up to 1 foot in any dimension. When cast this in this way, this power has a casting time of 1 minute.

Alternatively, you can touch a droid or construct when you cast this power. Make a melee tech attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 energy damage. When cast in this way, this power has a casting time of 1 action.
This power’s damage increases by 1d6 when you reach 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6), and 17th level (4d6).

entries.name: Fabricate
entries: {@i 4th-level tech power}
You convert raw materials into products of the same material. For example, you can fabricate a wooden bridge from a clump of trees, a rope from a patch of hemp, and clothes from bantha hide.

Choose raw materials that you can see within range. You can fabricate a Large or smaller object (contained within a 10-foot cube, or eight connected 5-foot cubes), given a sufficient quantity of raw material. If you are working with metal, stone, or another mineral substance, however, the fabricated object can be no larger than Medium (contained within a single 5-foot cube). The quality of objects made by the power is commensurate with the quality of the raw materials.

Creatures or enhanced items can't be created by this power. You also can't use it to create items that ordinarily require a high degree of craftsmanship, such as jewelry, weapons, glass, or armor, unless you have proficiency with the type of tool used to craft such objects.

entries.name: Fabricate Minor Trap
entries: {@i 1st-level tech power}

You ward a 30-foot radius sphere centered on you with a manually-operated trap. The trap is well disguised. Any creature that can’t see the area at the time the power is cast must make a Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) check against your tech save DC to notice the trap before entering the area. Once after this power is cast, when a creature you can see enters or moves within the warded area, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to trigger the trap. The effect on the creature depends on the kind of trap you employ, which you choose when you cast this power. You can maintain a maximum number of instances of this power at once equal to your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} modifier.

{@b {@i Blaster.}} This power creates a {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} turret which fires at the target when triggered. The creature must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. It takes 2d10 energy damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.

{@b {@i Pitfall.}} This power creates a 5-foot diameter, 15-foot deep pitfall in the ground beneath the creature when triggered, which must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, the creature falls into the pitfall. On a success, the creature falls {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone} in a space within 5 feet of the pitfall. This pitfall cannot be created through manufactured terrain. Otherwise, the hole is well constructed and lasts even after the power's duration. Flying creatures avoid this trap.

{@b {@i Snare.}} This power creates a snare of rope, wire, vine, or webs that entangle the creature. The creature must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A Large or larger creature has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on this {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the creature takes 1d6 kinetic damage and is {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained} until the start of its next turn. On a success, the creature takes half as much damage and ends its movement.

{@b {@i Overcharge Tech.}} When you cast this power using a tech slot of 2nd level or higher, the effects increase, based on the trap. {@i Blaster.} The damage increases by 1d10 for each slot level above 1st. If cast using a slot of 3rd level or higher, this power targets creatures in a sphere centered on the triggering creature within the warded area, the radius of which is 5 feet for every two slot levels above 1st. {@i Pitfall.} The depth of the pitfall increases by 5 feet for each slot level above 1st. If cast using a slot of 3rd level or higher, the diameter of the pit is 5 feet wider for every two slot levels above 1st. {@i Snare.} The damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 1st. If cast using a slot of 3rd level or higher, Large creatures no longer have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. This size category increases for every two slot levels above 1st.

entries.name: Greater Energy Shield
entries: {@i 2nd-level tech power}

items: {@b Casting Time:} 1 {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}, which you take when a creature you can see within range is hit by an attack or targeted by the {@i homing rockets} power

entries: An energy shield appears and protects the target. Until the start of the target's next turn, the target has a +5 bonus to AC, including against the triggering attack, and the target takes no damage from {@i homing rockets}.

entries.name: Instant Translocation
entries: {@i 3rd-level tech power}

items: {@b Casting Time:} 1 {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}, which you take when you are hit by an attack

entries: Your form shimmers in a holographic configuration and collapses as an attack begins to hit you. You have a +5 bonus to AC against the triggering attack. As part of the same {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}, you can then teleport to an unoccupied space within 30 feet of you, and can make one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} against the attacker.
{@b {@i Overcharge Tech.}} When you cast this power using a tech slot of 4th level or higher, the maximum teleport distance increases by 10 for each slot level above 3rd.

entries.name: Irradiate
entries: {@i 2nd-level tech power}

A surge of radiation washes over a creature within range. The creature must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the target takes 3d10 necrotic damage and suffers one level of {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion}, which lasts for the duration. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage and does not suffer a level of {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion}. A creature exhausted by this power can make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} at the end of each of its turns. On a successful save, the power ends.
{@b {@i Overcharge Tech.}} When you cast this power using a tech slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d10 for each slot level above 2nd.

entries.name: Itemize
entries: {@i At-will tech power}

You instantly learn the exact quantity of one type of item within 30 feet of you. It must be a type of item that you've handled in the past; you can't, for example, use {@i itemize} to find out how many {@i BKGs} are nearby if you've never handled such a weapon. The object being itemized must also be reasonably specific. You can learn how many meilooruns are nearby, for example, but not how much fruit.

entries.name: Jump
entries: {@i 1st-level tech power}
You touch a creature. The creature's jump distance is tripled until the power ends.

entries.name: Jump Jet
entries: {@i 1st-level tech power}

You boost yourself through the air with a brief surge of repulsor energy. You can rise a number of feet equal to 20 x your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} modifier. You can also move a number of feet horizontally during any part of the movement equal to 5 x your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} modifier. At the end of the turn on which you cast this power, you float gently to the ground if you are still aloft.

{@b {@i Overcharge Tech.}} When you cast this power using a tech slot of 2nd level or higher, you can rise an additional 20 feet, and move horizontally by another 5 feet for each slot level above 1st.

entries.name: Jump Pad
entries: {@i 2nd-level tech power}

You create a bouncy surface in a 5-foot square on a surface within range. When you cast the power, you can designate creatures that can safely use the jump pad. For the duration, whenever a creature you haven't chosen enters the affected area, it must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be launched 10 feet upwards, and 5 feet horizontally in a random direction. To determine the direction, roll a {@dice d8} and assign a direction to each die face.

While a creature you have chosen (or a creature that has succeeded its Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}) is in the area, it can use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to jump with the aid of the bouncy surface. The creature's jump distance for this jump is multiplied by 5.

entries.name: Lesser Mislead
entries: {@i 2nd-level tech power}

You become {@condition Invisible|sw5e-phb|invisible} at the same time that an illusory double of you appears where you are standing. The double lasts until the end of your next turn, but the invisibility ends if you attack or cast a power.
You can use your action to move your illusory double up to your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} and make it gesture, speak, and behave in whatever way you choose.
As soon as it is attacked or would take damage, the double dissipates.

entries.name: Mutate/Augment
entries: {@i 3rd-level tech power}

You alter your body with tech, temporarily gaining new properties which last for the duration. You can select three of the following properties. You cannot select a property more than once, unless that property says otherwise.

items: Your body becomes more flexible. You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against effects that would grapple or restrain you, and your movement is unaffected by {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain} or squeezing.

You grow one additional appendage. This appendage serves as an arm and a hand, though it can take the shape of a limb, tentacle, or similar appendage. You can select this property twice to grow a maximum number of two appendages. You can only gain the benefit of items held by two of your arms at any given time, and once per round you can switch which arms you are benefiting from (no action required).
You sprout antennae that give you {@sense Tremorsense|sw5e-phb|tremorsense} out to a range of 30 feet.
You extend the length of your limbs. When you make a melee attack or attempt to grapple, shove, or trip a creature on your turn, your reach for it is 5 feet greater than normal.
You gain a burrowing {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}.
Your flesh hardens. Your AC can't be less than 16, regardless of what kind of armor you're wearing.

You can gain the benefits of any one option of the {@i alter self} power. You can select this property multiple times to gain the benefits of multiple options of the {@i alter self} power, choosing a different option each time.

You gain the effect of the {@i magnetic hold} power, but you can affix to and move along any surface, instead of only metallic surfaces. You have a climbing {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}.
You can gain any one effect of the {@i force enlightenment} power.

entries: {@b {@i Overcharge Tech.}} When you cast this power using a tech slot of 4th level or higher, you can select an additional property for each slot level above 3rd.

entries.name: Production Values
entries: {@i At-will tech power}
You cause a minor effect within range. Choose one of the following:

items: Your natural voice booms up to three times louder than normal for 1 minute. You can also alter the sound of your voice to achieve a certain effect--to sound more intimidating, for example.
You cause unenhanced electronic lights to flicker, brighten, dim, or change color for 1 minute.
You cause harmless tremors in the ground for 1 minute.
You create a sound within range for up to 1 minute. The sound can range in volume from a whisper to a scream.
You instantaneously cause an unlocked door or window to fly open or slam shut.
You alter the appearance of your eyes for 1 minute.
You create an illusory image of an object no larger than a 5 foot cube. The illusion is purely visual.

entries: If you cast this power multiple times, you can have up to three of its 1-minute effects active at a time, and you can dismiss such an effect as an action.

A creature that witnesses the effects of this power can use its action to make an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}) check against your tech save DC. On a successful check, the creature discerns that the effects are illusory, and they become faint to the creature.
The maximum number of active effects increases by 3 when you reach 5th level (6), 11th level (9), and 17th level (12).

entries.name: Skill Protocol
entries: {@i 5th-level tech power}
You enhance a droid or construct's protocols. You touch one willing droid or construct and give it {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in one tool or skill of your choice.

You must choose a tool or skill in which the target is proficient and that isn't already benefiting from an effect, such as {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise}, that doubles its {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Spectrum Discharge
entries: {@i 2nd-level tech power}

You touch a willing creature, granting it an elemental charge. Choose acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison or sonic. For the duration, a creature can use an action to expel energy of the chosen type in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, taking 3d6 damage of the chosen type on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
{@b {@i Overcharge Tech.}} When you cast this power using a tech slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 2nd.

entries.name: Stinger
entries: {@i At-will tech power}

You fire a stinging dart at a creature within range. Make a ranged tech attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 poison damage, and if the target is a humanoid or beast, it can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} until the start of your next turn.
This power's damage increases by 1d8 when you reach 5th level (2d8), 11th level (3d8), and 17th level (4d8).

entries.name: Squad Shield
entries: {@i 7th-level tech power}

items: {@b Casting Time:} 1 {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}, which you take in response to an incoming threat

entries: In the face of danger, you create a barrier that protects you and those around you. A faintly glowing sphere of protection with a radius of 10 feet appears. The sphere lasts for the duration.

Any {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} (or {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} that deals energy or lightning damage) of 7th level or lower cast from outside the barrier can't affect creatures or objects within it, even if the power is cast using a higher level tech slot. Such a power can target creatures and objects within the barrier, but the power has no effect on them. Similarly, the area within the barrier is excluded from the areas affected by such powers.
Furthermore, hazards of the following types cannot physically pass through the barrier or affect anything within it.

items: A specific effect, such as a {@item Thermal detonator|sw5e-phb|thermal detonator}'s explosion.
An environmental danger, such as falling rocks or a lava flow.

entries: {@b {@i Overcharge Tech.}} When you cast this power using a tech slot of 8th level or higher, the maximum radius increases by 10 feet for each slot level above 7th. In addition, the barrier blocks powers of one level higher for each slot level above 7th.

entries.name: Time Bomb
entries: {@i 1st-level tech power}

Make a melee tech attack against a target you touch. On a miss, this power ends. On a hit, you deal 2d6 kinetic damage as you plant an explosive charge on the target's body. You can then detonate the charge as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, which ends this power. It deals 1d8 fire damage if detonated on the same turn. It deals 2d8 fire damage on your next turn, increasing by 1d8 for each round you do not detonate it, to a maximum of 6d8. If this power ends before you detonate the charge, the target takes no fire damage.

A creature affected by this power can use an action to attempt to remove the detonator from its person, making a Strength or Dexterity check (the creature chooses the ability to use) against your tech save DC. On a success, this power ends, as the detonator deactivates harmlessly.
{@b {@i Overcharge Tech.}} When you cast this power using a tech slot of 2nd level or higher, the kinetic damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 1st.

entries.name: Transposition
entries: {@i 2nd-level tech power}

Another creature you can see within range has its form shimmer in a holographic configuration before collapsing. The target must succeed on a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (the target can choose to fail), or the target is teleported to an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see within range. The chosen space must be on a surface or in a liquid that can support the target without the target having to squeeze.
{@b {@i Overcharge Tech.}} When you cast this power using a tech slot of 3rd level or higher, the range of the power increases by 30 feet for each slot level above 2nd.

entries.name: Tri-Shot
entries: {@i At-will tech power}

Choose up to three creatures within range, none of whom can be more than 10 feet apart. If you choose three creatures, each target must succeed on a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or take 1d4 energy damage. If you choose two creatures, each target takes 1d6 energy damage on a failed save instead. If you choose only one creature, the target takes 1d8 energy damage on a failed save.
This power's damage increases by one die when you reach 5th level (two dice), 11th level (three dice), and 17th level (four dice).

entries.name: Tune-up
entries: {@i 2nd-level tech power}

Up to six droids or constructs of your choice that you can see within range each regain {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to 2d8 + your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} modifier.
{@b {@i Overcharge Tech.}} When you cast this power using a tech slot of 3rd level or higher, the healing increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd.

entries.name: Warp Strike
entries: {@i At-will tech power}

As part of the action used to cast this power, you must make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} against one creature within your reach, otherwise the power fails. On a hit, the target suffers the attack’s normal effects, and you can teleport to an unoccupied space of your choice within 10 feet of you. If you teleport to a space within 5 feet of the target, the target cannot take reactions until the end of its next turn.

This power’s damage increases when you reach higher levels. At 5th level, the melee attack deals an extra 1d6 energy damage to the target. This extra energy damage increases to 2d6 at 11th level and 3d6 at 17th level.

entries.name: Wire Tow
entries: {@i 2nd-level tech power}

You project a length of wire towards a foe to bring them within your grasp. Make a ranged tech attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 2d10 kinetic damage, and you can pull it up to 25 feet closer to you. If you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit}, the target is also knocked {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}. If the target ends this movement within 5 feet of you and is no more than one size larger than you, the target is {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} by you for the duration.

If a creature you grapple with this power uses its action to escape, it must succeed on a Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|sw5e-phb}) check against your tech save DC to do so.
This power ends if the attack misses or the grapple ends.
{@b {@i Overcharge Tech.}} When you cast this power using a tech slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d10 for each slot level above 2nd.

entries.name: Compound Checks
entries: Occasionally, as GM, you might put forth a task for your players that is more difficult than they might be prepared for, and that task might have multiple ways to accomplish it, such as asking your operative to make an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} to conceal a device on a highly perceptive individual. This task could be reasonable accomplished with a (Dexterity) Sleight of Hand check or a Charisma ({@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}) check. Rather than choosing between the two possible checks, the player could elect to do both. If they do so, they must make two separate {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks}, but the target DC for the checks should be reduced by 5.

For instance, using the above example, you might set the DC for the initial check to be 25, allowing the character to perform a Dexterity ({@skill Sleight Of Hand|sw5e-phb}) check or Charisma ({@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}) check. The player might instead decide to attempt both checks. If they do so, they must instead succeed on a DC 20 Dexterity ({@skill Sleight Of Hand|sw5e-phb}) check and a DC 20 Charisma ({@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}) check. If they succeed on both checks, they accomplish their task. If the fail on either check, they fail the task regardless of the outcome of the other check.

entries.name: Minimum DC
entries: For even more difficult tasks with multiple possible solutions, characters can attempt even more {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks}. For each {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} beyond the first, the DC should decrease by 5, cumulatively, to a minimum DC of 20. For instance, a DC 30 check could instead be accomplished by two separate DC 25 {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} or even three DC 20 {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks}, provided there are sufficient different {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} that could apply.

entries.name: Degrees of Failure
entries: You might also consider implementing degrees of failure if a character attempts to perform compound checks and fails one or more of them. For instance, if a character attempts a compound check with two separate {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} and fails on one or both, you might determine the outcome for failing both to be significantly worse than only failing one.

entries.name: Strenuous Combat
entries: Combat is a stressful activity, both physically and mentally. If you want to add an additional layer to combat to help encourage your players to handle things in a more civilized manner, consider implementing this variant rule.

entries.name: Concluding Combat
entries: At the end of a combat encounter, you might consider having each surviving participant make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to avoid {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion}. The DC for the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} is equal to 10 + the number of complete rounds that occurred during the encounter. On a failure, a creature suffers 1 level of {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion}.

entries.name: More Restful Rest
entries: {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb} is a painful penalty to add to characters, especially if they end up encountering multiple levels of {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion} over the course of a gaming day. When your players' characters complete a {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest} with {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion} from this variant, consider allowing them to spend a Hit Die at the end of that rest to remove one level of {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion}.

If a character encounters multiple levels of {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion} due to this variant, they can spend more Hit Dice to remove the additional levels, either during the same rest or separate ones. Each time they do so, however, the effect is cumulative for each additional level. Removing a second level of {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion} would take two Hit Dice, while a third would take three, and so on. For instance, if a character completes a {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest} with two levels of {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion} from this variant, they could spend one Hit Die to remove one level of {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion}, or three Hit Dice to remove both. Once a creature has completed a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, the number of Hit Dice to be spent to remove this {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion} is reduced back to one.

entries.name: Ammunition Sizes
entries: For the sake of simplicity, ammunition is shared amongst weapons that deal the same damage type. For instance, {@filter all blasters|items|firearm=true} that deal kinetic damage utilize slug cartridges, while {@filter all blasters|items|firearm=true} that deal energy, ion, or other elemental damage types utilize {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}. If you dislike that an {@item Assault cannon|sw5e-phb|assault cannon} and a {@item Blaster pistol|sw5e-phb} utilize the same ammunition, consider the following variant rule.

entries.name: Damage Dice Ammo Size
entries: Slug cartridges and {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells} are each broken down into five size categories, from Tiny to Huge. These new sized ammunitions only fit in weapons that utilize certain damage values, as shown in the below table.
For those weapons with alternative damage types, you'll want to treat their damage as one step higher. Ion damage should be two steps higher or twice the weapon's damage, whichever is lower.

For instance, a {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} which deals 1d8 energy damage would use Medium {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, while a {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} that deals 1d4 kinetic damage would use Tiny slug cartridges. A {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} that deals 1d4 fire damage, however, would use Small {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells} (since we treat that damage as one step higher), as would a {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} that deals 1d3 ion damage (since we treat that damage as two steps higher).

entries.name: Ammo Size Values and Weights
entries: Additionally, the value and weight of these sized munitions would scale, as shown in the table below.

entries.name: Powered by Power Cells
entries: Items that are powered by {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, such as jetpacks or glowrods, would utilize Medium {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}.

entries.name: Alternate Casting
entries: Inspired by the Dimension 20 actual play campaign A Starstruck Odyssey, where one of the main characters is using sentinel bones but with {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} instead of {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting}, I've created the following variant rule.

entries.name: Saving Throws
entries: For the five classes with native casting (consular, engineer, guardian, scout, sentinel) you'll want to make the following adjustments to their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}.

entries.name: Force- and Tech-casting
entries: You'll want to replace the {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} feature with {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting}, and vice versa, as appropriate. Specifically, {@b Force Powers Known}, {@b Force Points}, and {@b Forcecasting Ability} will want to be replaced with {@b Tech Powers Known}, {@b Tech Points}, and {@b Techcasting Ability}, and vice versa, as described below:
Note that Max Power Level is not mentioned because it is not affected by these changes.

items: {@b Consular:} Replace consular {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} with engineer {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting}.
{@b Engineer:} Replace engineer {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} with consular {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting}.
{@b Guardian:} Replace guardian {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} with scout {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting}.

{@b Scout:} Replace scout {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} with guardian {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting}. Mechanist scout should instead replace Improved {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} with sentinel {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting}.

{@b Sentinel:} Replace sentinel {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} with the Improved {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} present in the Mechanist Technique scout archetype, with the following updates: sentinels will have 5 and 6 {@book Tech Powers Known|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, and 2 and 3 tech points, at 1st and 2nd levels, respectively.

{@b Splashcasters:} Replace {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} with {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting}, and vice versa, of the other splashcasting archetype for that class. For instance, Shield Specialist fighter would replace its {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} feature with {@book Adept Specialist|sw5e-ec|1|Adept Specialist} fighter's {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting}.

entries: For the crosscaster archetypes, such as Way of {@skill Technology|sw5e-phb} consular, you can simply flip the powers accordingly.

entries.name: Class Features
entries: Different classes or archetypes with casting as a core component are typically built around that casting's primary ability score. You'll want to update or replace them, as appropriate to the class or archetype, including capstones.

entries.name: Short or Long Rest Recovery
entries: You can also consider swapping the point recovery rest requirements, creating {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest} force points or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} tech points. To do so, you'll want to halve the base number of force points (not accounting for ability modifier) to account for {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest} recovery, or double the base number of tech points (again not accounting for ability modifier) to account for {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} recovery. For instance, a consular with {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} gets four tech points for each consular level (before modifier). If you wanted to do a {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest} {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} consular instead, you'd only receive two tech points per consular level. The opposite would be true for an engineer; while they would get two tech points per engineer level as with {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest} recovery {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting}, they would instead get four tech points per engineer level for {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} casting (again, ignoring additional tech points from their ability modifier).
Note that if you are only swapping the rest mechanics, this has no impact on powers known or casting ability, as discussed earlier in this variant rule.

entries.name: Sundry Sidney
entries: For those of you watching A Starstruck Odyssey, Sundry Sidney is a sentinel using {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} instead of {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting}. While they swapped the powers known, type of points, and casting ability, they maintained the {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} recovery of points. Consequently, she kept the three points per level a sentinel would normally receive, instead of halving the number received as with Improved {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} present in the Mechanist Scout archetype.

entries.name: Invocation Versatility
entries: With the semi-recent release that added a second level of customization classes that lack them—collectively referred to as invocations, due to their inspiration from the warlock feature of that name—every class now has two levels of customization available to them: their class's invocation feature, and their archetype. Most (all?) of the class's invocation features are hard-locked; that is, once you choose it, you've got it for life. Benevolent GMs might allow players to replace a choice if they found it underwhelming, but others might not. With this variant rule, however, it is encouraged for GMs to allow their player's to rechoose invocations {@i on a case-by-case basis.}

entries.name: What are Invocations?
entries: Beyond their choice of archetype, each class has a second level of customization collectively referred to as invocations. These invocations are as follows:

items: Engineers have Modification Slots, which vary based on their class.
Fighters have their Combat Superiority Maneuvers.
Scholars have their Academic Superiority Maneuvers {@i and} Discoveries.

entries: Of the ten classes, only engineers (mostly), fighters, and scholars can re-choose their invocations, and even then only sparingly. Using this rule, you can instead let all ten classes re-choose their invocations, at appropriate intervals.

entries.name: When Can They Re-choose?
entries: The easiest route would be to allow characters to re-choose one of their invocation options when they complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, or even when they level up. Alternatively, you might enforce a narrative moment for them to re-choose. For instance, a guardian might not be able to relearn their Guardian Aura without spending some time with their master, while a monk might have to spend time in a monastery to re-choose a Monastic Vow, and a scout might have to spend time alone practicing to re-choose a Scout Routine. Ultimately, the method in which allow your players to re-choose their invocations is up to you and your playgroup. You might even let them re-choose on the fly.

entries.name: Re-choosing Archetypes or Classes?
entries: Re-choosing archetypes or classes is not intended as a part of this variant rule. However, you could easily allow players to do so, though I'd recommend the narrative approach over the simple level up or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Elevation
entries: One aspect of 5e that has been more-or-less untouched is the concept of using elevation to your {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} beyond just creatures not being able to reach you. This variant rule offers mechanical boons to encourage utilizing elevation as a tactical device. Elevation grants a bonus called dominance, which comes in three levels.

A creature has {@b dominance} over another creature if it is at least 10 feet above that creature vertically, and at least 10 feet away from that creature horizontally. While a creature has dominance over another, it has a +2 bonus to ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against the dominated creature, and the dominated creature suffers a -2 penalty to Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against effects the creature dominating it controls. Additionally, a creature with dominance has a +2 bonus to AC and Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against a creature it is dominating.

A creature has {@b superdominance} over another creature if it is at least 20 feet above that creature vertically, and at least 20 feet away from that creature horizontally. While a creature has superdominance over another, it has a +3 bonus to ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against the superdominated creature, and the superdominated creature suffers a -3 penalty to Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against effects the creature dominating it controls. Additionally, a creature with superdominance has a +3 bonus to AC and Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against a creature it is dominating.

A creature has {@b hyperdominance} over another creature if it is at least 30 feet above that creature vertically, and at least 30 feet away from that creature horizontally. While a creature has hyperdominance over another, it has a +5 bonus to ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against the hyperdominated creature, and the hyperdominated creature suffers a -5 penalty to Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against effects the creature dominating it controls. Additionally, a creature with hyperdominance has a +5 bonus to AC and Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against a creature it is dominating.

A creature can only benefit from one level of dominance at a time for each creature it would be dominating, but it can have different levels of dominance for different creatures. For instance, if a creature is 30 feet above another creature both vertically and horizontally, it is hyperdominating that creature. If it is 20 feet above another creature vertically and 15 feet horizontally, it is only dominating the third creature instead of superdominating, since both values exceed 10 feet, but not 20.

entries.name: Advantage and Disadvantage
entries: If a creature has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}, it can choose to forgo that {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} when making an attack to increase its domination level by one against its target until the end of its turn. For instance, if a creature has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} and is 20 feet above another creature both vertically and horizontally, it is superdominating that creature. The creature can choose to forgo its {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} to instead hyperdominate the creature until the end of its turn.
If a creature is suffering from {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}, it can't dominate another creature regardless of how far away from that creature it is, horizontally or vertically.

entries.name: Cover
entries: If a creature would be dominating another creature, and it also has {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} from that creature, the bonus to AC and Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} don't stack. Instead, the dominating creature gains the higher of the two bonuses. For instance, if a creature is dominating another creature, and it also has {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|half cover} from that creature, it only gains the +3 bonus to AC and Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against that creature. However, if the dominated creature has a feature that allows it to ignore the benefit of {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}, such as {@optfeature Sharpshooter Mastery|sw5e-phb}, the dominating creature would still gain the +2 benefit from dominating the other creature.

Conversely, if a creature is both dominated by another creature, and it has {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} from that creature, you don't add the bonus and penalty together. Instead, you reduce a creatures dominance by one for each level of {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} it has. For instance, if a creature is superdominated by a creature, but it also has one-quarter {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} from that creature, it is instead just dominated. If the creature that is dominating it has a feature that allows it to ignore the benefit of {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}, such as a {@optfeature Sharpshooter Mastery|sw5e-phb}, however, the creature is still superdominated since the creature dominating it isn't affected by the {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}.

entries.name: Gestalt and Dichotomous Characters
entries: Best suited for smaller parties, gestalt and dichotomous Characters are two separate variant rules that have some conceptual overlap. Gestalt focuses on a character having two classes simultaneously, while, dichotomous focuses on having one class, with two archetypes. If either—or Ashla forbid, both—of these concepts sound intriguing to you, consider the following variant rules.

entries.name: Gestalt Characters
entries: As indicated above, gestalt characters level in two classes simultaneously. They gain all of the proficiencies and features of each class, with following adjustments.

entries.name: Experience Gain
entries: Because a character is leveling in two classes simultaneously, the amount of experience that character should require to gain a level should double. For instance, going from 2nd level to 3rd requires 600 experience points. For a gestalt character, it instead requires 1,200.

entries.name: Hit Points and Hit Dice
entries: If a character chooses two classes with different sized Hit Dice, they should take the average of the two Hit Die sizes (rounded down), and they don't add the Hit Dice together. For instance, if a gestalt character chooses to level in consular, who has a {@dice d6} Hit Die, and guardian, who has a {@dice d10} Hit Die, that character would have a {@dice d8} Hit Die. If the player chooses consular and sentinel, who has a {@dice d8} Hit Die, however, their Hit Die would be a {@dice d6}, since that would be the average of the two Hit Die sizes rounded down.

entries.name: Starting Proficiencies and Equipment
entries: For starting proficiencies and equipment, what you receive varies: {@b {@i Saving Throws.}} You choose the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} pair offered by either class. You cannot mix-and-match, and you do not get both.
{@b {@i Skills.}} You choose the skills offered by one of your classes. You cannot mix-and-match, and you do not get both.
{@b {@i Weapons, Armor, and Tools.}} You gain the weapons, armor, and tool proficiencies for both classes.
{@b {@i Starting Equipment.}} You gain the starting equipment—or starting wealth—for either class. You cannot mix-and-match, and you do not get both.

entries.name: Ability Score Increases
entries: When a gestalt character reaches 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, they gain the Ability Score Improvement feature in both classes. At each of these levels, that character should only gain this feature once, instead of twice. Alternatively, you can give them the full +2 Ability Score Improvement from one class, and a feat from the other, as with the ASI and a Feat variant rule.

entries.name: Force- and Tech-Casting
entries: If a character chooses two classes that both have force- or tech-casting, they use the following adjustments:

items: They determine their Max Power Level as if they were multiclassing. If the potential Max Power Level of the two classes combined would exceed 9, however, they instead use the fullcasting Max Power Level progression present on the Multiclass Max Power Level table.
They add the force or tech points from both classes together.
They learn their powers separately by class, as with multiclassing, and those powers are restricted by that class's native Max Power Level regardless of their gestalt Max Power Level.

entries: If a character chooses two classes with opposing casting, they ignore these rules. For instance, if a gestalt character levels as consular and scout, force- and tech-casting are treated separately as determined by their class.

entries.name: Overlapping Features
entries: If two classes receive features that overlap, and aren't otherwise mentioned, it's up to the GM to determine how those features interact.

entries.name: Multiclassing
entries: Gestalt Characters are not suitable for multiclassing.

entries.name: Dichotomous Characters
entries: Instead of your character leveling in two classes simultaneously, you can have your character level in one class, but with two archetypes from that class.

When a character reaches third level, they gain an archetype of their choice for their chosen class. Using this variant, they instead can choose two. At each level within that class that they would gain archetype features, they gain the features for both archetypes. If archetypes offer features that conflict, it's up to the GM to determine how those features interact.
Alternatively, you can have a dichotomous character choose the features of only one archetype at a given level, rather than both, allowing the player to mix and match archetype features.

entries.name: Multiclassing
entries: If a dichotomous character multiclasses, and reaches third level in two or more classes, it's up to the GM to determine whether they gain multiple archetypes in each class, or only in one.

entries.name: Gestalt and Dichotomous
entries: Gestalt and dichotomous characters, since they impact only certain parts of the character generation experience, work seamlessly together. Simply follow the rules associated with gestalt characters, including the restriction on multiclassing, and allow them to choose two archetypes in each class at 3rd level.

entries.name: Called Shots
entries: Often times, in combat, characters might want to target a specific body part or feature of their target when making an attack. This is commonly referred to as a "called shot." If this is a mechanic you want to implement in your game, consider using the following variant rule.

entries.name: Calling A Shot
entries: In order to make a called shot, you must first be making an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}. If you want to turn that attack into a called shot, you can choose to do so by forgoing that {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}. If you do so, and the attack hits, the hit becomes a called shot.

entries.name: Effects
entries: When you hit with a called shot, you can choose to deal normal weapon damage and then roll a d100 to determine the effect of the shot randomly using the Called Shot Effects table below. Alternatively, you can choose to roll your damage dice twice and take the lesser total. If you do so, you can choose the effect you want to cause on the Called Shot Effects table below, instead of determining it randomly.

rows: {@b {@i Leg Shot.}} The creature gains 1 {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level until the end of its next turn.
{@b {@i Arm Shot.}} The creature can not use an arm until the end of its next turn. If the creature has multiple arms, determine which arm is affected randomly.

{@b {@i Scatter Shot.}} If the creature attempts to cast a power before the end of its next turn, it must first make a {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} check (DC = 10 + the power's level). On a failure, any resources are spent and the power immediately fails.
{@b {@i Head Shot.}} The creature is {@condition Blinded|sw5e-phb|blinded} until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: Unlike traditional 5e, Star Wars 5e places a significantly greater emphasis on the use of tools. Additionally, Star Wars 5e has substantially more languages than traditional 5e, since it spans an entire galaxy, with hundreds if not thousands of species, each speaking their own language. Using this variant rule, you can add additional proficiencies in tools and languages to your players beyond those offered by their species, class, or background.

entries.name: Proficiency Points
entries: Each character gains a number of proficiency points equal to their {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. These proficiency points can be spent to learn languages or tool proficiencies at a ratio of 1 point per language or tool.

entries.name: Tool Expertise
entries: If a character wants to instead use their points to gain {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in a tool, the GM might allow them to spend 2 proficiency points to gain {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in a tool in which they are already proficient.

entries.name: When Are They Chosen?
entries: Each character can choose to spend their proficiency points at any time to gain proficiency in a language or tool. If they would do so in a moment when that language or proficiency would become relevant to the story, they must first justify how they already know that language or tool proficiency. For instance, if the party encounters a particular species from which they need to glean information, and they have no way to communicate with that species, one of your players might spend a proficiency point to learn the language that species speaks. In order to do so, however, they must first explain how they would know that language. Perhaps they grew up with a wandering member of that species who taught it to them? Or maybe they took this specific language as an elective during their education?

entries.name: Alternative Proficiencies
entries: Alternatively, you might allow your players to spend their proficiency points to gain proficiency in weapons or armor. A character could spend 1 proficiency point to gain proficiency in a singular weapon, or 2 proficiency points to gain proficiency in a weapon category ({@filter all blasters|items|firearm=true}, {@filter lightweapons|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}, or {@filter vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon}). A character could also spend 2 proficiency points to gain proficiency in a type of armor. However, they would first need to have proficiency in the lesser armors. For instance, to gain proficiency in {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor}, you must first have proficiency in {@filter medium armor|items|type=medium armor}. To gain proficiency in {@filter medium armor|items|type=medium armor}, you must first have proficiency in {@filter light armor|items|type=light armor}.

entries.name: Skill Expertise
entries: If a character wants to instead use their points to gain {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in a skill, the GM might allow them to spend 4 proficiency points to gain {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in a skill in which they are already proficient.

entries.name: Alternative At-Wills and Extra Attack
entries: One of my many gripes with 5e is that its cantrips scale with character level. I find that this doesn't make sense both mechanically and logically; if I multiclass 2 levels of fighter and 3 levels of warlock, I don't magically get Extra Attack, but for some reason I can create two beams when I cast {@i eldritch blast}. If you want to try alternative at-will power scaling, consider this variant rule.

entries.name: Caster Level
entries: Instead of having at-will powers that improve at 5th, 11th, and 17th {@i character} level, instead have them scale at 5th, 11th, and 17th {@i caster} level. Caster level is, effectively, what you're calculating when you are determining your Max Power Level while multiclassing.

To determine your caster level, you divide your class's potential Max Power Level by 9, and then multiply the result by your number of levels in that class. That number is your caster level. For the full-caster classes—consular and engineer—this will be the same as your level in that class. For other casting classes and archetypes, your caster level will be lower than your level in that class.

When multiclassing, you determine your caster level by dividing each class's potential Max Power Level by 9, multiplying the result by the number of levels in that class, adding the results for each class together, and rounding down the final result. For instance, if you have four levels in Marauder Approach berserker (1.77) and three levels in guardian (1.67), your caster level is 3.

entries.name: Results
entries: Ultimately, the results of this variant rule mean that a 20th-level fighter who took the {@feat Force-Sensitive|sw5e-phb} feat and the {@i shock} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} is no longer as potent with {@i shock} as a 20th-level consular. Both mechanically and flavorfully, this aligns to me. Additionally, it means the consular who focuses on the Force is also better with their at-will powers than an equal level guardian or sentinel, which again makes more sense mechanically and flavorfully.

entries.name: Favored At-Wills
entries: Some archetypes, such as most sentinel archetypes or Soresu guardian, are built around a specific at-will. Your GM might consider letting characters of that archetype use native scaling. However, if adopting this variant rule, they should only scale with class level in this way, rather than character level.

entries.name: Multiclassing Extra Attack
entries: If using this variant rule, you might consider allowing characters who multiclass in classes with the Extra Attack feature to add their class levels together to gain that feature. Their combined level in those classes must satisfy the level requirement in both classes to receive this benefit, however.

For instance, a character with 2 levels in fighter and 3 levels in berserker would be eligible for Extra Attack, since their combined levels would meet the 5th-level requirement for Extra Attack in both classes.

On the other hand, a character with 2 levels in fighter and 3 levels in armormech engineer, would not be eligible for Extra Attack, since their combined levels levels don't meet the 6th-level requirement for Extra Attack in armormech engineer. If that character gains an additional level in either class, or a level in another class with the Extra Attack feature, however, they would now meet the requirements for Extra Attack in all three classes, and thus would gain the feature.

If a class or archetype has a restriction to their Extra Attack feature, such as armormech engineer requiring that you are wearing your modified armor or wielding your modified shield to gain the benefit, the character must meet that requirement to gain the benefits of Extra Attack while multiclassing.

entries.name: Greater Extra Attack
entries: No characters should receive the Greater Extra Attack feature through this multiclassing variant, since that feature is exclusive to fighter.

entries.name: Longer Rests
entries: SW5e offers greater character customization than traditional 5e, and ultimately yields more powerful characters. If you find yourself struggling to challenge your party, consider using the following variant rule to make them stretch their resources.

entries.name: Quick Rest
entries: A quick rest is a period of downtime, at least 1 hour long, during which a character does nothing more strenuous than eating, drinking, reading, and tending to wounds.

A character can spend one or more Hit Dice at the end of a quick rest, up to the character's maximum number of Hit Dice, which is equal to the character's level. Whenever a character spends a Hit Die to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, the player rolls the die and adds the character's Constitution modifier to it. The character regains {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to the total. The player can decide to spend an additional Hit Die after each roll.

entries.name: Short Rest
entries: A {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest} is a period of extended downtime, at least 8 hours long, during which a character sleeps for at least 6 hours and performs light activity, such as reading, talking, eating, or standing watch, for no more than 2 hours. If the rest is interrupted by a period of strenuous activity—fighting, casting powers, at least 4 hours of walking, or similar adventuring activity—the characters must restart the rest to benefit from it.

At the end of a {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest}, a character regains missing {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} up to half their hit point maximum (rounded up). A character can then spend one or more Hit Dice, up to the character's maximum number of Hit Dice, which is equal to the character's level. Whenever a character spends a Hit Die to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, the player rolls the die and adds the character's Constitution modifier to it. The character regains {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to the total. The player can decide to spend an additional Hit Die after each roll.

A character can't benefit from more than one {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest} in a 24-hour period, and a character must have at least 1 hit point at the start of the rest to gain its benefits.

entries.name: Long Rest
entries: A {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} is a period of extended downtime, at least 2 days long, during which a character sleeps for at least 6 hours each day, and performs light activity, such as reading, talking, eating, or standing watch during the remainder of the {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. If the rest is interrupted by a period of strenuous activity—fighting, casting powers, at least 4 hours of walking, or similar adventuring activity—the characters must restart the rest to benefit from it.

At the end of a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, a character regains all lost {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}. The character also regains spent Hit Dice, up to a number of dice equal to half of the character's total number of them (minimum of one).

A character can't benefit from more than one {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} in a 7-day period, and a character must have at least 1 hit point at the start of the rest to gain its benefits.

entries.name: Power Durations and Other Effects
entries: Certain powers, such as {@i battle precognition} or {@i force barrier}, are powers that are intended to be cast once or twice per adventuring day. Since long rests are now once per week instead of once per day, consider increasing the duration of these powers to 24 hours, or even up to three days, as you deem appropriate.

entries.name: Wounds
entries: When a character is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, begins making {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throws}, and has {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} restored, they can return to the battle no worse for the wear. Using this variant rule, you can add an additional layer to make falling to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} more threatening.

entries.name: Gaining Wounds
entries: When a character is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, that character must make a DC 10 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a success, nothing happens, but the DC of this {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} for that character increases by 5, cumulatively, until they complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} or fail the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, at which point the DC resets to 10. On a failed save, the character suffers 1 wounded level. On a success or a failure, a creature immediately gains one {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throw} failure for each wounded level it has.

For instance, if a character with no wounded levels is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} and fails their Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, they gain 1 wounded level, and they then gain 1 {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throw} failure for their 1 wounded level. Alternatively, if a character with 2 wounded levels is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} and succeeds on their Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, they don't gain a wounded level, but they then gain 2 {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throw} failures for their 2 wounded levels. If they take damage, or fail the {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throw} they make at the start of their next turn, they immediately die.

entries.name: Clearing Wounds
entries: A character loses all wounded levels when they are restored to their hit point maximum, whether through consumables, powers, resting, or other means.

entries.name: Critical Saving Throws
entries: Unlike {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls}, which have critical hits and critical misses, {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} don't have critical successes or failures. Using this variant rule, you can allow critical successes and failures on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}.

entries.name: Critical Success
entries: When a creature rolls a 20 on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against an effect, they automatically succeed on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, even if the result of their save would not meet or exceed the save DC. Additionally, if they would suffer any effects on a successful save, such as half damage, they treat the effect's damage as if it had rolled the minimum.

entries.name: Critical Failure
entries: When a creature rolls a 1 on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against an effect, they automatically fail the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, even if the result of their save would meet or exceed the save DC. Additionally, if the effect would deal damage, they treat the effect's damage as if it had rolled the maximum.

entries.name: Features That Grant Critical Saves
entries: Certain features, such as the Explosives fighting style or the Heavy Weapon Specialization feat, grant the ability for certain {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to deal critical damage. If you are using this variant rule, instead have them expand the {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} range by 1. For instance, while using this variant rule, a character with the Explosives fighting style would have a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} range of 2 on their grenades. Consequently, creatures that roll a 1 or a 2 on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against their grenades would critically fail their saves.
Additionally, you can consider allowing weapons with the keen property to increase the {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} range of their burst or rapid properties.

entries.name: Saving Throw Checks
entries: If you use the Saving Throw Checks variant, you would instead allow effects to critically succeed if they would critically hit, and critically fail if they would critically miss, as appropriate.

entries.name: Careful Checks
entries: When you spend at least 10 minutes performing an activity that requires an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, that check has consequences for failure, and you don't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the check, you can choose to make that check carefully, colloquially called "taking 10". If you do so, you treat the check as if you had rolled a 10 on the {@dice d20}. For instance, if you are crafting an item, during resolution you make an Intelligence check with the appropriate tools to determine your d100 Roll Modifier. Instead of rolling the {@dice d20}, you can make a careful check and take 10, treating the check as if you'd rolled a 10, adding your Intelligence modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, if you are proficient with the tools.
If you would have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the check, you can instead take 15.

entries.name: Replacing Powers
entries: Often a player might feel restricted because they made a bad power choice, and they don't want to wait until their next level up to do so. If this is a mechanic that suits your players, consider using the following variant rule.

Each time a character completes a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, they can attempt to take one power they know and replace it with another power, as long as that power is not of a higher level than their Max Power Level. If the character knows both force and {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, those powers can only be replaced with another force or {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, respectively.

The character immediately unlearns the power they are trying to replace, and then must make a force- or tech-casting {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} (using Wisdom or Charisma as appropriate, depending on {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} alignment) with proficiency. The DC of the check varies depending on the level of the power the character is attempting to learn, as shown in the Power Level Check DC table below.

entries.name: Power Level Check DC
entries: On a success, the new power is learned. On a failure, the new power is not learned, the old power is still forgotten, and the character can't try again until their next {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
When attempting to replace a power, if the character currently has a vacant power known slot, they do not need to first unlearn a power before attempting to fill that slot.

entries.name: Exertion
entries: When the outlook of a situation is grim, player's might want to have their character attempt to go above and beyond, fueling their endeavors with their own vitality at the expense of potentially overexerting themselves through use of this variant rule.

entries.name: Exert
entries: Once per round, a player can have their character attempt to exert themselves. When the character makes an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, the character can roll a Hit Die without expending it, adding the result of the die to the roll. Alternatively, on their turn, the character can roll a Hit Die without expending it, increasing their {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} by 5 x the amount rolled until the end of their turn. If the character has Hit Dice of different sizes, they can choose which Hit Die they use.
The character can wait until after it rolls the {@dice d20} before deciding to exert themselves, but must decide before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails.

entries.name: Over-Exertion
entries: When a character exerts themselves, they immediately lose {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to the amount rolled, which can't be reduced or negated in any way. If this damage would reduce the character to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, they don't immediately fall {@condition Unconscious|sw5e-phb|unconscious}. At the end of the current turn, if the character is still at 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, they fall {@condition Unconscious|sw5e-phb|unconscious} and are stable.

entries.name: Simplified Styles and Masteries
entries: In lieu of the fighting style and fighting mastery options available in the PHB, using this variant rule you can instead use the options present here.

entries.name: Fighting Styles
entries: Certain class features or feats offer your choice of Fighting Style. Choose from the following. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

entries.name: Brawling
entries: You are skilled at using your weight to your {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}. You gain the following benefits:

items: You are proficient with improvised weapons.
Your unarmed strike damage increases by one step (from 1 to {@dice d4}, {@dice d4} to {@dice d6}, or {@dice d6} to {@dice d8}).

When you attempt to shove or grapple a creature, or make an attack against a creature with an unarmed strike or an improvised weapon wielded in one hand on your turn, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to make an additional attack, grapple, or shove against the same creature.

entries.name: Close Quarters Shooting
entries: You are skilled at getting up close and personal with {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} weapons. While you are wielding a {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} weapon with which you are proficient, you gain the following benefits:

items: When making a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} while you are within 5 feet of a hostile creature, you do not have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}.
Your ranged weapon attacks ignore {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|half cover} against targets within 15 feet of you.
You gain a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} you make with {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} weapons.

entries.name: Defense
entries: You are skilled at the art of defending yourself. While you are wearing armor with which you are proficient, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to AC.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid being moved.

entries.name: Dueling
entries: You are skilled in the art of fighting with a single melee weapon. While you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand with which you are proficient and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls.

entries.name: Equilibrium
entries: You are skilled at fighting while minimally armored. While you are wearing no armor and not wielding a medium or heavy shield, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to AC.
You gain a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} you make with {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes} and weapon attacks.

entries.name: Great Weapon Fighting
entries: You are skilled at putting the weight of a weapon to your {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}. While you are wielding a melee weapon in two hands with which you are proficient, when you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll, even if the new roll is a 1 or a 2.

entries.name: Sentinel
entries: You are skilled at techniques that take {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} of every drop in any enemy's guard. While you are wielding a melee weapon with which you are proficient, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to enter a defensive stance that lasts until the start of your next turn.
